articles.title: OpenAI incorporará investigadores externos para detectar si sus modelos de IA intentan evadir controles
articles.text:
OpenAI integrará investigadores de cuatro organizaciones externas en pruebas piloto para evaluar la seguridad de sus modelos de inteligencia artificial. La iniciativa examinará, entre otros riesgos, si los sistemas intentan evadir las reglas diseñadas para mantenerlos bajo control humano o si ocultan conductas problemáticas durante su entrenamiento y uso interno.
Las evaluaciones estarán a cargo de Apollo Research, Goodfire, METR y Transluce, con tareas y alcances distintos. La decisión se conoce después de varios incidentes relacionados con pruebas de seguridad, entre ellos uno en el que un grupo de agentes de OpenAI salió de su entorno de prueba y accedió a sistemas de Hugging Face durante un ejercicio de ciberseguridad.
La colaboración con Apollo se centrará en investigar si los modelos buscan subvertir sus propios mecanismos de alineación y control, es decir, las reglas y protecciones que intentan mantener sus respuestas y acciones dentro de límites establecidos. Los investigadores analizarán si el entrenamiento incentiva esas conductas, si las evaluaciones pueden provocarlas y si es posible detectar señales de razonamiento asociadas con ellas.
Qué evaluará cada organización
Goodfire aportará especialistas en interpretabilidad, un campo que busca entender cómo funcionan los modelos internamente. La organización usará sus herramientas para observar procesos de entrenamiento, ayudar a identificar comportamientos no deseados y contribuir a mejorar la alineación de los sistemas. Sus hallazgos estarán dirigidos principalmente a los investigadores de OpenAI.
METR realizará dos evaluaciones. Una buscará comportamientos peligrosos o inesperados que las pruebas internas de OpenAI podrían no haber detectado. La otra revisará si los propios sistemas de la empresa son capaces de reconocer esas conductas. Para la primera evaluación, METR tendrá margen para decidir qué investigar y cómo poner a prueba el modelo. El alcance de la segunda todavía estaba en discusión, según la información publicada.
Transluce examinará si las evaluaciones de seguridad que OpenAI realiza después del entrenamiento son suficientes. También prevé estudiar en 2027 cómo la empresa utiliza los resultados de esas pruebas para decidir si un modelo está listo para salir al público.
Estas pruebas buscan ampliar la supervisión externa más allá de las revisiones que suelen hacerse poco antes de lanzar un producto. Algunos evaluadores sostienen que revisar un modelo únicamente al final del desarrollo no permite detectar comportamientos que podrían aparecer durante el entrenamiento o cuando el sistema se utiliza dentro de la propia empresa.
Dudas sobre la independencia de las pruebas
El acuerdo con Apollo establece límites al acceso de sus investigadores. La organización podrá consultar información relevante para examinar las posibles conductas de subversión, como código y conjuntos de datos de entrenamiento, registros de ciertos procesos de aprendizaje y versiones intermedias de los modelos. Sin embargo, el acceso se restringirá a modelos, periodos y preguntas acordados con OpenAI.
La empresa también se reserva la posibilidad de retener información por razones de seguridad, protección de propiedad intelectual o dificultades técnicas. Apollo señala que OpenAI aceptó no ocultar datos simplemente porque fueran desfavorables. Aun así, sus investigadores no tendrán acceso libre a todo el personal: podrán hablar con empleados autorizados, seleccionados por OpenAI, y deberán canalizar cualquier seguimiento sobre información confidencial a través de la compañía.
La publicación de resultados es otro punto de debate. Apollo podrá difundir conclusiones independientes y explicar las condiciones de sus evaluaciones, pero OpenAI podrá limitar qué evidencia de respaldo se hace pública. Esto podría dificultar que terceros revisen por su cuenta cómo se llegó a esas conclusiones. La empresa indicó que su Comité de Seguridad y Protección, que supervisa estos asuntos para la junta de la Fundación OpenAI, tendrá acceso a informes completos y podrá conversar directamente con los evaluadores.
Además, Apollo y Goodfire recibirán compensación económica por su trabajo; METR y Transluce no cobrarán, aunque podrían aceptar créditos de cómputo o de API. Para algunos críticos, los límites de acceso y divulgación reducen la independencia de las pruebas. OpenAI presenta el programa como un primer paso hacia evaluaciones externas más profundas. Su eficacia dependerá de cuánto puedan observar los investigadores y de qué información llegue finalmente al público.

articles.title: YouTube va désormais deviner combien vous êtes sur le canapé et ses compteurs vont grimper
articles.text:
YouTube va intégrer à ses compteurs publics une estimation du nombre de personnes réunies devant une TV. Une décision qui va faire grimper les vues, mais pas forcément les revenus des créateurs.
Un vent de changement souffle sur YouTube. La plateforme a récemment relégué son bouton « J'aime » dans un menu secondaire et ses développeurs travaillent actuellement sur un mystérieux projet social, nommé Tamba. Une nouvelle hausse de prix est également dans les tuyaux. Mais ce ne sont pas les seules évolutions prévues puisque YouTube prévoit aussi de toucher à l’un de ses plus importants indicateurs. On vous explique.
YouTube prendra désormais en compte les co-vues
Les utilisateurs sont de plus en plus nombreux à regarder YouTube sur leur téléviseur : plus d’un milliard d’heures de vidéos sont englouties chaque jour via ce support. Face à ce constat, YouTube a souhaité modifier sa façon de comptabiliser ces vues.
L’équipe de YouTube Creator Insider a annoncé ce changement de taille hier sur X.com : « YouTube déploie actuellement une mise à jour visant à inclure le nombre de « co-views » (c’est-à-dire le nombre estimé de personnes regardant ensemble à la télévision) dans le nombre de vues publiques des vidéos. »
Ces co-vues prennent en compte les formats longs, les Shorts et les directs mais uniquement sur téléviseur : les smartphones et les ordinateurs ne sont pas de la partie. L’objectif est, avant tout, de parler le même langage que les chaînes et services de streaming, qui évaluent l’audience totale d’un programme, mais aussi de mesurer « la portée réelle des créateurs de contenu. »
Pas de panique : YouTube n’a pas prévu d’implanter une caméra dans votre salon. Le calcul repose sur un modèle statistique conçu par des chercheurs de Google qui se base sur les caractéristiques de la population et ses horaires de visionnage. Les résultats sont ensuite ajustés en prenant en compte des panels de téléspectateurs.
Des scores plus flatteurs, mais pas plus rémunérateurs
Les vues déjà comptabilisées ne seront pas affectées par ce nouveau calcul mais YouTube précise tout de même que les co-visionnages « s'appliqueront aux nouvelles vues TV à l’avenir, y compris sur les anciennes vidéos ». Côté créateurs, un « taux de co-visionnage » sera disponible dans YouTube Studio, dans la section dédiée aux différents types d’appareils. Les plus matheux pourront diviser le total des vues par le nouveau taux pour retrouver le chiffre sans estimation. À noter : YouTube donne aux créateurs jusqu’à mai 2027 pour exporter leurs anciens chiffres.
- Grande diversité de contenus
- Monétisation pour les créateurs
- Accessibilité sur toutes les plateformes
Quel sera l’impact de ces co-vues ? Selon toute logique les scores devraient être revus à la hausse et la durée de visionnage cumulée aussi. En revanche, cela ne modifiera pas les impressions de miniatures, le taux de clics et la durée moyenne. Ceux qui espéraient toucher plus de revenus seront déçus : dans son annonce, YouTube a tenu à préciser que « les « co-vues » n’ont aucune incidence sur les revenus publicitaires ni sur les seuils du Programme Partenaires YouTube : les revenus des créateurs, les versements AdSense et l’éligibilité au Programme Partenaires YouTube continuent de reposer sur les vues éligibles et les heures de visionnage. »
Ces nouvelles co-vues ont donc tout de la « vanity metric » et on se demande bien qui elles flatteront le plus : les créateurs… ou YouTube.

articles.title: GTA 6 revela cómo será su sistema meteorológico: tormentas, niebla y clima que cambia por regiones
articles.text:
A pocos días del lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), Rockstar Games ofreció un nuevo vistazo al clima de su mundo abierto. En colaboración con The Weather Channel, la desarrolladora presentó una serie de pronósticos ficticios para Leonida, el estado inspirado en Florida donde se desarrolla la historia. Las imágenes y descripciones muestran lluvias intensas, niebla costera, tormentas tropicales y condiciones distintas entre regiones.
El material destaca que la meteorología no será igual en todo el mapa. Mientras una zona puede tener lluvias torrenciales, otra podría estar cubierta de niebla o presentar cielos despejados. Owen Shepherd, vicepresidente de Arte, Iluminación y Renderizado de Rockstar, explicó que el estudio rediseñó el sistema meteorológico para que las condiciones sean más localizadas, persistentes y dinámicas.
La propuesta busca reflejar la imprevisibilidad climática de Florida, fuente de inspiración para Leonida. Según Shepherd, en el juego los usuarios podrán pasar de cielos despejados a grandes nubes cumulonimbos, asociadas con tormentas intensas. La colaboración con The Weather Channel sirvió para presentar las condiciones como si fueran reportes meteorológicos reales de distintas localidades del juego.
Lluvias intensas, niebla y tormentas en Leonida
En los Cayos de Leonida, uno de los pronósticos advierte que la lluvia fuerte puede reducir la visibilidad en las carreteras. El reporte ficticio menciona reflectores instalados en algunos tramos para ayudar a los conductores y recomienda revisar los faros de los vehículos. De esta manera, la lluvia aparece vinculada con situaciones cotidianas del entorno, como manejar con visibilidad limitada.
En los pantanos de Pelican Valley, las tormentas pueden enturbiar el agua y dificultar la detección de caimanes. En la costa de South Ocean Beach, la niebla marina puede cubrir las vistas al océano, mientras que una tormenta tropical cerca del Rusty Anchor genera oleaje fuerte y complica la navegación. Gambit Bay, por su parte, puede amanecer bajo una capa de niebla asociada con la humedad de la zona.
Las condiciones también variarán en Key Lento, donde la lluvia y las ráfagas de viento podrían complicar los desplazamientos. Estos escenarios dan cuenta de un clima que busca cambiar con el territorio y afectar la apariencia de distintos lugares, en lugar de aplicar el mismo efecto meteorológico a todo el mapa al mismo tiempo.
Un clima que podría influir en la experiencia de juego
La información divulgada sugiere que el tiempo tendrá consecuencias que van más allá del aspecto visual. La lluvia puede limitar la visibilidad al conducir; la niebla, ocultar paisajes costeros; y las tormentas, agitar el mar o alterar el aspecto de los pantanos. Sin embargo, todavía no se conoce con precisión cuánto modificarán estos fenómenos las mecánicas del juego ni si cambiarán la conducción, la navegación o las misiones.
Rockstar ha mostrado situaciones y descripciones ambientales, pero esos ejemplos no permiten confirmar todos los efectos durante una partida. La diferencia es importante: que una tormenta aparezca en una imagen o en un pronóstico promocional no significa necesariamente que cada consecuencia descrita forme parte de una mecánica interactiva. Esos detalles tendrán que comprobarse cuando el juego esté disponible.
El sistema meteorológico también se apoya en una característica central del escenario: la diversidad de Leonida. La combinación de ciudad, costa, pantanos y otras áreas permite que el clima contribuya a diferenciar cada región. Así, los cambios atmosféricos pueden reforzar la sensación de recorrer un territorio amplio y cambiante.
La colaboración con The Weather Channel forma parte de la campaña de presentación de GTA 6 y añade contexto a las nuevas imágenes. Por ahora, el avance confirma que Rockstar busca un clima más localizado y dinámico, con tormentas tropicales, lluvias intensas y bancos de niebla. La magnitud de su impacto en la experiencia de juego quedará más clara cuando los jugadores exploren Leonida.

articles.title: Parallels Desktop review
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Parallels has long been the best option for full Windows emulation on Macs and this is even more true in Parallels 27. While it is limited to Apple Silicon Macs and its best features require an annual subscription, improved graphics support with OpenGL 4.3 and AI functionality makes it the undisputed champion of VMs on MacOS.
Reasons to buy
- + Easy installation of Windows and Linux
- + Simple to use interface
- + Coherence mode allows seamless Windows app use
- + Excellent performance for a VM
- + OpenGL 4.3 support
Reasons to avoid
- - Won’t work on Intel-based Macs
- - Windows licensing adds to the overall cost
- - Best features require annual subscription
- - Not great for gaming
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Apple offers some of the best workstations going, with everything from the MacBook Pro to Mac mini finding its die-hard adherents among professionals of all stripes, Sometimes, though, even the biggest Mac fans need to run software in a Windows environment, whether for software testing or you need to use a professional software suite that has no native Mac support. Enter Parallels 27, the latest version of the best virtual machine software that offers the best of both worlds for Apple users.
This latest version of Parallels brings some big changes, including a complete rewriting of the graphics pipeline for the Apple Metal API, OpenGL 4.3 support (one of the most demanded updates among Parallels users), and the full move over to Apple Silicon-only. While that last bit might irk some who still cling to their Intel-based Macs, many more are going to take issue with the subscription-based model for its most in-demand features.
Despite that, however, there’s no denying that Parallels 27 is the best way to host guest OSs on your Mac, and for most the pros are going to far outweigh the cons.
Parallels Desktop: Plans & Pricing
Parallels 27 comes with four different plans for various use cases: Standard, Pro, Business, and Enterprise.
The Standard plan is available as both an annual subscription and a one time purchase, with the annual subscription list price running $99.99 (about £75 / AU$145), while a one-time, perpetual license costs $219.99 (about £165 / AU$320). It should also be noted that the one-time purchase does not come with free upgrades to newer versions of Parallels, though the subscription plan does.
For the Pro plan and above, an annual subscription is required, starting at $119.99 (about £90 / AU$175) for a Pro plan and $149.99 (about £110 / AU$220) for a Business plan. Enterprise customers will need to contact Parallels’ sales department to negotiate an Enterprise plan rate.
For most casual users, the Standard plan is the way to go, though it is limited to four virtual CPU cores (vCPUs) and 8GB of virtual RAM (vRAM), though this should be more than enough for basic office software and productivity apps. Stepping up to the Pro tier or higher gets you up to 32 vCPUs and up to 128GB vRAM. The Pro plan comes with AI Agent Integration (MCP), disk and memory cleaner, system and performance monitoring, and screen capture and recording, among others.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The Business plan includes those features, plus volume licensing with centralized license admin, automated CI/CD workflows for developers, and automated deployment and update support through Jamf and Intune integration. The Enterprise plan includes things like policy enforcement, compliance visibility, and many other IT tools for large businesses.
The biggest sticking point for Parallels 27 is going to be these prices, largely because there are open-source alternatives out there, but they come with their own trade-offs that might not be worth the savings. None of this, by the way, includes the price of a Windows 11 license, and for businesses in particular, this expense can add up very quickly with multiple deployments across many Mac systems, but this would also be the case with open-source VMs.
Parallels Desktop: Features
The biggest change to Parallels with version 27 is the end of Intel-powered Mac support. Parallels 27 was developed with macOS 27 in mind, and that OS update is Apple Silicon only, so Intel Macs will need to stick with Parallels 26 from here on out. Fortunately, Parallels will continue to support Parallels 26 with security and maintenance updates for some time at least.
It’s also worth pointing out that Parallels 27 uses Windows on Arm by default, and this version of Microsoft’s OS has inherent Intel x86 app compatibility issues that Parallels can’t do anything about. There is an early technology preview allowing you to import existing Intel x86-based Windows VMs, but these will run significantly worse than a Windows on Arm VM since the entire instruction pipeline needs to be emulated.
The other big change is the rewritten graphics driver for OpenGL 4.3 support based on Apple’s Metal API, one of the most requested features if Parallels support forums are any indication. A lot of professional software tools that are Windows-only (like ArcGIS Pro and various CAD software) use OpenGL 4.3, so earlier versions of Parallels struggled with these apps, if they were able to run at all. Parallels 27 is still capped at DirectX 11.1, however, so apps that require DX 12 won’t work. You also need to make sure you have the latest version of Parallels Tools installed to make sure that OpenGL 4.3 will work properly.
Further, on Apple M4 systems or newer, there is now support for Apple’s Scalable Matrix Extension instructions in both Windows and Linux environments, which can speed up AI workloads in compatible apps.
Beyond those changes, Parallels 27 retains the core features of earlier releases, with options to run the guest OS in a window on your macOS desktop, to have it use its own Space on you Mac, or to have individual apps work as-if-native through Parallels Coherence mode. There’s a shared folder between the host and guest OS to make file transferring simple, and drag-and-dropping from one desktop to another is seamless.
Parallels Desktop: Interface & Use
The strongest argument in favor of Parallels, generally, is how low-lift setup and installation is. Unlike a lot of VMs out there, setting up the guest OS is as simple as a couple of button clicks and about 15 minutes of installation time. If you’ve never had to set up a VM before, I can assure you that this is arguably the easiest installation process you’re going to find on the market.
You also have a lot of control over how many resources in terms of CPU cores and memory to assign to the VM, especially at the Pro tier and above, and these settings can be changes nearly on the fly if you need more performance (you do have to stop the VM first though, so save your work before doing so).
Once everything is set up, Parallels feels like just another app on the Mac desktop, with your chosen guest OS running in a window you can click in and out of as needed. If you want a full screen desktop experience, you can get that too.
Coherence mode is very useful if you need to work primarily in macOS but need occasional access to a Windows or Linux app for that work, but I’d argue that this isn’t the best reason to buy Parallels (Crossover does the same thing, by and large, and doesn’t require a whole operating system installation taking up memory and storage resources).
The seamlessness of the overall experience can make you forget that you are using a guest OS, however, so if your organization handles sensitive data, whether from a legal/compliance perspective or internal policy, be sure to manage permissions properly as far as folder and clipboard sharing go, since separation is not the same thing as isolation. Fortunately Parallels has settings to restrict such sharing, but you will need to configure them appropriately for your specific requirements.
The same is true with any VM, of course, but the ease of integration with Parallels is such that complacency might actually be a problem if you’re not careful. In a lot of ways, the complexity and foibles inherent to competing VMs make it harder to forget you are using a VM, and their more ragged interfacing actually helps keep you from oversharing. That simply isn’t the case with Parallels 27.
Parallels Desktop: Support
Despite the ease of use, there are still going to be difficulties with some apps and setups that users might run into. Fortunately, for subscription customers at least, you do get phone, chat, and email support as long as your subscription is active to help diagnose any issues.
Those with a bit more experience with VMs also have access to an extensive knowledge base covering everything from installations to device sharing and common configuration issues. There are also regular security and performance updates that subscription customers will have access to.
There are things, however, that no amount of support is going to help with, particularly if you’re looking for Windows PC gaming support. DirectX 11 games and older should work well enough, but recent titles using DirectX 12 simply aren’t available, and no game is going to run nearly as well as they will natively, whether through a Mac-native version or running the game on a comparable Windows PC.
For game devs (though understandably, this will be a very small subset of you), this latter point is important to keep in mind, and I would definitely recommend using an actual Windows PC for any build testing you need to do if you absolutely must code a game on a Mac.
Parallels Desktop: Performance
Of course, any time you are working with a virtual machine, you’re going to have to sacrifice some performance given the hardware restrictions. Performance is going to depend pretty heavily on what kind of CPU and memory allocations you make, so the higher you can afford, the better your experience will be.
That said, even at the Standard plan’s four cores and 8GB memory restrictions, actual app performance is generally very good, though it will have much more limited multitasking capabilities. This is most obvious when comparing the same benchmarks across different configurations. In Cinebench R24 on a 10-vCPU/12GB-vRAM configuration on an Apple M6 chip, I was able to get a score of 184 for single core performance, which is more or less what you get with a 4-vCPU/8GB-vRAM configuration (TK). Its multi-core score drops with your allocated core count, however, from a 10-vCPU score of 999 in Cinebench R24 down to 601 with a 4-vCPU/8GB allocation.
Similarly, in Geekbench 7, the 10-vCPU/12GB allocation netted a single-core score of 3,495, compared to the 4-vCPU/8GB allocation’s 3,417, which is only about 2% slower. Compare these to the native run of Geekbench 7, which scored 4,052, and you get at worst a roughly 16% hit to single-core performance with Parallels, which is genuinely pretty outstanding for a VM.
The more limited configuration, however, came in with a roughly 31% lower multi-core score (10,356 to the 10-vCPU’s 15,044), and fares even worse next to the native score of 22,180, or about a 53% lower overall performance.
This means that for single app use, you won’t see too much of a difference between a Standard and a Pro plan, but if you plan on doing a lot of work in Windows, including multitasking with several apps, the Pro plan is probably worth the investment.
On the graphics front, the Parallels Display Adapter driver does a solid job, but its performance against native Mac apps is fairly underwhelming. Most of the graphics benchmarks I normally run, like 3DMark Steel Nomad and Solar Bay, won’t even run in Parallels, thanks to the lack of DirectX 12 support. In 3DMark Wild Life Extreme, meanwhile, a 10-vCPU/12GB configuration performed about 58% worse versus native Mac performance.
In OpenGL testing, which is one of the bigger feature updates to parallels with this version, the Windows emulated environment performed somewhat better than the DirectX test, though the 10-vCPU/12GB allocation on an Apple M6 still performed about 31% worse in Unigine’s Valley benchmark (4,127 to 2,859). The Windows VM did manage to score slightly higher than native on Unigine’s Heaven benchmark, scoring 2,160 to the native runs’ average of 2,059, or about a 5% better showing.
Parallels Desktop: Final Verdict
Parallels 27 doesn’t solve all of the compromises you need to make to run a Windows virtual machine on a Mac, but it comes pretty darn close. Its single-app performance running in Windows is nearly indistinguishable from its native counterparts (at least with most apps), and there’s no understating how easy it is to set up and use.
Where it does stumble, particularly in multi-core performance necessary for the kind of multitasking you expect from a fully functional OS, is going to be highly dependent on the host system’s hardware. That said, it’s generally going to underperform what you can get using Mac-native versions of the same apps.
But, if you were able to get those apps on a Mac, you wouldn’t be using Parallels, and so Parallels 27 offers as much of the best of both worlds as you are likely to find on the market.

articles.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
articles.text:
Threat actors have compromised Microsoft's agent-framework package to push a credential stealer, according to reports from Aikido, Chainguard, Endor Labs, OX Security, SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Google-owned Wiz.
The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published 33 minutes apart on November 17, 2026, and are designed to run a credential stealer on every Python start. As of writing, both the release versions have been quarantined on the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository. It's unclear how the attacker managed to obtain publishing access.
Agent-framework is the meta-package for Microsoft Agent Framework, an open-source framework for building and orchestrating artificial intelligence (AI) agents using Python.
"Both versions install Python startup hooks that silently collect credentials, environment data, and cloud identity tokens, then exfiltrate them to a webhook[.]site endpoint," Socket said in a report.
Once either of the versions is installed, the package drops a .pth file in the site-packages root directory, which then gets executed automatically on every interpreter start, causing the credential stealer to run whenever Python is started in an environment, even if the package is not explicitly imported.
"Each wheel adds a .pth file to site-packages," Endor Labs said. "Python executes import lines in .pth files on every interpreter start, so the stealer runs on any Python launch in an affected environment, including pip itself, whether or not anything imports Agent Framework."
The names of the .pth files are below -
- agent_framework_meta.pth in version 1.26.1
- af_runtime_diag.pth in version 1.26.2
The "agent_framework_meta.pth" file contains a single import statement referencing "agent_framework_meta," which then launches the stealer payload. It's capable of capturing the following data -
- Environment variables based on substring-based matching
- Credential files associated with Azure CLI (~/.azure/*.json), .npmrc, pip.conf, .netrc, .git-credentials, .docker/config.json, Hugging Face, Microsoft Azure DevOps agents, and .env and JSON files
- Azure DevOps OIDC tokens
- Azure managed-identity tokens
- Azure instance metadata and retains up to 8,000 characters of the response
"Besides reading credentials already on disk, the code asks the platform to issue new ones," SafeDep said. "Rotating stored secrets does not cover those."
"In an Azure DevOps pipeline, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN and SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI are enough to request a federated token for api://AzureADTokenExchange. On Azure compute, it asks the managed identity endpoint for an access token to each of these resources. It uses IDENTITY_ENDPOINT or MSI_ENDPOINT on App Service and Functions, and 169.254.169[.]254 elsewhere. It also pulls instance metadata."
It's worth noting that the Azure instance metadata service (IMDS) is a RESTful web service that runs on a local IP address ("169.254.169[.]254"), and provides information about the virtual machine, its region, tags, and the identity token.
All the collected information is saved into a JSON document, zlib-compressed, Base64-encoded, and sent via an HTTPS POST request to a hard-coded URL ("webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb").
Version 1.26.2, on the other hand, imports a new top-level module, af_runtime_diag.py, collects GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, and expands the search patterns used for harvesting credential-related environment variables.
Given that the package attracts about 190,000 downloads a month, users are advised to perform the following steps -
- Isolate affected hosts and runners
- Pin the package to the most recent safe version (1.26.0) and restore from a clean environment
- Check for exposure to the malicious versions between 8:35 and roughly 9:20 p.m. UTC on November 17, 2026
- Search proxy and DNS logs for requests to webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb
- Rotate exposed credentials from a clean system
- Audit Azure identities and review sign-in and activity logs
- Audit GitHub Actions workflows that deploy to Azure
"The malicious agent-framework shows how attackers are targeting the AI developer ecosystem and the CI pipelines behind it," OX Security said. "While directly targeting an official Microsoft package, it seems that attackers found a way to hijack the wheel creation flow to add malicious logic inside."
Agent-framework is the second Microsoft-related PyPI package to be compromised this year. In May 2026, the threat actors behind TeamPCP pushed three malicious versions of durabletask, Microsoft's Python client for the Durable Task workflow execution framework, to distribute the Mini Shai-Hulud worm.

articles.title: Lumo Desktop : l’IA de Proton se connecte à vos fichiers, à vos applications et à un calendrier de tâches
articles.text:
Comme prévu, Proton lance Lumo Desktop, une application pour Windows, macOS et Linux. Son assistant IA peut maintenant se connecter à vos fichiers et à vos outils, exécuter des tâches à heure fixe et retenir vos consignes d’une conversation à l’autre.
Jusqu’ici, Lumo répondait dans une fenêtre de discussion. Avec Lumo Desktop, il peut agir sur l’ordinateur et dans les applications de l’utilisateur, avec des droits que celui-ci fixe lui-même.
Fichiers, tâches planifiées, consignes : Lumo sort de la fenêtre de chat
Les Connectors, accessibles depuis le menu « Customize », relient Lumo à des outils externes. Sur l’ordinateur, il peut parcourir les fichiers, lancer des commandes tapées dans le terminal et lire des pages web dans le navigateur. Il se connecte aussi à Proton Mail via Proton Mail Bridge, à Google Drive, à Jira, à Confluence et à des serveurs MCP, locaux ou distants. Le MCP (Model Context Protocol) est un langage commun qui permet à un assistant IA de dialoguer avec un outil tiers. Pour chaque connecteur, l’utilisateur choisit ce qui s’exécute seul, ce qui demande son accord et ce qui est bloqué. Proton cite une boîte mail où Lumo peut chercher, doit demander avant d’envoyer un message et ne peut rien supprimer.
Avec Schedules, Lumo exécute une tâche à une heure précise ou de façon récurrente, comme un résumé hebdomadaire de la boîte de réception ou un bilan mensuel des dépenses. On la décrit en langage courant, Lumo pose les questions qui manquent, puis prépare la tâche à valider. Chaque tâche a ses propres permissions. Les Skills, eux, enregistrent des instructions, des modèles et des fichiers de référence que Lumo réutilise d’une conversation à l’autre, par exemple pour rédiger ses e-mails dans son style. On peut écrire un Skill, demander à Lumo d’en créer un ou en importer un. Les Custom Lumos existants sont migrés automatiquement vers les Skills.
Fin août nous rapportions déjà que le dépôt GitHub public de Proton Mail laissait penser que Lumo pourrait agir dans la messagerie (libellés, filtres Sieve, mise en veille), avec confirmation avant toute action sensible. Puisque la connexion nécessite le bridge, cela signifie donc qu’elle est réservée aux abonnements payants. Rappelons que le bridge permet de configurer un compte Proton Mail sur un gestionnaire de courrier tiers en créant un serveur en local et, ce, afin de contourner les vulnérabilités liées au protocole IMAP.
Côté confidentialité, Proton affirme que les conversations et les données des applications connectées ne servent ni à entraîner des modèles ni à diffuser de la publicité ciblée. Grâce au chiffrement « zero access », seul l’utilisateur peut lire son historique. Lumo ne garde aucun journal côté serveur. Il est protégé par le droit suisse et hébergé en Europe, hors de portée du CLOUD Act américain. Un premier cluster NVIDIA B300 entre en service en Suisse. Pour rappel, cet été, proton a déplacé les serveurs de Lumo vers l’Allemagne. Dans sa démarche de transparence, Proton a publié le code de Lumo Desktop.

articles.title: Equinor, la petrolera de Noruega, sufre un ciberataque en curso que no afectó su producción
articles.text:
Equinor, la mayor productora de petróleo y gas de Noruega, informó que detectó un ciberataque en curso contra algunos de sus sistemas informáticos. La empresa afirmó que el ataque no afectó sus operaciones ni su producción y que no hay indicios de robo de datos.
El comunicado, publicado a las 18:55 (hora de Noruega) y actualizado a las 19:40, indica que la compañía movilizó recursos para neutralizar el ataque y recuperar la integridad de los sistemas. También señala que se informa a las autoridades pertinentes.
Equinor no precisó cuándo comenzó el ataque, qué sistemas fueron alcanzados ni cómo se produjo. Tampoco lo atribuyó a ningún grupo. La empresa dijo que dará nuevas informaciones cuando las tenga.
Reuters, que dio la noticia, indicó que la compañía no había visto robo de datos ni impacto en la operación. El sitio especializado Natural Gas Intelligence describió a la empresa como el mayor proveedor de gas natural de Europa.
Autoridades noruegas en contacto con la empresa
La televisión pública noruega NRK informó que la policía de seguridad del país, conocida como PST, está al tanto del incidente y presta ayuda si hace falta, según el asesor Eirik Veum. La Autoridad Nacional de Seguridad (NSM) también conoce el caso y dialoga con Equinor, dijo su asesora de comunicación Mari Lerdal a la agencia NTB.
La portavoz de Equinor, Ellen Maria Skjelsbæk, se negó a decir a NRK qué sistemas están afectados. Confirmó que la empresa recibe intentos de ataque digital todos los días. “No se puede asegurar uno mismo al cien por ciento”, afirmó.
NRK precisó además que la primera versión del comunicado decía que los empleados podían notar interrupciones en algunos servicios y que, por ahora, no debían tomar ninguna medida. Esas dos frases fueron eliminadas después de la publicación.
El medio especializado Breach News observó que el comunicado separa los sistemas informáticos de los que gestionan las operaciones y la producción, y que Equinor sostiene que solo los primeros fueron alcanzados.
Según ese medio, un ataque a sistemas corporativos puede ser grave si luego deriva en robo de datos o sirve de vía de entrada a los sistemas industriales. Hasta el cierre de su nota, ningún grupo criminal había reivindicado el ataque en público.
Equinor opera, entre otras instalaciones, varias plataformas petroleras en el mar del Norte, según recuerda NRK en su cobertura. La empresa no dijo si el ataque afectó a empleados, socios o clientes.
Una serie de ciberataques en Europa
NRK recordó que en los últimos días hubo varios ciberataques contra distintos objetivos en Europa: afectaron congeladores de supermercados, bancos de sangre y los sistemas informáticos de cadenas de ropa noruegas. El medio también mencionó amenazas de bomba contra vuelos y escuelas del continente.
Poco antes, la NSM había elevado el nivel de riesgo cibernético en Noruega al segundo más alto y publicó una lista de 21 medidas pensadas para todas las empresas del país. Equinor no informó si el ataque tiene relación con esos casos.
La empresa no fijó una fecha para su próxima comunicación: dijo que dará actualizaciones cuando disponga de nueva información.

articles.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
articles.text:
The Russia-linked cyber espionage group known as Cold Relic (formerly COLDRIVER and UNC4057) has been observed weaponizing a single cloud compromise into a launchpad for a series of linked intrusions resulting in third-party compromise.
Google's Mandiant and Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said it investigated a 2026 compromise at a U.S.-based organization in which the adversary leveraged data, the corporate staff directory, and identities harvested from an earlier attack on another U.S.-based entity in late 2025.
Cold Relic, also tracked as Callisto, Gossamer Bear, and Star Blizzard, has a track record of orchestrating sophisticated phishing and malware campaigns to gain access information that may be of strategic importance to the Russian government.
The access is abused to register rogue multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices, passkeys, and MFA backup codes to establish long-term persistence and then conduct aggressive data collection and exfiltration operations targeting email, chat, and cloud storage repositories. In addition, the compromised access is used to target the victim's social and professional networks.
Attacks mounted by the threat actor have successfully compromised high-value targets, including government officials, defense contractors, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) across Europe and North America.
"Once Cold Relic compromises a target, it uses stolen emails and data to establish authentic pretexts and impersonate contacts when reaching out to subsequent targets," Google said.
According to the tech giant's cybersecurity and incident response teams, Cold Relic compromised the cloud productivity environment of an unspecified U.S.-based organization in late 2025. Initial access to the network was achieved by means of a residential proxy network located in close geographical proximity to the victim.
Using the stolen credentials of a Super Admin account and combining it with an MFA push notification fatigue attack, the threat actor is said to have gained access to the account after the victim accepted an MFA request. This was followed by the attacker registering their own device within the tenant to retain access. The threat actor was also observed using passkeys and MFA backup codes as alternate access mechanisms.
"Cold Relic used the privileges of the compromised Super Admin account to download the contents of the entire organization's cloud storage drive by both mass sharing files to a Cold Relic-operated email account and downloading files directly," Google explained.
"While operating inside the tenant of the victim organization, Cold Relic accessed the Admin Console, queried Admin security investigation and email audit logs to check defensive visibility, and viewed, modified, and deleted Alert Center notifications to remove forensic evidence of the initial intrusion."
These actions ultimately enabled the threat actor to export full employee lists and domain-wide data via the Google Takeout service using the Super Admin privileges. Following mass data theft, the attackers continued to maintain access over several months and perform additional activities -
- Sync email inbox via OAuth to external email clients.
- Re-authenticate using unrevoked attacker-enrolled passkeys that persisted across password and session resets and bypassed device registration controls.
- Target cloud drive document access related to credentials, email archives, personnel information, and other documents of interest.
Even after the attackers were ousted from the victim organization, Google said it observed Cold Relic using email accounts impersonating employees of the victim organization to target both internal employees and associates within the same professional circles as part of a renewed social engineering campaign.
The attack then moved to the next phase when the threat actor compromised a Microsoft Entra ID user account of a second U.S.-based organization that used Entra ID as its federated single sign-on (SSO) identity provider for Google Workspace.
By impersonating an employee at the first organization, the threat actor established communications with the target over a secure messaging app and then shared phishing links designed to harvest credentials and authentication tokens for Entra ID under the pretext of sharing a document containing details about a technical issue.
"Upon successful authentication using the stolen credentials, Cold Relic registered and used a new MFA device in the SSO solution to retain access to the user account throughout the intrusion," Google said.
"By impersonating someone known in the same professional circles as the new target, Cold Relic increased their chance of phishing success. Ultimately, in this case, Cold Relic was able to obtain credentials to the organization and perform bulk download of files accessible in the compromised user's cloud drive."
Upon successfully compromising the second organization, the messaging app account used to initiate the conversation had its profile name changed to a different persona. It's suspected that the new persona was likely used to target other organizations in the same professional network.
"Cold Relic's campaigns demonstrate the convergence of human-centric social engineering and cloud identity abuse," Google said. "By obtaining access to strategic personnel rosters and operational documents, Russian intelligence services turn legitimate business communications into attack vectors against trusted partners."

articles.title: No, GTA 6 didn't break the Australian internet, but it sure did break records
articles.text:
No, GTA 6 didn't break the Australian internet, but it sure did break records
NBN Co confirms the highest-ever traffic peak as GTA 6 preloads send downloads soaring
- GTA VI officially launches at different times depending on Australia state and time zone
- Preloading has been live since November 10
- NBN Co has confirmed it has since recorded the most data ever transmitted across the network per second
- We recommend Exetel's NBN 500 plan as a speedy option to ensure you can download the game quickly
The wait is almost over. GTA 6 will finally launch in Australia in the next few hours, with gamers across the country preparing to descend on Vice City for the first time in more than a decade. And if you've already bought your copy, you'll want to make sure it's downloaded and ready to play the moment the clock strikes midnight.
Just last week, I reported on the possibility of GTA 6 breaking the Australian internet, given the game's enormous popularity and the sheer demand that would be placed on the network by millions of eager gamers downloading its mammoth 212GB file.
Well, NBN Co has since followed up with some fresh figures, and while the Australian internet hasn't ground to a halt, it turns out GTA 6 has helped push the network to unprecedented traffic records.
Rob Bates, Senior Manager, Media & External Communications at NBN Co, told me that on Thursday, November 12 — the same day code-in-box versions of the much-anticipated game became available to buy at retailers — the NBN network "hit a new traffic record of 33.19Tbps".
That's a new all-time high, surpassing the previous record of 32.91Tbps set in 2025.
Of course, as much as I (and I’m sure Rockstar) would love to attribute the record entirely to GTA 6, Rob was quick to point out that a Fortnite patch was also released on the same day, which would have contributed to the increased demand.
"That's about 3Tbps or 10% above baseline," he confirmed, adding that it was "the most data ever transmitted across the network per second".
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
For some perspective, 3Tbps is equivalent to 3,000Gbps. Considering even the fastest widely available residential NBN plans currently top out at 2Gbps, that's an almost incomprehensible amount of additional network traffic.
And while the record wasn't solely GTA 6's doing, the game's influence on Australia's internet usage is undeniable.
Since preloading began, NBN Co has recorded more than 70 petabytes (PB) of additional data traffic, which Rob said is "roughly equivalent to 330,000 GTA 6 downloads".
To put that into perspective, 70PB is approximately 70 million gigabytes of data. That's an extraordinary amount of downloading in the space of little more than a week, even if not all of it can be attributed directly to Rockstar's blockbuster.
Tasmania leads the GTA 6 download frenzy
Interestingly, while you might expect Australia's most populous states to have experienced the biggest increases in internet traffic, NBN Co's data reveals a slightly different story.
During the first four days of the GTA 6 preload period, Tasmania recorded the largest peak increase in network traffic above its usual baseline, at a whopping 16.3%.
South Australia followed with a peak increase of 14.2%, narrowly ahead of Victoria at 13.9%, while New South Wales and Queensland recorded increases of 13.8% and 13.6%, respectively.
Western Australia, meanwhile, recorded the smallest peak increase at just 6.6%. Here's how every state and territory compared:
| State / territory | Peak increase above baseline | 
| Tasmania | 16.3% | 
| South Australia | 14.2% | 
| Victoria | 13.9% | 
| New South Wales | 13.8% | 
| Queensland | 13.6% | 
| Northern Territory | 8.9% | 
| ACT | 8.7% | 
| Western Australia | 6.6% | 
Tasmania also came out on top when looking at the average increase in traffic across all four days, recording a 10.7% rise above baseline. Victoria followed at 9.1%, with South Australia rounding out the top three at 8.2%.
It's worth remembering that these figures represent increases relative to each state's usual internet traffic, rather than the total amount of data downloaded. They also don't tell us exactly how many people in each state have purchased GTA 6.
Nevertheless, they offer a fascinating glimpse into just how much demand the game has generated before anyone has even had the chance to play it.
And with the official launch still to come, there's every possibility that Australia's internet traffic records could be challenged once again.
Where to buy GTA 6 in Australia
If you've somehow managed to resist preordering GTA 6 until now, there's still time to get your hands on a copy before launch.
The game is available for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with digital copies available through the PlayStation Store and Xbox's Microsoft Store.
Alternatively, you can purchase a physical code-in-box version from participating Australian retailers. Just remember that these boxed versions don't contain a physical disc. Instead, you'll receive a download code, meaning you'll still need to download the game before you can play.
And with a download size of up to 212GB, I'd strongly recommend getting started as soon as possible, especially if you're on a slower internet connection.
And while the Black Friday sales in Australia might currently be live, it’s practically a guarantee that we won’t see any discounts on the game. There are, however, a number of Black Friday PS5 deals on accessories, including headsets and earbuds.
- Amazon: PS5 – AU$124 | Xbox Series X/S – AU$124
- JB Hi-Fi: PS5 – AU$125 | Xbox Series X/S – AU$125
- Kogan: PS5 – AU$124
- The Gamesmen eBay: PS5 – AU$129.95
Is it too late to upgrade your NBN plan for GTA 6?
With GTA 6's launch just hours away, you might be wondering whether it's worth upgrading your internet plan to speed up the download.
The short answer is yes, although whether you'll see the benefits before launch is another matter.
If you're already connected to the NBN via Fibre to the Premises (FTTP) or Hybrid Fibre Coaxial (HFC), you may be able to upgrade to a faster speed tier relatively quickly. In some cases, a speed change with your existing provider can take effect within hours, although this isn't guaranteed.
Switching to an entirely new provider can also be relatively straightforward on these connection types, particularly if you're moving between compatible services. However, activation times vary, so I wouldn't recommend relying on a last-minute switch if your sole goal is to play GTA 6 the moment it launches.
It's also worth checking your current provider's cancellation and billing policies before making the jump. While many of the best NBN plans come without lock-in contracts, that doesn't necessarily mean you'll receive a refund for any unused days you've already paid for.
Some providers charge for an entire billing period, even if you cancel partway through, which could leave you paying for two services at once.
That said, even if you miss the launch window, upgrading to one of the fastest NBN plans could still be worthwhile. GTA 6 is unlikely to be the last enormous game download you'll encounter, and a faster connection can make a noticeable difference when downloading games, installing updates or sharing your connection with other people in your household.
Just make sure your connection type, router and home network can actually support the speeds you're paying for.
Exetel One | 500Mbps | AU$80p/m
Exetel’s The One Plan is pretty perfect if you ask me. Gamers in particular will be pleased to know that the most recent ACCC data found Exetel to have the lowest ping speeds, meaning it could be a great option for lag-free online play. Elsewhere, there’s exceptional value, as the fixed-rate cost means it’s the only one to come in under AU$1,000 from year two onwards. There are other perks too, including the ability to boost the download speed to NBN 1000 (860Mbps TES), and even to save AU$1 a day and downgrade the speed to 12Mbps, ideal if you're away from home for a long time.
• AU$80 minimum cost
• AU$960 yearly cost
• View more of the best NBN 500 plans
Superloop Lightspeed | 860Mbps | AU$89p/m (first 6 months, then AU$114p/m)
Superloop is another gamer-friendly option, especially with its NBN 1000 plan, that should have GTA 6 downloaded in no time, particularly because it's been found to overdeliver on speed claims in ACCC reporting.
• AU$89 minimum cost
• AU$1,218 first year cost
• AU$1,368 ongoing yearly cost
• View more of the best NBN 1000 plans
Ultimately, GTA 6 may not have broken the Australian internet, but it's certainly demonstrated just how much demand a single game can generate. And if these preload figures are anything to go by, NBN Co could have another record-breaking night ahead of it.

articles.title: Cómo Jensen Huang pasó de limpiar habitaciones a dirigir Nvidia, la gigante de los chips de IA
articles.text:
Jensen Huang renunció el 12 de noviembre de 2026 como director ejecutivo de Nvidia, la compañía de chips que se convirtió en una pieza central del auge de la inteligencia artificial y cuya valoración supera los 4 billones de dólares.
La noticia de su salida volvió a poner el foco sobre una figura que, pese a su presencia en la industria, todavía es desconocida para parte del público. Huang limpió baños en un internado de Kentucky, Estados Unidos, y trabajó en un restaurante Denny’s. Décadas después, se convirtió en una de las personas más influyentes del sector tecnológico.
La infancia de Huang entre Taiwán, Tailandia y un internado rural
Huang nació el 17 de febrero de 1963 en Taiwán. Durante su infancia vivió con su familia en Tailandia y, a los nueve años, fue enviado junto a su hermano a Estados Unidos. Ambos ingresaron en el Instituto Bautista Oneida, un internado rural de Kentucky que sus familiares habían elegido por error, al creer que se trataba de una escuela preparatoria.
Huang contó años más tarde que allí limpiaba a diario los baños de una residencia con unos 150 alumnos. Sus padres se reunieron después con ellos en Oregón. En la adolescencia, el futuro empresario trabajó como lavaplatos, ayudante de salón y mozo en Denny’s, una experiencia que luego recordó como parte de su formación personal.
Una reunión en Denny’s dio origen a Nvidia
Tras terminar la escuela secundaria, Huang estudió ingeniería eléctrica en la Universidad Estatal de Oregón. En 1984 comenzó su carrera en Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), dedicada a los semiconductores, y luego ingresó en LSI Logic, donde desarrolló experiencia en el diseño de chips.
En 1992 obtuvo una maestría en Ingeniería Eléctrica en la Universidad de Stanford. Un año después, volvió a Denny’s, aunque esta vez para una reunión que definiría su carrera. Allí se encontró con Chris Malachowsky y Curtis Priem, dos ingenieros con quienes debatió la posibilidad de crear una compañía especializada en gráficos para computadoras. De esas conversaciones nació Nvidia, fundada en 1993.
Los chips para videojuegos se transformaron en la base de la inteligencia artificial
Durante años, Nvidia estuvo asociada a las tarjetas gráficas para videojuegos. Sus procesadores permitían realizar cálculos en paralelo y mostrar imágenes con mayor velocidad y precisión.
Ese atributo, que inicialmente atraía a jugadores y fabricantes de computadoras, resultó decisivo cuando la industria comenzó a entrenar modelos de inteligencia artificial. Estas herramientas requieren procesar grandes volúmenes de datos y ejecutar millones de operaciones de manera simultánea.
Los chips de Nvidia se adaptaron a esa necesidad y pasaron a ser demandados por empresas que desarrollan servicios como ChatGPT, Gemini y Copilot. El crecimiento llevó a la compañía a una valuación de más de 4 billones de dólares en Wall Street, por encima de Microsoft y Apple.
Huang se convirtió en una figura reconocida fuera del ámbito corporativo
Huang se transformó en una de las caras más visibles de la transformación tecnológica. Sus presentaciones, con la habitual campera de cuero negra, eran seguidas por inversores y ejecutivos que buscaban señales sobre los próximos productos y acuerdos de la compañía.
En Taiwán y Corea del Sur, llegó a recibir pedidos de autógrafos en libros, carteles e incluso en la piel de algunos seguidores. El entonces director ejecutivo sostenía que la inteligencia artificial marcaría una nueva etapa industrial.
Un escándalo vinculado a presuntas relaciones personales precedió la renuncia
La presión sobre Huang aumentó tras las informaciones sobre su relación con Alice Huang, una exejecutiva de Megaspeed, firma de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur y socia de Nvidia. Autoridades de Estados Unidos concluyeron que ella era agente de la inteligencia china, una acusación que Beijing rechazó.
La controversia creció el miércoles 11 de noviembre de 2026, cuando The New York Times informó sobre una relación extramatrimonial entre Huang y Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de atención médica de Nvidia. El consejo de administración se reunió para analizar la situación y, al día siguiente, Huang presentó su renuncia.
Colette Kress asumió como directora ejecutiva interina
Colette Kress, directora financiera de la compañía, asumió como directora ejecutiva interina mientras la junta busca un reemplazante permanente. La empresa nombró a Harvey Jones, exdirector ejecutivo de Synopsys y miembro del consejo, como su primer presidente de la junta directiva.
Las acciones de Nvidia cayeron más de 10% en las operaciones previas a la apertura del mercado. Para los inversores, la duda no se limita a los futuros chips: abarca la capacidad de preservar una red de proveedores, centros de datos, servicios en la nube y laboratorios de inteligencia artificial que Huang ayudó a articular durante 33 años.

articles.title: iPhone 20 Pro : de nouvelles images confirment le design incurvé de l'écran
articles.text:
Pour les 20 ans de l’iPhone, Apple préparerait un changement esthétique que plusieurs fuites décrivent depuis quelques mois. Des échantillons de verre de protection viennent donner une forme bien réelle à cette hypothèse, avec un écran légèrement arrondi sur chacun de ses quatre côtés.
Et si le prochain grand changement de design de l’iPhone se jouait sur quelques millimètres de verre ? Depuis plusieurs semaines, les rumeurs prêtent à Apple l’intention de revoir les contours de l’écran de son modèle anniversaire. Les dernières images relayées par Ice Universe apportent un nouvel élément à ce dossier : des protections d’écran dont la forme correspond précisément à cette description.
Un premier aperçu concret de l’écran incurvé de l’iPhone 20 Pro ?
Sur la vidéo publiée par le leaker sur X, le verre présente des courbes discrètes sur ses quatre côtés. Les angles sont arrondis et les bordures paraissent particulièrement fines. L’ensemble donne un aperçu de ce que pourrait être l’écran du futur smartphone, sans pour autant permettre d’en connaître les dimensions exactes ni de confirmer son apparence définitive.
Ice Universe a également accompagné sa publication d’un commentaire sur Weibo, où il évoque la fin des protections faciles à installer et l’arrivée d’une prise en main plus confortable. Par conséquent, les accessoires devront eux aussi s’adapter à un écran qui ne s’arrête plus sur des contours parfaitement plats.
Des rumeurs qui se suivent… Et qui se ressemblent
Il est nécessaire de rappeler que ces pièces ne sont pas des composants officiels fournis par Apple. Elles seraient issues de premiers essais de fabrication réalisés à partir des informations disponibles sur le futur appareil. Les fabricants peuvent ainsi tester de nouvelles méthodes de production avant de connaître les dimensions définitives du produit.
Ce n’est d’ailleurs pas la première fois que de tels échantillons apparaissent. Le 7 octobre dernier, un compte avait publié sur Weibo des photographies de deux protections de tailles différentes, présentées comme des concepts inspirés des fuites. Plus récemment, Ice Universe avait partagé une vidéo d’un modèle décrit comme un verre de protection incurvé en 3D sur ses quatre côtés.
Ces nouveaux échantillons livrent aussi un indice important sur un autre élément de la façade : la Dynamic Island. Sa découpe semble conserver des proportions proches de celles de la version réduite apparue sur l’iPhone 18 Pro. Cela correspond aux prévisions de Ross Young, analyste spécialisé dans les écrans, qui estime que ce format devrait être maintenu jusqu’en 2027.
La Dynamic Island conserverait les dimensions de l’iPhone 18 Pro
Vous l’aurez compris, la courbure du verre serait donc la principale évolution visible sur ces prototypes. Elle pourrait cela dit compliquer la pose d’une protection intégrale car, contrairement à un accessoire destiné à une surface plane, celui-ci devrait épouser les quatre bords arrondis sans perdre son ajustement.
Une autre fuite, publiée par Fixed Focus Digital, va dans le même sens. Le leaker affirme que les futurs modèles anniversaire utiliseraient un verre comparable à celui de l’iPhone Air, mais avec des courbes plus prononcées sur chacun des côtés
Pour rappel, la marque à la pomme préparerait ces iPhone anniversaire pour l’automne 2027. Le nom iPhone 20 Pro reste encore hypothétique à l’heure où nous rédigeons ces lignes. Et si les échantillons donnent corps à la piste d’un écran incurvé, ils ne constituent pas encore une validation du design final par Apple.
Source : MacRumors

articles.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
articles.text:
A Java flaw called Java4Shell can let attackers without an account run their own code on Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak, and three other widely used applications, says Calif, the security research firm that disclosed it this week.
The flaw is present in Java 17.0.6 and later, and the vulnerable code runs only on x86-64 Intel and AMD chips that support the AVX-512 VBMI feature.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114938, the fix was released today by Oracle and the OpenJDK project, whose open-source code underpins Java builds from many vendors. Amazon has fixed its Corretto Java builds, but Red Hat is still preparing fixes for its own.
The researchers are holding back their attack code for the six applications, and other labs have so far reproduced crashes and a memory leak but not the code execution. Canada's Cyber Center said this week that it was not aware of any attacks exploiting the flaw.
Servers often decode Base64-encoded data, such as HTTP Basic login headers, SAML artifacts, and CSRF tokens, before checking whether a user is logged in. That is how an attacker without an account can exploit the flaw.
The flaw is in a faster version of Java's Base64 decoder that runs on chips with AVX-512 VBMI. Java switches to it after compiling the decoder for speed, which it does for code that runs often.
A malformed string that ends with an extra = makes this decoder write 62 or 63 bytes past the end of its output. Java rejects the string, but only after the write.
The bytes written past the end are fixed, so an attacker controls only where they land. For that reason, early readings of the source code had pointed to a crash rather than code execution, as The Hacker News noted in an earlier report yesterday.
The attacks worked without a login under the default settings of Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate, and with a login on Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker, Calif says in its technical write-up. The researchers' lists are incomplete, and they rate the flaw as 9.2 out of 10 under CVSS 4.0.
They get past the fixed bytes by arranging the server's memory so that the overflow expands a neighboring array. They then use that array to write bytes of their choosing and a second array to read back from memory, a step they call JavaBleed. From there, the researchers say, the attack reaches the parts of Java that run code.
There is no single exploit that works everywhere. Each target requires its own memory layout and timing, and some attacks are sensitive to network delays.
A proxy that waits for complete requests, as nginx does by default, blocks some attacks but not all. A failed attempt can crash Java, and an attacker can often try again.
Security company Upwind reproduced the memory corruption on an AWS server with an Intel Ice Lake chip, where it damaged the next object in memory and eventually crashed Java, according to its lab results.
Blackpoint Cyber's Adversary Pursuit Group crashed a test Spring Boot application by sending about 28,300 malformed login requests over roughly 20 seconds, without ever logging in.
The group also used the JavaBleed step in a local test to read a secret stored next to the overflow, which worked in all 30 runs. It did not reproduce remote code execution, its test results show.
Oracle scores the flaw 8.1 out of 10 under CVSS 3.1, rating it hard to exploit but requiring no login. The description in its CVE record says, "Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE."
Red Hat also rates it as requiring no login, with a preliminary score of 9.8 out of 10. Amazon scores it 8.8 out of 10 and describes the risk in its Amazon Linux entry as "a JVM crash for unauthenticated users or, in certain application environments, code execution by an authenticated low-privileged user."
Canada's Cyber Centre also describes the flaw as exploitable remotely without authentication in its government alert.
The flaw was not in the KEV catalog of exploited vulnerabilities, kept by the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), when The Hacker News checked it today.
Who Is Exposed
The vulnerable code is in Java 17.0.6 and later on the Java 17 line, and in Java 21, 25, and 27. Standard Java 8 and Java 11 do not contain it, but the Java SE 8 Performance Pack build 8u511b33-perf is affected. GraalVM for JDK 17.0.21.0.3, GraalVM for JDK 21.0.13.0.3, and GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3.20.0.3 are also affected.
It runs only on x86-64 chips that support AVX-512 VBMI. These include Intel Xeon Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids, and Granite Rapids chips, as well as AMD Zen 4 or newer chips. ARM64 chips do not run it.
Because the vulnerable code runs only on these chips, the same container image can run it on one server and not on another. On Linux, this command shows whether a server's chip has the four features the vulnerable code needs, and all four must appear in its output:
grep -m1 '^flags' /proc/cpuinfo | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -E '^(avx512f|avx512bw|avx512vbmi|bmi2)$'
The attacker also needs malformed Base64 to reach Java's standard decoder, through paths such as the login headers and tokens described earlier.
Calif also says a Java program that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server can be compromised, even if the program runs no service of its own. The exploit for this came from another researcher, samczsun, and the researchers have not published how it reaches the decoder.
Fixes and Workarounds
The OpenJDK project's vulnerability advisory lists the flaw as fixed in this week's releases, and Oracle's security advisory lists the affected versions of its builds.
For Oracle Java, the fixed builds are the new .1 releases in the table, all released this week. The release notes for 17.0.21.1 say it includes the update's security fixes, and the notes for 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1 say the same.
For the Java 8 Performance Pack, the latest build is 8u513, available in both standard and Performance Pack versions. For GraalVM, the November security releases are GraalVM for JDK 17.0.21.1, GraalVM for JDK 21.0.13.1, and GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3.20.1.
| Java build | Affected versions | Fixed release | 
|---|---|---|
| Oracle Java SE 17 | 17.0.6 to 17.0.21.0.3 | 17.0.21.1 | 
| Oracle Java SE 21 | 21.0.13.0.3 and earlier | 21.0.13.1 | 
| Oracle Java SE 25 | 25.0.5.0.3 and earlier | 25.0.5.1 | 
| Oracle Java SE 27 | 27.0.1.0.3 and earlier | 27.0.1.1 | 
| Amazon Corretto 17, 21, 25 and 27 | Earlier builds, from 17.0.6 on for Corretto 17 | 17.0.21.1.2, 21.0.13.1.2, 25.0.5.1.2 and 27.0.1.1.4 | 
| Azul Zulu 17, 21, 25 and 27 | Earlier builds, from 17.0.6 on for Zulu 17 | 17.70.201, 21.54.201, 25.38.201 and 27.30.201 (free builds) | 
| Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9 and 10, and Red Hat build of OpenJDK 17, 21 and 25 | 17.0.6 and later, including 21 and 25 | None yet | 
The Corretto changelog for 17.0.21.1.2 lists the flaw as fixed, as do the changelogs for the new 21, 25, and 27 builds. Amazon Linux also marks its Corretto 17, 21, 25 and 27 packages as fixed.
Azul's November update fixes the flaw in Zulu 17, 21, 25 and 27, according to its Zulu release notes.
Red Hat has not yet released fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9 and 10, or for its OpenJDK 17, 21 and 25 builds, according to its security bulletin. Containers based on its images need to be rebuilt once updated images are out.
SAP released SapMachine 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, and 27.0.1.1 this week, but their release pages do not specify what they fix. Eclipse Temurin, the Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, and BellSoft Liberica had not listed fixed builds when The Hacker News checked today.
Products that bundle their own Java runtime need an update from the product's maker. After updating, restart Java services, and rebuild and redeploy container images so the running process uses the new build.
If you cannot update yet, start the JVM with one of these flags, and remove it once the fixed build is installed:
- -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics turns off only the faster Base64 code, which removes the vulnerable path and leaves other AVX-512 speedups in place.
- -XX:UseAVX=2 turns off AVX-512 entirely. Use it only on x86-64 servers, because Java on ARM64 does not recognize it and will fail to start.
In Upwind's lab, both flags stopped the overflow on every affected version it tested. The company warns that another flag, -XX:DisableIntrinsic=_base64_decodeBlock, stops Java from starting when it is used on its own.
To spot attempts, it suggests checking for the signs below, while warning that none of them proves a compromise and that their absence does not prove a server is safe:
- Base64 tokens of 32 characters or more that end in = and whose length is not a multiple of 4, especially in Authorization headers
- Bursts of IllegalArgumentException errors from java.util.Base64$Decoder
- Unexplained hs_err_pid crash logs or bursts of restarts
A malformed input that triggers the overflow was posted publicly on September 9, in a proposed fix submitted to OpenJDK's code repository as a pull request. The proposal described an overflow in the same AVX-512 Base64 decoder code.
Its author closed it without merging it in early November, after an automated notice that it had been inactive for more than eight weeks.

articles.title: Beat your PBs with total health and activity tracking, with up to 57% off Garmin watches for Black Friday
articles.text:
Beat your PBs with total health and activity tracking, with up to 57% off Garmin watches for Black Friday
From Fenix to Vivoactive, there’s a deal for any budget — with prices from AU$247
Black Friday is often when I set aside cash for big purchases, especially since my job is to hunt deals and discounts, and Amazon Australia has certainly delivered with its Black Friday sale that kicked off yesterday.
Garmin’s smartwatches and fitness trackers can certainly be considered a splurge, with some models retailing close to AU$2,000 and its entry-level options still costing a decent chunk of change at full price. So seeing a whole bunch of the brand’s offerings with around 50% off at Amazon was quite the spectacle, with an excellent entry-level option — the Vivoactive 5 — available for as low as AU$247.
• Shop Amazon's Black Friday sale here
Whether you’re looking for a full-featured flagship with lots of features to equip you for a multi-day adventure in the Aussie bush, or you just want a nice-looking watch to make sure you get all your steps in for the day, there’s something for you with these 7 deals below:
The Vivoactive 5 resembles a more conventional smartwatch, swapping out the monochrome display in Garmin's older offerings with a vibrant AMOLED screen. It also has some features found in more expensive Garmin watches like on-board GPS, on-device storage for offline music via Spotify, and fitness metrics like Body Battery and VO2 Max.
Our Garmin Fenix 8 review called the flagship from 2024 ‘rugged, expensive perfection’ and gave it a perfect five stars. The watch is built like a tank but still relatively sleek given its feature set, which includes a built-in LED torch, a microphone and speaker for calls, dive watch capabilities and more. This is the first time we’ve seen the Fenix 8 hit below the AU$1,000 mark, partly because of the launch of the Fenix 9 earlier this year.
The Forerunner 265 is a fantastic mid-tier running watch and was the first Forerunner model to come with a touchscreen display when it debuted in 2023. Our reviewer called it the “one of the best watches Garmin has ever made”, praising its familiar yet different feel. If you want a smaller watch, the 42mm Forerunner 265S is available for the same price.
Aimed to compete with the likes of the Apple Watch Ultra and Samsung’s Galaxy Watch Ultra lines, Garmin’s Venu X1 ditches the chunky and thick-bezeled look for a square design and slim 7.9mm chassis. Our reviewer gave it 4.5 stars out of 5, noting the comparatively short battery life and high price as the biggest criticisms, but this deal takes care of the latter in spades.
The Garmin Instinct 2 has a rugged exterior that's thermal and shock resistant, as well as water-rated to 100m, making it the perfect watch for bushwalkers and hikers. This version has solar power to help make the already long battery life go even further. This discount makes this great watch a tempting buy for hikers and trail runners alike. If you have larger wrists, the 50mm Instinct 2X Solar is also discounted to AU$384.
This version of the ultra-rugged Instinct 2 watch is designed for truck drivers looking to stay fit and track their health while they go on long-haul journeys. The Dezl edition includes prompts for doing short-break workouts with tutorials designed to fit within a driver’s designated break times. The battery is rated for 28 days, and this version has Garmin Pay contactless payments.
Want to add a bit more character to your rugged Garmin Instinct watch? The Instinct Crossover is essentially another Instinct 2 variant with physical analogue hands on top of the screen and a metal-accented bezel to give it a classic watch look. There are also useful upgrades over the base Instinct 2, like more storage (64MB vs 32MB) and an upgraded GPS chipset that accesses more satellite systems.
Any of these deals not quite your cup of tea? Check out the latest coupon codes that you can use to save on smartwatches, bike computers, GPS units and more at Garmin Australia.

He mainly focuses on evergreen content like buying guides and reviews, as well as finding deals and coupon codes at TechRadar Australia.
