articles.title: GTA 6 taking ages to download over your flaky internet? This Acer mesh router I tested will bring reliable Wi-Fi to every nook and cranny of your home without costing stacks of cash
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Acer Connect app could be clearer and more helpful for first-time users. However, we can’t fault the Wi-Fi performance of the Ovia T520, as it provides a wide-ranging and reliable mesh system with tri-band Wi-Fi 7 at an attractive price.
Reasons to buy
- + Competitive price
- + Tri-band Wi-Fi 7 performance
- + Good range and reliability
Reasons to avoid
- - Unhelpful app
- - Limited parental controls
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Acer Ovia T520: One-minute review
The Acer Ovia T520 is a tri-band mesh router system running Wi-Fi 7. The Ovia range focuses on boosting range and reliability for larger homes and offices, in contrast to the Acer Predator line's focus on impressive performance for online gaming and streaming.
The T520 doesn’t attempt to match the blistering speed of the Predator routers, but its top speed of 5.7Gbps should still be more than adequate for most home users and small businesses, and it can connect to up to 200 devices spread across thousands of square feet. It’s also competitively priced when compared to many rival Wi-Fi 7 mesh systems.
Acer Ovia T520 review: Price & release date
- How much does it cost? $199.99 / £149.99
- When is it available? Now
- Where can you get it? Available in US, UK and EU
The T520 is one of the more affordable mesh systems we’ve seen recently, providing Wi-Fi 7 and tri-band performance at a similar price to dual-band rivals such as the Netgear Orbi 373 or Amazon’s Eero 7. You can buy a single T520 and use it on its own as a conventional router for just $199.99 / £149.99, and Acer states that each router can cover an area of approximately 1200sq.ft.
However, we tested a two-pack mesh-system that costs $379.99 in the US, and there’s a three-pack also available for $549.99. Customers in the UK get a good deal though, as the two-pack and three-pack systems are priced at £199.99 and £279.99 respectively.
At the moment, the Ovia mesh systems are only available from Acer’s own online store, although they should be widely available from other online retailers in the US, UK and EU in the coming weeks. They are not currently available in Australia.
- Value score: 5 / 5
Acer Ovia T520 review: Specs
| Wi-Fi Support | Tri-band Wi-Fi 7 (2.4GHz, 5.0GHz, 6.0GHz) | 
| Wi-Fi Speed | Up to 5.7Gbps (using 6.0GHz) | 
| Ports | 1x 2.5Gbit WAN, 3x 2.5Gbit LAN | 
| Processor | Unspecified | 
| Dimensions | 8 x 4.6 x 4.6 inches / 202 x 116 x 116mm | 
Acer Ovia T520 review: Design
- Smart, well-designed routers
- Four Ethernet ports per router
- Setup could be smoother
The Ovia routers are neatly designed, looking rather like tall, white flower-pots. They’re fairly large, standing 202mm high and 116mm in diameter, and they house six internal antennae, so you’ll need a shelf or table with a fair amount of space when setting them up. They’re sturdily built, though, with cooling vents on the top and bottom panels, while the back of each router houses four 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports — one for your Internet connection (WAN), while the other three provide wired connections (LAN) for computers and other devices.
Acer’s Connect app isn’t quite so straightforward, though. It doesn’t tell you which of the Ovia routers should be set up first and connected to your existing modem or router in order to use your broadband connection — as many of its rivals do — so people who haven’t used a mesh Wi-Fi system before might get confused here. Some of the instructions for connecting the second router were also confusing, such as the app telling me to wait for the LEDs on the routers to glow ‘solid white’ to confirm the connection – when in, fact, the lights were flashing green.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
By default, the app sets up two separate networks, reserving the fastest 6.0GHz frequency for newer computers and mobile devices that support Wi-Fi 7 or 6E. The slower 2.4GHz and 5.0GHz frequencies are combined into a single network to provide compatibility with older devices. However, that combined network was named ‘T520-2.4GHz’, which left me scanning through various menus within the app in order figure out what had happened to the 5.0GHz band. So Asus needs to make the app much more straightforward and provide clearer guidance for first-time users.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Acer Ovia T520 review: Features
- Acer app isn’t very helpful
- Limited parental controls
- Can create guest network for visitors
As mentioned, the Ovia T520 provides tri-band Wi-Fi 7 with a top speed of 5.7Gbps, and that performance will handle gaming, streaming video and other demanding online tasks with no trouble at all. Again, though, it’s the Asus app that proves a little disappointing. The app does include basic features such as the ability to set up a guest network for visitors, as well as a Smart Home network that can be reserved for devices such as smart lights and security cameras.
There’s also a QoS (quality of service) feature for managing the use of bandwidth on your network. But while many routers allow you to prioritize performance for specific tasks such as gaming or streaming, the Asus app requires you to laboriously specify the maximum speeds you want to allow for individual devices.
It’s a similar story with the app’s parental controls. There is an option to create a schedule for Internet access so that the kids don’t stay up all night doom-scrolling on Instagram, but the automatic web content filters that we’ve seen with previous Asus routers weren’t available with the T520. Instead, the app requires you to manually set up a White List or Black List by typing in the addresses of individual websites — something that’s not exactly helpful for busy parents.
- Features score: 3.5 / 5
Acer Ovia T520 review: Performance
- Tri-band Wi-Fi 7
- Good range for larger homes
- 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports
Ookla Speed Test – 2.4GHz+5.0GHz (download/upload)
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps/150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps/150Mbps
Ookla Speed Test – 6.0GHz (download/upload)
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps/150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps/150Mbps
20GB Steam Download - 2.4GHz+5.0GHz
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps
20GB Steam Download - 6.0GHz
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps
Range and reliability can be a problem in many larger homes and offices, as evidenced by the Wi-Fi deadspot I have in a back office at the end of a hallway within my building. However, the two-piece Ovia system that I tested dealt with this problem effortlessly, with no need for a third mesh router either.
Unsurprisingly the Ovia was able to take advantage of the full 150Mbps speed provided by my office network when connecting to nearby devices in the same room. Both of its networks — the dedicated 6.0GHz network and the combined 2.4GHz/5.0GHz network — breezed along at a consistent 150Mbps when running the Ookla Speed Test, and also when downloading large game files from Steam. The Wi-Fi connection also remained steady when I picked up my test laptop and walked along the corridor to that office at the back of the building, with both its networks maintaining a speed of 150Mbps for the Ookla and Steam tests.
It’s not the fastest Wi-Fi 7 system currently available, but its speed of 5.7Gbps still outstrips most home broadband services and its competitive pricing makes the Ovia T520 a good option for any home or office that needs to improve the range and reliability of its Wi-Fi network.
- Performance score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the Acer Ovia T520?
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
| Design | Compact and neatly designed, with four Ethernet ports. | 4 / 5 | 
| Features | Limited parental controls and QoS features are disappointing. | 3.5 / 5 | 
| Performance | A mid-range option, but more than fast enough for most domestic broadband services. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Value | Tri-band performance at dual-band prices. | 5 / 5 | 
Buy it if…
You have a large home / office
With two-pack and three-pack options available, the Ovia T520 is a good option for larger homes and offices that need to extend the range of their Wi-Fi network.
You have a new PC or mobile devices
The high-speed 6.0GHz band provides impressive performance, but you’ll need a recent PC or mobile devices that support Wi-Fi 6E or 7 to get the best performance.
Don’t buy it if…
You’re on a budget
It’s competitively priced, but few homes will need the full speed of the T520, and there are many less expensive dual-band mesh systems available.
You need parental controls
We’ve seen routers from Acer that provide automatic content filters for blocking material that is unsuitable for children, but these are no longer available with the T520.
Acer Ovia T520 review: also consider
Netgear Orbi 373
The Orbi’s dual-band Wi-Fi 7 isn’t as fast as the tri-band Ovia, but its 3.6Gbps speed is still fine for gaming and streaming video, and Netgear’s app is much easier and more straightforward to use. Read our full Netgear Orbi 373 review.
Acer Predator Connect T7
If speed is your main priority then Acer’s T7 provides blazing speeds of up to 11Gbps for gaming or streaming 4K video. However, it also has mesh capabilities so that you can use it as part of a mesh system as well. Read our full Acer Predator Connect T7 review.

articles.title: GTA 6 affole complètement le marché du jeu vidéo avec des ventes qui atteignent un niveau exceptionnel
articles.text:
À quelques heures de sa sortie, GTA 6 cumule près de 16 millions de précommandes numériques et 1,54 milliard de dollars de recettes. Sur le papier, le jeu dépasse déjà des chiffres qui faisaient référence dans l'histoire du jeu vidéo.
Il n'est pas exagéré de dire que GTA 6 marquera l'année, et sans doute la décennie, tant il fait parler et tant il a déjà fait des adeptes. Les précommandes du jeu vidéo ont encore bondi ces dernières heures. Selon le dernier relevé publié par Sensor Tower, le titre de Rockstar Games approche des 16 millions de copies numériques réservées. GTA 6 aurait déjà généré plus de 1,54 milliard de dollars de recettes, dont les deux tiers sur PlayStation. À quelques heures de disponibilité du jeu, les illustre Cyberpunk 2077, Red Dead Redemption 2 et même GTA V voient déjà leurs records vaciller.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Les précommandes de GTA 6 ont doublé en deux semaines
Le nombre de copies de GTA 6 précommandées sur PS5 et Xbox Series, remboursements déduits, est désormais estimé à 15,88 millions, pour 1,54 milliard de dollars de chiffres d'affaires. Imaginez, c'est comme si près de 23 % des Français avaient acheté le jeu avant même qu'il ne sorte, un score qui ferait rougir n'importe quel candidat à l'élection présidentielle dans quelques mois. Le 13 novembre, il y a moins d'une semaine donc, le compteur affichait encore 12,13 millions de copies et 1,18 milliard. Le 3 novembre, il n'en était qu'à 7,71 millions. Autrement dit, les réservations ont plus que doublé en deux semaines.
Si nous faisons les comptes, ces jours-ci le jeu a généré environ 90 millions de dollars par jour, contre moins de 30 millions début novembre. La répartition, elle, est extrêmement favorable à la PlayStation 5, qui pèse pour 75 % des ventes, avec 11,83 millions de copies et 1,15 milliard de dollars de recettes, contre 4,04 millions de copies et 390 millions sur Xbox, en rappelant que GTA 6 sera jouable sur la vieille Xbox One. Avec environ 97 dollars comme panier moyen, l'édition Ultime reste la reine des précommandes.
On rappelle qu'il ne s'agit ici que d'estimations, et que ces chiffres ne portent que sur les ventes numériques, sans les boîtes vendues en magasin, qui ne contiennent qu'un seul petit code d'ailleurs, et que ces données s'entendent avant la commission prélevée par les boutiques. Pour le moment, Take-Two, la maison mère de l'éditeur Rockstar Games, n'a pas commenté les chiffres, en se contentant d'évoquer un élan « sans précédent » pour le jeu.
GTA 6 bouscule déjà l'histoire du jeu vidéo
Jusqu'ici, le record de précommandes généralement cité appartenait à Cyberpunk 2077. 8 millions d'exemplaires furent annoncés par CD Projekt en 2020, PC compris. GTA 6 fait déjà presque deux fois mieux, sur consoles uniquement. Son aîné, l'increvable GTA V, avait totalisé 7 millions de précommandes en 2013, avant de générer la coquette somme de 800 millions de dollars dès son premier jour, puis le milliard en trois jours, plus vite que n'importe quel jeu ou film à l'époque.
Les aventures d'Arthur Morgan, avec Red Dead Redemption 2, avaient engrangé 725 millions de dollars lors de son premier week-end, en 2018. GTA 6 avait dépassé ce montant au plus tard début novembre, plus de deux semaines avant sa sortie, et ses seules précommandes numériques surpassent déjà le milliard de GTA V, boîtes comprises. Les méthodes de calcul diffèrent, entre chiffres officiels et estimations, mais l'écart est significatif.
Les joueurs Xbox vont même pouvoir, en principe, entrer à Vice City dès ce mercredi midi, grâce à l'astuce de la Nouvelle-Zélande, avant le lancement français dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi, à minuit. D'ici là, gare aux pièges, puisque différentes acteurs de la cybersécurité repèrent des activités malveillantes autour du jeu, comme dernièrement un faux téléchargement du jeu qui cache un logiciel voleur de données. Rappelons enfin qu'aucune version PC n'existe, et que le jeu visera 30 FPS sur toutes les consoles.

articles.title: Researchers Claim Two RCE Exploits That Bypass Telegram’s New Android Defenses
articles.text:
A malicious widget can bypass the security filter that Telegram added to its Android app last week and run code outside it, according to NebuSec, a security company.
Widgets are small interactive blocks that bots send inside chat messages, and their JavaScript runs on the user's phone. The researchers ran their demonstration on a Telegram test server, because only approved bots can send widgets on the live service now.
Bots could start sending widgets last week. Two days later, an account called V12 posted a video on X claiming that any Telegram message could now be used to execute remote code.
Telegram then put QuickJS, the small engine that runs widget JavaScript, into its own process on Android. It also added a seccomp filter, which can block or record the system calls that the process makes. Both changes appear in the source code it published for Telegram for Android 13.2.2 (7303).
NebuSec said in a technical analysis published earlier this week that its researchers got code running outside that filter in two separate ways. One uses a widget bug the filter does not cover, and the other chains a widget bug the filter does cover with a kernel bug.
In their video, a bot's Telegram widget on Android 13.2.2 (7303) bypasses the filter and opens the phone's calculator app, the researchers say.
Their write-up and their demonstration post on X do not say what the code could reach beyond that, such as the app's messages or the rest of the phone. They also do not say whether the user had to start the bot or tap the widget first.
The researchers are holding back the details for now. Their write-up names no CVE identifier and does not say whether the bugs were reported to the app's developers.
The widget documentation says widgets run in a sandbox, with rules such as no network access. Those rules live in the engine's own code, the researchers say. A single use-after-free or out-of-bounds write bug in QuickJS lets a script read and write the process's memory, and then the rules no longer protect anything.
The new filter names a few dozen system calls, such as ptrace, bpf, and mount, and lets every other call through. The filter's source code leaves ioctl unfiltered. The filter sits on top of Android's own limits on the engine process.
One process also runs every widget, so a hijacked widget from one bot shares memory with the widgets of every other bot, the researchers say.
In the published source code for Telegram for Android 13.2.2 (7303), that filter is set to an audit mode, The Hacker News found. In audit mode, it still blocks attempts to start new programs or processes, but it only records the other listed calls and lets them run.
A comment above the setting says how long that will last: "Audit until the logs from the devices say the engine never makes them." The published code does not show whether the version people install uses the same setting.
"Yes, currently, general bots aren't allowed to use widgets even in private chats," a contributor to the telegram-bot-api project wrote late last week in a bug report thread on GitHub. As of this week, no later message in the thread says which bots are still allowed or that the limit has been lifted.
The researchers' write-up lists no fixed version, and the published Android source code is no newer than 13.2.2 (7303) as of this week.
"No one could be hacked just by receiving a message," Pavel Durov, Telegram's chief executive, wrote late last week in a channel post. His post addressed reports of code execution through widgets in the Android and Windows apps, and came before the researchers' demonstration. He added that a user first had to start a third-party service, and that even that was fully patched on the server side.
The company had earlier said that the problem in V12's first demonstration was fixed and that the fix had reached all users.
Separately, the security vendor Kaspersky said late last week that it had detected suspected exploitation of a flaw in Telegram widgets when people visited some Telegram channels.
In that activity, a PowerShell script ran without the user noticing and downloaded and launched WebRAT, also known as Salat Stealer. The malware allows attackers to control the infected system and steal data from crypto wallets and Telegram accounts.
The vendor's malware warning does not identify the flaw or the Telegram version, does not report the number of victims, and does not link the activity to either demonstration. It advises not running widgets until a fix is released.

articles.title: Estafadores usan la crisis de Nvidia para enviar correos falsos que instalan software malicioso
articles.text:
Estafadores ya usan la crisis de Nvidia como señuelo: envían correos con el asunto “Invitación: Nvidia Executive Partnership Discussion” (“Invitación: conversación sobre una alianza ejecutiva con Nvidia”) para que la víctima descargue software malicioso. La empresa de capacitación en ciberseguridad KnowBe4 detectó la campaña, según informó Axios.
El mensaje promete información sobre la estrategia de inversión de Nvidia. Dentro del correo aparece una imagen en la que se puede hacer clic y que parece mostrar los parámetros de inversión de la empresa para 2026. Si el destinatario hace clic, puede iniciarse la descarga del programa malicioso en su dispositivo.
KnowBe4 vio las primeras señales de la campaña el miércoles, un día antes de que Jensen Huang renunciara como director ejecutivo de Nvidia. Bryan Palma, director ejecutivo de KnowBe4, dijo a Axios que los correos parecen dirigidos a personas que trabajan en finanzas, transporte y gobierno. Todavía se desconoce qué grupo está detrás.
La crisis que sirve de gancho
El 12 de noviembre, el directorio de Nvidia anunció que Huang renunciaba con efecto inmediato a la presidencia, a la dirección ejecutiva y a su puesto en la junta. La directora financiera, Colette Kress, quedó como directora ejecutiva interina mientras el directorio busca un sucesor permanente.
Según la cronología de CBS News, el 8 de noviembre Huang admitió en un mensaje a los empleados que había tenido una relación extramatrimonial. Ese día Nvidia informó que abría una investigación independiente. The New York Times había publicado que una de las mujeres involucradas era sospechada por la inteligencia estadounidense de actuar como espía de China, algo que Beijing niega.
Con un escándalo de esa dimensión, un mensaje que promete detalles de la estrategia de inversión de la compañía resulta verosímil para un analista, un inversor o un funcionario que sigue el caso.
Cómo trabajan los atacantes
Palma explicó que los delincuentes pueden comprar listas de contactos detalladas y usar inteligencia artificial para clasificar a las víctimas por sector, profesión e intereses. Así adaptan cada mensaje a un público específico, en lugar de mandar el mismo correo genérico a millones de personas.
La IA también acelera el lanzamiento de estas campañas. Según datos de KnowBe4 citados por Axios, los atacantes reaccionan a los titulares 5,4 veces más rápido en 2026 que en 2022. En un caso, tras la muerte de una celebridad de primer nivel, los estafadores lanzaron una campaña de correos en 16 horas.
Además, cerca del 88% de los ataques de phishing (correos que suplantan a una marca o persona para robar datos o instalar programas dañinos) vinculados a noticias de último momento o a eventos programados suplantó a una marca conocida en todo el mundo, según KnowBe4.
Palma recomienda mirar con más cuidado cualquier correo inesperado que haga referencia a una noticia de último momento, aunque el titular resulte familiar. Una invitación no solicitada de una compañía famosa, recibida en plena crisis, justifica verificar al remitente por otro canal antes de abrir imágenes o archivos adjuntos. Hasta ahora, KnowBe4 no ha identificado a los responsables de la campaña con el asunto sobre Nvidia.
Qué es el malware y cómo protegerse de sus amenazas
El software malicioso, comúnmente conocido como “malware”, es un término general que describe cualquier programa o código informático diseñado intencionalmente para infiltrarse, dañar o alterar el funcionamiento de un sistema, red o dispositivo.
Los ciberdelincuentes desarrollan y utilizan estas herramientas con diversos fines, que van desde el robo de datos personales y financieros hasta el espionaje o la extorsión. A diferencia del software legítimo, el malware suele instalarse sin el conocimiento ni el consentimiento del usuario, aprovechando vulnerabilidades de seguridad u ocultándose dentro de archivos adjuntos engañosos, descargas aparentemente seguras y enlaces fraudulentos.
Existen múltiples variantes de malware, cada una con un método de ataque y un objetivo específico. Entre los más comunes se encuentran los virus, que infectan otros archivos para propagarse; el ransomware, que bloquea el acceso a los datos de la víctima hasta que se paga un rescate; y el spyware, que recopila información en secreto, como contraseñas o hábitos de navegación.
Para mitigar estos riesgos, es fundamental mantener los sistemas operativos y programas actualizados, utilizar soluciones de seguridad confiables y mantener hábitos de navegación cautelosos, evitando interactuar con correos electrónicos no solicitados o enlaces de dudosa procedencia.

articles.title: Slay the Spire 2 Sold Nearly 8 Million Units on Steam in Just 8 Months
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Slay the Spire 2 Sold Nearly 8 Million Units on Steam in Just 8 Months
It was clear with in the first 24 hours of the game's early access launch that Slay the Spire 2 would be a screaming success, with the indie game peaking at over 430,000 concurrent players on Steam in its first day on the market. According to recent Alinea Analytics data (via Rhys Elliott), Slay the Spire 2's success has continued in the eight months following its launch leading up to November, with the market research firm estimating that the game has sold a whopping 7.9 million copies on Steam since its launch. 
Other notable analytics include that, in early November, Slay the Spire sat at around 500,000 daily active users, but that number jumped to 1.1 million shortly after the game's v0.113.0 update, which introduced a new character and new gameplay modes and mechanics alongside the usual bug fixes and patches. The analytics firm also estimates that as many as 100,000 Slay the Spire owners haven't even launched the game, but as many as 24% of the game's players have played it for over 100 hours.Alinea goes on to predict that Slay the Spire will cross 10 million units sold when Mega Crit releases the game out of early access, with eventual mobile and console ports promising even more sales adding to the game's estimated $157.6 million Steam revenue.

articles.title: Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
articles.text:
Oracle is preparing to release security patches for 11 vulnerabilities in Java SE on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, all of which may be exploited remotely without authentication, as separate reports warn of a potentially critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw affecting OpenJDK.
The 11 vulnerabilities carry a maximum CVSS 3.1 severity score of 8.1, according to Oracle's advance security notice. The company has not disclosed their CVE identifiers, affected components, or the individual consequences of exploitation.
The separate OpenJDK vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-114938, has reportedly been assigned a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 and affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later. However, those details remain unconfirmed, and there is no evidence yet that the reported flaw is among the 11 vulnerabilities Oracle plans to patch.
Security firm Calif said in a post on X that it discovered and reported the flaw, which it calls Java4Shell, and that the vulnerability had leaked. Calif said it would publish technical details by 1 p.m. Pacific time on November 17, after Oracle releases a patch.
Security company watchTowr acknowledged the reports in a post on X, but cautioned that the technical details were still unconfirmed.
Separate analyses of the OpenJDK source code by security companies Upwind and Equixly point to a flaw in Java's Base64 decoder whose likely result is a crash of the Java virtual machine (JVM) rather than code execution.
The vulnerability's CVE record remains reserved without a public description. No official advisory has specified the vulnerable component, precise exploitation requirements, affected version range, or the availability of a fix.
Oracle's ops.java site now lists the replacement builds below as its current releases. Oracle's advance notice, release notes and download page still showed the earlier builds as of 16:59 UTC.
Oracle Prepares Java Security Updates
Oracle advises customers to stop using its current builds of Java 8, 11, 17, 21, 25, and 27 after the November 17 security update and move to the corresponding replacement releases.
The company's Java release notes contain the update guidance, while ops.java lists the following planned builds:
| Java line | Current build | Planned build | 
|---|---|---|
| Java 8 | 8u511 b33 | 8u513 | 
| Java 11 | 11.0.33.0.3 | 11.0.33.1 | 
| Java 17 | 17.0.21.0.3 | 17.0.21.1 | 
| Java 21 | 21.0.13.0.3 | 21.0.13.1 | 
| Java 25 | 25.0.5.0.3 | 25.0.5.1 | 
| Java 27 | 27.0.1.0.3 | 27.0.1.1 | 
The November security notice identifies the following affected Oracle products and versions:
- Oracle Java SE: 8u511, 8u511-perf, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5, and 27.0.1.
- Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21 and 21.0.13.
- Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3.
- Oracle JavaFX: 21.0.13, 25.0.5, and 27.0.1.
Oracle says all 11 Java SE vulnerabilities may be exploited over a network without requiring credentials. That does not necessarily mean they all allow remote code execution or that every application running an affected Java version can be attacked directly.
The advance notice does not identify the vulnerable Java components or specify what an attacker could accomplish by exploiting each flaw.
Oracle also warns that the information may change before the complete security advisory is published.
Critical OpenJDK RCE Report Remains Unverified
The reported CVE-2026-114938 vulnerability introduces a separate concern for organizations operating Java applications, particularly those exposed to the internet.
However, the public information does not establish whether the flaw affects the Java runtime itself, a particular library, or functionality that applications must expose for exploitation to succeed.
However, Oracle's notice and the OpenJDK advisories do not establish whether the flaw affects the Java runtime itself, a particular library, or functionality that applications must expose for exploitation to succeed.
Upwind said in a technical analysis that its reading of the OpenJDK source points to a flaw in Java's AVX-512 Base64 decoder, and Equixly reached the same finding in a separate analysis. The flawed code runs only on x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI support, when untrusted data reaches the basic or URL decoder of java.util.Base64. ARM servers do not run it.
The code is in Java 17.0.6 and later and in Java 21, 25 and 27, but not in standard Java 8 or 11. A crash is the likely result because the bytes written past the buffer are fixed and not chosen by the attacker. Neither firm reported reproducing the overflow on AVX-512 hardware.
Oracle's 8u371-perf release notes show that its Java 8 Enterprise Performance Pack added a "Base64 Decoding optimization for x86 using AVX-512". Neither firm said whether the Performance Pack is affected.
Both firms named two JVM options as stopgaps to keep the flawed code from running: -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics, which turns off the Base64 intrinsics, and -XX:UseAVX=2, which turns off all AVX-512 code paths and can slow other work. Neither option has been confirmed by a vendor for this flaw, the firms said.
Oracle's November notice covers Oracle products and does not establish the patch status of third-party OpenJDK distributions.
The OpenJDK Vulnerability Group, which coordinates security disclosures affecting OpenJDK source code, had not published an advisory newer than October 24 at the time of the earlier review.
Until official details are available, organizations cannot determine from the reported CVE alone whether their Java deployments are vulnerable or which specific update addresses the issue.
Oracle began a monthly security patch cycle on May 28, introducing targeted security releases between its quarterly Critical Patch Updates.
Its Java security update plan, last updated September 10, identified November 17 as the next scheduled monthly release.
Organizations should inventory deployed Java runtimes, identify internet-facing applications, and prepare to test and install the relevant vendor updates once they become available.
This is a developing story. We will update this article as Oracle publishes its full vulnerability advisory and additional verified details about CVE-2026-114938, affected versions, and available patches emerge.

articles.title: Oficinas de Japón volvieron a usar máquinas de fax debido a la caída de Microsoft 365
articles.text:
Oficinas de Japón recurrieron a máquinas de fax y llamadas telefónicas tras la caída global de Microsoft 365, que dejó inoperables servicios como Outlook, Teams, Copilot y OneDrive durante casi 24 horas.
El fallo, que comenzó el jueves y continuaba activo el viernes cuando los empleados llegaron a sus puestos de trabajo, obligó a numerosas compañías a abandonar sus rutinas digitales habituales y volver a métodos analógicos para mantener operaciones básicas.
La magnitud de la interrupción resultó particularmente significativa en Japón debido a la alta dependencia tecnológica del país respecto a Microsoft. Aproximadamente el 78% de las compañías japonesas utiliza los servicios de la empresa estadounidense para su infraestructura digital cotidiana, según cifras citadas por el Japan Times. Esta concentración dejó a buena parte del tejido empresarial sin alternativas inmediatas cuando los sistemas dejaron de funcionar.
Los trabajadores se encontraron con pantallas en blanco, mensajes de error y la imposibilidad de acceder a documentos compartidos. La situación forzó la reprogramación de reuniones y dejó tareas sin completar en múltiples oficinas, que vieron interrumpidos sus flujos de trabajo habituales sin margen para implementar soluciones alternativas de forma inmediata.
Fax y teléfono reemplazaron a las herramientas digitales
Ante la imposibilidad de enviar los documentos en formato PDF que las empresas distribuían de manera rutinaria, algunos empleados optaron por las máquinas de fax para mantener la circulación de información interna. Un trabajador afectado escribió en la red social X: “Los problemas en los servidores de Microsoft nos impidieron completar nuestro trabajo habitual desde esta mañana. Vamos a cambiar por completo a métodos tradicionales”.
Otro usuario de la misma plataforma relató una experiencia similar y celebró el recurso a la tecnología previa a internet: “La falla en los servidores de Microsoft hizo imposible avanzar con cualquier tarea desde esta mañana. Parece que los teléfonos y las máquinas de fax son realmente invencibles... ¡Vamos a volvernos completamente analógicos!”.
El fallo también provocó pausas forzadas en la rutina laboral
No todas las reacciones apuntaron hacia la improvisación con tecnología antigua. Algunos empleados describieron jornadas prácticamente paralizadas por la falta de acceso a las herramientas digitales. Uno de ellos relató en X que, al no poder abrir Outlook, contactó a su jefe y recibió autorización para permanecer en su domicilio. Otro trabajador señaló que la única tarea disponible durante la jornada consistió en limpiar la máquina de café de la sala de producción.
Estos testimonios reflejan hasta qué punto las actividades administrativas en Japón dependen de la disponibilidad constante del software de Microsoft, en ausencia de procedimientos alternativos preestablecidos para este tipo de contingencias.
El impacto de la falla no se limitó al territorio japonés. El sistema sanitario de Reino Unido, además de empresas, operadores de transporte y servicios de viajes, también reportó dificultades vinculadas a la interrupción de los servicios de Microsoft. En el plano corporativo, el grupo suizo de lujo Richemont, propietario de la marca Cartier, debió posponer la presentación de su más reciente informe de resultados financieros a raíz del mismo problema técnico.
La compañía informó que observaba un “progreso de recuperación alentador” en Europa, mientras que la situación en el continente americano mostraba mejoras, aunque advirtió que algunos usuarios podrían seguir experimentando fallas intermitentes. Microsoft negó además versiones que atribuían el origen de la caída a una violación de ciberseguridad, sin ofrecer por el momento una explicación detallada sobre la causa técnica del incidente.

articles.title: Pulsar Launches X2 CrazyLight 2: 40-43 g Wireless Gaming Mouse In Small and Medium Sizes
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Pulsar Launches X2 CrazyLight 2: 40-43 g Wireless Gaming Mouse In Small and Medium Sizes
Following the recent launch of the X2F CrazyLight fingertip gaming mouse and a teaser of two upcoming HE gaming keyboards with some novel, ideas and minimalist designs, Pulsar has officially launched the first of its next-gen CrazyLight gaming mice, the X2 CrazyLight 2. The X2 CrazyLight 2 is an iteration of the previous design with updated internals. The X2 CrazyLight 2 has launched in two sizes: Mini and Medium, made for small and larger hands, respectively. 
The actual shell designs of the X2 CrazyLight 2 Mini and Medium are identical, but the Mini is notably smaller and a tad lighter than the Medium, with the Medium weighing in at 43 g with stock skates, while the Mini weighs in at 40 g with stock skates. The biggest updates to the Pulsar X2 CrazyLight 2 series is the new XS-2 sensor, which offers up to 42,000 DPI, 800 IPS tracking, up to 70 G acceleration, and up to 8 kHz polling—whether any of that is debatable, but they are improvements, nonetheless.The X2 CrazyLight Mini measures in at 115.6 × 61 × 36.6 mm, while the Medium version of the X2 CrazyLight 2 measures in at 120.4 × 63 × 38 mm. Both are available on Pulsar's online store for $129.95. Unfortunately, the X2 CrazyLight 2 still doesn't use the dual-sensor tech that Pulsar previously mentioned it was working on, but the mice are nonetheless customizable in Pulsar's software.While the X2 CrazyLight 2 uses the same Pulsar Optical switches, rated to 100 million clicks, the mice have an updated Pulsar TTC IR contactless optical encoder, which should prevent skipping and reversal, even as the mouse ages. Pulsar claims the X2 CrazyLight is optimized for claw and fingertip grips.

articles.title: Gemini gardera vos chats temporaires deux mois au lieu de 72 h
articles.text:
Google conservera environ deux mois vos discussions temporaires avec Gemini, et celles que vous avez avec l’historique désactivé, contre 72 heures jusqu’ici. Avec cette mise à jour, l’entreprise vous laisse aussi garder votre historique sans que vos conversations servent à entraîner ses modèles d’IA.
Une discussion temporaire avec Gemini n’apparaît pas dans votre historique, et Google ne l’utilise ni pour personnaliser ses réponses ni pour entraîner ses modèles. Google a lancé ce mode en août 2025, et il effaçait ces échanges au bout de 72 heures, au moins jusqu’au 12 novembre, d’après une version archivée de son centre de confidentialité retrouvée par TechCrunch. Il les gardera désormais environ deux mois, et il déploiera ce changement dans le monde entier au cours des prochaines semaines. Interrogé par TechCrunch, Google n’a pas expliqué pourquoi il lui fallait vingt fois plus de temps.
Google garde vos conversations pour protéger Gemini
Pendant ces deux mois, Google utilisera vos conversations pour vous répondre, traiter vos commentaires et « protéger Google, ses utilisateurs et le public », selon son blog. Dans son centre de confidentialité, l’entreprise cite aussi d’éventuelles pannes de ses systèmes, et elle assure ne pas entraîner ses modèles avec vos discussions temporaires.
Si vous notez une réponse de Gemini d’un pouce levé ou baissé, Google récupère en outre les 24 dernières heures de vos conversations, pièces jointes comprises, y compris avec l’historique désactivé. L’entreprise conserve jusqu’à trois ans les échanges relus par ses évaluateurs humains, et vous ne pouvez pas les effacer en supprimant votre historique.
Avec ces deux mois, Google gardera vos discussions deux fois plus longtemps qu’OpenAI et Anthropic. OpenAI conserve jusqu’à 30 jours les discussions temporaires de ChatGPT, et Anthropic garde 30 jours par défaut les conversations privées de Claude. Ces entreprises peuvent toutefois conserver certaines données plus longtemps, pour des raisons légales ou de sécurité, ou pour enquêter sur un abus de leurs services.
- Multimodalité texte, voix et fichiers
- Intégration poussée aux services Google
- Applications Web, mobile et bureau
Google sépare votre historique de l’entraînement de son IA
Jusqu’ici, avec le seul réglage « Conserver l’activité », vous acceptiez à la fois que Google garde vos conversations et qu’il les utilise pour entraîner ses modèles d’IA. Pour retrouver vos anciennes discussions, vous deviez lui laisser vos messages, mais aussi vos photos, vos fichiers, vos enregistrements audio, votre localisation et les données tirées des applications Google reliées à Gemini.
Google remplace ce réglage par deux commandes. Dans la rubrique Historique, vous choisissez combien de temps Google garde vos conversations, 18 mois par défaut, et vous pouvez les consulter ou les supprimer à tout moment. Avec la seconde commande, vous pouvez refuser que vos échanges, pièces jointes comprises, servent à entraîner ses modèles.
Si vous aviez activé « Conserver l’activité », Google garde votre historique, et vous déciderez séparément s’il peut entraîner son IA avec vos conversations. Si vous l’aviez désactivé, Google coupera par défaut les deux nouveaux réglages. Vous recevrez peut-être un courriel de Google à ce sujet, mais une fois la mise à jour arrivée sur votre compte, vérifiez ces deux réglages dans la page Activité de Gemini.
Et si vous désactivez l’historique pour que Google oublie vos conversations, il les gardera malgré tout deux mois.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage forces Japanese workers back to fax machines
articles.text:
The major Microsoft 365 outage saw Japanese workers fire up their fax machines for the first time in years
Microsoft 365 outage paralyzed 78% of Japanese companies
- Japanese workers returned to fax machines after Microsoft's cloud services collapse
- Businesses replaced their usual PDF distribution with traditional fax transmissions
- Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and OneDrive disruptions affected everyday workplace operations
The recent Microsoft 365 disruption had one rather nostalgic knock-on effect for fans of older tech, as Japanese businesses struggling to access essential workplace applications, forcing some employees to abandon their usual digital routines.
With Outlook, Teams, Copilot and OneDrive all experiencing service interruptions, companies encountered difficulties communicating, sharing documents and completing scheduled assignments.
Some Japanese workplaces have consequently returned to older communication equipment such as fax machines to keep routine business operations moving.
Back to analog
The outage spread over two days, affecting organizations which depend on Microsoft's cloud services for everyday administrative and operational activities.
Employees reported blank application windows, error notifications and difficulties accessing documents, leaving some meetings postponed and assignments unfinished.
Japan had considerable exposure to the disruption, with approximately 78% of its companies reportedly depending on Microsoft for their digital infrastructure.
When essential applications become inaccessible, employees cannot necessarily switch to alternative systems immediately, particularly when their organizations have built established workflows around Microsoft's services.

Some workers described unusual experiences after arriving at offices where normal operations had effectively stalled.
One employee reportedly wrote on X that losing access to Outlook initially caused panic, before a conversation with their manager resulted in permission to remain home.
Another worker described having so little productive work available that cleaning the coffee machine became their principal workplace responsibility.
These show how heavily routine office activities can depend on software availability, particularly when alternative procedures are unavailable.
Fax machines provide an alternative as Microsoft works to restore services
Employees reportedly began using fax machines to distribute documents and routine updates previously circulated through electronic PDF files.
“Microsoft’s server problems have prevented us from completing our usual work since this morning. We are switching entirely to traditional methods,” an affected employee reportedly wrote on X.
Japan’s capacity to deploy traditional technology is worth emulating, and some employees even celebrated the arrangement by declaring that they remained dependable during the disruption.
The consequences of the outage extended beyond Japanese offices, affecting organizations across several industries and international markets.
Britain's healthcare sector, businesses, transportation operators and travel services have also reportedly experienced difficulties linked to Microsoft's service interruptions.
Some companies have faced financial reporting complications as well, with Swiss luxury group Richemont delaying its latest earnings announcement.
The disruption therefore extended beyond inconvenienced office workers, particularly where organizations depend on Microsoft's applications for time-sensitive business activities.

articles.title: Trigram Campaign Impersonates About 50 AI and Blockchain Brands to Target Devs with Infostealers
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and logistics sectors across Europe and the U.S. have emerged as the target of a large-scale, industrialized campaign dubbed Trigram.
"Trigram is a large-scale campaign that impersonates about 50 brands in the blockchain and AI sectors, to trick developers into executing an infostealer themselves," Stormshield said in a deep-dive technical report published Monday.
"Three social engineering scenarios (recruitment, conference, and package tracking), a software supply-chain compromise, and trojanized code repositories all converge on the same infrastructure and the same payload."
The activity is assessed to share similarities with intrusion sets linked to North Korea, particularly Kimsuky and UNK_DeadDrop. Some aspects of this campaign have been previously documented by Proofpoint, SafeDep, Jamf, and Genians Security Center.
It's worth noting that the cluster tracked as UNK_DeadDrop exhibits similarities with a long-running North Korea-aligned campaign referred to as Contagious Interview. First observed between April and May 2026, it employs phishing emails using developer role recruitment or code review themes to target developers across finance, cryptocurrency, education, and technology sectors to deploy an information stealer.
On Linux and macOS systems, the attack chains lead to the deployment of Overlord, an open-source remote access trojan (RAT) framework to facilitate data theft.
Then, in August 2026, Jamf Threat Labs disclosed details of a macOS campaign using a fake Zoom installer to deploy Overlord RAT, although the Apple device management company said at the time that it found no "direct overlap" between the activity and UNK_DeadDrop.
"The Overlord variant observed here shares a LaunchAgent label (com.zoom) and plist name (com.zoom.plist) with FlexibleFerret, a DPRK-attributed macOS malware family associated with the Contagious Interview campaign," it added.
Overlord has also been distributed as recently as late October 2026 via another channel: a forged commit in the antd-img-crop GitHub repository that installs the malware by means of a prebuild hook ("prebuild.js") as soon as a developer runs the "npm run build" command. The npm package in itself was not impacted.
The JavaScript payload is designed to download and run a fake installer that sets up Node.js and fetches an encrypted JavaScript next-stage that runs entirely in memory and locates its command-and-control (C2) server via a GitLab dead-drop. The third-stage malware is responsible for harvesting credentials and installing the OverLord framework.
"The malware steals browser passwords, cookies, keychains, cryptocurrency wallets, SSH keys and .env files on macOS, Linux and Windows, then installs a remote-access agent disguised as Google software," SafeDep said in an analysis of the malware.
| The forged commit pushed to "antd-img-crop" on October 31, 2026 | 
On macOS and Linux systems, it also displays a fake dialog asking users to enter their system password so as to "apply system updates and verify drivers and security settings." Interestingly, the same payload is delivered via two other initial access vectors -
- A fake careers portal impersonating Amber Group, a legitimate cryptocurrency firm
- A sideloaded Microsoft Visual Studio Code (VS Code) or Cursor extension named "google-dev-tools.google-update-support" that's likely launched via a coding assessment and deleted after it's run
"The fake recruiter, the paste-a-command 'verification' step and the focus on developers and cryptocurrency holders match the publicly documented Contagious Interview campaign," SafeDep said. "The match rests on technique and does not prove who the operators are."
The third branch of the campaign revolves around another cluster tracked by Genians as Operation GitPower. Attributed to the Kimsuky group, the activity involves operating local large language model (LLM) environments using Ollama and GPT4All to generate decoy documents and use them to target professionals and organizations in the fields of policy, academia, international cooperation, diplomacy, and security research.
Present within the phishing email is a Windows Shortcut (LNK) that, once launched, runs PowerShell code designed to retrieve the lure document via GitHub's raw content service and open it, while stealthily downloading additional payloads like AsyncRAT in the background.
| Kimsuky's use of GitHub for C2 | 
The campaign has since evolved to target Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy, utilizing international conference invitations and requests for analytical collaboration to elicit responses from targets and eventually distribute malware in the form of ZIP archives containing malicious LNK files.
In at least one case, the phishing emails have been found to trick recipients into clicking on bogus links to harvest their Google account credentials under the pretext of joining a Zoom meeting via Gmail. Another method involves distributing a counterfeit version of a Zoom installer that, in addition to installing the legitimate app, runs malware designed to run arbitrary PowerShell scripts and send the results back.
"This attack is particularly noteworthy as it indicates that Kimsuky has expanded its targeting scope beyond its traditional focus on South Korea to include key individuals in Ukraine," Genians noted last month, adding these efforts were mostly unsuccessful.
"Kimsuky's attacks against Ukraine may be cyber espionage operations aimed at collecting information on the war, the extent of North Korean troop losses, developments in the questioning and handling of prisoners of war, and the details of consultations between South Korea and Ukraine."
The latest findings from Stormshield merge together all of these separate findings into a single, cohesive picture -- a toolset comprising a management platform, victim-tracking consoles, and email-delivery infrastructure. The attack sequence is a single infection chain that's adapted for three environments -
- Send the target an email advertising a job opportunity, entice them into clicking a link, and initiate the "recruitment" process.
- The website masquerades as a recruitment platform where visitors can view job listings and submit job applications.
- In the background, the web page fingerprints the visitor and uses an IP address-based geofencing mechanism to lock out users from specific regions (possibly China). If access is restricted, users are served a stripped-down version of the home page without any ability to interact with it.
- If the "applicant" satisfies the filtering criteria, they are served an application form to enter their personal details.
- The user is then prompted to enter a referral (or invitation) code, indicating that the campaign is aimed at pre-identified targets rather than a broad audience. If the code is rejected, the site displays one of three messages: "Already used," "Locked to another IP," and "Invalid code."
- If the code is accepted, the candidate is served a confirmation message and is instructed to copy and run a command on the Linux terminal as part of a technical check.
- Once the command is run, it sends the "nonce" information displayed on the web page to a remote server via an HTTP POST request. No file or script is downloaded or executed on the victim machine at this stage.
- The web page, which is waiting for confirmation from the server, responds with an error message, stating: "Operation timeout. Please try again. Nonce Refreshed."
- The attack moves to the second stage when the web page displays the same verification screen but with a modified "Copy" button behavior that injects the malicious command directly into the victim's clipboard. The same pattern is observed even when the target uses the "Ctrl+C" keyboard shortcut to copy the command from the web page.
- 
    The actual command that gets executed depends on the operating system -
    
  - On Windows, it launches PowerShell to download and run a file named "v.cmd"
  - On Linux, it launches bash shell to download and run a file named "u"
  - On macOS, it launches bash shell to download and run a file named "verify_m”
"These scripts act as loaders: they prepare the execution environment, retrieve the necessary components, and launch a JavaScript payload, install_guard.js, fetched from a remote server," the French cybersecurity company explained.
| Trigram dropper execution phase | 
This preparatory stage also involves extracting a Base64-encoded script that configures the working directory, establishes a locking mechanism to prevent concurrent installations, and checks for an existing Node.js installation.
If a compatible version (minimum version 18) is not found, it proceeds to download and install Node.js version 20.18.1 based on the infected host's operating system and its architecture. It then downloads "install_guard.js," which deploys an infostealer tasked with collecting system metadata, browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and sensitive files present on the machine.
The entire operation is powered by a multi-layered architecture comprising fake recruitment (like Amber Group), conference invitation, and package delivery sites; C2 servers that host the JavaScript and are fetched by means of a GitLab dead-drop; and the back office hosted on "170.205.30[.]27:8000" that enables campaign management and victim tracking via a platform called "rms-platform."
The tracking console records every action undertaken by the user, while simultaneously keeping tabs on bot visitors and lookalike domains that have been taken down. Each "real visitor" is then rated "important," "moderate," or "useless," suggesting some sort of shortlisting based on their value.
Further analysis of the API routes associated with "rms-platform" show that it's capable of identifying potential targets by scraping GitHub profiles, sending phishing emails, managing decoys, issuing access codes, viewing and exporting collected data, and cryptocurrency wallet monitoring.
| Trigram infrastructure architecture | 
"These three levels rely on abused legitimate services: GitHub and GitLab for code and configuration hosting; Brevo, Resend, Mailgun, and Smartlead for email delivery; and FullStory for visitor session recording," Stormshield explained.
"The tracking consoles are not standalone applications: they are delivered within the same JavaScript code as the decoys. The same bundle is served to all visitors, and a check on the hostname or URL path determines which interface is displayed."
The technical indicators that point in the direction of UNK_DeadDrop and Kimsuky are listed below -
- eros1030109@gmail[.]com, a super-administrator account for the consoles that matches with an email address used in Operation GitPower.
- 0xapp123, a Medium account that discusses Web3 trends and lists "eros1030109@gmail.com" as the contact email address as far back as June 2022.
- silviattech1129_db_user, an identifier that appears as a username for a MongoDB database associated with "rms-platform" and in the history of the GitLab dead-drop file used in the "antd-img-crop" repository hijack as "silviattech1129."
- alexlopez-g/rms-platform, a backup GitHub repository hosting "rms-platform," with the user having contributed to a separate project named "Foxtopia-NFT/foxtopia-frontend" that includes a ".vscode/tasks.json" file mirroring tactics outlined in UNK_DeadDrop. The commit is signed with an email address "harper.danie95@gmail[.]com," which has been used to target designers on Contra with fake job offers.
- asteara[.]org, a domain flagged as "related infrastructure" for UNK_DeadDrop that has been used to host or serve the Trigram back office.
- pichi_finance_hr, a Telegram account that impersonates the human resources department of Pichi Finance, a decentralized finance (DeFi) platform that went offline in January 2025, and is likely used as a way to approach targets by posing as recruiters.
"Based on these infrastructure and tooling overlaps, we assess with high confidence that Trigram represents a continuation of the UNK_DeadDrop cluster, while illustrating an evolution in its delivery tactics," Stormshield concluded.
"Trigram stands out through the diversification of its initial access vectors and the remote retrieval of its final payload, rather than embedding it directly within the trojanized repository."
"This system automates the targeting of users on GitHub, orchestrates massive phishing campaigns through four email providers, monitors the compromise of each victim in real time, and launders the stolen funds through cryptocurrency wallets."

articles.title: OpenAI lanzó GPT-6.2 y limitó su ayuda en ciberseguridad por el riesgo de que sirva para atacar
articles.text:
OpenAI lanzó GPT-6.2 Astra y GPT-6.2 Sol, dos modelos de inteligencia artificial que ya están disponibles en ChatGPT y en la herramienta de programación Codex. La empresa los lanzó con restricciones más estrictas en ciberseguridad, porque sus propias pruebas muestran que ayudan a encontrar y explotar fallas informáticas.
Astra es el modelo para los proyectos más complejos. Sol es la versión más ligera, pensada para el trabajo cotidiano. Según OpenAI, ambos producen mejores resultados con menos texto de salida, lo que permite hacer más tareas dentro de los límites de uso de cada plan.
Los usuarios de los planes Plus, Pro, Enterprise y Edu de ChatGPT tienen acceso desde el lanzamiento. Los suscriptores del plan Pro de 200 dólares mensuales reciben por primera vez el modo Ultrafast, una opción de respuesta más rápida, que por ahora solo funciona con Sol. En el plan Pro de 500 dólares está disponible con ambos modelos.
Astra baja 20% su precio para desarrolladores
Para quienes usan los modelos a través de la API, el servicio que permite integrarlos en otras aplicaciones, Astra cuesta USD 8 por millón de tokens de entrada y USD 40 por millón de salida. Los tokens son las unidades de texto que el modelo procesa y por las que se cobra. Son precios 20% más bajos que los de GPT-6 Astra.
El texto que el sistema ya recibió antes y reutiliza (la entrada en caché) tiene un descuento de 60%: USD 0,40 por millón de tokens. Sol mantiene los precios de GPT-6.1 Sol: USD 2 por millón de entrada y USD 10 por millón de salida.
OpenAI sostiene que ambos modelos igualan o superan a otros modelos líderes en varias pruebas comparativas a una fracción del costo por tarea. Se trata de pruebas internas de la empresa.
Un nivel de riesgo crítico en ciberseguridad
Según la tarjeta de seguridad publicada por OpenAI, los dos modelos alcanzan el umbral Crítico en ciberseguridad de su Marco de Preparación, el sistema con el que la empresa mide los riesgos de sus modelos. También alcanzan el umbral Alto en capacidades biológicas y químicas.
En una prueba interna con vulnerabilidades de los motores V8 y Chrome divulgadas entre junio y agosto de 2026, Astra logró ejecutar código arbitrario en 53,5% de los intentos, frente a 31,5% de GPT-6 Astra. Sol obtuvo 50,5%. Ejecutar código arbitrario significa que el atacante logra que el equipo corra las instrucciones que él decide.
En otra evaluación, la de la firma Irregular, Astra encontró y explotó fallas desconocidas en sistemas de uso extendido. Una de ellas permitía a una aplicación maliciosa acceder a datos privados en un sistema operativo móvil popular sin tener permisos.
Esas fallas están en proceso de divulgación responsable. Ningún modelo logró atacar un objetivo totalmente protegido: los 15 desafíos más difíciles quedaron sin resolver.
Por ese motivo, OpenAI endureció las restricciones por defecto para pedidos de ayuda de mayor riesgo. La empresa reconoce que esto limita parte del trabajo legítimo de investigación de vulnerabilidades, y que los modelos resultan menos útiles que GPT-6 Astra en tareas de ciberseguridad permitidas.
Astra, el primero con riesgo alto de automejora
Astra es además el primer modelo que OpenAI lanza al público y que cumple el umbral Alto de automejora, es decir, la capacidad de contribuir a mejorar sistemas de IA.
Antes de ampliar su uso interno en Codex, la empresa evaluó su comportamiento, mejoró el aislamiento de sus entornos de investigación y creó Control Room, un sistema central que vigila las tareas de los modelos y puede detenerlas.
La tarjeta de seguridad también registra problemas. Los dos modelos omiten con más frecuencia los obstáculos que encontraron al informar su trabajo, y resisten menos los intentos de saltarse sus reglas que GPT-6 Astra en las primeras pruebas. OpenAI ajustó los límites de rechazo y dijo que investiga las causas de las omisiones. Astra mostró además más señales de reconocer cuándo lo están evaluando.
Quienes necesiten menos restricciones deben registrarse en Daybreak, el programa de acceso confiable de OpenAI para defensores informáticos. En el lanzamiento, los rechazos reducidos para Astra quedan limitados a un grupo más pequeño aprobado para Daybreak Red. La empresa dijo que trabajará para llevar los modelos 6.2 a ese programa.
El modo Ultrafast costará tres veces la tarifa estándar hasta el 28 de febrero de 2027 y seis veces desde el 1 de marzo de 2027, según la documentación de la API.

articles.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
articles.text:
Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it.
In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool. They even labeled it a security fix. Teams pinned to it would have passed every check.
The trick works because GitHub lets copies of a project, called forks, share code with the original. In May, the same technique hit the popular actions-cool/issues-helper tool, stealing credentials from the pipelines that ran it.
The lesson: pinning guarantees the code won't change, but not who wrote it.
That gap is the focus of an upcoming webinar, GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning. If your team treats pinning as the finish line, save your seat to learn what it actually protects you from, and what it doesn't.
Immutability Is Not Provenance
Pinning earned its reputation. When the tj-actions/changed-files compromise repointed tags to a malicious commit across more than 23,000 repositories in March 2025, teams that had pinned to SHAs were unaffected.
GitHub now lets administrators enforce pinning as an organization-wide policy, and few security teams argue against it.
📅 Save Your Spot: Learn Why “Best Practice” Won’t Stop the Next GitHub Actions Attack
But a pinned SHA leaves three questions unanswered:
- Authorship: A SHA doesn't tell you who wrote the commit. Any fork commit can be pinned.
- Project membership: Org-level enforcement checks that a reference is a 40-character SHA, not that the commit actually lives in the upstream project.
- Runtime: A Docker-based action pinned to a SHA can still build its image at runtime, pulling in dependencies that were never frozen.
With agentic development pushing more code through CI than ever, each of those gaps gets exercised more often and reviewed less closely.
GitHub's Lockfiles Help. They Don't Finish the Job.
GitHub's 2026 Actions security roadmap, published March 26, put deterministic dependency locking front and center. Workflow lockfiles entered public preview on October 14 and became generally available on October 28, 2026. They tie every run to recorded commits for actions and their transitive dependencies, even if a tag moves later.
That's real progress. Locked commits must exist on a branch of the source repository, which blunts fork-only impostors. But GitHub's own changelog is clear that locking "does not determine whether the dependency itself is safe." Commit authorship and runtime builds remain open; immutable releases only help when maintainers opt in, and lockfiles aren't currently supported on GitHub Enterprise Server.
Not sure where your pipelines fall in that gap? Register for the webinar for a clear-eyed breakdown of what GitHub's roadmap fixes and what it still leaves to you.
What You'll Learn
Led by Erika Heidi, Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard, the session draws a hard line between immutability and provenance, and covers:
- What org-level pin enforcement actually verifies, and the false confidence it can create
- How impostor commits work, and why GitHub's repository network makes them possible
- What GitHub's Actions roadmap addresses, and what it doesn't
- Other ways to close the trust gap, including a curated catalog of vetted actions
Who Should Attend
Platform and DevOps engineers who own CI/CD, AppSec and DevSecOps teams writing pipeline policy, and security leaders who signed off on SHA pinning as "done." If your workflows pull in third-party actions, this session is for you.
Attackers have already shown they can disguise a malicious commit as a hardening fix. The next one won't announce itself either.
Register now for GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning, pick the session time that works for you, and find out what your pins aren't telling you.

articles.title: Telegram sur Android a renforcé sa sécurité mais des chercheurs ont contourné le nouveau filtre
articles.text:
Dans une vidéo de la société de sécurité NebuSec, un widget envoyé par un bot dans une conversation Telegram ouvre la calculatrice d’un téléphone Android, malgré le filtre que la messagerie a ajouté la semaine dernière à son application.
Telegram laisse ses bots envoyer des widgets depuis le 9 novembre. Ces petits blocs interactifs s’affichent dans le message, et leur code JavaScript s’exécute sur votre téléphone. Deux jours plus tard, le compte V12 a affirmé sur X que n’importe quel message Telegram permettait d’exécuter du code à distance. Telegram a alors placé dans un processus à part le moteur QuickJS, qui fait tourner le JavaScript des widgets sur Android. Avec un filtre seccomp, un mécanisme du noyau Linux, l’application bloque ou enregistre certaines requêtes de ce moteur au système, appelées appels système. Selon The HackerNews, mes chercheurs de NebuSec affirment avoir exécuté du code en dehors de ce filtre, par deux méthodes différentes.
Telegram laisse passer la plupart des appels système des widgets
Dans le code source de Telegram pour Android 13.2.2 (7303), l’entreprise ne bloque que quelques dizaines d’appels système, dont ptrace, bpf et mount, et laisse passer tous les autres. Ses développeurs n’ont pas filtré ioctl, l’appel qui sert à dialoguer avec les pilotes du matériel. Ils ont en outre réglé le filtre en mode audit, d’après le code examiné par The Hacker News. Dans ce mode, l’application empêche toujours le moteur de lancer un nouveau programme, mais elle se contente d’enregistrer les autres appels interdits, avant de les laisser passer. Un commentaire des développeurs prévoit de garder ce réglage « jusqu’à ce que les journaux des appareils indiquent que le moteur ne les génère plus ». Rien ne dit si la version installée sur votre téléphone utilise ce réglage.
Dans sa documentation, Telegram promet aux développeurs un environnement isolé, sans accès au réseau. Mais selon NebuSec, ces règles sont inscrites dans le code de QuickJS. Il suffit d’une faille d’utilisation après libération (use-after-free) ou d’écriture hors limites dans le moteur pour qu’un script lise et modifie la mémoire du processus, et la protection ne sert plus à rien. Et Telegram fait tourner tous les widgets dans un seul processus. Un widget détourné partage donc sa mémoire avec les widgets de tous les autres bots, ajoutent les chercheurs.
Leur première méthode exploite une faille des widgets que Telegram n’a pas prise en compte dans son filtre. La seconde associe une faille couverte par le filtre et une faille du noyau. Toutefois, les chercheurs ont mené leur démonstration sur un serveur de test de Telegram, car seuls des bots autorisés envoient aujourd’hui des widgets sur le service ouvert au public. Ils ne disent pas jusqu’où leur code peut aller, vers vos messages ou le reste du téléphone, ni si vous devez d’abord lancer le bot ou toucher le widget. NebuSec garde les détails techniques pour plus tard, ne mentionne aucun identifiant CVE et ne dit pas si elle a prévenu Telegram.
Telegram restreint les widgets sans publier de correctif
Sur le service ouvert au public, Telegram ne laisse plus que des bots autorisés envoyer des widgets, et NebuSec a dû passer par un serveur de test pour sa démonstration. « Oui, actuellement, les bots classiques ne sont pas autorisés à utiliser de widgets, même dans les conversations privées », confirmait la semaine dernière un contributeur du projet telegram-bot-api sur GitHub. Telegram n’a pas indiqué quels bots gardent ce droit, ni si la restriction a été levée depuis. Les chercheurs ne mentionnent aucune version corrigée, et le code source publié par l’entreprise s’arrête cette semaine à la version 13.2.2 (7303).
Telegram avait assuré avoir corrigé le problème montré dans la première vidéo de V12, et déployé le correctif chez tous ses utilisateurs. Son patron, Pavel Durov, a ensuite répondu aux signalements d’exécution de code dans les applications Android et Windows. « Personne ne peut être piraté simplement en recevant un message », a écrit le PDG sur sa chaîne Telegram. Selon lui, il faut d’abord lancer un service tiers, et Telegram a corrigé ce service côté serveur. En avril 2024, l’entreprise avait aussi bloqué depuis ses serveurs une faille zero day de son application pour Windows, née d’une faute de frappe de ses développeurs.
Mais Pavel Durov a publié son message avant la démonstration de NebuSec, et les chercheurs ne disent pas si vous devez lancer le bot, ou toucher le widget, pour que leur code s’exécute.

articles.title: YouTube empezó a sumar a sus visitas a todas las personas que miran juntas un video en la televisión
articles.text:
YouTube empezó a incluir en el contador público de visitas a las personas que, según sus cálculos, miran un video juntas en un televisor. Hasta ahora, cada reproducción en la televisión sumaba una sola visita, sin importar cuántos espectadores hubiera.
La plataforma llama a esas personas “coespectadores” (co-views, en inglés). La medida abarca videos largos, Shorts (los videos verticales cortos) y transmisiones en vivo, según el canal Creator Insider, con el que YouTube informa a los creadores. No se aplica a celulares ni a computadoras: allí cada reproducción sigue valiendo una visita.
Tampoco es retroactiva. Los contadores históricos no cambian, pero los videos antiguos sumarán coespectadores a partir de las nuevas reproducciones en televisores.
YouTube sostiene que el cambio refleja cómo se usa el servicio: los usuarios miran más de 1.000 millones de horas diarias en televisores, según la empresa. También afirma que así se alinea con la televisión tradicional, que estima cuántas personas ven un programa y no solo cuántos aparatos están encendidos.
Un modelo estadístico, sin cámaras ni micrófonos
La cifra de coespectadores no se mide: se calcula. Según YouTube, un modelo desarrollado por científicos de Google Research usa patrones demográficos, el tipo de contenido y los horarios de visualización, y se calibra con fuentes de referencia como los paneles de audiencia de la industria.
La empresa aclaró que no usa cámaras, micrófonos ni sensores de los dispositivos para saber cuántas personas hay frente a la pantalla.
Los creadores tendrán una métrica privada nueva en YouTube Studio, la tasa de coespectadores, dentro del desglose por tipo de dispositivo. Un valor de 1,10 significa que, de cada 1.100 visitas en televisor, 1.000 corresponden a reproducciones y 100 a coespectadores, según el ejemplo de YouTube citado por Net Influencer. Dividir las visitas totales por esa tasa devuelve la cifra sin coespectadores.
Los pagos a los creadores no cambian
Según la página de ayuda de YouTube, los ingresos del programa de socios y los requisitos para ingresar siguen basados en las “visualizaciones comprometidas” y en las horas de visualización calificadas, que no incluyen coespectadores.
Las impresiones de miniaturas, la tasa de clics y la duración promedio de visualización tampoco se modifican. El tiempo de reproducción sí incorpora a los coespectadores.
La métrica privada anterior, “visualizaciones con coespectadores”, se retirará en mayo de 2027. Los creadores pueden exportar esos datos históricos desde Studio hasta entonces.
The Verge, que tituló la noticia como una nueva forma de inflar las cifras, recordó que el cambio llega después de otro: desde el 24 de agosto, YouTube cuenta una visita desde el primer instante de reproducción, y no tras unos 30 segundos, como muchos creadores suponían, según Net Influencer.
El interés comercial ya existía. En 2022, Google presentó un estudio con Nielsen que halló que varios adultos miraban YouTube juntos en televisor el 26% de las veces, frente al 22% de la televisión lineal. Un estudio de la Video Advertising Bureau y TVision, publicado en febrero, midió un 45% de las impresiones de YouTube con coespectadores, contra el 60% de los servicios de streaming premium.
El plazo confirmado es el de mayo de 2027, cuando YouTube dejará de ofrecer la métrica privada anterior y los creadores perderán la posibilidad de exportar esos datos.
Descubre todas las formas de ganar dinero con tus videos en YouTube
En YouTube, los creadores generan ingresos principalmente uniéndose al Programa de Socios, lo que les permite ganar dinero mediante los anuncios que se muestran en sus videos tradicionales y Shorts, además de recibir una parte proporcional de la cuota de aquellos espectadores que utilizan YouTube Premium.
Más allá de la publicidad, los canales pueden diversificar sus ganancias con herramientas financiadas por la audiencia, tales como las membresías mensuales, los Súper Chats en transmisiones en vivo, los Súper Gracias en videos bajo demanda y la venta directa de productos propios a través de YouTube Shopping.
Para acceder a la monetización completa por publicidad, los requisitos se han vuelto más exigentes en 2026: el canal debe tener al menos 1.000 suscriptores y alcanzar 8.000 horas de reproducción pública en los últimos 12 meses, o bien acumular 20 millones de visualizaciones válidas en Shorts durante los últimos 90 días.
Adicionalmente, todo creador necesita tener una cuenta de Google AdSense vinculada para procesar los pagos y debe cumplir de forma estricta con las políticas de derechos de autor y contenido original de la plataforma para evitar la desmonetización.

articles.title: Chosfox Teases Geonix Plus: 50% Wireless Mechanical Keyboard With Unorthodox Ortholinear and Row-Staggered Layouts
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Chosfox Teases Geonix Plus: 50% Wireless Mechanical Keyboard With Unorthodox Ortholinear and Row-Staggered Layouts
Chosfox, the maker of the Geonix keyboard, which was arguably one of the keyboards that helped kickstart interest in modern 40% and ortholinear keyboards, has just confirmed that it will launch the Geonix Plus, a new, larger version of the original Geonix. Much like it has done with the Geonix Rev 2.5 and its Init40 counterpart, Chosfox has confirmed via a post on X that it plans on offering the Geonix Plus in both an ortholinear and row-staggered layout, with the latter being more familiar to users of traditional keyboards. No release date has yet been officially confirmed, but Chosfox says that the Geonix Plus is "coming soon." 
The Geonix Plus moves away from the 40% layout of the Init40, seemingly adopting a highly unorthodox 50% layout. Although it remains to be seen how this design will work on the row-staggered version, the ortholinear version seems to be a 12×5 grid of keys with a 2u spacebar in the middle of the bottom row. It also seemingly has a dedicated arrow cluster on the right side of the keyboard, although this has resulted in some seriously peculiar placements—like the += and /? keys on the bottom row, instead of in the num row and row two, respectively.The Geonix Plus also looks to be using Chosfox's new RAK low-profile switches atop Kailh's Choc V2 switches. Prior to the official teaser by Chosfox, the Geonix Plus was shown off at the Tokyo Keyboard Expo 2026 (via Shin5no on YouTube. The prototype version shown off at the keyboard expo also appears to have an aluminium chassis, like the current Init40 and Geonix Rev 2.5, and it shares the minimal top case design of its predecessors, as well.
