articles.title: 10 desk upgrade gifts to improve PC work and gaming spaces — a monitor riser with charging and USB ports, an excellent speaker upgrade, modern charging hubs, and more
articles.text:
10 desk upgrade gifts to improve PC work and gaming spaces — a monitor riser with charging and USB ports, an excellent speaker upgrade, modern charging hubs, and more
Upgrading a PC right now may be a non-starter, but you can still improve someone's overall desk experience without spending a lot.
It’s a tough time for PC gamers and enthusiasts. Graphics cards are scarce, RAM and storage are prohibitively expensive, and the PC port of GTA VI isn’t expected until sometime in 2027 at the earliest. But core components aside, there are plenty of other ways to improve someone's PC PC-related experience, and upgrading their desk space is a good place to start looking. 
We’ve already covered key peripherals, like keyboards and gaming accessories, so below we’ll be focusing on desk devices that let you connect more devices, stay more organized, improve comfort, or just keep things cleaner. From some of the best desk-friendly PC speakers I’ve tested to tactile media and software controls, and a monitor riser that integrates a USB hub and charging, there’s something here to improve everyone’s desk experience. 
I own most of these devices, or similar previous-gen versions that are no longer available, and can attest to their usefulness. Some live on my desk at the office, while others are better suited for home PC setups, but they all make for a better experience when I'm at my desk.
These unique wrist and elbow rests are designed to hang over the edge of your desk, making them great for those who lean on their elbows, or just for a cramped desk setup. Available in multiple colors and sizes, the 11.8-inch version I have is wide enough that I only need to use one for my compact keyboard at work. So I use the other one at home for my gaming setup.
If your phone has magnetic wireless Qi charging, there's no nicer, more convenient way to charge it than a stand like this, especially when there's additional power and ports for other devices. This Anker model has a built-in retractable cable that can handle up to 60W, so you can charge a non-gaming laptop with this stand at the same time as your phone. I've used a similar charging stand for years, and it helps keep things clean while making charging a second device as simple as grabbing the pull-out cable.
With 11 ports and up to 10 Gbps speed, a solid aluminum shell, and buttons so you can cut power to individual ports, this USB hub is a great addition to a desk without enough ports. It has external power for better stability, and even a 20W USB-C PD port on the end for charging phones or peripherals.
Just plug this simple device into a USB port, and you can control the volume and select tracks without reaching for your keyboard or mouse. It supports recent Windows versions, as well as Mac, without the need for a driver.
The Stream Deck Mini features six configurable buttons for launching software or controlling devices. It's compatible with the full suite of Stream Deck tools from Elgato. There are cheaper alternatives, but the ecosystem (supporting software as well as lights and smart devices) makes these devices more versatile than the competition.
This quirky device combines an under-desk headphone hook and a 20W PD USB charger with one USB-C and two USB-A ports. It brings a bit of extra convenience and tidiness to your desk setup. It comes in four colors and I've been using one under my standing desk since 2023.
These speakers are some of the best desk-friendly options we've tested, with great sound, lots of connection options, and excellent build quality. They're a great audio upgrade to most desk setups, and I have a pair that I bought in 2012 that still look and sound as good as they did when they were new.
We've all dealt with a crumb-covered desk or a dusty PC at some point. This all-in-one desk vacuum and portable air blower can tackle both those issues, and much more. Connect the included accessories to one end for blowing, and the other for suction. It's lived near my desk for years, and my main complaint is that Hoto doesn't ship with a wall mount or a good way to hold its many accessories. I solved that issue with my 3D printer.
This compact 1920 x 720 IPS monitor supports touch input and a 75 Hz refresh. I wouldn't recommend actually playing games on it, but it's a great second screen for game or work chats (or whatever else you want to keep a close eye on while doing other things). Its 24:9 aspect ratio (and a built-in kickstand) make it a good fit under your primary desktop monitor. It also costs less than competing name-brand alternatives.
You can think of this monitor stand as a sort of all-in-one desk upgrade. It packs a USB hub, 15W Qi charging, a 20W PD charging hub, built-in storage drawers, and a metal frame that has space for up to two 32-inch monitors. That's a lot of functionality in one device. I've owned a previous version of this stand since 2020. In fact, it's currently holding the monitor I'm looking at as I type this, and I've found it a good fit for my cramped office desk, since it helps keeps things tidy.
After a rough start with the Mattel Aquarius as a child, Matt built his first PC in the late 1990s and ventured into mild PC modding in the early 2000s. He’s spent the last 15 years covering emerging technology for Smithsonian, Popular Science, and Consumer Reports, while testing components and PCs for Computer Shopper, PCMag and Digital Trends.

articles.title: Surfshark One ou McAfee Premium : deux bundles, deux façons de se protéger
articles.text:
Surfshark One vs McAfee Premium : quelle suite choisir en 2026 ?
Face à la multiplication des cybermenaces, les suites de sécurité tout-en-un séduisent de plus en plus d’utilisateurs. Surfshark One est actuellement affiché à 2,79 €/mois sur 24 mois, avec 3 mois offerts, soit 75,33 € pour les 27 premiers mois. McAfee Premium reste affiché à 44,95 € pour la première période. Voici ce qui distingue réellement les deux offres.
Avis : Surfshark One se distingue surtout par son VPN très complet et son approche centrée sur la confidentialité, tandis que McAfee Premium propose une suite plus classique, pensée pour protéger un grand nombre d’appareils. Le choix dépend moins du nombre de fonctions que de leur usage réel au quotidien.
Points forts
• Surfshark One : VPN sur appareils illimités, antivirus, Alert, Search et Alternative ID
• McAfee Premium : nombre illimité d’appareils, antivirus, Secure VPN et surveillance de l’identité
• Deux offres réunissant plusieurs outils dans un seul abonnement
Points faibles
• Surfshark Antivirus reste limité à 5 appareils, malgré le VPN illimité
• Les prix Surfshark varient selon la durée, la promotion et les conditions affichées
• Les tarifs de renouvellement doivent être vérifiés avant souscription
À l’heure où les cybermenaces se diversifient — logiciels malveillants, phishing, vols de données ou encore espionnage en ligne — s’équiper d'un simple antivirus ne suffit plus. Pour être totalement serein, les utilisateurs se tournent désormais vers des suites de sécurité « tout-en-un », capables de protéger efficacement leurs appareils.
Contrairement aux idées reçues, ce type de solution n’est plus réservé à des budgets élevés. Surfshark One est actuellement proposé à 2,79 €/mois sur 24 mois, avec 3 mois offerts, soit 75,33 € pour les 27 premiers mois. McAfee Premium est affiché à 44,95 € pour la première période. Les deux offres restent accessibles, mais leur mode de facturation n’est pas directement comparable.
Ce comparatif vous aide à mieux comprendre leurs points forts et à choisir la solution la plus adaptée à vos besoins.
Surfshark One à 2,79 €/mois : un bundle VPN + antivirus sur 27 mois
Surfshark One repose d’abord sur Surfshark VPN, qui donne accès à plus de 4 500 serveurs dans 100 pays, tous annoncés comme compatibles 10 Gbit/s. Il prend notamment en charge WireGuard et OpenVPN, avec CleanWeb, blocage des pop-up de cookies, Bypasser, IP tournante et Dynamic MultiHop. Le VPN peut être utilisé sur un nombre illimité d’appareils avec un seul compte, mais cette limite ne s’applique pas à l’antivirus.
Au-delà du VPN, Surfshark One regroupe Alternative ID, Scam Protection, Antivirus et Alert. L’antivirus propose notamment des analyses programmées, la protection en temps réel et la protection de la webcam, avec une couverture limitée à 5 appareils. Alert surveille les fuites de données personnelles. La couverture contre le vol d’identité jusqu’à 1 million de dollars mentionnée par Surfshark est réservée aux résidents américains éligibles et ne s’applique donc pas aux utilisateurs en France.
Surfshark One est actuellement affiché à 2,79 €/mois sur 24 mois, avec 3 mois supplémentaires offerts, soit 75,33 € pour les 27 premiers mois. Le prix barré indiqué est de 538,65 €, pour une remise annoncée de 86 %. La TVA peut s’appliquer et Surfshark propose une garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours.
McAfee Premium à 44,95 € : une suite pour un nombre illimité d’appareils
McAfee Premium est actuellement affiché à 44,95 € pour la première période, contre un tarif de référence de 129,95 € indiqué par l’éditeur. La formule couvre un utilisateur et un nombre illimité d’appareils. Comme pour la plupart des suites de sécurité, le prix promotionnel ne doit pas être confondu avec le tarif applicable lors d’un renouvellement ultérieur.
Côté protection, McAfee Premium adopte une approche plus traditionnelle de la suite de sécurité. L’offre comprend notamment l’antivirus, la protection anti-fraude, la protection web, un destructeur de fichiers, un pare-feu avancé et la suppression des traqueurs. Elle vise surtout les utilisateurs qui veulent centraliser plusieurs couches de protection dans un même abonnement.
McAfee Premium ajoute Secure VPN, la surveillance de l’identité, un gestionnaire de mots de passe, l’analyse des comptes en ligne et des réglages de confidentialité pour les réseaux sociaux. La différence avec Surfshark One tient surtout à la philosophie du pack : McAfee privilégie une suite antivirus et identité très large, tandis que Surfshark place le VPN et la confidentialité au centre de l’expérience.
Surfshark One ou McAfee Premium : lequel choisir ?
Surfshark One convient davantage à ceux qui utilisent beaucoup le VPN et veulent réunir confidentialité, protection contre les arnaques, surveillance des fuites et antivirus dans le même écosystème. À 2,79 €/mois sur 24 mois avec 3 mois offerts, le coût initial atteint 75,33 € pour 27 mois. McAfee Premium reste plus simple à comparer sur une première période à 44,95 € et couvre un nombre illimité d’appareils. Avant de choisir, il faut surtout comparer le coût total, les fonctions réellement utiles et le tarif de renouvellement.

AMD just sent out invitations to its CES 2027 media event to be held in Las Vegas next January. The invitation has a curious peak-shaped motif. This could hint at "Olympic Ridge," codename for the next-generation Ryzen desktop processor powered by the "Zen 6" microarchitecture. AMD in its recent EPYC 9006 "Venice" server processor release unveiled "Zen 6" to offer significant IPC increases in enterprise workloads; but these gains were evaluated in enterprise benchmarks. articles.title: Apple tuvo fallas globales: iCloud, Apple Pay, Apple Store, Apple TV+ y otros servicios sufrieron caída
articles.text:
Varios servicios de Apple registraron fallas y dejaron a miles de usuarios sin acceso a aplicaciones y plataformas de uso cotidiano. La interrupción golpeó a iCloud, Apple Pay, App Store, Apple Music y Apple Care, con picos de reportes que superaron las dos mil incidencias en algunos de estos servicios.
El episodio se suma a una seguidilla de fallos tecnológicos que afectaron en los últimos días a bancos estadounidenses, aerolíneas y a Microsoft.
Qué servicios de Apple sufren la caída
Apple confirmó que App Store, Apple Music y Apple Care presentaron una interrupción del servicio. En simultáneo, Apple informó que los usuarios se veían afectados por problemas con la cuenta y el inicio de sesión de iCloud.
El portal DownDetector, que monitoriza este tipo de incidencias en el mundo, fue el encargado de dimensionar el alcance del problema. La plataforma registró más de 2.300 informes de fallas vinculados a Apple Pay y una cifra similar relacionada con Apple Support, el portal de asistencia técnica de la empresa.
A ese número se sumaron cerca de 700 reportes de incidencias asociados a Apple Store y Apple Music, dos de los servicios más utilizados por los usuarios de la marca para realizar compras y consumir contenido.
El servicio de almacenamiento en la nube, iCloud, fue uno de los más golpeados por la falla. Según los registros de DownDetector, usuarios no podían iniciar sesión ni acceder con normalidad a sus cuentas.
La interrupción de los servicios de Apple comenzó a manifestarse con quejas aisladas cerca de las 8:00 a. m. en la Costa Este de Estados Unidos, un horario que obligó al equipo técnico en su sede de California a enfrentar las primeras alertas desde las 5:00 a. m. locales.
Sin embargo, el colapso masivo de la plataforma ocurrió unas horas más tarde: entre la 1:00 p. m. y la 1:30 p. m. (hora del Este), las fallas se dispararon drásticamente hasta alcanzar un pico de casi 1.800 reportes, marcando el momento más crítico del incidente para las oficinas centrales de Apple, donde recién pasaban de las 10:00 a. m.
Tras ese pico máximo, la curva de la gráfica muestra que la compañía logró estabilizar los sistemas de manera progresiva durante las siguientes horas. Para las 3:26 p. m. en la Costa Este, el volumen de quejas de los usuarios ya había descendido a solo 405 reportes, confirmando que el equipo en California consiguió recuperar gran parte de la operatividad de sus servicios al pasar su mediodía local (12:26 p. m.), superando la fase más grave de la interrupción.
Fallas tecnológicas en bancos de Estados Unidos y su posible vínculo
Los inconvenientes en los servicios de Apple se produjeron un día después de que el banco estadounidense JPMorgan Chase, el más grande del país, sufriera un fallo en sus sistemas. La entidad atribuyó el problema a un “error de software”.
JPMorgan Chase descartó de manera expresa que el incidente se tratara de un ciberataque. El fallo tecnológico no se limitó a esa entidad: también afectó las cuentas bancarias de otros grandes bancos de Estados Unidos, entre ellos Bank of America, Wells Fargo y US Bank.
La coincidencia temporal entre la caída de los servicios de Apple y el error registrado en el sistema bancario estadounidense se dio en un lapso de apenas 24 horas, lo que generó atención sobre la seguidilla de fallos tecnológicos que atraviesan distintas industrias en el país.
Vuelos cancelados y el apagón de Microsoft 365 en los días previos
La ola de fallas tecnológicas en Estados Unidos no se limitó al sector bancario ni al tecnológico vinculado a Apple. Días antes, el transporte aéreo a nivel nacional se paralizó por un fallo técnico que dejó en tierra a más de 12.000 vuelos.
El problema derivó en más de 10.000 cancelaciones durante el viernes y el sábado previos. Las autoridades estadounidenses atribuyeron el inconveniente a la sustitución del antiguo cableado de cobre por fibra óptica en los sistemas de telecomunicaciones aéreas.
En paralelo, Microsoft también sufrió el viernes un apagón en sus servicios de Microsoft 365, entre los que se incluyen Teams y Outlook. La falla afectó tanto a la versión web como a la aplicación de escritorio de ambas herramientas.
Entre las consecuencias directas del apagón de Microsoft se registró un retraso en la entrega de mensajes, lo que generó inconvenientes para los usuarios que dependen de estas plataformas para sus comunicaciones laborales diarias.

articles.title: Italia quiere prohibir las redes sociales a menores de 13 años con una ley en noviembre de 2026
articles.text:
El gobierno de Italia quiere prohibir por completo las redes sociales a los menores de 13 años. La mayoría de centroderecha presentará el 18 de noviembre, en la Cámara de Diputados, una enmienda al decreto de seguridad sobre criminalidad juvenil, con el objetivo de que sea ley antes de que termine el mes.
La información fue adelantada por la Repubblica y confirmada por fuentes parlamentarias, según La Stampa. El texto fue redactado con la participación de Palazzo Chigi, la sede del gobierno de la primera ministra Giorgia Meloni.
La norma divide a los jóvenes en tres tramos. Por debajo de los 13 años, la inscripción en plataformas quedará vedada. Entre los 13 y los 16 solo se permitirá un perfil vinculado al de un padre o una madre. A partir de los 16, el registro será libre.
Según los diarios, el esquema sigue la línea del reglamento europeo sobre protección de menores en internet, que la prensa italiana llama Kids Act. El gobierno no quiere esperar a que esa norma comunitaria entre en vigor.
Bruselas pidió no legislar todavía
La Comisión Europea invitó a los Estados miembros a no aprobar leyes propias hasta que exista la normativa común, según La Stampa. El gobierno italiano decidió avanzar igual: aprobará la enmienda y abrirá después un diálogo con Bruselas.
El texto retoma dos proyectos de ley ya redactados: el de la senadora Lavinia Mennuni, de Fratelli d’Italia, el partido de Meloni, y el de la diputada Marianna Madia, de Italia Viva. La Stampa prevé un apoyo de varios partidos.
Hoy la ley italiana exige que los menores de 14 años cuenten con el consentimiento de sus padres para abrir una cuenta. Rainews informó en octubre que esa regla se elude con facilidad, porque no existen herramientas certificadas para comprobar la edad de los usuarios.
De los disturbios de Milán a la enmienda
El impulso político nació en octubre, después de los violentos disturbios callejeros en Milán. Meloni dijo entonces a la Repubblica que no se oponía a vetar las redes a menores de 14 años y dejó el asunto en manos del Parlamento, según Il Sole 24 Ore y Rainews.
El Consejo de Ministros había aprobado el decreto de seguridad el martes 20 de octubre, sin incluir la restricción. La propuesta actual fija el límite en 13 años, no en 14.
Las críticas de la oposición apuntaron al retraso. La senadora del Partido Democrático Simona Malpezzi afirmó que la primera ministra “descubre hoy una urgencia que en el Parlamento conocemos desde hace tiempo” y atribuyó el bloqueo al gobierno. La senadora del Movimiento 5 Estrellas Barbara Floridia dijo que los proyectos estaban detenidos desde hacía más de dos años.
Mennuni sostuvo que su proyecto ya estaba acordado con Bruselas y listo para votarse. Madia anunció en octubre que su grupo presentaría su propia enmienda al decreto.
La enmienda se depositará el 18 de noviembre, fecha en que vence el plazo para presentar modificaciones al decreto en la Cámara de Diputados. Después deberá pasar por las comisiones competentes antes de llegar al pleno.
Países que siguen iniciativas similares
Más de 20 países —entre ellos Grecia, los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, Canadá y Francia— replicaron desde diciembre de 2025 la prohibición de redes sociales a menores que inauguró Australia para los jóvenes de 16 años, en un contexto de litigios millonarios contra Meta y YouTube (que desembolsaron más de 17.000 millones de dólares) y de una documentada crisis de salud mental juvenil, con estudios que muestran un aumento de hasta el 104% en enfermedades mentales graves entre adolescentes respecto a hace 50 años.
Sin embargo, los primeros datos sobre la eficacia de estas medidas generan escepticismo: en Australia, el país con la restricción más avanzada, un sondeo de la Molly Rose Foundation reveló que el 61% de los menores con cuentas en plataformas restringidas seguía accediendo a ellas, y el 70% calificó de “fácil” burlar la prohibición mediante VPN, identidades falsas o alteración de datos biométricos.
Ari Lightman, profesor de la Universidad Carnegie Mellon, cuestiona que el veto total sea la solución y propone en cambio estándares de seguridad por defecto en las plataformas, educación digital y mecanismos accesibles de derivación a servicios de salud mental, ante la falta de pruebas concluyentes de que las redes sociales sean la causa principal de los problemas psicológicos juveniles.

articles.title: Nvidia claims Vera CPU can gain up to 39% performance boost via software optimization at SC26 — architectural fine-tuning for Arm cores needed to take full advantage of chip
articles.text:
Nvidia claims its Vera CPU can gain up to 39% performance boost via software optimization at SC26 — architectural fine-tuning is needed to fully unleash custom Olympus cores
Vera can speed up old code out of the box, but there's more performance to unlock
Nvidia's Vera CPU, designed as both a standalone data-center part and a host for Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 servers, offers impressive performance thanks to substantially higher execution resources per core than its predecessor, Grace. However, Nvidia admits at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) that existing software cannot always take full advantage of Vera's resources without adaptation for the architecture.
The company shared that architecture-specific software optimizations can boost Vera's performance by nearly 39% in certain computationally intensive workloads. But despite offering unbeatable single-thread performance, the CPU is not positioned for general-purpose workloads.
Get the full Tom's Hardware experience on your device with our brand-new app. Bookmark articles, use our smart search feature, personalize your feed, and get push notifications so you never miss a beat.
Unlike Grace, which relies on off-the-shelf Neoverse V2 CPU cores developed by Arm, Vera uses Nvidia's proprietary Olympus cores specifically designed to maximize per-core performance as well as to ensure high aggregate throughput. To that end, Nvidia equipped Olympus with a wide front end that features a 10-wide decoder, a neural branch predictor, a deep out-of-order execution engine, six vector execution units, four load pipelines, two store pipelines, all backed with large private caches and advanced prefetch mechanisms.
In fact, Nvidia deliberately opted for 88 high-performance general-purpose cores with support for its proprietary spatial multithreading technology (176 threads in total) rather than maximizing the number of cores per socket, as the maximum possible single-thread performance was one of the key design goals for Vera.
"CPU design is really just a game of trade-offs," said Hannah Coutand, who leads Vera CPU marketing at Nvidia, in an interview with Tom's Hardware Premium. "You could maximize for a lot of cores, but literally when you maximize the die for lots of cores, you do not actually have space to maximize for IPC, like instructions per clock."
Although Nvidia primarily positions Vera as a CPU for agentic AI and other AI-related workloads, the company originally conceived its Olympus microarchitecture with data processing applications in mind. As it turned out, the key attributes of Vera — high per-core performance, high memory bandwidth, and low memory access latency — are precisely what agentic AI workloads need as well, according to Coutand.
"We are very clear in our strategy with Vera and our positioning with Vera that it is not a general-purpose CPU," Coutand said. " If you want a web server for your cloud data center, there are probably other choices that are better suited for that than Vera. [Vera is made for] workloads […] that require that high per-core speed, high memory bandwidth, low latency. […] It has great fungibility for lots of workloads as long as those workloads value the things that Vera is good for."
Software optimizations make good things better
To assess the computational capabilities of Nvidia's custom Olympus microarchitecture and its advantages over Neoverse V2, Nvidia's researchers used a double-precision general matrix multiplication (DGEMM) workload based on an assembly kernel from OpenBLAS, an open-source linear algebra library. While OpenBLAS features a kernel tailored for the Arm Neoverse V2 cores that power Nvidia's Grace processor, it lacks one specifically designed for Olympus.
To examine the efficiency of the two microarchitectures, the researchers used a standalone benchmark called miniKernelGEMM with a 128 × 128 matrix multiplication problem that fits into the L1 cache of both processors.
The Grace CPU achieved 4.51 instructions per clock (IPC) and 13.03 FP64 operations per cycle with the Neoverse V2 kernel, whereas Vera executed 5.43 instructions per clock and 15.69 FP64 operations per cycle with the very same code, an improvement of approximately 20%.
However, when the researchers used a kernel specifically optimized for Olympus, Vera’s performance increased to 7.53 instructions per clock and 21.75 FP64 operations per cycle. As a result, Vera outperformed its predecessor by nearly 67% on a per-core, per-clock basis in this particular workload.
Grace's Neoverse V2 microarchitecture has four 128-bit SIMD pipelines that can perform a total of 16 FP64 operations per clock, whereas Nvidia's Olympus has six such pipelines that can execute up to 24 FP64 operations per cycle, a 50% improvement.
But where the Neoverse V2-optimized kernel uses 81.4% of Grace's peak FP64 throughput, it uses only about 66.5% of Vera's computational capabilities. With changes to matrix tile organization, register allocation, and instruction scheduling that better suit the Olympus microarchitecture, the researchers managed to utilize 90.6% of its peak FP64 throughput, according to Nvidia's tutorial published at SC26.
While software developed and optimized for existing Arm-based data center processors can still benefit from the capabilities of Nvidia's Olympus cores without any specific optimizations, the company's SC26 benchmark results demonstrate that at least some applications will need to be fine-tuned for the new microarchitecture to take full advantage of its execution resources. Of course, it remains to be seen how much performance can be gained through Olympus-specific optimizations in workloads other than matrix multiplication.
As Nvidia expands beyond CPUs that primarily serve as companions to its data center GPUs and chases the standalone server CPU market, the company will have to ensure that performance-critical software takes advantage of the architectural peculiarities of its processors, much like Intel and AMD have done for decades.
But the company is already deeply experienced with partner and ecosystem development for platforms like CUDA, so as Vera is more widely adopted, that experience could prove useful in spurring optimizations for these CPUs going forward.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday, Intego ONE Complete réunit antivirus Mac, pare-feu, VPN et nettoyage à -50%
articles.text:
À l’approche du Black Friday, qui tombe le 27 novembre, Intego baisse de moitié la formule qui protège à la fois un Mac et un iPhone. Intego ONE Complete, avec antivirus, pare-feu et VPN, est à 65 € HT pour deux ans chez Intego, et notre test en a aussi relevé les limites, à commencer par la mémoire.
Fondé en 1997, Intego conçoit des outils de sécurité pour l’écosystème Apple. Lancée en avril 2026 pour remplacer la gamme X9, la suite Intego ONE réunit antivirus, pare-feu, nettoyage et VPN dans une seule application. Intego ONE Complete est la seule formule à inclure le VPN, et elle couvre aussi un iPhone sans abonnement supplémentaire.
Pour le Black Friday, la formule de deux ans pour un Mac et un iPhone est à 65 € HT, soit 2,71 € HT par mois, au lieu de 129,99 € HT. Avec la TVA à 20 %, la facture revient à 78 € TTC, soit 3,25 € par mois.
Intego ONE Complete, pour un Mac et un iPhone pendant deux ans, est à 65 € HT au lieu de 129,99 € HT chez Intego, avec une garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours.
Pourquoi choisir Intego ONE Complete ?
- Quatre outils dans une seule application : L’antivirus et le pare-feu surveillent le Mac, SmartClean libère de l’espace et désinstalle proprement les applications, et le VPN chiffre la connexion. Vous n’installez plus de modules séparés.
- Une détection mesurée en laboratoire : En mars 2026, AV-TEST a relevé 100 % de détection sur 405 échantillons de malwares macOS, sans faux positif, avec la note maximale de 6/6 en protection, en performance et en utilisation.
- L’iPhone dans le même abonnement : L’application iOS apporte le VPN, un diagnostic du Wi-Fi et un contrôle des réglages de sécurité, sans second abonnement. Elle ne joue pas les antivirus : iOS ne le permet pas.
Entre Wi-Fi d’hôtel et entretien du Mac, ce que la suite fait au quotidien
Le pare-feu montre application par application ce qui sort vers Internet, et le VPN couvre 51 pays avec un kill Switch. Dans notre test d’Intego ONE, le VPN affiche des performances excellentes, comparables à celles d’ExpressVPN : il sert d’abord à celles et ceux qui travaillent en déplacement, sur les Wi-Fi d’hôtel, de gare ou de café. Côté iPhone, l’application contrôle le code, Face ID ou Touch ID et les mises à jour.
SmartClean suit le processeur, la mémoire et le stockage du Mac, une aide pour un ordinateur qui ralentit, à manier avec parcimonie. La formule est moins adaptée à un Mac de 8 Go : sur un MacBook M1 de ce type, nous avons relevé environ 1,3 Go de mémoire occupés par Intego et un scan complet de 26 minutes qui pèse vite sur l’usage. Pour plusieurs Mac, il faut viser les formules à 3 ou 5 appareils.
Un spécialiste du Mac face à Bitdefender et Norton
Intego garde la première place de notre comparatif des meilleurs antivirus pour Mac, avec 9,6 sur 10, devant Bitdefender Total Security et Norton 360. Sa fiche n’affiche pourtant ni anti-phishing, ni anti-ransomware, ni contrôle parental, ni essai gratuit, là où Bitdefender et Norton les intègrent et couvrent davantage d’appareils. Le choix se joue donc entre une suite pensée pour macOS, qui protège un Mac et un iPhone, et une couverture plus large pour toute la famille.
✅ Les points forts
- 100 % de détection sur 405 malwares macOS chez AV-TEST en mars 2026
- Antivirus, pare-feu, SmartClean et VPN dans une seule application
- VPN de 51 pays avec kill Switch, aux performances comparables à ExpressVPN dans notre test
- iPhone couvert par le même abonnement
- Garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours
❌ Les limites
- Moteur anti-malware d’environ 1 Go de mémoire au repos et scans complets très lourds
- Ni anti-phishing, ni anti-ransomware, ni contrôle parental, ni essai gratuit
- Pare-feu qui multiplie les alertes au premier lancement
- Renouvellement automatique à 129,99 € HT tous les deux ans, soit 155,99 € TTC
Le tarif de 65 € HT s’affiche une fois les options « 2 ans » et « 1 Mac + 1 iPhone » sélectionnées, et la remise de 50 % s’applique au moment du paiement.
À 65 € HT pour deux ans, soit 78 € TTC, Intego ONE Complete coûte 23,39 € de moins que lors de notre bon plan du 8 octobre, où la même formule affichait 101,39 € TTC. Elle s’adresse à celles et ceux qui possèdent un Mac et un iPhone, se connectent souvent à des Wi-Fi qu’ils ne contrôlent pas et préfèrent une suite unique à plusieurs abonnements séparés. Sur la durée, la facture revient à 3,25 € TTC par mois.
Elle convient moins à un Mac de 8 Go de mémoire, à un foyer qui équipe plusieurs machines ou à quelqu’un qui dispose déjà d’un VPN. Notre test reste mesuré sur le reste : une suite agréable à prendre en main, mais encore lourde pour la mémoire. Le renouvellement est automatique à 155,99 € TTC tous les deux ans : notez l’échéance dans votre agenda, ou désactivez-le avant.

articles.title: CloudBackend grabs €6.6M to turn AI-generated prototypes into productive business applications - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
CloudBackend grabs €6.6M to turn AI-generated prototypes into productive business applications
Just about anyone can knock up a working prototype application these days using artificial intelligence coding tools, but what happens when they want to turn that app into a viable business?
That’s the question that Swedish AI infrastructure startup CloudBackend AB thinks it can answer after raising €6.6 million ($7.25 million) in seed funding today. Leading the round was the family office of Carl-Henric Svanberg, formerly chairman of the Swedish government’s AI Commission, with participation from M2 Asset Management.
CloudBackend says it’s targeting the parts of application development that can’t be whipped up in seconds by generative AI tools. While vibe coding platforms such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex can deliver a working application, they can’t go the whole hog and turn it into a revenue-generating product.
The problem is that although vibe coding tools are great at generating application logic and user interfaces, they don’t know much about building the backend infrastructure. There’s a lot to do, because applications can’t just function – they also need robust security in place, the ability to scale up to thousands of users, they need to provide customer support, and they must work reliably in every situation. There’s also the question of how to monetize the app, getting insights from users, pricing considerations and marketing operations.
All of this is what CloudBackend’s Operations Platform is designed to handle, founder and Chief Executive Daniel Arthursson (pictured) told SiliconANGLE. It provides all of the backend infrastructure needed to turn any AI-generated prototype into a viable and profitable business within a single, accessible environment. “AI has made it much easier to build the first version of an application, but the challenge comes when customers sign in and expect the service to be secure, reliable and available every day,” he said.
Arthursson said the Operations Platform has five key components, including the extremely flexible Singularity Database that unifies relational data, object storage, caching and user files within a single platform. It offers robust identity and access controls integrated at the data layer, so users don’t have to stitch together multiple services to secure their application data.
Another key component of CloudBackend’s platform is “Build,” which allows skilled developers to create application frontends using declarative XML or native software development kits and then bind them to live data and deploy them in cloud environments without a continuous integration and deployment pipeline. Then there’s “Run,” which provides built-in tools for user subscriptions, customer relationship management and support, and revenue tracking within a single interface.
CloudBackend also offers collaboration tools that allow apps to keep their user’s data in perfect synchronization so multiple users can work together on projects. Finally, there’s a data sovereignty component that’s aimed at European organizations that must ensure all customer data is stored in Europe.
“We’re building the AI cloud infrastructure that helps creators make the leap from prototype to production without extensive technical knowledge,” Arthursson said. “It’s a new type of infrastructure designed for applications built with AI.”
CloudBackend’s infrastructure has been up and running with early access users so far, and with today’s funding round under its belt, it’s now planning to open it up to more users, with a free developer beta slated to open Nov. 24. The money from today’s round will also help CloudBackend to build deeper integrations with select vibe coding tools and large language models, Arthursson said.
The long-term vision, according to Arthursson, is to make the backend infrastructure and business operations as simple as the generative AI coding process has become.
Hans Lindroth, CEO of the Svanberg Family Office, said there will be lot of demand for what CloudBackend is offering, because it makes generative AI coding tools much more attractive when anyone can use them to start a business.
“AI makes it easier to build applications, but turning them into production-grade solutions for businesses is a different challenge,” he said. “We see a growing need for infrastructure that helps businesses to operate securely, serve customers reliably and expand their offerings. Daniel and his team have the experience and expertise to address that need and that’s why we chose to lead this round.”

articles.title: Test Sony 85 Bravia 7 II : l'alternative Mini-Led RGB abordable face au très haut de gamme
articles.text:
| Qualité d'image |  | 
| Diagonale d'écran | 85 pouces (214 cm) | 
| Définition | 3840 x 2160 (4K) | 
| Technologie de rétroéclairage | Mini LED | 
| Formats HDR supportés | HDR10, Dolby Vision, HLG | 
| Jeux vidéo |  | 
| Fréquence de la dalle | 120 Hz | 
| Ergonomie |  | 
| Dimensions (L x H x P) | 189.5 x 115.9 x 44.1 cm | 
| Poids | 42.1 kg | 
| Connectique | 4 x HDMI, 2 x USB, Vidéocomposite, Ethernet, S/PDIF optique | 
| Ports HDMI 2.1 | 4 | 
| Système d'exploitation | Google TV | 
| Connexion sans-fil | Bluetooth, Wi-Fi | 
| Protocoles sans-fil | AirPlay 2, Chromecast | 
| Assistant vocal intégré | Google Assistant | 
| Réparabilité |  | 
| Indice de réparabilité | 7.6 /10 | 
Avec son rétroéclairage Mini-Led RGB, un design soigné et Google TV, le Sony Bravia 7 II reprend une partie de la recette du Bravia 9 II, à un tarif néanmoins plus accessible.
Le Sony 85 Bravia 7 II est la déclinaison 55 pouces du modèle 65 Bravia 7 II (65 pouces) que nous avons testé. Les deux modèles sont donc identiques et nous vous conseillons de lire notre test complet pour en savoir plus. Vous trouverez un résumé ci-dessous, dont les mesures proviennent de notre exemplaire de 65 pouces.
Le Bravia 7 II associe une dalle LCD VA à un rétroéclairage Mini-Led RGB, avec des noirs profonds et un contraste convaincant. Sur le 65 pouces que nous avons testé, le Delta E SDR de 2,7 masque toutefois des dérives marquées dans les rouges et les bleus. Le HDR est mieux maîtrisé, avec un Delta E de 1,9, un suivi précis de la courbe EOTF et un pic lumineux de 2164 cd/m² sur une fenêtre de 10 %. De quoi donner de l’éclat aux effets lumineux, avec une compatibilité HDR10, HLG et Dolby Vision, mais sans HDR10+. Le bilan est malheureusement terni par un blooming variable selon les scènes et des dégradés mal gérés, qui laissent apparaître du banding. Les reflets sont aussi beaucoup trop présents, avec une réflectance mesurée à 40,7 %, gênante dans les scènes sombres en pièce éclairée. Enfin, les angles de vision restent étroits : mieux vaut s’installer face à l’écran pour préserver les couleurs et la luminosité.
La dalle 4K 120 Hz du Bravia 7 II permet de profiter d’une fréquence élevée, même si certains concurrents atteignent désormais 165 ou 180 Hz. Les mesures réalisées sur le modèle 65 pouces révèlent néanmoins un comportement contrasté. En 1080p à 60 Hz, l’input lag de 10,4 ms est excellent et assure une réponse rapide aux commandes. À 120 Hz, toujours en 1080p, il grimpe malheureusement à 30,9 ms, un résultat décevant. La rémanence de 30 ms constitue une autre limite : les transitions assez lentes de la dalle peuvent produire des traînées derrière les objets en mouvement, loin de la netteté d’un Oled. Le mode Jeu conserve heureusement une colorimétrie satisfaisante, avec un Delta E moyen de 2,7 en SDR et de 2,0 en HDR. Côté connectique, seuls deux des quatre ports HDMI sont en version 2.1, ce qui pourra devenir contraignant pour brancher plusieurs consoles et une barre de son.
Le pied central du Bravia 7 II soigne le design et facilite l’installation sur un meuble étroit, mais sa hauteur n’est pas réglable. Google TV offre un vaste choix d’applications, tandis que les menus Sony et la barre de réglages rapides sont pratiques. My Cinema permet de préparer des profils associant image et son selon ses habitudes. La télécommande est rétroéclairée et rechargeable en USB-C. Deux ports USB, une prise Ethernet et une sortie optique complètent les quatre HDMI, sans prise casque mini-jack. L’audio est une belle réussite, avec une spatialisation convaincante et des graves présents, mais bien maîtrisés. Une barre de son d’entrée de gamme ne paraît donc pas indispensable. Enfin, le 65 pouces s’est montré sobre : 65,5 W sur notre mire à 150 cd/m², soit 56,2 W/m², et 0,151 kWh pour deux heures de film HDR.
Le Sony Bravia 7 II reprend plusieurs des qualités de son grand frère, le Bravia 9 II, dans un téléviseur Mini-Led RGB plus accessible. Sa luminosité et sa colorimétrie en HDR offrent une belle qualité d’image, dont le rendu se rapproche parfois de celui de notre Oled de référence. Le design est également réussi et le système audio constitue une excellente surprise, avec une restitution ample et bien maîtrisée.
Difficile toutefois de faire abstraction de certains défauts à ce niveau de gamme. Les reflets sont beaucoup trop visibles, les rouges et les bleus manquent de justesse en SDR et le traitement des dégradés laisse à désirer. Le blooming, plus ou moins marqué selon les scènes, vient également rappeler les limites de son rétroéclairage.
Proposé désormais autour de 1200 € en 65 pouces, et 2000 € en 85 pouces, le TCL C89L constitue un rival assez costaud sur le terrain du rapport qualité/prix. Il s'avère plus lumineux sur les fenêtres HDR de 2 et 10 %, moins sensible aux reflets et mieux taillé pour le jeu vidéo avec ses quatre ports HDMI 2.1. Aux alentours de 1800 € en 65 pouces et 2800 € en 83 pouces au moment d’écrire ces lignes, les LG C6 et Samsung S92H (Oled) opposent quant à eux un contraste inégalé, l’absence de blooming et une bien meilleure réactivité. Le S92H ajoute même en bonus un excellent filtre antireflet.

articles.title: Disney's Batuu Adventure Buddies are finally here — I've tried the interactive Star Wars Ewok, and I'm impressed
articles.text:
Disney's new Star Wars companions are here for Life Day — I've tried the Ewok, and it's more than a plush toy
The Batuu Adventure Buddies are a team of 3
Well, first and foremost, if you’ve ever wanted an Ewok of your own, Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge is the place to be. Disney is finally making that dream a reality, and while this little furry companion is certainly adorable, there’s much more going on beneath the surface.
Meet the Batuu Adventure Buddies, Disney’s latest interactive Star Wars companions that were created by the Anzellans, from The Mandalorian and The Rise of Skywalker. The interactive Ewok toy debuted at Disneyland in August, and now, fittingly on Life Day, November 17, Grogu and a Huttlet are joining the fray. All three are available for $99 each at Droid Depot in Galaxy’s Edge at Disneyland and Disney’s Hollywood Studios at Walt Disney World.
I’ve spent some time with the Ewok, and calling it a stuffed animal doesn’t quite do it justice. Sure, it’s soft, but with expressive LCD eyes, moving ears and nose, sensors, sounds, and haptic feedback, it’s almost like having a miniature animatronic of your own. There’s a surprising amount of personality packed into this little creature, and while the eyes look a bit odd in photos, they’re much more expressive in person.
The Huttlet is especially adorable, too, and all three have their own unique reactions and personalities. But what makes these Buddies particularly interesting isn’t just what they can do on their own. It’s how they interact with the world around them.
More than just a stuffed animal
At $99 each, these are much more than your typical plush toys. The Ewok’s arms are soft, while its legs have a slightly weighted feel, not unlike a Beanie Baby or Jellycat. The main body is soft to the touch as well, though you can definitely feel the harder structure housing all the technology underneath. It’s still pretty cuddly and, frankly, adorable.
Once you start interacting with it, the personality really comes through. Its ears wiggle, its nose moves, and its LCD eyes blink, move around, and open and close. It also makes plenty of Ewok noises when it’s excited. The haptic feedback is surprisingly strong, too, adding another layer to the experience.
There are also two attachment points, one on each arm. One features an exposed interactive port, while the other is a more traditional attachment point. It lets you connect accessories from optional packs to unlock even more reactions.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You can attach the Ewok’s Battle Horn and hear it chant and blow, with animated eye reactions and movement in the nose and ears. It’s a neat touch that hints at how Disney could eventually expand the experience with more accessories.
Each Buddy has its own personality, too. Triple-tapping the Ewok’s head triggers an Endor dance party, complete with eye animations, Ewokese chanting, and drumming sounds. Nearby Ewoks can even join in if they detect each other. Grogu can show off his Force abilities or let out a belch after being fed, while the Huttlet has a laugh and a triumphant grin.
The real magic happens in the parks
As fun as these companions are on their own, the bigger idea is bringing them into the parks. Each comes with a carrying sling, letting you explore Black Spire Outpost with your Buddy along for the adventure.
The experience starts at Droid Depot, where an activation process brings your new companion to life. It’s a fitting introduction, especially considering how much these have in common with the interactive droids you can already build and purchase at Galaxy’s Edge.
Those droids are part of the fun, too. Bring an Ewok near a compatible Droid Depot droid, and the two can interact. The droid might move its head and chirp, while the Ewok responds with sounds, expressive eyes, wiggling ears, or a moving nose.
It’s a bit like watching a puppy encounter another animal for the first time, except here it’s two interactive devices communicating with one another.
The Buddies can also recognize other companions and respond to interactive elements throughout Galaxy’s Edge, creating unique moments as you explore the land. You could be wandering through Batuu, encounter another guest carrying Grogu or an Ewok, and suddenly the characters are reacting to one another.
That’s what I find so clever about the concept. Rather than simply taking home a souvenir from Galaxy’s Edge, you’re bringing something into the park that can become part of the story itself.
A glimpse at the future of Disney’s immersive experiences
Disneyland has been experimenting with interactive merchandise for some time, from MagicBand+ to clever popcorn buckets, including one inspired by Pixar Pal-A-Round. But the Batuu Adventure Buddies take things a step further, combining physical movement, expressive LCD eyes, sounds, and interactions with other devices and the surrounding environment.
Disney developed these companions in-house, and that integration with the existing experiences at Galaxy’s Edge is a big part of their appeal. There’s plenty of opportunity to build on the concept with more characters, new interactions, and additional surprises throughout Black Spire Outpost.
It’s also part of a larger trend I’ve been seeing from Disney Imagineering. I recently got an early look at Imagineering Labs, including Secrets of the Spire. This new augmented reality Star Wars experience builds on Batuu Bounty Hunters and gives guests another way to explore Galaxy’s Edge. Disney is also experimenting with an AI-powered Enchanted Guide at Disneyland, designed to help guests navigate the park using their phones, earbuds, or even smart glasses.
The Adventure Buddies take a different approach, but the goal feels similar: making these worlds feel more alive and giving guests new ways to become part of the story.
And at $99, they’re a bit more approachable than some of the other interactive Star Wars experiences at Galaxy’s Edge, including building your own lightsaber.
I love seeing Disneyland lead the way with technology that’s fun, immersive, and doesn’t necessarily require staring at a screen. And after spending time with my Ewok, I’m excited to see where Disney takes this idea next and glad to see it's occurring on both coasts. Maybe, one day, the timelines will sync up again as well.
If you’re sold, the Ewok, as well as Grogu and Huttlet Batuu Adventure Buddies, are available at Galaxy’s Edge at Disneyland in Anaheim, California, and Galaxy’s Edge at Hollywood Studios at Disney World in Orlando, Florida, found in the Droid Depot. Of course, these are subject to availability and, in some cases, will require joining a virtual queue to purchase.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return as Nvidia CEO — first statement since resignation follows support from billionaires, investors, and some employees
articles.text:
Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return as Nvidia CEO — first statement since resignation follows support from billionaires, investors, and some employees
Nvidia's board reportedly isn't considering Huang's return.
Jensen Huang, the former CEO of Nvidia who resigned last week amid the fallout from two extramarital affairs, said in his first public statement since abdicating his position that he would be willing to return to the corner office at the company he co-founded.
"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a statement posted on X. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
Huang has seen public support from other tech founders and CEOs, such as SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick. They and some investors and Nvidia employees signed an online petition and have continued to be vocal on social media, namely Musk's X. President Donald Trump also said that he "would not mind" Huang's return.
Huang resigned on Thursday following two scandals: one affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Megaspeed believed by some US Intelligence officials to be a potential Chinese government asset; and another with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care and Huang's direct report.
Despite Huang's apparent willingness to return, Nvidia's board doesn't seem likely to make that move. Reports yesterday claim that the board is more focused on its ongoing investigation into Huang's affairs and a national security inquiry and is not considering Huang's return. The board has also put together its own National Security and Export Control Oversight to provide high-level oversight of Nvidia’s “national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management,” with its National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team reporting directly to the group and to interim CEO Colette Kress.
In his post on X, Huang further apologized, writing that "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation."

articles.title: Amazon casse les prix de ses Fire TV pour le Black Friday : 5 modèles dès 23,99€, jusqu’à -63%
articles.text:
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre, mais Amazon a déjà baissé le prix de ses Fire TV, du stick Full HD au Fire TV Cube. Nous en avons retenu cinq, en commençant par les deux sticks que nous avons testés, en précisant pour chacun ce qui le distingue du reste de la gamme.
Cette sélection s’ouvre sur les deux Fire TV Stick que nous avons testés, le 4K Plus et le 4K Max, avant de passer aux trois modèles que nous n’avons pas eus en main : le Stick HD, le Stick 4K de nouvelle génération et le Fire TV Cube. Elle couvre cinq modèles, du streaming en Full HD au boîtier piloté à la voix, avec des remises de 43 % à 63 % par rapport au prix conseillé affiché par Amazon. La plus forte économie en euros concerne le Fire TV Cube, à 100 €, la plus forte en pourcentage le Fire TV Stick HD, à 63 %.
- Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus à 37,99 € au lieu de 84,99 € (-55 %)
- Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max à 52,99 € au lieu de 114,99 € (-54 %)
- Amazon Fire TV Stick HD à 23,99 € au lieu de 64,99 € (-63 %)
- Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K (nouvelle génération) à 35,99 € au lieu de 74,99 € (-52 %)
- Amazon Fire TV Cube à 129,99 € au lieu de 229,99 € (-43 %)
Fire TV Stick 4K Plus : noté 8/10 par notre rédaction, à 37,99 €
Notre test du Fire TV Stick 4K Plus face au 4K Select lui a attribué 8/10. Il prend en charge le Dolby Vision, le HDR10+ et le Dolby Atmos, passe au Wi-Fi 6 et embarque 2 Go de RAM, contre 1 Go pour le 4K Select. Nous l’avons jugé le modèle le plus équilibré de la gamme.
✅ Points forts
- Une image plus fine : le Dolby Vision, en plus du HDR10+, ajuste le rendu scène par scène sur un téléviseur ou un vidéoprojecteur compatible.
- Une interface stable : avec 2 Go de RAM, la navigation entre applications reste plus constante que sur le 4K Select, selon notre test.
- À savoir : il se contente de 8 Go de stockage, dont 4,6 Go libres lors de notre test, et son interface met très en avant les contenus Amazon. Le 4K Max, présenté juste après, en offre 16 Go.
Fire TV Stick 4K Max : 16 Go de stockage et noté 8/10, à 52,99 €
Notre fiche du Fire TV Stick 4K Max affiche une note de 8/10. Le stick embarque 2 Go de RAM et 16 Go de stockage, le double des 8 Go du 4K Plus, et prend en charge le Wi-Fi 6E tribande, le Dolby Vision, le HDR10+ et le Dolby Atmos.
✅ Points forts
- Du stockage en réserve : 16 Go, contre 8 Go sur le 4K Plus, pour installer davantage d’applications et de jeux.
- Un écran d’accueil artistique : la fonction Écran dynamique affiche plus de 2 000 photographies ou œuvres d’art, selon Amazon.
- À savoir : à 52,99 €, il coûte 15 € de plus que le 4K Plus (37,99 €), qui prend déjà en charge le Dolby Vision et le Dolby Atmos. Notre fiche relève aussi la mise en avant très présente des services Amazon.
Fire TV Stick HD : la plus forte remise de la sélection, -63 %, à 23,99 €
Le Fire TV Stick HD est le modèle d’entrée de gamme d’Amazon : il diffuse en Full HD, prend en charge le Wi-Fi 6 et se branche au port HDMI du téléviseur, qui l’alimente via le câble USB-C fourni. Il propose la nouvelle interface Fire TV de 2026 et une télécommande vocale Alexa dotée de boutons marche/arrêt et volume. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un ticket d’entrée minimal : 23,99 € au lieu de 64,99 €, soit 41 € d’économie, pour accéder à Prime Video, Netflix, YouTube, Disney+ ou Canal+.
- Aucune prise secteur : le téléviseur alimente le stick via le câble USB-C fourni, sans adaptateur.
- À savoir : la définition s’arrête à la Full HD. Sur un téléviseur 4K, mieux vaut regarder les modèles 4K de cette sélection.
Fire TV Stick 4K : la 4K et le Wi-Fi 6, avec 39 € de remise, à 35,99 €
Le Fire TV Stick 4K de nouvelle génération diffuse en 4K avec prise en charge du HDR10+ et du Wi-Fi 6. Il arrive avec la nouvelle télécommande Fire TV, qui pilote l’alimentation et le volume du téléviseur, et donne accès à Alexa+ pour la recherche vocale. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- La 4K à petit prix : 35,99 € au lieu de 74,99 €, soit 39 € d’économie.
- Une télécommande plus complète : elle ajoute un anneau de navigation et des boutons dédiés à la TV en direct et au panneau de raccourcis.
- À savoir : la fiche Amazon ne cite que le HDR10+. Le Dolby Vision et le Dolby Atmos du 4K Plus, testé plus haut, ne coûtent que 2 € de plus.
Fire TV Cube : 100 € de remise et commande vocale mains libres, à 129,99 €
Le Fire TV Cube se présente en boîtier plutôt qu’en stick. Amazon y loge un processeur octocœur, deux fois plus puissant selon la marque que celui du 4K Max, le Wi-Fi 6E, la 4K avec Dolby Vision, HDR et Dolby Atmos, ainsi qu’un micro et des haut-parleurs pour commander la TV à la voix. Il permet aussi de brancher une box, une console de jeu ou une webcam. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Les mains libres : micro et haut-parleurs intégrés pour piloter la TV, la barre de son et les récepteurs compatibles à la voix, même depuis l’autre bout de la pièce.
- Un processeur octocœur : Amazon annonce un démarrage ultra-rapide des applications et une puissance deux fois supérieure à celle du 4K Max.
- À savoir : à 129,99 €, il coûte plus de trois fois le prix du 4K Plus. Si vous ne comptez ni commander l’installation à la voix ni brancher d’autres appareils, un stick de cette sélection suffit.
Black Friday 2026 : que faire avec ces Fire TV avant le 27 novembre ?
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre, et le Cyber Monday le lundi 30. Quatre des cinq modèles de cette sélection affichent déjà la mention « Offre Pré-Black Friday » sur leur fiche Amazon, avec des prix relevés le 17 novembre. Ils peuvent évoluer d’ici là, à la baisse comme à la hausse, car Amazon ajuste ses tarifs d’un jour à l’autre. Les Fire TV Stick reviennent par ailleurs régulièrement en promotion lors des temps forts de l’enseigne, comme nous l’avons constaté lors de précédents Black Friday et Prime Day. Pour suivre l’ensemble des offres retenues par la rédaction, consultez notre page Black Friday.
Quel Fire TV choisir selon votre télévision et vos usages ?
Commencez par la définition de votre téléviseur : sur un modèle Full HD, le Stick HD suffit, alors qu’un téléviseur 4K justifie un stick 4K. Le Dolby Vision et le Dolby Atmos comptent si votre téléviseur ou votre barre de son les gèrent : le 4K Plus et le 4K Max les prennent en charge, alors que la fiche Amazon du Stick 4K de nouvelle génération ne cite que le HDR10+. Le stockage joue aussi, puisque le 4K Plus n’offre que 8 Go, dont 4,6 Go libres lors de notre test, contre 16 Go pour le 4K Max. Le Fire TV Cube s’adresse enfin à ceux qui veulent commander leur installation à la voix, sans toucher la télécommande, ou brancher d’autres appareils.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Apple limitará el acceso de los agentes de IA al sistema de cualquier Mac en el mundo
articles.text:
Apple incorporó nuevos controles de privacidad en la segunda versión beta de macOS 27.3, con cambios en los permisos que permiten a las aplicaciones acceder a archivos y controlar otras apps. La medida cobra relevancia ante el crecimiento de los agentes de inteligencia artificial, que pueden realizar tareas en una Mac y requieren permisos amplios para interactuar con el sistema.
La actualización no impide instalar ni usar agentes de IA. En cambio, modifica la forma en que las aplicaciones solicitan acceso y permite limitarlo a los elementos necesarios. Los usuarios podrán elegir qué aplicaciones pueden controlar otros programas y qué carpetas pueden consultar aquellas que soliciten acceso completo al disco.
Apple también permitirá configurar ciertas aplicaciones para que pidan autorización cada vez que necesiten acceder a un recurso. De ese modo, el usuario podrá aprobar o rechazar cada solicitud, en lugar de conceder un permiso permanente. La opción podría reducir el acceso innecesario a información personal, aunque implique más avisos durante el uso.
Nuevos controles para archivos y aplicaciones
Uno de los cambios principales separa el permiso que antes reunía el control de dispositivos y el acceso a datos en dos opciones: “System & App Protection Override” y “Accessibility”. La primera permite que una aplicación controle otras apps o anule algunas protecciones del sistema. La segunda está destinada a tecnologías de accesibilidad, como las herramientas que ayudan a personas con discapacidad a utilizar la computadora.
macOS también incorporará una forma unificada para conceder permisos: el usuario elegirá la aplicación solicitante desde una lista. Además, el sistema ofrecerá información más clara sobre los datos a los que podría acceder un programa si recibe autorización amplia. Apple recomienda conceder acceso solo a las aplicaciones y carpetas que sean necesarias para cada tarea.
Cuando una aplicación utilice “System & App Protection Override” para controlar otro programa, aparecerá un indicador de transparencia. Esta señal busca hacer más visible cuándo un software está interactuando con otras aplicaciones. En el caso del permiso “Full Disk Access”, el usuario podrá limitar el acceso a carpetas específicas, en vez de habilitar todo el contenido del disco.
La compañía advirtió a los desarrolladores que sus aplicaciones deben funcionar incluso cuando tengan acceso limitado. Algunas herramientas, como las destinadas a copias de seguridad o tecnologías de asistencia, podrán solicitar permisos especiales para conservar su funcionamiento en nuevas instalaciones. Apple señaló que dará más detalles sobre ese proceso próximamente.
El riesgo de dar acceso amplio a la IA
Los agentes de IA se diferencian de los chatbots que solo responden preguntas: pueden realizar acciones en nombre del usuario, como consultar información, interactuar con aplicaciones o ejecutar tareas en segundo plano. Para hacerlo, algunos necesitan leer archivos, mensajes o datos de otras herramientas. Si reciben permisos demasiado amplios, podrían exponer información privada o actuar de una manera que el usuario no esperaba.
Apple advirtió que otorgar acceso completo a una aplicación puede poner en riesgo los datos almacenados en la Mac. En octubre, la empresa ya había anunciado que reforzaría los controles de “Full Disk Access”, una función que permite a determinados programas acceder a información protegida para operar, por ejemplo, servicios de respaldo.
La discusión sobre estos permisos se intensificó con la llegada de asistentes capaces de actuar en los equipos. Un reporte de Associated Press describió preocupaciones sobre aplicaciones de IA que interactúan con mensajes, correos y otros datos personales. El acceso puede involucrar información de terceros que aparece en esas conversaciones, aunque esas personas no hayan autorizado directamente al agente.
Apple indicó que las nuevas opciones aparecen al aprobar solicitudes de permisos de aplicaciones. Las autorizaciones que los usuarios ya habían concedido seguirán vigentes después de la actualización. Por eso, el cambio no revoca automáticamente los accesos existentes: los controles más detallados se aplicarán cuando se soliciten nuevos permisos.
La beta 2 de macOS 27.3 está dirigida a desarrolladores. Apple no precisó en el anuncio cuándo estará disponible la versión final para todos los usuarios. Mientras tanto, la actualización anticipa un mayor control sobre cómo los programas —incluidos los agentes de IA— acceden a archivos y aplicaciones en las computadoras Mac.

articles.title: Como desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok
Se você desbloquear alguém no TikTok, a pessoa voltará a ter acesso ao seu perfil, enviar mensagens e interagir com seus vídeos
Se você mudou de ideia e quer desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok, o processo pode ser feito pelo aplicativo no celular ou pela versão web. No app, basta acessar as configurações de privacidade para gerenciar as contas restritas, enquanto no PC é preciso localizar o perfil desejado para desfazer a restrição.
Após o desbloqueio no TikTok, o usuário recupera o acesso ao seu perfil, podendo visualizar seus vídeos e interagir novamente nas publicações abertas ao público. Vale lembrar que a plataforma não restabelece o vínculo de seguidores automaticamente, exigindo que ambos voltem a se seguir para retomar o contato antigo.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te explica como desbloquear alguém no TikTok pelo celular e pelo PC.
Você consegue desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok pelo aplicativo, acessando a lista de restrições nas configurações da conta. Veja o passo a passo no celular Android ou iPhone.
Abra o aplicativo do TikTok no seu smartphone e toque em “Perfil”, no canto inferior direito da tela.
Toque no botão de três riscos, no canto superior direito, e selecione a opção “Configurações e privacidade”.
Navegue até a seção “Visibilidade” e toque na opção “Contas bloqueadas”.
Encontre o usuário restrito na lista e toque no botão “Desbloquear”. Assim, ele poderá voltar a ver seu perfil nas buscas e seus vídeos publicados no TikTok.
Você pode desbloquear alguém no TikTok pelo PC acessando diretamente o perfil do contato restrito. Para isso, siga os seguintes passos:
Ao desbloquear alguém no TikTok, você remove imediatamente as restrições impostas anteriormente, mas a plataforma não restaura automaticamente o vínculo entre os perfis. Veja o que muda após essa ação:
Não, o usuário não volta a seguir você automaticamente após o desbloqueio. Como a ação de bloquear alguém no TikTok rompe o vínculo entre os perfis na base de dados da rede, é preciso clicar em “Seguir” novamente para restabelecer o contato.
Se o seu perfil no TikTok estiver configurado como uma conta privada, o usuário desbloqueado precisará enviar uma nova solicitação para acompanhar suas publicações. Nesse caso, o acesso ao seu conteúdo só será liberado após a sua aprovação manual nas notificações.

articles.title: At Ignite 2026, Microsoft reinvents Copilot as the autonomous engine of enterprise work - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
At Ignite 2026, Microsoft reinvents Copilot as the autonomous engine of enterprise work
Business knowledge workers spend their days running a gauntlet of emails, spreadsheets, messaging platforms, meetings and productivity applications, wasting hours of their time switching from one to another to get mundane tasks done.
Microsoft Corp. is now proposing an alternative: It wants Copilot to evolve from a somewhat useful generative artificial intelligence assistant into the autonomous foundation for all business work. At Microsoft Ignite 2026 today in San Francisco, it unveiled a slate of powerful new capabilities and features for its favorite autonomous tool as part of its ongoing effort to transform Copilot into the new workplace operating system.
The company’s new vision was outlined in a blog post by Microsoft Chief Marketing Officer Jared Spataro, who pointed to its comprehensive intelligence layer for work, called WorkIQ, as the critical engine behind this shift.
Spataro explained that enterprise work is notoriously messy. Microsoft 365 stores roughly 19.5 exabytes of customer’s business data, and it’s adding billions of new files, documents, emails and messages each day. For businesses, it’s not enough to just give an autonomous AI agent access to this data and expect it to start making sense of it. It needs WorkIQ, which acts as the centralized reasoning layer for all Copilot agents, retrieving data, understanding its intent, identifying what’s important for the task it has been assigned while ignoring everything else.
While WorkIQ sits under the hood, Spataro says, the average worker’s day will soon begin in “Home,” which is the new user interface for Copilot. Home merges traditional chat with a portal called Cowork, which is where people can start delegating different tasks to AI agents. Spataro said Home is like a grounding anchor, or a place where workers can log in each day to pick up where they left off.
Home’s key element is Auto, which is an intelligent composer that dynamically routes users’ requests and prompts to the most suitable AI model. It’s the place where most people will typically begin each new task.
“Tell Copilot what you want to accomplish and it intelligently routes the work to the right models and effort for the task,” Spataro explained. “For more complex work, Auto may recommend moving from Chat to Cowork. If you agree, Copilot transfers the tasks seamlessly, helping to deliver the outcome with the right level of investment.”
Another key part of Home is called Today. It’s a “proactive command center” that’s currently available in private preview that scans a user’s email, calendar and Teams threads in order to highlight the things they have to get done that day.
Best of all, it won’t leave users feeling overwhelmed, Spataro said, because it also helps them to complete that work. For instance, it can quickly draft replies to emails, propose alterations to someone’s schedule and queue other messages for the user to review.
How Copilot gets work done
Copilot’s ability to get work done has been advanced by its deeper integration with Microsoft’s Office suite. Spataro said the company is bringing the full capabilities of Office directly into the Copilot application.
As a result, users will be able to move effortlessly from ideation on a notepad or whiteboard to conjure up a completed Word document or Excel spreadsheet based on what they just outlined. Those files will live entirely within Copilot, which gains the ability to co-author alongside human colleagues. Because Office is now native to Copilot, every document and file will be secured by Microsoft 365’s strict security and compliance controls, Spataro said.
Human-to-agent collaboration is being boosted too with the arrival of Copilot Workspaces, which is a kind of canvas that both can access, Spataro said. Within Copilot Workspaces, an agent might draft a section of a document, then notify a human to come and review it when they get the chance. The human will be able to leave comments for other agents to address.
Further aiding Copilot in work automation is a new capability called Autopilot, which dramatically enhances what the tool can now do. Autopilot is available now to subscribers who have enrolled in Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program. It’s a fully autonomous and always-on AI agent that comes with its own Microsoft Entra identity, memory and an ecosystem of productivity tools.
Autopilot is very different from standard AI agents that are programmed to wait for a user’s prompts. It’s continuously available, watching various Teams channels and the user’s email inbox for updates. It can automate recurring work processes, and it can manage entire project pipelines, such as a multistep supplier review, fully autonomously, Spataro said.
Autopilot is powerful, but safeguards are in place. Information technology teams have complete control over what it can and can’t access, and if something goes wrong they can step in and block it from doing anything else at a moment’s notice.
“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail,” Spataro explained. “Powered by WorkIQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions. You decide what work Autopilot takes on and it will always check with you before key actions.”
More apps, more data
Coding continues to be a major focus, and now Microsoft is giving everyday knowledge workers the ability to build software that can help them get their work done even faster. With Copilot Code, launching in a few week’s time, users will be able to generate interactive dashboards, persistent desktop widgets and lightweight business applications from simple, natural language prompts.
All of these Copilot-generated apps will be hosted within Copilot Managed Runtime, which is a new, highly-secure environment that IT teams can monitor to ensure none of them pose a risk to the company’s data.
To reassure organizations that their AI agents are not only secure, but also providing real value, Microsoft has updated the Agent 365 platform to give teams more control and visibility into their AI spending. Agent 365 now comes with a Business Analytics feature that brings a FinOps-style approach to AI budgeting.
Whereas most platforms just track token consumption, it goes further, measuring each agent’s return on investment by looking at the “work completed” and the number of hours it took. According to Spataro, this will give companies a much clearer picture of the benefits of their AI investments.
Finally, there’s a lot going on in terms of business data connectivity. For one thing, Microsoft said, it’s making sure that Dynamics 365, its combined customer relationship management and enterprise resource planning platform, doesn’t live in isolation. With Dynamics 365 in Copilot, its AI agents gain more than 100 prebuilt “skills” that allow them to perform tasks in sales, service and finance.
But Dynamics 365 isn’t for everyone, and Microsoft recognizes that many of its customers prefer to use alternative CRM tools. That’s why it announced a major new partnership with Salesforce Inc. that gives Copilot unprecedented access to the Salesforce platform too.
Their new offering is called Copilotforce, and it’s enabled by two-way “Zero Copy” integrations between Microsoft Fabric and Salesforce Data 360. The idea is that Copilotforce will bring trusted context from Salesforce directly into Copilot and also productivity and collaboration tools like Teams and Office. The new platform has 38 prebuilt skills to help Copilot start automating sales-related tasks, allowing them to retrieve customer data, generate meeting follow-ups and update CRM records based on tasks they’ve just completed.
There’s a lot to digest, but the deluge of updates sends a clear message that AI agents are on the march, expanding their role as they take on much more complex enterprise work.

articles.title: New Battery Law Shuts Down Keychron Orca Echo Shipments In EU
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
New Battery Law Shuts Down Keychron Orca Echo Shipments In EU
Keychron recently announced the upcoming Orca Echo wireless split ergonomic mechanical keyboard, simultaneously launching the device's early bird reservations ahead of the official crowdfunding campaign. Now, just a day before the launch of the aforementioned crowdfunding campaign, Keychron has refunded Orca Echo reservations in the EU, citing concerns about non-compliance with new EU regulations that require user-serviceable batteries in consumer electronics. Keychron sent out emails to reservation holders confirming the withdrawal and refunds (via u/Dosalod on Reddit), part of which reads:
Orca Echo has a built-in battery that is not designed to be removed by users. After reviewing the applicable EU battery requirements, which also apply in Northern Ireland, we're unable to offer shipping to EU countries or Northern Ireland for this version of Orca Echo during this campaign.
The keyboard company adds that "if availability in your region changes in the future, we'll share an update on the official website," suggesting that there may be a potential re-launch for European buyers at a later date. Generally, keyboard brands, like Keychron, use off-the-shelf batteries from OEMs, which already makes the Orca Echo compliant with many of the EU's requirements, however, it would also need to make sure that the battery is easily removable with included tools or easily accessible third-party tools available to consumers. Replaceable batteries would also need to be available for five years after the device's launch, and there would have to be no restrictions on third-party batteries. 
This isn't the first time we've seen the EU's replaceable batteries potentially cause hassles for peripherals companies. Previously, it was revealed that Logitech altered the internals of the G Pro X3 Superstrike in order to comply with the new regulations, which mandate that, with a few exceptions, all consumer electronics with a built-in rechargeable battery will need to have user-replaceable batteries as early as 2027. It's unclear if Keychron plans to update the Orca Echo's design, but TechPowerUp has asked the company for comment and will update this article if any is provided.
Source:
				u/Dosalod on Reddit

articles.title: Vazamento pode ter revelado tela do iPhone comemorativo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Vazamento pode ter revelado tela do iPhone comemorativo
Vídeo atribui vidro curvado nos quatro lados e bordas quase invisíveis ao possível modelo especial de 20 anos.
Um novo vídeo pode ter antecipado parte do visual do iPhone comemorativo de 20 anos — até agora conhecido como iPhone 20 — esperado para 2027. A gravação exibe um vidro frontal com curvatura nas quatro bordas, cantos arredondados e um espaço reservado para a Ilha Dinâmica.
Segundo o leaker Ice Universe, conhecido por vazamentos da cadeia de suprimentos da Apple, o componente seria destinado ao “iPhone 20 Pro” e corrobora com rumores anteriores, que apontam um redesenho na linha com telas praticamente sem bordas.
A intenção da Apple seria criar a impressão de que a tela ocupa quase toda a parte frontal do aparelho. Nesse sentido, a proposta difere um pouco das telas curvas populares em smartphones Android com “tela infinita”. Em modelos como os antigos Samsung Galaxy com tela curva ou a linha Motorola Edge, a curvatura aparece apenas nas laterais.
Outro detalhe visível na peça é a abertura destinada à Ilha Dinâmica. O recorte aparece menor do que nas gerações anteriores, em linha com a redução já adotada pela Apple no iPhone 18 Pro. O modelo contraria rumores mais antigos de que a versão comemorativa chegaria sem nenhum entalhe na parte frontal, colocando sensores e câmera por baixo do display.
A empresa já adotou essa prática, de forma mais limitada, nos lançamentos mais recentes. O iPhone 18 Pro, por exemplo, introduziu o sensor do Face ID debaixo da tela, enquanto o iPhone Duo fez o mesmo com a câmera frontal para FaceTime, na tela interna.
A manutenção da Ilha Dinâmica no dispositivo, que possivelmente marcará o design para os iPhones futuros, coincide com outras previsões. Segundo o MacRumors, a Apple deve manter um recorte menor pelo menos até o ano que vem, e prevê o celular sem elementos visíveis na tela apenas para o fim da década.
Segundo rumores, a Apple deve usar painéis OLED microcurvos fabricados pela Samsung Display, e pode adotar uma tecnologia chamada Color Filter on Encapsulation (COE).
Nesse tipo de painel, a película polarizadora tradicional é removida e o filtro de cor passa a ser aplicado diretamente sobre a camada de encapsulamento do OLED, reduzindo a espessura do conjunto. Sem o polarizador, porém, o projeto incluiria uma camada difusora de luz para evitar diferenças de luminosidade nas extremidades.
A linha de 2027 marca os 20 anos do primeiro iPhone, apresentado em 2007, e a empresa pode repetir o anúncio de um novo conceito assim como fez em 2017, quando lançou o iPhone X.
O modelo, que planejado para ser todo em vidro, estaria sendo testado com painel de até 6,41 polegadas, chegando a 6,96 polegadas num suposto iPhone 20 Pro Max.
A empresa também estuda substituir mecanismos de controle laterais por sensores capacitivos, enquanto a câmera principal pode receber um novo componente HDR capaz de capturar até 20 pontos de alcance dinâmico em um único quadro. O processador, por outro lado, manteria o processo de fabricação de 2 nanômetros.
Tudo isso, claro, são apenas rumores: para 2027, temos confirmados apenas os últimos modelos da linha iPhone 18, com a possibilidade de um novo iPhone Air e novas versões do iPhone Duo.
