articles.title: IKEA, ASOS, Zoom… Plus de 175 sites piratés ont peut-être tenté de voler vos données bancaires
articles.text:
Comme le révèle l’entreprise de cybersécurité Report URI, les sites de 178 entreprises et organisations ont été exposés à un malware ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, entre 5 h 21 du matin et 22 heures environ (heure de Paris). Parmi les sites compromis, nous pouvons notamment citer GitLab, Transavia, Air France-KLM, IKEA, ASOS, HSBC ou encore la plateforme de visioconférence Zoom. Pour être plus précis, ce ne sont pas les sites en eux-mêmes qui ont été compromis, mais un outil externe baptisé Optimizely, qui permet à ces sites de tester plusieurs versions de leurs pages web.
Un malware capable de voler des informations bancaires
Durant environ 15 heures, les sites web compromis ont chargé sans le savoir un malware. Les internautes de passage ont donc été exposés à ce malware durant ce laps de temps. Pour y parvenir, les pirates ont injecté des scripts JavaScript malveillants dans les projets de leurs clients, en passant par la plateforme Optimizely.
Le malware, défini par Report URI comme « un kit multifonctionnel », était capable de récupérer les cookies et les numéros de carte saisis dans les formulaires de paiement du site, mais aussi de remplacer les adresses des portefeuilles de cryptomonnaies par celles de l’attaquant. Il était également capable d’installer des kits d’exploitation sur des iPhone et des iPad non mis à jour. À noter toutefois que le malware n’aurait pas pu avoir accès aux paiements effectués via des modules externes comme Stripe ou Adyen.
La faille aurait été comblée, mais la prudence reste de mise
Optimizely, la plateforme qui a été victime de cette cyberattaque, a confirmé l’incident, tout en assurant que la faille a maintenant été comblée et le code malveillant supprimé. En théorie, visiter les sites mentionnés plus haut ne représente donc aujourd’hui plus de risque.
Si vous avez consulté l’un de ces sites ce 16 novembre, Report URI conseille de surveiller vos relevés de compte et de contacter votre banque immédiatement à la moindre détection de transaction suspecte. Veillez également à mettre votre iPhone ou votre iPad à jour. Précisons au passage que Report URI estime que sa liste de sites compromis est sans doute incomplète, et donc plus importante. Nous avons ici cité les plateformes compromises les plus utilisées en France, les autres sites concernés étant peu visités sous nos latitudes (la chaîne CNN, la plateforme de streaming Peacock, Levi’s Japan, etc.).
Cet épisode nous rappelle qu’il faut faire attention à notre comportement en ligne, même lorsque l’on visite des sites réputés pour être fiables. Un site web peut être très bien sécurisé, mais rester vulnérable à cause d’un outil externe qu’il utilise et qui aurait été compromis.

articles.title: On a enfin trouvé une multiprise qu’on n’a pas envie de cacher derrière le canapé
articles.text:
Des prises disponibles, mais toujours derrière le canapé ou sous le bureau : le problème est familier. Pour le Black Friday, Komult fait baisser de 25 % le prix de ses cubes Ohmie, des multiprises pensées pour remettre les branchements à portée de main sans gâcher la déco.
Une multiprise peut-elle trouver sa place dans la déco ? Les Ohmie de Komult misent sur une forme cubique, un angle coupé et plusieurs coloris pour se faire accepter sur un meuble ou près d’un comptoir. Le bloc reste visible, mais son apparence tranche avec celle d’une traditionnelle barrette blanche.
Avec le code promo BF25CLUBIC, l’Ohmie Wall passe de 39,95 € à 29,96 € et l’Ohmie Floor de 49,95 € à 37,46 € sur le site de la marque. La remise s’applique aux deux modèles.
Les prises Komult sont à −25 % avec le code BF25CLUBIC
Black Friday : le code BF25CLUBIC fait passer l’Ohmie Wall sous les 30 €
Pour le Black Friday, Komult accorde 25 % de remise sur ses deux multiprises Ohmie avec le code BF25CLUBIC, valable sur sa boutique en ligne. L’Ohmie Wall passe ainsi de 39,95 € à 29,96 €, soit près de 10 € d’économie, tandis que l’Ohmie Floor descend de 49,95 € à 37,46 €, ce qui représente 12,49 € de moins sur la facture. En passant par notre lien, le code est directement appliqué au panier.
La livraison est offerte en point relais Colissimo, et Komult annonce une expédition sous 48 heures. À domicile, les frais de port ne deviennent gratuits qu’à partir de 75 € d’achat, un seuil qu’une seule multiprise remisée ne permet pas d’atteindre : il faudra alors compter 4,90 € supplémentaires. La marque propose par ailleurs habituellement un duo Wall + Floor et une remise de 15 % dès trois produits commandés, sans préciser si ces offres se cumulent avec le code Black Friday, le plus simple étant de vérifier le montant final avant de valider la commande.
Deux formats selon l’endroit où vous manquez de prises
L’Ohmie Wall, à brancher directement au mur
L’Ohmie Wall se branche directement sur une prise murale, sans câble ni vis. Elle ajoute trois prises et trois ports USB à l’endroit précis où l’on en manque, dans une entrée, sur le plan de travail de la cuisine ou à côté du canapé, sans faire courir la moindre rallonge au sol. Avec seulement 195 g sur la balance, elle se déplace aussi facilement d’une pièce à l’autre selon les besoins du moment.
C’est la version la plus épurée de la gamme, puisqu’aucun fil ne vient dépasser, et celle qui offre le plus de choix côté finitions, avec neuf coloris allant des teintes unies aux motifs façon bois ou constellation. Il faut en revanche tenir compte de son gabarit : le cube occupe bien plus de place qu’un simple adaptateur, et une prise coincée derrière un meuble plaqué contre le mur ou trop proche d’une autre risque de ne pas lui laisser assez d’espace. Mieux vaut donc vérifier les dégagements avant de l’installer, en gardant à l’esprit qu’elle est réservée aux pièces sèches.
L’Ohmie Floor, avec son câble de deux mètres
L’Ohmie Floor reprend le même cube et la même connectique, mais l’équipe d’un câble de deux mètres. Elle quitte ainsi la plinthe pour venir se poser sur un bureau, une table de chevet ou un meuble TV, au plus près des appareils à alimenter. Avec 443 g, soit plus du double de la version murale, elle bénéficie d’une assise plus stable sur un meuble, ce qui n’est pas superflu quand on y branche et débranche un chargeur plusieurs fois par jour.
Elle dispose surtout d’une fixation magnétique qui ouvre d’autres possibilités de placement. Sur un pied de bureau ou un caisson en acier, il suffit de la plaquer pour qu’elle tienne, et Komult fournit une plaque métallique adhésive pour les surfaces qui ne le sont pas, à coller par exemple sur le côté d’un meuble ou sous un plateau. Une manière pratique de garder les prises à portée de main sans encombrer le dessus du bureau, avec là encore plusieurs coloris pour l’accorder à la pièce.
Les prises Komult Ohmie sont à −25 % avec le code BF25CLUBIC
À ce prix, les Ohmie s’adressent d’abord à ceux qui veulent ajouter des prises et de la recharge USB dans un salon, une chambre ou un bureau, sans exhiber une barrette blanche. Komult annonce jusqu’à 45 W sur un port USB-C utilisé seul : de quoi recharger rapidement un smartphone ou une tablette. Il faudra en revanche adapter ses attentes pour recharger plusieurs appareils à la fois en USB, la puissance tombant alors à 15 W partagés.
Comment profiter des offres du Black Friday ?

Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.

articles.title: Business as usual for Nvidia as it beats expectations in first earnings call after Huang's resignation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Business as usual for Nvidia as it beats expectations in first earnings call after Huang’s resignation
Nvidia Corp. delivered earnings and revenue that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations and offered strong guidance for the current quarter in its first earnings call since the shocking resignation of its iconic co-founder and Chief Executive Jensen Huang.
The results were so impressive that they slammed the brakes on a weeklong slide, as Nvidia’s stock rose more than 4% in late trading today.
The chipmaker reported third-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $2.68 per share, surpassing Wall Street’s target of $2.48 per share by a comfortable margin. Revenue for the period came to $115.84 billion, more than double a year earlier and above the $109.1 billion consensus estimate.
The vast majority of those sales stemmed from Nvidia’s core data center business, which delivered revenue of $107.6 billion, higher than the Street’s $101.87 billion forecast. For the current quarter, Nvidia said it’s expecting its revenue to grow by about 90%, to $130 billion. Though that suggests a slowdown sequentially from the prior quarter, it’s still nicely above Wall Street’s target of $125.1 billion.
Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress (pictured, with Huang in the background) has become a familiar face to analysts on Nvidia’s conference calls, but today she found herself in a very different position. For the first time, she was fielding questions as the company’s interim CEO, which means her responsibilities now go well beyond the numbers. She was joined on the call by Nvidia’s Chairman of the Board Harvey Jones, who insisted that the board has no intention of bringing Huang back as CEO.
Nvidia has been under a cloud all week following the abrupt resignation of Huang, which came days after he admitted to having an affair with a businesswoman who’s alleged to be a Chinese spy. In the days that followed that scandal, which included rumors of a second affair with an Nvidia executive and also a potential third fling with yet another company employee, the chipmaker’s stock had been in a downward spiral. But that trend was finally reversed following the company’s strong guidance today.
One of the central questions investors had going into the call was if Nvidia would scrap its previous forecast for 70% revenue growth in the fiscal year ending January 2028. However, Kress did the opposite and raised the company’s full-year guidance to 75% growth.
In raising the company’s outlook, Kress told analysts on the call that “it’s business as usual at Nvidia,” despite all that has happened. And indeed, throughout much of her commentary, she focused strictly to the numbers that revealed a business still in good health. With regard to the guidance, Kress stressed that this forecast “considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of customer demand and our customers’ access to capital.”
“Our leadership has stood up so strongly over the last week to support both what we are doing here at earnings, but also supporting all of our different employees around the world,” Kress said. “Remember, we have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class, multiyear roadmap. And I think that’s important from a business perspective.”
Kress said Nvidia expects frontier labs such as OpenAI Group PBC, Anthropic Group PBC and others to account for about 15% of its data center revenue this year, in a sign that they’re increasingly standing up their own data center infrastructure rather than renting from cloud providers.
“As frontier models become more capable, adoption and revenue are scaling rapidly, with Anthropic annualized revenue reaching $181 billion at the end of October,” Kress said.
Another big chunk of Nvidia’s revenue comes from so-called neocloud infrastructure providers. Much of the money those customers spend on its chips stems from a complex web of financing, with much of it being traceable back to Nvidia itself. Kress told analysts that the company is continuing to help neoclouds and frontier labs to secure the land, power and data center capacity they need to grow, and that it may be willing to share revenue from neoclouds together with the upfront sales of its products, if they meet certain conditions.
Kress said Nvidia currently has more than $32 billion in total commitments to neoclouds through 2032, but insisted that these take effect only if those customers are able to “secure the funding they need to purchase the data center infrastructure products they require, and if the related compute capacity is deployed and made operational.”
Another closely watched number is Nvidia’s gross margin, which has narrowed in recent quarters as its supply commitments have slowly piled up. Investors will have been pleased to see that Nvidia beat Wall Street’s expectations on that metric, with its nonstandard gross margin ending the quarter at 74.9%, above the forecast of 74%. Its margins still declined compared to the previous quarter, though, blamed on the ramping up of production of its latest generation Rubin graphics processing units.
The results prove that AI demand remains as strong as ever. But the bigger question for the market now is not how long Nvidia can sustain its growth, rather whether or not it can sustain its current level of profitability, Forrester analyst Naveen Chhabra told SiliconANGLE.
“The next battle is not against competitors. Nvidia must navigate export controls, sovereign AI initiatives, supply chain expansion and rising capital intensity, all while trying to protect its industry-leading margins,” Chhabra said. “Nvidia continues to defy gravity with triple-digit growth, software-like margins and a strong outlook despite trade restrictions. The next test is whether it can preserve its economic dominance as geopolitics and AI infrastructure costs rise.”
Despite the after-hours gain, Nvidia’s stock is still down 24% this month, and last Friday it completed its sixth successive weekly decline. That’s the company’s longest losing streak since 2012, and its shares are now trading at their lowest level since July 2025.
The decline began several weeks before news of Huang’s extramarital escapades became public knowledge. The company has also faced rising concerns about a possible slowdown in the artificial intelligence industry and a political shift in Washington D.C. as a result of the Republicans’ stunning losses during the midterm elections earlier this month.
Despite Jones’ insistence that Huang will not be returning to the CEO role, the prospect of his doing so cannot be ruled out. In his first public comments since his ousting, Huang said in a post on X that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
There are plenty of people who would like to see Huang return, including U.S. President Donald Trump and various luminaries from the technology world. Last Thursday, someone created an online petition calling for the reinstatement of Huang, and it has been signed by names including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games Inc. CEO Tim Sweeney.
It could be possible that Huang ends up returning to the company in a different capacity than CEO. Susquehanna analyst Chris Rolland told CNBC that the chipmaker could end up taking him back under a new role, such as a consultant or a strategic adviser.
“I think that helps bridge the gap here, he can give technical and strategic advisory services that I think would be incredibly important to the company,” the analyst said.

articles.title: Massive Kik data breach exposes more than 150 million images — experts say popular messaging app may have leaked incredibly sensitive material
articles.text:
Massive Kik data breach exposes more than 150 million images — experts say popular messaging app may have leaked incredibly sensitive material
Some of the images could be described as containing child sexual abuse material
- Researchers found an exposed database containing more than 150 million Kik profile images, including around 75 million original photos
- Exposed images were publicly accessible online and included content involving minors, prompting reports to child-safety authorities
- Database was secured after disclosure, but questions remain about exposure duration and potential prior access
Kik, a popular American instant messaging app, was leaking profile pictures on the clearweb, putting even children and young adults in harm's way. To make matters worse, some of the images that were leaking were disturbing enough for the researcher who found them to report them to the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children.
Security researcher Jeremiah Fowler disclosed discovering an unencrypted, non-password-protected database available to anyone with a browser and an internet connection - as long as they knew where to look.
This time around, he found a database containing just over 150 million images uploaded between 2021 and 2026. They were marked as thumbnails and originals, meaning that at least half - some 75 million - were unique, large-format images and photos. Fowler later determined they were marked as “profiles” and associated with Kik.
Kik locks it down
Launched in 2010, Kik has historically reported more than 300 million registered accounts, although its current active-user figures have not been publicly disclosed. Google Play lists more than 100 million downloads, and Fowler claims it has more than 120 million registered users and around 15 million active users.
Kik is owned by MediaLab, a US-based company that also owns social networking platform Whisper and other digital media properties.
“The files were hosted in a cloud storage database and could also be viewed in any web browser through the direct hosting URL and a subfolder on the primary Kik domain,” Fowler said.
“The name of the database and the fact that the image resources were also hosted on a Kik-associated subdomain provided strong evidence that the exposed records were associated with the platform.”

The researcher notified Kik of his findings, and the database was quickly locked down. However, the company did not reply to a request for comment, so we don’t know how many people were exposed (75 million original pictures does not necessarily mean 75 million people - there are likely duplicates and fake accounts), for how long the database remained open, who managed it (Kik, MediaLab, or a third party), and if any malicious actors found it before Fowler did (which is always a possibility).
A dark turn
This is all relatively standard news in the world of unintentionally misconfigured databases. The findings took a dark turn when Fowler discovered that in a sample of some 2,000 images, there were 66 profile images appearing to contain child sexual abuse material (CSAM).
Fowler suggests Kik is primarily a platform for teens and young adults: “In 2016, the messaging platform was used by approximately 40% of American teenagers and a recent article published by the American Enterprise Institute stated that 70% of Kik users are in the 13 to 24 age bracket.
“In 2025, Kik's terms of service were updated to state that the app is only for individuals aged 18 and older. In my limited review of the publicly exposed images, I saw numerous images of individuals who appeared to be under the age of 18," the report notes.
While the report does plenty of hedging, saying that a single image is not enough to determine someone’s age, it does state that Fowler reported some of the images to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) and the Connecticut Attorney General’s office.
“In a random selection from the limited sample of files, I saw a large number of profile images containing nudity or adult-themed content,” the researcher stressed.

articles.title: Hacker que vazou GTA 6 usou Fire TV Stick para invadir a Rockstar • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Hacker que vazou GTA 6 usou Fire TV Stick para invadir a Rockstar
Integrante do grupo Lapsus$ confessou ataque de 2022 à Rockstar Games. Sentença será definida em 23 de novembro.
Quatro anos depois, o hacker responsável pelo vazamento de 90 vídeos de Grand Theft Auto 6 em 2022 se declarou culpado pela invasão à Rockstar Games. Arion Kurtaj, de 21 anos, admitiu os crimes perante a Justiça britânica nessa segunda-feira (16/11). Na época, o ataque expôs imagens do jogo ainda em desenvolvimento.
Segundo o Ministério Público britânico (CPS), Kurtaj também confessou invasões aos sistemas da Uber, Revolut e da operadora de telecomunicações BT/EE. O jovem integrava o grupo hacker Lapsus$ e utilizou um dispositivo Amazon Fire TV Stick para realizar parte dos ataques enquanto estava hospedado em um hotel.
O caso ganhou repercussão quando dezenas de gravações de GTA 6 foram publicadas na internet. O Tecnoblog noticiou o vazamento e a tentativa de extorsão à Rockstar, que mais tarde confirmou o acesso não autorizado aos seus sistemas. Em 2026, a empresa voltou a enfrentar um vazamento, mas o responsável ainda não foi identificado.
Kurtaj estava em liberdade sob fiança quando foi transferido para um hotel em setembro de 2022 por razões de segurança. Mesmo após ter equipamentos apreendidos, ele continuou realizando ataques com um celular, a conexão Wi-Fi da televisão do quarto e um Fire TV Stick da Amazon.
O esquema permitiu que Kurtaj continuasse acessando sistemas de empresas, apesar das restrições impostas pela Justiça. Entre os alvos estava a Rockstar Games. Sob o pseudônimo TeaPotUberHacker, o invasor publicou as gravações em um fórum dedicado à franquia. Ele também ameaçou divulgar o código-fonte do jogo caso a desenvolvedora não entrasse em contato.
A invasão foi um dos episódios de maior repercussão associados ao Lapsus$, grupo que também ganhou notoriedade no Brasil. Em 2022, a Polícia Federal também prendeu um suspeito de integrar a organização, investigada por ataques que afetaram o ConecteSUS e outras plataformas.
A situação judicial de Kurtaj passou por mudanças desde o vazamento. Em 2023, ele foi considerado incapaz de participar de um julgamento criminal convencional por questões de saúde.
Na época, a Justiça determinou sua internação por tempo indeterminado em um hospital de custódia. Posteriormente, uma nova avaliação médica considerou Kurtaj apto a responder ao processo. Ele foi transferido para uma prisão em janeiro de 2026, abrindo caminho para o julgamento.
A sentença será definida em 23 de novembro, no Tribunal da Coroa de Woolwich, em Londres, quatro dias depois do lançamento oficial de GTA VI.

Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Arctic Introduces the PX-1 Thermal Putty Pad Series
ARCTIC introduces the PX-1 Series, a new approach to thermal interface materials. Combining a moldable putty-like texture with reliable thermal performance, PX-1 and PX-1 Extreme adapt to uneven surfaces, varying component heights, and complex hardware layouts - offering a flexible alternative to conventional thermal pads. Both products come with a dedicated application kit for easy handling and precise application.
PX-1 - Versatile Cooling for PC Hardware
Designed for versatile use across PC hardware, PX-1 features a soft, clay-like texture that adapts easily to different component heights and uneven surfaces. Its moldable consistency makes application straightforward and allows the material to be shaped and adjusted to fit a wide range of hardware configurations.
- Easy to Apply: Soft, moldable texture can be shaped, trimmed, and adjusted as needed.
- Flexible Fit: Adapts naturally to uneven surfaces and varying component heights.
- Versatile Use: Ideal for GPU VRAM, VRM arrays, MOSFETs, chokes, and other PC components.
- Reliable Cooling: Provides consistent thermal contact without the need for precise pad thickness matching.
PX-1 Extreme - Enhanced Cooling for High-Pressure Applications
For applications with higher cooling demands, PX-1 Extreme combines a firmer, high-density composition with artificial diamond powder. Its more robust consistency provides additional stability while adapting to different component heights and uneven surfaces. Designed for applications requiring increased mounting pressure, PX-1 Extreme enables efficient heat transfer in demanding hardware environments.
- Enhanced Thermal Transfer: Artificial diamond powder supports superior thermal conductivity.
- Stable Composition: Firmer texture provides additional stability during installation.
- Adaptable Application: Moldable material adjusts to uneven surfaces and different component heights.
- For Demanding Applications: Designed for high-pressure applications requiring efficient heat transfer.
Availability
The PX-1 series is now available in the ARCTIC webshop - with a 40% discount. Also available on Amazon, eBay, and from selected partners.

articles.title: AMD touts the advantages of native FP64 for HPC with its MI430X accelerator at SC26 — company says emulated FP64 is a poor fit for many HPC workloads
articles.text:
AMD attacks Nvidia's FP64 emulation at SC26, touts native double-precision on Instinct MI430X — says Ozaki schemes fit less than 10% of HPC workloads and triple memory use and emulated FP64 is a poor fit for many HPC workloads
AMD says Ozaki FP64 emulation is no replacement for the real thing when it's needed.
As Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) opens in Chicago this week, AMD is indirectly needling Nvidia about the lack of native FP64 data type support in its data center GPU products. FP64, or double-precision floating-point math, is widely used in the high-performance scientific computing and simulation fields that are the focus of SC26. For those customers, AMD is trumpeting the value of its latest Instinct MI430X accelerator for customers that still need native FP64, like national laboratories and supercomputing centers.
Over the past few years, Nvidia has reallocated die area on its data center GPUs to favor the lower-precision matrix math that boosts the operations needed for much of modern AI inference. That reallocation only makes business sense, as the total addressable market for AI compute has exploded while the demand for double-precision math in large supercomputing installations has remained flat by comparison.
To make up for the lack of native FP64 support, Nvidia has turned to techniques that allow it to emulate FP64 operations using methods like the Ozaki schemes. But AMD claims this kind of emulation is nowhere close to a replacement for native double-precision processing for a few reasons—hence continued development of specialized products like the MI430X.
For one, AMD notes that Ozaki emulation assumes that the workload in question resembles a dense general matrix multiply (GEMM). In its own application profiling, the company says "less than 10%" of HPC workloads perform dense GEMM operations, so this emulation is a good replacement for native compute. Dense linear algebra is the one common workload for which AMD says Ozaki emulation is a natural fit.
For workloads like sparse iterative linear algebra, stencils and hydrodynamics, high-order finite element analysis, Monte Carlo and particle transport, and classical molecular dynamics, AMD says developers still need strong FP64 vector performance for the best results.
Furthermore, even for workloads that map well onto GEMM operations, AMD says matrix sizes must be large in order to achieve the best performance, and that might also not be a given for every operation. The operands of those matrices also have to be sized well to the hardware, as incorrectly scaled operands can reduce performance. The FP64 vector math capabilities of the MI430X are insensitive to those operand sizing issues.
Beyond those stumbling blocks, AMD also notes that using Ozaki emulation methods can cause the memory footprint of an application to balloon, requiring up to three times more capacity than native FP64 would.
Since HBM capacity is directly tied to GPUs in modern supercomputing installations, fitting a workload to a machine that can only emulate FP64 operations could have cascading effects on the number of GPUs and compute nodes required, causing knock-on challenges for the floor area, power, and cooling required to support the system.
AMD says the high 432GB of HBM4 memory capacity per MI430X node allows its customers to provision fewer GPUs and compute nodes in a system, saving on networking, power, and floor space.
In addition to its FP64 HPC performance, AMD positions an MI430X-powered supercomputer as an AI inference platform for developing workloads that utilize those models as part of the research process. But there are some key differences between those systems and the Helios rack-scale accelerator powered by MI455X GPUs from the same CDNA 5 architectural family.
Each MI430X GPU offers 9.2 PFLOPS of theoretical FP4 compute performance for inference, but that should be understood in the context of the whopping 40.3 PFLOPS of FP4 compute from each AI-focused MI455X accelerator.
Beyond raw performance, the native scale-up domain size of four MI430Xs over AMD’s Infinity Fabric interconnect when coupled with a sixth-generation EPYC host CPU pales in comparison to the domain size of 72 MI455X accelerators in a Helios rack. AMD says this interconnect is optimized more for latency-sensitive operations rather than a massive scale-up domain.
Of course, every customer and user of such a system will have different requirements, and institutional supercomputing installations usually aren’t trying to do double duty as cloud inference providers.
For scientists and engineers whose AI models of choice work well within the 1.72 TB of aggregate HBM4 capacity and 93.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth offered by four MI430X's working together across the 12.3 Tbps of scale-up bandwidth available within such a node, the inference performance of each node is likely more than up to the task of the kinds of AI applications that need to be run alongside double-precision compute workloads.
In any event, the MI430X can already count several supercomputing design wins in its corner. The upcoming Discovery supercomputer at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Alice Recoque installation in France, the LUMI-AI system at Finland’s CSC, and the Herder system in Germany will all take advantage of the native FP64 support offered by the MI430X.
AMD’s continued support for native FP64, even as Nvidia retreats from that capability in its products, will doubtless be a point of pride for its architects and engineers, even as those institutional supercomputers will be dwarfed by both AMD and Nvidia-powered AI inference installations the world over. The company's semi-custom silicon design chops and chiplet experience give it the flexibility needed to tailor products like the MI430X to these specialized markets instead of pursuing a one-size-fits-all approach.
As the Senior Analyst, Graphics at Tom's Hardware, Jeff Kampman covers everything that has to do with graphics cards, gaming performance, and more. From integrated graphics processors to discrete graphics cards to the hyperscale installations powering our AI future, if it's got a GPU in it, Jeff is on it.
- bit_user I'm surprised they didn't focus on energy-efficiency, as well. There's no way that using low-precision tensors to emulate FP64 is as energy-efficient as native FP64 hardware.
That said, the Ozaki approach is pretty clever. When all you have is a hammer, try to make everything look like a nail! It could provide a second life for a lot of AI inferencing hardware, since that's a heck of a lot more common than full-throughput native fp64 support. Reply
- ejolson When buying GPU accelerators I would get ones that can also be used for scientific computing. If AI fails, use the accelerator for science. If AI succeeds, new co-designed AI accelerators will be much more efficient and again you can use the GPU for science.Reply

The last graphics card AMD made with decent fp64 throughput was the Radeon VII, in 2019. Nvidia's was the Titan V, in 2017.

articles.title: Ingeniería y neurociencia: así es la pulsera que nació en el MIT y hoy ayuda a controlar temblores en decenas de pacientes
articles.text:
La Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos (FDA) de Estados Unidos autorizó, a comienzos de 2026, una pulsera de la empresa de neurotecnología Encora Therapeutics para ayudar a adultos con temblor esencial, un trastorno que provoca sacudidas frecuentes en las manos y puede dificultar tareas cotidianas.
Más allá del avance, el dispositivo cuenta con una historia muy particular: fue desarrollado a partir de un proyecto estudiantil del Instituto Tecnológico de Massachusetts (MIT), aplica vibraciones mecánicas en la muñeca para enviar señales al cerebro y reducir los movimientos involuntarios, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
La autorización llegó en febrero, 9 años después de que un hombre con Parkinson de inicio temprano probara un prototipo ante un auditorio lleno en el MIT. Al activar la vibración, pudo dibujar una espiral con una precisión muy superior a la que tenía segundos antes.
En ensayos posteriores, una prueba de uso domiciliario durante 90 días mostró que el 78% de los pacientes informó beneficios. Con base en el conjunto de la evidencia clínica, el dispositivo obtuvo la autorización 510(k) de la FDA, un mecanismo regulatorio que certifica que el aparato es seguro y equivalente en eficacia a otros dispositivos ya aprobados en el mercado.
De un prototipo universitario a una empresa médica
La historia comenzó en 2017, en la asignatura 2.009 del MIT, dedicada a los procesos de ingeniería de productos. Daniel Carballo, Allison Davanzo y Kyle Pina, entonces estudiantes avanzados, formaron parte del equipo que ideó una tecnología portátil para atenuar temblores mediante vibraciones.
Carballo había propuesto un aparato que transmitiera estímulos mecánicos al cerebro para aliviar los síntomas de Parkinson. La iniciativa fue elegida por 16 votos contra uno: el único voto en contra fue el suyo, porque consideraba improbable construir un dispositivo funcional en un solo semestre.
Durante gran parte del curso, el grupo quedó rezagado frente a otros proyectos. La situación cambió una semana antes de la presentación final, cuando conocieron a Michael, un renovador de viviendas cuyos temblores le impedían usar un destornillador, un taladro e incluso completar formularios.
El equipo le acercó su prototipo —una caja de espuma con un chip Raspberry Pi y cables expuestos— para que lo probara. Cuando Michael lo utilizó, sus temblores disminuyeron de manera marcada. “Fue como si se encendiera un interruptor y sus temblores se detuvieran”, compartió Carballo.
Michael repitió la demostración en el auditorio Kresge del MIT. Tras presionar un botón de la pulsera, dijo al público: “Cuando este dispositivo está encendido, siento lo mismo que sentía antes de tener Parkinson. Es una sensación increíble, increíble”.
Las consultas de personas que querían adquirir el dispositivo para familiares con temblores llevaron, aparte del equipo, a continuar el desarrollo fuera del aula. La empresa Encora Therapeutics, fundada por los tres estudiantes, se constituyó formalmente en 2020, después de utilizar recursos de emprendimiento del MIT, entre ellos MIT Sandbox, MIT FUSE y el Servicio de Mentoría para Emprendimientos del instituto.
La ciencia detrás de la pulsera antitemblores
La compañía realizó en 2022 su primer ensayo clínico con 20 pacientes con Parkinson, en colaboración con el sistema de salud MassGeneral Brigham. Luego orientó el desarrollo hacia el temblor esencial, al detectar que más personas viven con esa afección y que existen menos innovaciones terapéuticas que para el Parkinson.
Los científicos consideran que los temblores surgen de señales defectuosas en las regiones cerebrales que interpretan la información sensorial y coordinan el movimiento. En estas enfermedades, las deficiencias de neurotransmisores generan señales pulsadas que se expresan como movimientos motores involuntarios.
Algunas intervenciones actuales buscan modificar esas señales mediante cirugía: se perfora el cráneo para implantar electrodos que introducen nuevos patrones eléctricos en el cerebro. El producto de Encora apunta a las mismas zonas cerebrales sin recurrir a una operación, mediante estímulos mecánicos en la muñeca.
La vibración estira receptores que informan al organismo sobre la posición del cuerpo en el espacio. Esos receptores se activan y envían una señal estructurada a los nervios periféricos de la muñeca, que la trasladan al sistema nervioso central y a las regiones cerebrales vinculadas con el control del movimiento.
En 2024, la empresa realizó un ensayo controlado y aleatorizado con 47 pacientes con temblor esencial. Una evaluación posterior incluyó a 59 personas que utilizaron el dispositivo en sus hogares; en ambas pruebas, más del 70% tuvo una mejora clínicamente relevante.
La mayoría de los pacientes percibe beneficios rápidos, y algunos lo usan entre 12 y 14 horas diarias. Encora busca formar una red nacional de ventas y obtener cobertura de aseguradoras mientras aumenta la producción para los pacientes que cumplan los requisitos.

articles.title: Tesla peut déployer sa conduite autonome en Finlande, mais la France résiste toujours
articles.text:
Tesla franchit une nouvelle étape dans le déploiement de son système de conduite autonome en Europe. Le constructeur américain vient d’obtenir le feu vert de Traficom, l’agence finlandaise des transports et des communications. Il pourra prochainement commercialiser son système Tesla Assisted Driving auprès des propriétaires d’environ 6 500 véhicules compatibles. La Finlande rejoint ainsi les dix autres pays européens ayant reconnu l’homologation provisoire délivrée aux Pays-Bas en avril. Mais la France reste encore à convaincre.
Tesla Assisted Driving : ce qui change pour les automobilistes finlandais
Le FSD (Full Self-Driving) de Tesla change de nom et devient Tesla Assisted Driving. Une évolution réclamée par plusieurs responsables politiques européens, qui jugeaient l’ancienne appellation trompeuse pour un système nécessitant toujours la surveillance du conducteur. « Le changement de nom aide les utilisateurs et le marché à comprendre la vraie nature du système », explique Jukka Juhola, expert principal chez Traficom.
La Finlande autorise son déploiement avant même le vote européen. L’agence justifie sa décision par ce changement de nom, mais aussi par les modifications apportées à la gestion de la vitesse. Jusqu’à présent, le FSD pouvait autoriser un dépassement de 50 % de la limitation. Cette marge est désormais réduite à 10 % et revient à zéro à chaque démarrage du véhicule.
L’arrivée de l’hiver a également pesé dans la décision. Traficom préfère laisser aux propriétaires le temps de découvrir le système avant les premières chutes de neige et l’apparition du verglas. Les caméras peuvent en effet être perturbées par la neige, la neige fondue ou les saletés. L’agence recommande notamment de garder les mains sur le volant face à une plaque de verglas, une flaque de profondeur inconnue ou de fortes rafales de vent.
Car, malgré son nouveau nom, le Tesla Assisted Driving ne rend pas les voitures autonomes. Le conducteur reste responsable de la conduite et doit pouvoir reprendre le contrôle à tout moment, y compris en cas d’excès de vitesse.
La France toujours réticente face au système de Tesla
En France, le constructeur américain est encore loin d’obtenir une autorisation. En juillet dernier, le ministre des Transports, Philippe Tabarot, avait notamment critiqué la possibilité de dépasser jusqu’à 50 % la vitesse autorisée, mais aussi le manque de garanties concernant la vigilance du conducteur lors des changements de voie, aux intersections et dans les ronds-points.
En septembre, une visioconférence avec Elon Musk a toutefois permis d’ouvrir le dialogue. Le gouvernement a depuis autorisé des essais sur route avec deux véhicules Tesla, sans pour autant s’engager sur une reconnaissance de l’homologation néerlandaise.
Tesla encore loin de convaincre l’ensemble de l’Europe
Le dossier doit désormais passer devant le comité technique des véhicules à moteur (TCMV), qui réunit les représentants des 27 États membres. Un vote était initialement attendu le 6 octobre, mais le comité ne devrait finalement pas se réunir à nouveau avant décembre.
Pour obtenir une reconnaissance européenne, Tesla doit réunir au moins 15 États représentant 65 % de la population de l’Union. Malgré onze pays favorables, le constructeur ne rassemble pour l’instant qu’environ 70 millions d’habitants sur 450 millions, soit un peu plus de 15 %.
L’Allemagne pourrait apporter son soutien après avoir obtenu les modifications réclamées à Tesla. Mais même avec Berlin, les pays favorables ne représenteraient qu’environ un tiers de la population européenne. Le constructeur devra donc encore convaincre plusieurs grands marchés, dont la France, l’Italie et l’Espagne. La généralisation du Tesla Assisted Driving en Europe n’est donc pas encore pour demain.

articles.title: "13 enganches ilegales cada día": en Málaga han robado 33 millones de kWh de electricidad en diez meses y las plantaciones de marihuana tienen mucho que ver
articles.text:
El fraude eléctrico ya no es lo que era (es decir, un vecino haciendo un puente a una PIA del cuadro de contadores). Ya contamos cómo Endesa usa la IA contra las plantaciones de marihuana y cómo cazó a 16 restaurantes de Barcelona con los vídeos de unos influencers. Y Málaga es el último retrato de esa profesionalización: en los 10 primeros meses de 2026, e-distribución, la filial de redes de Endesa, ha detectado más de 3.900 fraudes en la provincia. 13 al día. La energía asociada suma 33 millones de kWh, el consumo de más de 9.500 hogares. ¿Y quién lo paga?
Una plantación por semana. Entre enero y octubre, e-distribución desmanteló en Málaga, junto a las fuerzas de seguridad, 43 fraudes ligados a plantaciones de marihuana. Suman 4,5 millones de kWh, el 14% de la energía defraudada. Haciendo la cuenta, son el 1% de los casos y cada uno defrauda unos 105.000 kWh, 14 veces más que el resto, que ronda los 7.400.
Endesa calcula que una plantación consume como 80 viviendas: es como si un bloque entero se colgara de un solo enganche. Además, según el Informe Europeo sobre Drogas 2026, España concentró en 2024 el 75% de las plantas de cannabis incautadas en toda la UE.
Fusibles y reconexiones. Málaga vive un momento tensionado: a un lado de la ladera, los nómadas digitales desequilibrando la economía local. Abajo, en los barrios periféricos, los cultivos de marihuana suponen el 13% de ese consumo. Pero estos robos generan problemas extra: un enganche sobrecarga la red y saltan las protecciones ante averías (no para consumo diario).
En las peores zonas se funden hasta 15 fusibles al día y se corta la luz a todos los clientes del tramo, casi todos con contrato. Subir la potencia no arregla nada: en algunos sitios ya multiplica por 5 la necesaria y el consumo ilegal vuelve a saturarla. A cada desconexión, una reconexión, a menudo de varias horas.
Cómo los detectan. Contadores inteligentes y sensores de la red generan datos, y modelos de machine learning y deep learning buscan consumos anómalos. Esa IA encuentra robo en una de cada dos inspecciones, el doble que en 2017. Los avisos ciudadanos completan el cuadro: entre enero y septiembre, e-distribución recibió 51.010 en toda España y de ahí salieron cerca de 29.000 inspecciones. Desde 2025 trabaja además con la Policía Nacional bajo un protocolo de colaboración.
La Palma-Palmilla. El caso más visible es este barrio. Endesa intervino allí el 30 de junio y el 7 y el 15 de julio, con la Policía, y el 78% de lo inspeccionado resultó fraude. Después, terceros manipularon la red para reconectar, y una decena de casas de la calle Doctor Gálvez Moll pasó casi 3 días sin luz. Una vecina contó que su abuela, de casi 90 años, depende de una máquina de oxígeno. FACUA y Con Málaga denuncian que las operaciones criminalizan a una barriada entera. Endesa responde que el riesgo de electrocución y de incendio justifica actuar.
Qué dice el Código Penal. El artículo 255 castiga con multa de 3 a 12 meses defraudar fluido eléctrico. Si no pasa de 400 euros, la multa baja a entre 1 y 3 meses. La Ley Orgánica 1/2026 cambió el panorama para las plantaciones. Desde el 10 de abril, un nuevo 255.3 impone prisión de 6 a 18 meses o multa de 12 a 24 meses al enganche que abastece instalaciones del artículo 368, sea cual sea la cuantía.
Por cierto, la nueva ley no es retroactiva: los hechos anteriores se juzgan con la ley vieja. El cultivo en sí ya era delito, con 1 a 3 años de cárcel para el cannabis, y más si la cantidad es notoria (no como la del chico vasco que solo tenía para consumo propio).
La vía eléctrica. Al margen del juzgado, la distribuidora tiene sus armas. El artículo 52.6 de la Ley 24/2013 del Sector Eléctrico y el artículo 87 del Real Decreto 1955/2000 le permiten suspender el suministro de forma inmediata ante un enganche sin contrato. También facturar: sin criterio objetivo, cobra la potencia por 6 horas diarias durante un año. El artículo 90 resuelve el contrato de forma automática. El Defensor del Pueblo critica que la compañía fije por su cuenta la cantidad y el corte, sin audiencia al interesado.
Un vacío, según Endesa. Fuera de las plantaciones, el resto de fraudes solo acarrea multa. En Francia, Portugal, Italia o Alemania, recuerda la compañía, puede conllevar prisión incluso en su modalidad básica. Ya criticaba la Fiscalía General, en su memoria de 2025, que el delito se quede en multa. Aunque las consecuencias operan en todas direcciones: las agresiones a técnicos de e-distribución y de sus contratas se multiplicaron por más de 3 desde 2024. Aunque son meros trabajadores, este año ya superan en cerca de un 20% las de todo 2025.

articles.title: GPUs alone won't carry enterprise AI pilots into production - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Token sticker shock pushes enterprises from frontier labs toward open-weight AI factories
Enterprises have spent the AI boom racing to secure graphics processing units, or GPUs, but the harder decisions now sit above the hardware. Token bills, data sovereignty and model choice increasingly decide which AI pilots reach production, a shift on display at the SC26 supercomputing conference.
Dell Technologies Inc. has spent the past year pushing its AI Factory beyond servers and storage. Customers now want a full-stack outcome that covers software, open-source tools, models and operations, according to Brad Maltz (pictured), senior director of AI solutions at Dell.
“The hardware’s key because that drives the tokens,” he said. “You really, truly need a full-stack AI factory view above and beyond just the hardware stack.”
Maltz spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how token bills and data sovereignty are steering enterprises toward open-weight models and a full-stack AI Factory. The interview came as Dell rolled out AI Factory updates at the conference. (* Disclosure below.)
Why GPUs alone won’t carry AI pilots into production
Many enterprises are still stuck in pilot mode, and coding assistants are often the easiest place to start. Employees have already tried tools from Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC, so teams want to apply that experience to business use cases. Once those pilots grow, the bill arrives, Maltz explained.
“The token spend right now in the frontier labs and the hyperscalers — that’s a little more than we expected,” he said. “We didn’t expect to spend $10,000, $20,000 per person per month.”
Cost is only one trigger. Data sovereignty, intellectual property leakage, security and governance all have to be addressed before a pilot goes live. Those requirements are steering many enterprises toward open-weight models they can fine-tune and run on-premises, including U.S. options such as Nvidia Corp.’s Nemotron, according to Maltz.
“There will always be frontier labs. There will always be open-weight models,” he said. “The question is going to be: do we have enough diversity with the open weights to meet the enterprise use cases?”
To keep pace, Dell launched its AI Ecosystem Program to validate software partners on its AI Factory. About 60 more partners have applied or are under evaluation, and each addition lets Dell solve 10 to 30 more customer problems, Maltz noted. For sovereign deployments, that often means disconnected, on-premises systems that keep models next to the GPUs and data enterprises already control.
“People understand data is the lifeblood of AI,” he said. “It’s the thing that trains the models. It’s the thing the models operate against. It comes from your enterprise business applications.”

articles.title: I test hi-fi kit for a living and I've just found the best cheap turntable system for Black Friday (and you don't need McCartney's millions to buy it)
articles.text:
I'm an audio editor and this is the only turntable system I'm recommending this Black Friday
Plus discounted extras to get your full vinyl system singing
Several friends (and a few relatives) have messaged me over the past two weeks asking whether Black Friday is this weekend and whether they can recommend a turntable for under £400.
As it happens, that's all part of my job. No, it's not officially Black Friday yet — but yes, because the deals over this side of the pond are dropping like flies, I can.
Top of the pile for me is Sony's PS-LX5BT, now £291 (was £399) in a never-before-seen 27% off saving. Why has it never seen a discount like this? Because it's a January 2026-release deck. It also has Bluetooth, it's from a trusted name in affordable turntables (the follow-up to the excellent PS-LX310BT, which launched in 2019), and I called it "a winner eight days a week" in an in-depth 4.5-star review.
And I'd pair it with the Edifier MR5 active speakers, which were £279.99 and are now just £189.99, both on Amazon. The amplification's onboard, so you could stick with wired playback or use Bluetooth if you prefer. Simple. Done.
Want something with built-in speakers so you can plug in and play vinyl straight away? I've got you too, friend. I also love the Majority Folio. It comes with speakers in the base, an Audio-Technica cartridge, the option to rip your vinyl to USB and Bluetooth in and out (so essentially, the speakers are Bluetooth speakers too, so you could ping music from your phone to those, but you can play your vinyl on standalone Bluetooth speakers too, should you wish). And right now it's just £141 (was £169.95) as long as the ply finish suits — and it's the one we awarded four sweet stars to in a full review, so you can see a lot more of it there if you wish.
• Browse all the best early Black Friday deals at Amazon
My top two Black Friday turntable systems
It had big shoes to fill, this deck — and the good news is, it fills them beautifully. As the upgrade to the very popular 2019 Sony PS-LX310BT (and slightly pricier, slightly better sibling to the PS-LX3BT, which I wouldn't look to when this model is on sale) I was worried it wouldn't be a winner. I'm happy to report I was emphatically wrong. And owing to its January 2026 release, it's never been this cheap 'til now.
What a deal! Our glowing review of these July 2025-issue powered speakers ('powered' just means you don't need to buy a separate amp for them, because the amplification is inbuilt) has the header: 'Edifier's great-value new desktop monitor speakers exceeded all of my expectations', with the strapline 'These nearfield monitors pack in everything but the kitchen sink, and do a decent job of it too'. For this money, I think they also look far more expensive than they are — and wouldn't they look great next to the Sony deck also on sale above (and maybe with addition of the stand I'm suggesting below)…
Oh I love this cheap and cheerful deck with speakers inbuilt, for a full vinyl system. OK, it's not quite as rock solid as something that'll set you back thousands but come on, you know that. If you want a record player that's now well under £150 and will support plug-and-play vinyl for those new to it, you cannot go wrong here. It arrived in April 2025 and promptly jumped into our very good books, where it remains to this day. Recommended.
I feel like I should clear the whole dates thing up. Officially, Black Friday falls on November 27 and Cyber Monday follows on November 30. This is the date when, historically, products got crazy cheap to clear store shelves before the seasonal influx of Christmas stock (although it has kind of gone the way of fighting in Woolworths for a specific BMX bike or Cabbage Patch Kid, because these days we have a thing called online shopping).
In the US, people know these dates because of Thanksgiving, which is on Thursday November 26th this year, the day before Black Friday. Basically, it's a massive week Stateside before we get into any huge deals events, so everyone's diary is meticulously planned out.
Not so here and my point is, there are tons of discounts live now in the UK, ahead of Black Friday. Basically, retailers here are taking matters into their own hands — or at least going earlier with their Black Friday-branded discounts, to beat the online competition.
Will prices drop yet further as we approach Black Friday proper? I don't think so, not when the deals are already this good — it's just as early Black Friday this year.
Anyway, here are a few further deals I like.
Didn't come here for earbuds or headphones? That's OK. See TechRadar's pick of the best Black Friday deals.
More early Black Friday turntable deals
The AT-LP60XBT makes a top starter turntable for beginners, thanks to its now-incredibly low price, easy setup, and support for wireless playback. It arrived in 2019, so it's a little older, but vinyl does not move at the same dizzying speeds as wireless earbuds, say, so relative maturity is hardly an issue. Our full review gives the whole story (there are no nasty surprises!), but I do love the Audio-Technica badge on the front, because it's the mark of a trusted name in turntables.
This super affordable, good-looking automatic turntable (I love the aluminium look!) is an excellent first and/or fuss-free option with typical Denon sound quality. No built in speakers, but the point is to build a system here — and at this new low price, you can afford to. It has previously dipped to £119, but never this low, which makes it an honest bargain. It also features a moving magnet cartridge, easy setup and operation, plus a built-in phono stage.
Denon's flagship belt-driven turntables are chic, come with built-in phono preamps and feature quality cartridges. This one has dipped a tiny bit lower, to £393 in the past, so perhaps keep an eye on it and click through when you see this — I try to stay on top of prices but sometimes Amazon drops things very quickly during Black Friday proper. And while of course it's the sound that matters most, I always think the distinctive dust cover makes this model particularly striking, too.
The best early Black Friday speakers and vinyl accessory deals
Got the deck, want the speakers — or just need somewhere to put your vinyl? I've had a little look for these things too, and here's my pick of the bunch.
Top of the pile is the aforementioned and excellent Edifier MR5 powered speakers (so you won't need a separate amplifier), which will allow wired playback or wireless via Bluetooth, from say the Sony PS-LX5BT above. And right now they're just £189.99 (was £279.99) — and our 4.5-star glowing review of these speakers is the place to learn more about them.
But I have to say, I find this Costway turntable stand quite the looker too — and the bijou Audiogenie A2+ speakers, which are now just £186 (was £248) and look an awful lot pricier than they now are.
Anyway, have a browse (we've got a bit of time) and above all, enjoy the music!
Way to complete the look, no? Because what your turntable needs is its own dedicated, low resonance stand (don't be putting it on the coffee table where you regularly eat toast and expect smooth playback) and a few cubby holes for vertical vinyl storage. The cardinal sin of vinyl? Stacking them flat. It's not a model I've used but look, it's compact, it's got an open section at the back so you can plug in, it's got four vinyl storage compartments and it's 15% off, which can't be bad.
Another speaker option that'll support wired or wireless playback! They are also powered (so there's already amplification squirrelled away in the casework) and they come in delightfully bright colours including this red, which we reviewed, and a blue option. They're bijou but the sound they can deliver is mighty — and I think they might just suit someone's flat perfectly. Oh, and despite their August 2024 release date, they've rarely seen a discount of any kind until now, so 25% off is worth shouting about.
What a deal — it's so nice, I'm mentioning it twice! Our glowing review of these July 2025-issue powered speakers ('powered' means you don't need to buy a separate amp because the amplification is inbuilt) has the header: 'Edifier's great-value new desktop monitor speakers exceeded all of my expectations'. For this money, I think they also look far more expensive than they are — and wouldn't they look great next to the inexpensive Sony or Audio-Technica decks also on sale above (and maybe with addition of the stand I'm suggesting here too)…

articles.title: PC ou Console ? Xbox a du mal à expliquer ce que sera vraiment Helix
articles.text:
Dans le magazine publié le 15 novembre pour les 25 ans de la marque, Jason Ronald, vice-président chargé de la prochaine génération Xbox, précise enfin la nature de la future machine. « Nous sommes très clairs sur l’objectif de conception : Helix est conçue pour être une console capable aussi de faire tourner les jeux de votre PC. Ce n’est pas un PC qui peut aussi lancer des jeux console. » La formule tranche un débat ouvert depuis des mois, que Valve explore de son côté depuis plus de dix ans, en sens inverse.
Quatre générations de jeux Xbox, plus votre bibliothèque PC
Helix lira les jeux des quatre générations de Xbox, avec la progression et les sauvegardes du joueur disponibles dès le premier allumage. Ronald promet de « supprimer les contraintes arbitraires entre les jeux console et PC ». Côté PC, Microsoft confirme pourtant la capacité sans livrer le mode d’emploi : rien sur la façon dont ces jeux s’installeront, rien sur les boutiques acceptées, et Steam reste le grand absent de l’entretien.
L’interface sera propre à la console, distincte du mode Xbox déployé sur les machines portables sous Windows. Les retours des joueurs sur le ROG Xbox Ally, présenté comme un « précurseur » de Helix, ont déjà remodelé les plans de l’équipe, et les joueurs avancés garderont la main sur les réglages de performances.
Sous le capot, la puce AMD sur mesure annoncée en mars dernier s’accompagnera d’un rendu neuronal censé « offrir un nouveau niveau de fidélité visuelle de manière plus efficace et innovante ». Les premiers kits partiront chez les développeurs en 2027, et la rumeur situe la console en 2028, sans confirmation officielle.
Valve a essuyé les plâtres, deux fois
En 2015, les Steam Machines poursuivaient l’idée en sens inverse : des PC de salon fabriqués par des constructeurs tiers sous SteamOS, vendus comme des consoles. Catalogue de jeux famélique, système inabouti, positionnement illisible pour l’acheteur : Valve a rangé le projet sans bruit en 2018.
La relance de 2026 a corrigé la méthode : machine conçue en interne, écosystème mûri par le Steam Deck et sa couche de compatibilité Proton. Valve assume désormais l’ergonomie d’une console mariée au catalogue du PC. Restait l’étiquette : lancée le 29 juin dernier, la nouvelle Steam Machine dépasse les 1 000 euros, entre flambée des composants et refus de la vente à perte.
Microsoft avance vers le même mur. Ronald décrit la crise des composants comme « un moteur principal » de la conception de Helix et promet une machine accessible, quand les estimations qui circulent placent la facture au-delà de 1 500 euros.

articles.text:
Lidl ya ha colgado en su web y app su nuevo folleto dedicado al Black Friday para la semana que viene y, la verdad, es que hay multitud de dispositivos que merecen la pena. Uno de ellos es este calientapiés Vitalcontrol, ideado para los más frioleros y que llegará a sus tiendas físicas y online, el próximo lunes 23 de noviembre por 21,99 euros.
Si no quieres esperar a que llegue a Lidl, en Amazon hemos encontrado también un producto de este tipo y a buen precio. Este de la marca Alpina es el más vendido en estos momentos y ofrece tres niveles de calor y su funda es lavable. Su precio es de 24,99 euros.
alpina Calentador de Pies Eléctrico
Calor rápido, consumo mínimo y seis niveles de temperatura
Este calientapiés Vitalcontrol de Lidl está diseñado para ofrecer confort térmico localizado de forma inmediata sin necesidad de encender la calefacción de toda la vivienda. Con una potencia de 100 W, alcanza rápidamente la temperatura deseada con un gasto energético muy reducido.
Es un aliado ideal para poner debajo del escritorio mientras teletrabajas o a los pies del sofá por la noche mientras estás viendo la televisión, para tener los pies calientes sin tener que invertir mucho dinero.
Su diseño tipo bota envolvente con interior mullido permite introducir los pies con holgura (incluso si tienes un número de pie grande -hasta el 47-) y disfrutar de un tacto suave y agradable. Además, ofrece seis niveles de temperatura regulables a través de su mando integrado.
Otra de sus funciones destacadas es la desconexión automática de seguridad. Tras aproximadamente 90 minutos de uso continuo, el sistema se apaga automáticamente, evitando sobrecalentamientos y aportando total tranquilidad si te quedas dormido en el sofá, por ejemplo.

articles.title: Shure Launches MV360 and Previews MV360+ Spatial Audio Microphones
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Shure Launches MV360 and Previews MV360+ Spatial Audio Microphones
Shure today announced the MV360 Spatial Audio Microphone, a $349 USB-C microphone that makes immersive audio capture accessible to creators at every level. Available now, MV360 offers 360° spatial audio capture and four additional ready-to-use Capture Modes: immersive binaural, stereo, mono, and auto tracking.
The MV360 helps creators capture more than sound. It captures a sense of place. Listeners can feel closer to a podcast conversation, more immersed in an ASMR scene, or transported into the middle of a bustling market or quiet forest. Housed in a compact, all-metal design built to go wherever creativity leads, the MV360 combines versatile recording modes with professional-grade spatial audio capture, helping creators deliver a more engaging listening experience without adding complexity to their workflow.Creators can set their preferences in the free Shure MOTIV apps, then record any of MV360's Capture Modes directly to USB-C mobile devices, computers, and compatible third-party apps without reopening MOTIV. For 360° spatial audio capture, users can record directly in MOTIV apps or a DAW of their choice, providing full control in post-production for advanced applications such as VR.
Eduardo Valdes, Associate Vice President of Global Marketing and Product Management at Shure"Sound can make the difference between watching a moment and feeling part of it. Until now, capturing that sense of presence has required expensive equipment, technical expertise and time that many creators simply don't have. The MV360 changes that. It gives creators an easy way to bring listeners closer to the conversation, the performance or the world around them, while giving experienced professionals the control they need to shape every detail."
Immersive Audio, Simplified
The MV360 captures high-definition audio and connects to a phone, tablet, or computer over USB-C. Once connected, creators can record Capture Modes directly to any device and third-party apps or use the free MOTIV apps to record full 360° spatial audio. 
Capture Modes: - Mono: Capture simple directional mono audio with three selectable polar patterns: cardioid, supercardioid and bidirectional.
- Stereo: Control natural width and separation for music, environments, and everyday recording.
- Immersive Binaural: Unlock true-to-life immersive sound instantly with more spatial cues than stereo - perfectly suited for playback on headphones.
- Auto Tracking: Keep podcasts, interviews, and moving subjects in focus as a virtual microphone steers toward the loudest sound source.
Each Capture Mode records a ready-to-use two-channel file directly to compatible apps and devices, with no post-production required. Behind these workflows, Shure's patented acoustic array captures detailed, full-bandwidth audio in every direction at up to 32-bit float/96 kHz. Creators can fine-tune gain, EQ, compression, limiting, and denoising in the MOTIV apps, then monitor directly through the microphone's 3.5 mm output.
For creators who choose full 360° spatial audio, the MV360 captures the complete sound field in Ambisonic B-format (Ambix), preserving greater flexibility after recording. Using MOTIV Mix, the MOTIV Audio mobile app, or the Shure Virtual Mic Editor plugin within their preferred editing tools, creators can position, steer, and mix virtual microphones, then configure the same recording for mono, stereo, binaural, 5.1, or up to 7.1.4. This supports everything from simple recordings to advanced immersive projects for Atmos, surround sound mixing, virtual reality, game development, and 360° video.Looking Ahead: MV360+, Arriving Early 2027
For field recordists, videographers, and VR storytellers who want to pair immersive audio with mirrorless cameras, DSLRs, action cameras, or 360 camera systems—or use the microphone as a standalone field recorder—the MV360+ adds onboard 32-bit float recording to a microSD card, an internal rechargeable battery, and wireless control from a mobile phone.From up to approximately 100 feet away, creators can start and stop onboard recording and configure the MV360+ from a phone. The wireless connection controls the microphone, while audio records directly to the microphone rather than transmitting wirelessly. Recorded spatial audio can be synchronized with video in post-production. Onboard recording and wireless control also allow the MV360+ to be placed near a sound source and operated from a distance as a standalone plant microphone.
MV360 Pricing & Availability
The Shure MV360 Spatial Audio Microphone Kit is available today for $349 USD, and includes a compact USB-C microphone, tripod, cold shoe mic clip, 5/8" mic clip, phone clamp, two USB-C cables, carrying case and foam windscreen.MV360+ Pricing & Availability
The Shure MV360+ Spatial Audio Microphone, arriving early 2027 for $449 USD, will include the MV360+ microphone, tripod, 5/8" mic clip, cold shoe mic clip, carrying case, USB-C cable, foam windscreen, and 3.5 mm audio cable.
Source:

articles.title: Meta lança Achados, app para comprar e vender itens no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Meta lança Achados, app para comprar e vender itens no Brasil
Aplicativo reúne anúncios do Facebook Marketplace, Grupos e Instagram. Novidade estreia apenas no Android.
A Meta lançou no Brasil, nesta terça-feira (17/11), um novo aplicativo independente para compra e venda de produtos. A plataforma reúne ofertas que circulam pelo Facebook Marketplace e em grupos no Facebook e Instagram.
O aplicativo está disponível para usuários de Android, com 18 anos ou mais que tenham acesso ao Marketplace da Meta, seja entrando com uma conta existente do Facebook ou criando um cadastro pelo próprio Achados.
No Achados, o usuário pode encontrar todos os itens vendidos nos ecommerces da Meta, como roupas, tênis e móveis, incluindo itens anunciados como desapego. Os resultados podem ser filtrados por categoria, preço e distância.
Com o novo app de compra e vendas, a Meta dá mais um sinal de que tenta separar experiências até então integradas às suas redes sociais. Apenas um dia antes do anúncio do Achados, nesta segunda-feira (16/11), a companhia também anunciou o Direct, que leva as DMs do Instagram para um app isolado, funcionando para a rede de fotos e vídeos tal como o Messenger para o Facebook.
O novo aplicativo traz algumas ferramentas para destacar produtos e ajudar na comparação entre ofertas. No topo do feed, por exemplo, a seção Garimpo de hoje reúne uma seleção diária de itens, enquanto outros anúncios aparecem em destaque na busca.
Alguns produtos podem receber o “Selo de achado”, atribuído automaticamente a ofertas que se destacam pelo preço na comparação com anúncios semelhantes encontrados no Facebook Marketplace. O aplicativo também pode mostrar uma faixa de preço estimada em determinados classificados, para que o usuário tenha noção do valor praticado em itens semelhantes antes de negociar.
Quando encontra um produto de interesse, o comprador pode iniciar a conversa pelo próprio Achados ou levar a negociação para o WhatsApp. Da mesma forma, pagamento, entrega ou retirada do item não são intermediados pela plataforma — o usuário e o vendedor ainda precisam combinar os métodos por fora.
Para quem quer vender, o Achados também incorpora a Meta AI ao processo de criação do classificado. A partir de fotos e vídeos do produto, a IA pode analisar o item e sugerir informações para preencher o anúncio.
Entre os campos gerados estão título, descrição, categoria, estado de conservação e preço sugerido, este último calculado com base em anúncios semelhantes. Todas as informações podem ser revisadas e alteradas pelo vendedor.
Um anúncio criado no Achados fica disponível simultaneamente no novo aplicativo e no Facebook Marketplace, sem que o usuário precise cadastrar o mesmo produto novamente.
Assim como no Marketplace do Facebook, o Achados aproveita informações existentes nas outras plataformas da Meta para dar mais contexto sobre o anunciante. Dessa forma, o comprador pode visualizar dados como o ano em que o vendedor entrou no Facebook, histórico de vendas e avaliações recebidas.
Informações do Instagram podem aparecer nesse cartão quando o anunciante optar por vincular e exibir a conta. A Meta afirma que usa sistemas automatizados para identificar e remover possíveis golpes, mas usuários também podem denunciar anúncios e perfis suspeitos pelo aplicativo.

articles.title: Nvidia warns customers of new US rule that could expose them to lawsuits for serving Chinese clients — Commerce Department releases interim regulations preventing ‘foreign actors’ from using advanced compute based on American tech
articles.text:
Nvidia warns customers of new US rule that could expose them to lawsuits for serving Chinese clients — Commerce Department releases interim regulations preventing ‘foreign actors’ from using advanced compute based on American tech
The noose is tightening for Chinese AI labs that need U.S. AI GPUs to train their models.
CNBC reports that Nvidia has started warning its customers that impending legislation to clamp down on countries accessing AI GPUs remotely via data center rentals could put them in trouble with U.S. authorities. Chinese tech companies could take advantage of the performance of American AI hardware through a loophole in U.S. regulations. Instead of importing Nvidia chips, which are under export controls, they instead look to data centers located abroad and export their data instead. This is what Chinese AI lab Moonshot is apparently trying in Europe, which is why the U.S. Department of Commerce, through the Bureau of Industry and Security [PDF], released an interim final rule closing this loophole.
According to the report, Nvidia has been messaging chip buyers to warn that RASA could expose both Nvidia and chip buyers to legal risk.
The U.S. House of Representatives has already passed a bill called the Remote Access Security Act (RASA) that addressed this specific loophole, but it’s been in limbo in the Senate for over ten months now. It remains unclear if the Jensen Huang affair and suspected espionage scandal will help speed up its approval, but scheduling could be tight with only about 31 calendar days remaining before the Senate's adjournment. But even before any of these regulations are approved and published, the company is already taking steps to protect its customers and has started requiring partners that 51% of their services should go to non-Chinese clients. It has also required its partners to join Nvidia’s Fleet Intelligence tracking system if they want to retain their official partner status
It’s unclear if these changes have been planned over time or were a reaction to the renewed scrutiny that Nvidia is facing. But even though Jensen Huang is now out of the company, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that it’s unclear if the former Nvidia CEO was aware of the alleged smuggling operations and instead laid the blame on the entire company. Nvidia itself has taken steps to improve its security and export control teams by establishing an oversight committee that will be in charge of its “national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management,” and would work with third-party experts in law, national security, and trade compliance.
These measures would further tighten the noose around China’s AI GPUs. Even though it has several domestic chip makers, many AI operators still prefer Nvidia chips for their performance and reliability. There have even been allegations that Alibaba and ByteDance, some of China’s biggest tech companies, prefer training their LLMs in Southeast Asia to bypass bans and restrictions. So, if the U.S. finally shuts down this loophole, we can expect these companies to scramble and find a replacement for the Nvidia GPUs they could access right now.

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

The affordable, capable ACEMAGIC K1 mini PC gets a $121 discount on Amazon ahead of Black Friday
Look no further if you need a tiny PC - the ACEMAGIC Ryzen-powered K1 costs $338.99 with 16GB RAM and a 256GB SSD
Your next home or home-office PC doesn’t need to cost a fortune or take up loads of space.
The ACEMAGIC K1 mini PC combines a four-core AMD processor with 16GB of memory in a compact chassis that weighs just 1.1 pounds, and now it costs just $339.99 - a decent drop from its original $459.99 price.
Today’s best ACEMAGIC K1 mini PC deal
The offer saves $121, or around 26%, on the 16GB RAM and 256GB SSD configuration.
Why we recommend the ACEMAGIC K1
The AMD Ryzen Pro 7330U processor has four cores and eight threads and includes integrated Radeon graphics. It uses the Zen 3 architecture and is designed for everyday computing rather than demanding gaming.
This is the kind of PC that can handle everyday browsing, word processing and spreadsheet tools, media streaming, and light games like Fortnite on lower graphics settings.
The system supports up to three 4K displays and comes with Windows 11 Pro. Storage can be expanded, although the 16GB memory is not upgradeable.
Price context and historical value
At $338.99, this matches the lowest price listed for this system for quite some time - it was cheaper last year, but memory price increases mean that it’s not realistic to expect those prices again any time soon.

✅ Buy it if… you’re looking for an affordable, space-saving desktop for everyday usage.
