articles.title: Fraudes digitales en Black Friday y Cyber Monday: las señales que permiten identificar una promoción falsa potenciada por inteligencia artificial en Centroamérica
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial vuelve más creíbles y escalables los fraudes digitales durante Black Friday y las compras de fin de año, cuando las promociones falsas, los sitios fraudulentos y la suplantación de comercios pueden derivar en pérdidas financieras y exposición de datos personales.
El alcance del problema quedó reflejado en el Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026 del World Economic Forum: el 73 % de los ejecutivos y expertos consultados sufrió fraude facilitado por medios cibernéticos durante 2025.
Las herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa permiten elaborar páginas falsas, mensajes y piezas visuales que reproducen con precisión la identidad de negocios legítimos. También pueden adaptar las comunicaciones a cada destinatario y automatizar respuestas, lo que dificulta detectar el engaño.
Waldim Rossal, consultor senior de Supply Chain en EY Centroamérica, Panamá y República Dominicana, señaló que esta tecnología no necesariamente crea una modalidad nueva de riesgo, pero refuerza mecanismos ya conocidos. “La sofisticación de estas herramientas cambia la forma en que debemos abordar la seguridad digital. Una promoción puede parecer auténtica, utilizar la imagen de una marca reconocida e incluso ofrecer una experiencia de atención aparentemente legítima”.
Direcciones alteradas y descuentos difíciles de creer
Las direcciones web con cambios mínimos respecto del dominio oficial, los descuentos excesivos y los mensajes que presionan para comprar de inmediato son algunas de las señales que pueden advertir sobre una estafa. También requieren cautela los enlaces, remitentes o archivos provenientes de contactos desconocidos.
Las condiciones poco claras de una promoción, los pedidos inusuales de información personal y los pagos dirigidos a cuentas particulares constituyen otros indicios. Rossal recomendó verificar el origen de una oferta mediante el sitio web, la aplicación o las cuentas oficiales del comercio, sin ingresar desde los enlaces recibidos.
Antes de completar una operación, los compradores deben confirmar el precio, la vigencia y las condiciones de la promoción. También deben comprobar que el destinatario del pago corresponda al establecimiento legítimo.
Los medios de pago con alertas de seguridad y mecanismos de reclamación ofrecen una capa adicional de protección. EY aconsejó activar la autenticación multifactor, evitar transacciones desde redes públicas y no compartir contraseñas, PIN ni códigos de autenticación.
Bloqueo de credenciales ante una interacción sospechosa
Quien sospeche haber ingresado a una página fraudulenta o haber compartido datos sensibles debe interrumpir la interacción y cambiar de inmediato las credenciales comprometidas. Tampoco debe descargar archivos ni instalar aplicaciones enviadas mediante promociones sospechosas.
Si se proporcionó información financiera o se realizó un pago, la recomendación es contactar al banco o emisor del medio de pago para solicitar el bloqueo y revisar los movimientos de la cuenta. También conviene conservar las pruebas disponibles y denunciar el sitio o perfil ante la plataforma digital, el comercio afectado y las autoridades competentes.
“Durante la temporada de compras de fin de año, detenerse unos minutos para comprobar la autenticidad de una oferta puede evitar consecuencias financieras y la exposición de información personal”, concluyó Rossal.

articles.title: Jensen Huang: "I Would Be Honored to Return as CEO"
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Jensen Huang: "I Would Be Honored to Return as CEO"
Jensen Huang took to X today to declare that he is willing to return as NVIDIA CEO if the company's board wants him back. In his statement, the former NVIDIA CEO thanked all his supporters and claimed that many employees, investors, business partners, and customers had reached out to him, asking him to come back. That part of the statement also seems like an indirect acknowledgment of the various online movements that have sprung up in his favor since he stepped down. This is also Jensen Huang's first public statement since he resigned from all his roles at NVIDIA on November 12, following the start of an investigation by the NVIDIA board of directors into Huang's extramarital affairs.
Perhaps most importantly, Jensen Huang opened the door to his return as NVIDIA CEO, at least from his side. This is important after reports recently emerged that Huang had discussed the possibility of a comeback with his close confidants, and the "Stand with Jensen" open letter continues to gain momentum online. Other than that, Huang also admitted that he "did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA" and acknowledged the mistakes he made in his personal life. Jensen says he is cooperating with the board's investigation, and if the board judges that his return would be in the best interest of "our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America," then he would be honored to return to his former position as CEO.The board, however, might see things a little differently. According to CNBC, a person familiar with the matter told them that the board is not considering bringing Huang back and remains focused on the investigation. That was on Monday, but things have been moving fast in this whole situation from the beginning. Moreover, we cannot gloss over the report that NVIDIA, under Huang, allegedly funded AI startups to buy its GPUs to keep demand high. It should also be remembered that Interim CEO Colette Kress reportedly opposed Huang's stance in that situation. NVIDIA reports its third-quarter results on Tuesday, November 17, so it's reasonable to expect questions about the leadership situation on the earnings call.
Jensen Huang's full X post is as follows:
Jensen Huang on XOver the past week, I've been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life's work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation. 
Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.
Jensen

articles.title: Batterie ou kit solaire complet : Zendure baisse ses SolarFlow jusqu’à 880 €
articles.text:
Le Black Friday doit être synonyme de bonnes affaires ! Alors voilà une offre qui mérite clairement qu’on s’y intéresse : Zendure propose jusqu’à 880 € de remise sur ses kits solaires et batteries intelligentes… Tout ce qu’il faut pour réduire vos factures d’électricité.
Faire des économies à l’achat, puis continuer à en faire sur ses factures d’électricité… Pas mal comme idée, non ?
C’est ce que propose Zendure pour le Black Friday, avec des réductions allant jusqu’à 43 % sur ses solutions de stockage d’énergie solaire. Une bonne affaire, comme on les aime, qui mérite qu’on vous en parle.
Black Friday Zendure : deux offres à ne pas manquer (jusqu’à -43 %)
La marque propose des tarifs particulièrement agressifs sur deux de ses solutions phares :
- SolarFlow 2400 AC+ à 839 € au lieu de 1 279 €, soit 440 € d’économie, avec un compteur intelligent 1CT-S offert, d’une valeur de 84,99 €.
- SolarFlow 2400 Pro + 4 panneaux solaires à 1 439 € au lieu de 2 319 €, soit 880 € d'économie, avec les supports de fixation offerts.
Dans les deux cas, l’objectif est le même : favoriser l’autoconsommation et donc alléger sa facture d’électricité. Reste à déterminer quelle option est la mieux adaptée à vos besoins :
SolarFlow 2400 AC+ : favoriser l’autoconsommation et réduire sa facture (-440 €)
Avec une batterie comme la SolarFlow 2400 AC+, il existe deux grandes façons de faire des économies sur sa facture d’électricité.
Comment réduire sa facture d’électricité avec la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ ?
Premier cas de figure : vous possédez déjà une installation solaire.
Plutôt que de laisser votre surplus de production repartir sur le réseau, vous pouvez le stocker dans la batterie pour le réutiliser au moment où vous en avez vraiment besoin. Le soir, lorsque les panneaux ne produisent plus, ou tôt le matin, avant que le soleil ne prenne le relais.
Deuxième possibilité : tirer le meilleur parti des heures creuses.
Vous rechargez la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ lorsque l’électricité coûte le moins cher, puis vous puisez dans cette réserve lorsque les tarifs remontent au cours de la journée. Cette approche est d’autant plus intéressante si votre contrat propose un vrai écart de prix entre les heures pleines et les heures creuses.
Une gestion (vraiment) intelligente de l’énergie
Mais la véritable force de la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ est sa capacité à jongler entre ces différents scénarios pour maximiser les économies.
Pour cela, elle s’appuie sur son système de gestion énergétique HEMS, épaulé par son intelligence artificielle ZENKI. Ce duo analyse les habitudes de consommation, surveille la production solaire et suit l’évolution des tarifs de l’électricité en temps réel. Cette batterie a d'ailleurs été testé par nos lecteurs, lors d'une opération Lecteurs-Testeurs.
Grâce à toutes ces données, la batterie peut déterminer automatiquement les moments les plus intéressants pour se recharger ou restituer l’énergie stockée.
Les principaux atouts de la SolarFlow 2400 AC+ :
- Une capacité de 2,4 kWh évolutive jusqu’à 16,8 kWh
- Jusqu’à 2 400 W de puissance bidirectionnelle
- Intégration simplifiée aux installations existantes grâce au courant alternatif (AC)
- Une alimentation de secours en cas de coupure (puissance de pointe de 3 600 W pendant 200 ms)
- Une gestion énergétique automatisée avec HEMS et ZENKI
SolarFlow 2400 Pro : un kit solaire complet avec panneaux et batterie (-880 €)
Lorsqu’on souhaite se lancer dans le solaire, il n’est pas toujours facile de savoir quels équipements choisir, ni comment les associer.
Si vous faites partie de ceux qui hésitent à franchir le pas, le kit SolarFlow 2400 Pro avec ses quatre panneaux solaires, est ce qu’il vous faut ! C’est une solution clé en main pour produire, stocker et consommer votre propre électricité, sans vous lancer dans une installation complexe.
Produire, stocker et consommer sa propre électricité
Ce kit peut trouver sa place dans un jardin, sur une terrasse ou sur toute surface suffisamment spacieuse et bien exposée au soleil. Autrement dit, pas besoin de se lancer dans de lourds travaux pour installer des panneaux sur le toit.
Mais ce qui distingue le SolarFlow 2400 Pro du SolarFlow 2400 AC+, avec lequel il partage la même capacité de 2,4 kWh et la même puissance de 2 400 W, ce sont ses quatre entrées MPPT. Là où l’AC+ vient se greffer sur une installation existante, déjà équipée de son propre onduleur, le 2400 Pro permet de raccorder directement les panneaux solaires, jusqu’à 750 W par entrée, soit 3 000 W au total. L’électricité qu’ils produisent arrive ainsi en courant continu jusqu’à la batterie, sans les allers-retours entre continu et alternatif qu’impose un raccordement côté AC, ce qui limite les pertes d’énergie et permet de tirer un meilleur parti de chaque kilowattheure produit.
À l’instar du SolarFlow 2400 AC+, il embarque le système intelligent HEMS et l’assistant ZENKI. Ensemble, ils optimisent automatiquement les flux d’énergie en tenant compte des habitudes de consommation, des prévisions météo et des tarifs de l'électricité.
Une installation puissante et évolutive
Le SolarFlow 2400 Pro dispose de quatre entrées MPPT indépendantes acceptant jusqu’à 3 000 W de panneaux solaires, auxquelles s’ajoutent 1 800 W via le couplage AC, soit une puissance d’entrée totale annoncée de 4 800 W.
Sa batterie offre une capacité de 2,4 kWh, extensible jusqu'à 16,8 kWh pour accompagner l’évolution des besoins.
Les principaux atouts de la SolarFlow 2400 Pro :
- Jusqu’à 4 800 W d’entrée solaire : 3000 W MPPT + 1 800 W AC ;
- Stockage : batterie intégrée de 2,4 kWh extensible jusqu'à 16,8 kWh
- Puissance AC bidirectionnelle de 2 400 W ;
- Gestion intelligente HEMS et ZENKI ;
- Un tarif Black Friday très avantageux
Une réserve d’énergie qui passe l’hiver dehors sans broncher
Pour ceux qui souhaitent aller plus loin en autonomie, Zendure propose la batterie AB3000L à 659 € au lieu de 839 €, pensée pour venir compléter le SolarFlow 2400 Pro ou le SolarFlow 2400 AC+.
Chaque module ajoute 2,88 kWh aux 2,4 kWh déjà intégrés à la station, qui peut en accueillir jusqu’à cinq pour atteindre 16,8 kWh de stockage, de quoi mettre de côté une bonne partie de la production de la journée et la consommer une fois le soleil couché.
Certifiée IP65 et équipée d’un système d’auto-chauffage par temps froid, elle peut rester installée dehors toute l’année, juste à côté de la station.

articles.title: Google Messages va enfin corriger un défaut qui agace ses utilisateurs
articles.text:
Fut un temps, Google Messages triait les messages des utilisateurs en fonction de deux onglets : « Personnel » et « Professionnel », ce dernier regroupant les communications commerciales et transactionnelles. Cependant, sans donner d’explication, Google a supprimé ce système de classement en septembre 2023. Les utilisateurs se sont donc retrouvés avec un historique de conversations qui n’était plus catégorisé. Peu pratique et peu clair donc, mais bonne nouvelle, l’entreprise américaine préparerait un nouveau système de catégorisation des messages.
Les messages bientôt répartis en deux catégories
Le média américain Android Authority a exploré le code de la dernière version bêta de Google Messages. Il a ainsi trouvé plusieurs indices qui indiquent un nouveau système de catégorisation des messages sur l’application. Les utilisateurs feraient face à deux sections : « Principale » et « Autres ». Vous l’aurez compris, la catégorie « Principale » regroupe les messages personnels, tandis que la section « Autres » rassemble les messages promotionnels, les éventuels spams ou encore les mises à jour. Une nouveauté bienvenue donc, vu que les messages ne sont actuellement pas du tout triés.
Les utilisateurs pourraient déplacer leurs messages
Toujours selon Android Authority, il serait possible de faire glisser manuellement un message d’une catégorie à l’autre. À titre d’exemple, un message important tombé dans la section « Autres » pourrait être déplacé dans la section « Principale », ou inversement. Deux boutons seraient ainsi proposés : « Déplacer vers Autres » et « Déplacer vers Principal ». L’application prendrait par la suite en compte ce déplacement de conversation en classant les futurs messages de l’expéditeur dans la catégorie sélectionnée. Un bouton « Annuler » permettrait de rétablir la catégorisation initiale.
Il reste maintenant à voir comment Google effectuerait le tri des messages. Le risque est bien entendu qu’un message important ou personnel se retrouve dans la section « Autres », et qu’il passe ainsi inaperçu. En fin de compte, Google reprendrait plus ou moins le système de catégorisation des e-mails d’Outlook, avec ses deux sections : « Prioritaire » et « Autres ».

articles.title: Edge AI Moves Agricultural Intelligence from the Cloud to the Field - EE Times
articles.text:
An agricultural robot moving through a field must do more than collect information: It must interpret what its sensors detect, decide what to do, and potentially act before it reaches the next plant. Sending data to a remote computer for analysis is not always practical, particularly when connectivity is unreliable or decisions must be made immediately.
Xin “Rex” Sun, director of the Peltier Institute for Advancement in Agricultural Technology at North Dakota State University, is confronting that problem in research on AI-assisted crop monitoring.
His laboratory is developing a field platform equipped with sensors that could diagnose crop problems and eventually support interventions. The research involves powerful computing systems, but Sun wants the resulting applications to run on equipment that farmers can use in their fields.
“Edge AI will be the go-to approach, because if the technology can’t run on a robot, combine, or tractor, it’s of little use to farmers,” Sun said. “Farmers aren’t sitting in laboratories doing research. They need technology that works in the field.”
His team uses Nvidia GPUs for demanding research workloads, alongside smaller computing platforms such as Raspberry Pi and Arduino for other functions. The distinction illustrates a fundamental design choice: Different tasks require different amounts and types of processing.
As agricultural machinery becomes more autonomous, equipment manufacturers must make those choices across increasingly complex systems. The challenge is no longer simply getting an AI model to recognize something; it’s giving a machine enough intelligence to respond appropriately without exceeding its power budget or compromising safety.
From sensing to acting
Nvidia’s Chen Su, head of edge AI product marketing, said in written responses to EE Times that agricultural systems are moving beyond individual applications such as crop classification, weed detection, and plant health monitoring.
“Many systems are evolving from single-purpose vision applications into multi-workload edge AI platforms that run perception, crop analysis, localization, navigation, obstacle avoidance, and control together,” Su said.
A precision sprayer, for example, must identify a target and activate the appropriate mechanism at the right moment. A more autonomous machine must also determine its location, navigate the field, detect obstacles, and coordinate its movements with the agricultural operation.
These workloads place different demands on processors. According to Su, the computing requirements depend on sensor count and type, model complexity, machine speed, reaction times, and the number of simultaneous tasks.
The need for onboard processing goes beyond the limited connectivity common in rural areas. Even with a reliable network connection, sending information to the cloud and waiting for a response can introduce unacceptable delays when a machine is moving.
Su described the architectural change as a move from “sense and report” toward “sense, decide, and act.”
That requires more capable onboard computing, sensor fusion, real-time control, and software for developing and validating autonomous systems. Nvidia’s Jetson platforms target such embedded AI workloads, where computing performance must fit within constraints on size, power consumption, heat, and cost.
Not all of the processing needs to take place in one computer. Cameras and intelligent sensors can perform image processing, compression, filtering, and some object detection locally. A more powerful central processor can combine information from multiple sensors to support navigation and planning.
The cloud remains useful for training models, simulation, fleet management, and analytics. But Su expects the principal change over the coming years to be the emergence of complete autonomy stacks running onboard agricultural machines rather than individual AI features operating in isolation.
Matching intelligence to the machine
For NXP Semiconductors, the problem is not simply how to provide more computing power; it’s how to allocate processing across the functions of an agricultural machine.
According to Ramakrishna Karamsetty, senior director of product management for edge and physical AI hardware and software products at NXP, “agriculture is one of the toughest environments for computing.”
Karamsetty, who joined NXP after more than 25 years at Intel, pointed to differences in terrain, crops, climate, and connectivity. A system developed for a farm in Arizona may encounter entirely different conditions in Idaho, China, or India. “There is no one-size-fits-all solution,” he told EE Times.
The type of agricultural operation also determines the amount of intelligence required. Harvesting corn differs from picking delicate fruit, which requires evaluating color, ripeness, and other characteristics before harvesting. “Tasks that traditionally required a person to inspect and judge the crop need more intelligence at the edge,” Karamsetty said.
That doesn’t mean every agricultural machine requires a high-performance GPU, he said. Some functions can run on microcontrollers (MCUs), while others benefit from dedicated neural processing units (NPUs) or more powerful computing platforms.
Power consumption complicates the decision. Farm equipment must operate for extended periods, and its electronics must function within available thermal and electrical limits. Karamsetty argued that performance per watt can matter more than maximizing peak computing performance.
NXP is developing discrete and integrated NPUs intended to provide appropriately sized inference capabilities. The company’s broader strategy combines application processors, AI accelerators, and MCUs rather than treating inference as an isolated function.
Karamsetty described a processing pipeline in which application processors prepare information from cameras, LiDAR, and other sensors; NPUs execute AI inference; and MCUs handle control functions.
NXP calls its approach the Neural Axis Architecture, using the human nervous system as an analogy. Different processing layers take responsibility for planning, coordinating sensor information, and executing low-latency responses. The distinction becomes particularly important when AI is responsible for operating physical machinery.
Imagine a harvester moving through a cornfield, Karamsetty said. Its vision system is identifying crops and obstacles, while other components control the harvesting mechanism, steering, and braking. If AI inference slows down or encounters a problem, the machine must still be capable of stopping safely. “Safety functions must be isolated from AI inference and normal actuator functions so that an issue or delay in one does not compromise the other,” he said.
NXP’s approach is to integrate functional safety and security capabilities with its computing architecture. The objective is to prevent a problem in perception or an agricultural operation from compromising critical machine controls.
Software integration is another priority. Karamsetty said NXP wants developers to use a common software environment across MCUs, application processors, and NPUs rather than maintaining separate optimization and deployment processes for each processor type.
Beyond the proof of concept
The ability to adapt those models may ultimately matter as much as the processors running them. Agricultural conditions vary not only between regions but also within the same field over time. Lighting, dust, fog, weather, and changing crops can all affect how an AI system interprets sensor data.
Karamsetty envisages equipment manufacturers deploying models customized for particular locations, then managing updates remotely. A machine operating in one region might need a different model from an otherwise identical machine working elsewhere.
This could help manufacturers avoid developing entirely different equipment for every crop or environment. But it also introduces the challenge of validating and maintaining models across many locations. “I think the technology is at the point where cost-effective proofs of concept are possible, but that is not the same as having fully productized, widely deployable solutions,” Karamsetty said.
Commercial deployment requires more than successful demonstrations. Manufacturers must address functional safety, security, regulatory requirements, and reliability under conditions that may differ substantially from those used to develop the original model.
There’s also a question of ownership. Agricultural AI systems may increasingly rely on data collected from individual farms to improve their performance. Karamsetty sees a potential parallel with disputes over farmers’ rights to repair their own equipment.
Similar tensions could emerge if manufacturers use farmers’ data to customize models and subsequently charge those farmers for access to the resulting intelligence. “The ability to deploy customized models will be critical, especially while respecting farmers’ data privacy,” he said.
Karamsetty expects continued improvements in computing performance per watt, greater integration, and new semiconductor architectures. But he believes the larger competitive distinction may come from how manufacturers manage software and their relationships with equipment owners.
For agricultural autonomy, more computing power is only one part of the solution. The harder task is turning that power into dependable decisions that machines can execute safely, economically, and under the unpredictable conditions of working farms.

articles.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6.2 Astra for professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday work - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OpenAI rolls out GPT-6.2 Astra for professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday work
OpenAI Group PBC today announced the launch of GPT-6.2 Astra, a new frontier artificial intelligence model for complex professional work that is claimed to outperform its predecessor at less than a third of the cost, along with an updated version of its everyday model, GPT-6.2 Sol.
The new models are aimed at businesses and developers looking for frontier performance at a cost that works at scale, with both said to deliver better results on demanding tasks while using fewer output tokens.
According to OpenAI, GPT-6.2 Astra sets a new high on Agents’ Last Exam, a benchmark that tests multistep professional work, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT-6 Astra while costing under a third as much. It is claimed to have finished 5.5 points ahead of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost.
OpenAI is positioning GPT-6.2 Astra as the best model in the world for scientists, with the model scoring 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, a benchmark for scientific work carried out in a terminal. On Harvey LAB-AA, a test of legal assignments, the model more than doubled the pass rate of Fable 5.2 at about one-sixth of the cost.
Along with improved benchmark scores, GPT-6.2 Astra was trained to create slides, spreadsheets and documents that more closely follow the conventions used by professionals in fields such as law, sales, finance and accounting. The model can match a slide template from an original file or a screenshot, including layout, colors and typography down to the exact font size.
Early testers of the model include accounting AI startup Basis, which said that its average time for long-horizon accounting work fell by 50%, with the time for its most complex work falling by up to 73%.
Described by OpenAI as its go-to model for everyday work, GPT-6.2 Sol is claimed to let users complete more tasks on the same paid plan than GPT-6.1 Sol did. According to OpenAI, the model came within 0.5 points of GPT-6.2 Astra on Cognition AI Inc.’s FrontierCode 2.0 coding benchmark at about one-fifth of the cost.
GPT-6.2 Astra comes less than two months after OpenAI called off the planned October release of GPT-6.1 Astra, after internal testing found the model fell short on staying within scope and authorization. The decision was announced the day before the company’s DevDay event in September, where GPT-6.1 Sol launched on its own.
Like GPT-6 Astra, both GPT-6.2 models meet the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework, and their increased capabilities have led the company to launch them with tighter safeguards for higher-risk cybersecurity assistance that are also said to restrict some legitimate vulnerability research. The company said it will work to bring the GPT-6.2 models to Daybreak, its program for vetted cyber defenders.
GPT-6.2 Astra is also the first externally released OpenAI model to meet the High threshold for AI self-improvement, a measure of a model’s ability to accelerate AI research. OpenAI tracks the capability because models that help build future AI systems could outpace safeguards and human oversight, and earlier this month it disclosed Control Room, a system already deployed across its research infrastructure that can halt model output when intervention is needed.
The company noted that in two of its alignment tests, the new models were more likely than GPT-6 Astra to omit mentioning obstacles that blocked their work, such as a missing file. OpenAI said it has added instructions in Codex that substantially reduce the omissions and is continuing to investigate the behavior.
GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available starting today to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, with Enterprise and Edu access requiring a workspace admin to enable it. Developers can also access both models through the OpenAI API. API pricing for GPT-6.2 Astra is $8 per million input tokens, 40 cents for cached input and $40 per million output tokens, a 20% discount on input and output tokens compared with GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6.2 Sol carries forward GPT-6.1 Sol’s rates of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

articles.title: US government confirms criminal investigation into Singapore company at the heart of Jensen Huang scandal — Megaspeed identified over suspicious activity, company placed on ‘no sell’ list by Nvidia
articles.text:
US government confirms criminal investigation into Singapore company at the heart of Jensen Huang scandal — Megaspeed identified over suspicious activity, company placed on ‘no sell’ list by Nvidia
The Justice and Commerce Departments have announced an investigation into the company previously run by the woman officials have accused of being a Chinese spy while having an affair with Jensen Huang while he was Nvidia's CEO.
A criminal investigation into Megaspeed has been confirmed by the United States Justice and Commerce Departments, with a joint statement saying that they will “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.” Authorities believe that Megaspeed is one of a raft of companies that may have circumvented export rules designed to limit the sale of advanced AI chips, like those built by Nvidia, to approved companies and countries. The company is at the heart of the recent Jensen Huang scandal, which saw him resign from the company last week.
Megaspeed was added to Nvidia's no-sell list in June 2025, the statement reveals, but a New York Times report claims that a Malaysian Megaspeed subsidiary continued to receive large shipments of Nvidia chips for a full eight months after that date. It's believed that Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell and H200 chips were shipped to Speedmatrix, either via third parties or directly from Nvidia itself, before being handed off to China. Nvidia has argued that it was given Commerce Department permission to ship the components to Megaspeed. Notably, Nvidia continues to list Megaspeed as a cloud partner.
The new criminal investigation follows a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed that first kicked off in 2024 over possible export violations. By May 2025, it had requested Nvidia's data relating to sales it made to Megaspeed, and by June, officials visited Megaspeed and even interviewed Alice Huang, the now-former executive who is allegedly a Chinese spy. Ms. Huang is also the woman that then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with before resigning his position earlier this month. Following that visit, the Justice Department took the lead in the investigation into Megaspeed.
Megaspeed has long been accused of being a front for an AI component smuggling operation. In October 2025, an investigation claimed that it had helped move around $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China by importing them and then re-exporting them to the country. Megaspeed says that it complies with all laws and that the woman at the center of the affair scandal, Ms. Huang, is no longer at the company. The Chinese government has also dismissed claims that she was a state spy.
The joint Commerce and Justice Departments' statement pointed to its strong track record when prosecuting chip smugglers to date. 17 defendants across a total of six investigations have been charged so far, with more likely to follow. A Californian man was recently arrested after being accused of smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-restricted Nvidia chips to China. He now faces up to 20 years in prison.

articles.title: Como bloquear no TikTok: passo a passo do app ou PC • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como bloquear no TikTok: passo a passo do app ou PC
Ao bloquear alguém no TikTok, a pessoa não poderá encontrar seu perfil nas buscas, enviar mensagens ou interagir com suas publicações
Você pode usar o aplicativo do celular Android e iPhone ou a versão web para bloquear pessoas no TikTok. Independentemente da plataforma, basta acessar o perfil do usuário para encontrar a opção para afastar interações indesejadas na rede social.
Após bloquear no TikTok, a plataforma corta o contato discretamente, impedindo que a outra pessoa encontre seu perfil, veja seus vídeos, envie mensagens ou interaja com seus vídeos.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te mostra três formas de bloquear uma conta no TikTok.
Você pode bloquear alguém no TikTok e evitar interações indesejadas por meio do aplicativo para celular Android ou iPhone. Para isso, siga o passo a passo abaixo:
O meio mais rápido de bloquear pessoas no TikTok é utilizando a ferramenta dos comentários dos vídeos da plataforma, permitindo restringir até 100 usuários simultaneamente. Para isso, siga o seguinte caminho:
Abra o aplicativo do TikTok no celular Android ou iPhone e toque em “Perfil”, no canto inferior direito. Em seguida, escolha e abra qualquer vídeo publicado na sua conta.
Toque no ícone de balão com três pontos, localizado na barra no canto direito da tela, para acessar os comentários do seu vídeo.
Toque no botão de configurações de comentários, na parte superior da janela, e selecione a opção “Ger. Comentários” para ativar a seleção múltipla.
Toque nas caixas de seleção ao lado dos comentários publicados pelas contas indesejadas que você deseja bloquear no TikTok.
Toque em “Mais”, na parte inferior direita da tela, e escolha “Bloquear contas”. Por fim, confirme a ação na janela pop-up que surgirá na tela.
Abra o navegador do seu PC, acesse tiktok.com e faça login na sua conta. Clique na barra “Pesquisar”, localizada no topo da tela, e digite o nome de usuário da pessoa que você quer bloquear no TikTok.
No resultado da busca, clique em cima do perfil que será bloqueado para avançar.
Clique no botão de três pontos, ao lado do botão de compartilhar, e selecione “Bloquear”. Na janela pop-up, confirme a ação clicando novamente em “Bloquear”
Ao bloquear pessoas no TikTok, a plataforma corta o contato entre as contas discretamente. Confira as principais mudanças que acontecem na prática:
Ao bloquear alguém no TikTok, a plataforma não envia nenhum alerta ou notificação avisando a outra pessoa sobre a restrição. Contudo, ela pode descobrir indiretamente ao notar que seu perfil sumiu das buscas e que não consegue mais enviar DMs ou interagir com seus vídeos.
Vale dizer que esses sinais também podem ser confundidos com a exclusão da conta, mas você ainda pode aparecer em grupos compartilhados, Lives ou Duets com terceiros.
Ao bloquear no TikTok, as DMs antigas não são excluídas automaticamente e continuam visíveis na sua caixa de entrada. No entanto, o envio de novos textos fica bloqueado para ambos e os links de vídeos compartilhados anteriormente na conversa param de funcionar.
Caso você decida desbloquear a pessoa no TikTok, o histórico do bate-papo continua intacto e a troca de mensagens pode ser retomada normalmente. Ainda assim, será preciso seguir o usuário novamente para restabelecer o contato.
Existem alguns sinais claros que ajudam a descobrir se alguém decidiu bloquear seu perfil no TikTok. Veja os principais indícios para chegar:
Bloquear no TikTok significa cortar totalmente o contato, ocultando seu perfil e vídeos para outra pessoa e impedindo que ela siga, envie mensagens ou use recursos como o Duet e Stitch. Essa ação remove o conteúdo dela da sua tela e é indicada para afastar contatos indesejados ou casos de assédio.
Silenciar no TikTok é o ato que permite ocultar apenas os vídeos ou notificações de um usuário no seu feed, sem deixar de segui-lo ou romper o vínculo. O perfil silenciado continua vendo seus vídeos públicos e interagindo normalmente, sendo a opção ideal para reduzir a exposição sem criar atritos.

articles.title: People in Jordan turn to VPNs as Telegram goes dark nationwide
articles.text:
People in Jordan turn to VPNs as Telegram goes dark nationwide
Proton VPN sign-ups from Jordan jumped 110% above normal levels after authorities blocked the messaging app over security concerns
- Proton VPN sign-ups from Jordan rose 110% amid national Telegram ban
- Jordan's security services cited extremism, cybercrime, and blackmail
- Citizens are being urged to choose their VPN carefully
People in Jordan are turning to VPNs after authorities blocked Telegram across the country, with Proton VPN reporting a 110% surge in sign-ups above its usual baseline.
Jordan's Public Security Directorate (PSD) announced the block on Monday, November 16 — Reuters reported. It said the move aims to bolster digital security and stop the app being used to spread extremism and radicalization following a deadly church attack in October. Authorities have not said how long the restriction will last.
A VPN can get around this kind of block by routing your traffic through a server in another country. That's why demand for the best VPN services tends to climb whenever a government cuts off a popular app.
Proton VPN sign-ups more than double
Proton's Internet Censorship Observatory logged the spike in Jordan starting on November 15 and lists it as ongoing.
Proton says it regularly sees sign-ups jump after protests, contested elections, and government crackdowns. Jordan is a familiar name on that list. For example, when Discord stopped working in the country in October 2025, Proton VPN sign-ups peaked at 250% above baseline. Jordan also banned TikTok in December 2022.
The current surge is smaller than neighbouring Iraq's for now, where Proton recorded a 1,200% rise in sign-ups when Telegram was blocked in April.
Why has Jordan blocked Telegram?
As reported by Al Jazeera, the block follows a security crackdown after an October 23 attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate that killed nine people.
Jordan then carried out airstrikes in Syria that it said killed 20 Islamic State militants. This month, a security officer was killed in what authorities called a terrorist stabbing in Amman.
According to reports, Islamic State militants allegedly used Telegram to issue statements. The PSD has urged citizens to report unlawful content through official channels.

Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
Where else is Telegram blocked?
Jordan is far from alone. Around 30 countries have disrupted Telegram at least once, often during political unrest. Recent examples include:
- Russia: Moved to fully block the app in March 2026, prompting Telegram CEO Pavel Durov to urge Russians to stock up on VPNs.
- Iraq: Blocked Telegram in April 2026 amid tensions between the government and armed groups.
- India: Temporarily blocked the app in June 2026 to stop cheating ahead of a medical entrance re-exam.
- Vietnam: Ordered a block in May 2025, accusing Telegram of failing to cooperate on crime.
- Nepal: Banned the app in July 2025, citing online fraud and money laundering.
China, Iran, and Cuba have long-standing bans in place.
Choose your VPN carefully
If you need to get around a Telegram ban with a VPN, pick your provider with care. During Iraq's block, Proton warned that many of the most downloaded VPNs there were linked to China-based firms with hidden ownership, or to providers that sell user data.
Stick to independently audited services. If cost is a concern, our best free VPN guide lists safe options, including Proton VPN Free. A VPN also adds a useful privacy layer, since Telegram does not turn on end-to-end encryption by default.

articles.title: Phison Pascari X201P 15.36TB SSD Review: Fast PCIe 5.0 write performance for AI and ingest servers
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Phison’s Pascari X201P meets its rated specs and pairs 12 GB/s sequential writes with a steady 600K random write IOPS, making short work of AI checkpoints. It gives ground at low and moderate queue depths, where QD1 writes and mixed workloads lag, and it ran warm on our bench.
Reasons to buy
- + Fast sequential and random writes
- + Tight write latency under load
- + Quick AI checkpoint saves
Reasons to avoid
- - Slower low-queue-depth writes
- - Mixed-workload performance trails at middle QDs
- - Runs warm
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Phison is serious about enterprise storage, and the Pascari X201P was not released lightly; it came in the night, under NDA, alongside this week’s Supercomputing 2026 event. The drive is part of the Performance X-Series, which handles intensive workloads where consistency is the name of the game. We were nevertheless pleasantly surprised by its write performance, with a steady 12 GB/s for sequential and over 600,000 random write IOPS, considering it’s marketed at the 1 drive write per day (DWPD) endurance point.
Part of that surprise comes from the fact that this is Phison’s read-intensive PCIe 5.0 data center drive, a successor to the X200P. It comes in the U.2 form factor — which can be more convenient in many cases — from 1.92TB to 30.72TB, and an E3.S version from 3.84TB, in both single- and dual-port models. It stands next to its mixed-use sibling, the X201E, which is the one rated for 3 DWPD. What makes the X201P exciting, in part, is its own 16-channel X2 controller and the flash that’s inside.
This drive is aimed at AI, analytics, and database servers, with its case made in the 4K 70/30 mix at higher queue depths. It passed Phison’s one-million-IOPS mark at QD128 in our testing of the 15.36TB model, and the drive met all of its rated specs, though its random read rating required polled I/O to reach on our bench. It faced challenges with QD1 writes, log commits, and the middle range of our mixed sweeps. Given its blend of performance, capacity, and endurance, we consider it a very competent entry from the company that was perhaps better known in the consumer SSD market until recently.
Phison Pascari X201P Specifications

| Memory | 3D TLC | 3D TLC | 3D TLC | 321-layer 3D TLC | 3D TLC | 
| Sequential Read | 14,800 MB/s | 14,800 MB/s | 14,800 MB/s | 14,800 MB/s | 14,800 MB/s |

| Random Read | 1,400K | 2,700K | 3,300K | 3,250K | 2,800K |

| Security | ISE or SED (TCG Opal 2.02) | ISE or SED (TCG Opal 2.02) | ISE or SED (TCG Opal 2.02) | ISE or SED (TCG Opal 2.02) | ISE or SED (TCG Opal 2.02) |

| Part Number (ISE) | XP208H081T92P322T0410 | XP208H083T84P324T0910 | XP208H087T68P328T1910 | XP208H0815T3P3216T310 | XP208H0830T7P3232T710 |

The drive met or beat every rated performance figure that we can test, which should be the target of any enterprise SSD released today. If there’s an exception, it’s due to how we test; Phison lists a ceiling of 3,250K IOPS for 4K random read, which is higher than our bench allows with our interrupt-driven I/O, which we use rather than a polled approach. We also run a polled test on every drive for cases like this, and our result was 3,283K IOPS at the same queue depth Phison specifies, which shows the drive does exceed its specification.
Phison Pascari X201P Features and Management
| Feature | Phison Pascari X201P | 
|---|---|
| NVMe Specification | NVMe 2.0d | 
| OCP Specification | Datacenter NVMe SSD v2.0, with v2.6 telemetry features | 
| Host Link | PCIe 5.0 x4, single port (2x2 dual-port models offered) | 
| Power-Loss Protection | Yes | 
| End-to-End Data Protection | Yes | 
| Security Options | ISE, SED (TCG Opal 2.02) or non-SED; AES-XTS 256-bit | 
| Sanitize | Cryptographic erase and block erase | 
| LBA Formats | 512-byte and 4,096-byte, each with optional metadata | 
| Namespaces | Up to 128 | 
| Power States | Six: 25 W, 22 W, 20 W, 18 W, 15 W and 12 W maximum | 
| Temperature Thresholds | 77°C warning, 85°C critical | 
| Thermal Management | Host-controlled thermal management supported | 
| Firmware Slots | Seven; activation without reset | 
| Out-of-Band Management | NVMe-MI 1.2 over SMBus and PCIe | 
| Flexible Data Placement | Not supported | 
| Tested Firmware | X2WM6026 | 
Phison Pascari X201P: A Closer Look
Our sample is in the U.2 form factor, 15mm thick. We have the single-port SKU, ISE model XP208H0815T3P3216T310, with firmware X2WM6026. Some data we previously saw from the drive was reportedly on X2WM6025, but we confirmed X2WM6026 for all relevant results. We mounted the drive on a PCIe 5.0 x4 add-in card adapter for U.2, standing upright in the slot.
Phison did not provide firm hardware details, but we were able to discover some things on our own. The flash was probably the easiest, as the company claimed it was a 321-layer part. That can only be SK hynix’s V9 TLC, which is not flash we’ve tested before in any product. It’s exceptionally fast and uses a three-deck design, which is relatively new for TLC flash. The flash could be credited with some of the exceptional performance measurements we see on the drive.
As for the proprietary controller, we’ve heard that it’s using a combination of the standard Arm Cortex-R5 — these would be the main cores — with AndesCore RISC-V on the side. We’ve seen the latter before on the Phison E28 consumer SSD controller, which did have some enterprise-like aspects to it. The E28 is the newer design, built on a 6nm process with Andes’ newer N45 cores alongside the N25F, while the X2 is a 12nm part that, as far as we can tell, sticks with N25F-class co-processors.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
In this case, the X2 has twice the flash channels, which enables a superior level of performance out of TLC flash, as in enterprise you do not rely on pSLC. That mix of cores sets the X2 apart from other 16-channel PCIe 5.0 enterprise controllers: Marvell’s Bravera SC5 and Silicon Motion’s SM8366 rely on Arm cores throughout, whereas Phison pairs its Cortex-R5 cores with small RISC-V co-processors.

I don't recall how it did with QD=4, but I think that wasn't quite enough. What's weird about it is 128 kiB is the largest transaction size the drive supports! I think my Samsung 990 Pro supports either 1 MiB or 2 MiB transactions, in which case you can basically saturate the interface with QD=1. Reply
- thestryker I think it'd be interesting to see something like the Pascari X200Z tested (or dust off a P5800X) just to see where something latency optimized stands. It seems like we're getting a lot more variance on enterprise SSDs these days with regards to segmenting by performance.Reply

QD=8 will do it. I don't recall how it did with QD=4, but I think that wasn't quite enough. What's weird about it is 128 kiB is the largest transaction size the drive supports! And Q8, you say, is ok.
Q1 is for scenarios where you can not know the content of the next request (e.g. what to write or where to read from) untill the previous one is over. Reply

And Q8, you say, is ok.Well, I tested using unbuffered I/O via Linux' Flexible I/O tester which does low-level transactions and don't get segmented. So, any request size larger than 128 kiB failed. At an OS level, I also wouldn't trust it to overlap the segments of an application-level request. Maybe there's an I/O scheduler parameter you can set to make it do that.

articles.title: Razer Unveils the Carbon Fiber Collection
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Razer Unveils the Carbon Fiber Collection
Razer, the leading global lifestyle brand for gamers, today announced the Razer Carbon Fiber Collection, featuring two professional-grade wireless gaming mice: the Razer Viper V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition and the Razer DeathAdder V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition.
The #1 Mouse Brand takes the two shapes pros trust and reforged the shell in one of the strongest materials available: real woven carbon fiber.Carbon fiber is the hallmark of supercars, aerospace and motorsport, where every milligram counts and every part must perform flawlessly. The Carbon Fiber Collection brings that same excellence to Razer's esports mice, weaving real carbon fiber into the shell while preserving the iconic forms players know.
Charlie Bolton, Razer's Global Head of Design"Design is at the core of how we build at Razer, and the Carbon Fiber Collection is a clear example of that. Working closely with our engineers, we kept the shapes pros trust and rebuilt the shell in real carbon fiber. With no paint to hide behind, every stage had to be exact. The result is a gaming mouse where the material, the shape and the finish all sit at the same level of refinement."
Real Carbon Fiber. Real Engineering.
At the heart of the collection is woven carbon fiber, a material known for its strength-to-weight ratio. Shaping carbon fiber into a mouse shell is anything but simple, and it starts with the weave: the fiber is woven in a 2×2 twill, a pattern that gives carbon fiber its distinctive diagonal look.
Next, the woven sheets are hot-pressed into shape, curing under heat and pressure to hold their form. Computer Numerical Control machinery then cuts each shell to the precise contours of the iconic Viper and DeathAdder shape.
Finally, each shell is left bare under a clear UV-cured coating rather than painted over, so the weave stands out in every light. What players see and hold is real carbon fiber.
From weaving to the final finish, every stage is held to the same exacting standard, reflecting Razer's commitment to crafting top-tier products without compromise.
Light in Hand. Strong Under Pressure.
The result is a lighter shell that is also up to 53% stronger than ABS plastic, built to hold its shape under serious force.
The Viper V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition weighs 47 g and the DeathAdder V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition weighs 49 g, so every flick and swipe starts faster and stops sharper.
Jaccob "Zellsis" Whiteaker, VALORANT Masters Madrid 2024 Champion"It's the Viper shape I already love, and the carbon fiber makes it feel stronger and more premium".
Nikola "NiKo" Kovač, IEM Cologne Major 2026 Champion"I've used the DeathAdder for a long time, and the carbon fiber version feels a lot more premium and stronger. It's also noticeably lighter".
Crafted. For the Pro.
The Carbon Fiber Collection joins the Razer Viper V4 Pro and Razer DeathAdder V4 Pro lineup from Razer, giving pros the shapes they know in a trusted material that is lighter and stronger.
Both wireless gaming mice are powered by the Razer Focus Pro 50K Optical Sensor Gen-3, Razer HyperSpeed Wireless Gen-2 and Razer Optical Mouse Switches Gen-4, with up to 180 hours of battery life. For the Razer DeathAdder V4 Pro Carbon Fiber Edition, that also means a sensor and battery life upgrade from the base model.

articles.title: PowerEdge nodes turn into software-defined storage for AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell bets liquid-cooled, software-defined storage can keep AI factories fed
AI factories are growing so dense that storage, not just compute, now decides how quickly they turn data into tokens. For Dell Technologies Inc., the answer starts with turning its PowerEdge servers into flexible, software-defined storage nodes that can change roles as workloads shift.
The move from training toward inference and agents has put new pressure on time to value. Dell has spent the year extending its AI Data Platform with a semantic layer for agentic workloads. Its AI factory pitch now reaches well beyond compute and graphics processing units, according to George Papadopoulos (pictured), senior vice president of product and engineering at Dell.
“We look at our AI factory not just as a set of CPUs and GPUs, but networking becoming more and more important, particularly around speed, reliability of storage and the ability to take your raw data and generate context and knowledge from it,” he said.
Papadopoulos spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Dell is adapting its storage and cooling to keep AI factories running at scale. (* Disclosure below.)
PowerEdge storage built to change with AI workloads
Customers want storage they can buy for today’s needs and repurpose later. For instance, a customer might start with file and move to object or parallel file as workloads evolve. Agentic workloads lean on small input/output operations rather than streaming, so the right storage type can shift quickly, Papadopoulos explained. Dell’s answer is Dell Exascale Storage, which runs as licensed software on Dell servers.
“It’s our really purpose-built software-defined solution for allowing us to take a PowerEdge-based node and … with flexible licensing, allow you to deploy a file persona, a block persona, an object persona or a parallel file persona, and allow that flexibility to change over time as your needs change,” he said.
Density is also forcing a rethink of cooling. The power envelope of today’s AI systems is so large that customers are planning for 100% liquid-cooled data centers, according to Papadopoulos. That requirement now extends to storage.
“The conversations have really gotten down to how can we most effectively provide a direct liquid-cooled solution — and the storage, that means even liquid cooling the drives, which is something that hasn’t been done as of yet,” he said.
At SC26, Dell unveiled a 2U, 32-drive node with 100% liquid cooling, which it bills as the first direct liquid-cooled storage for rack-scale AI. The node deploys as an Exascale system with any persona. Separating the software from an appliance also lets Dell bring new PowerEdge generations to market faster. That flexibility matters for neocloud operators, who need an off-ramp for every purchase, Papadopoulos noted.
“That allows them to make an upfront purchase and know that they won’t be locked into one particular storage type,” he said, “or have a set of data silos that they can’t leverage as they go forward.”

articles.title: Saudi tech group iMENA secures $214 million to support regional growth
articles.text:
Saudi tech group iMENA secures $214 million to support regional growth
- Saudi Arabia-headquartered technology group iMENA has completed a SAR 802 million ($214 million) capital increase in two tranches, aimed at supporting its growth in Saudi Arabia and across the Middle East and North Africa.
- Co-founded in 2012 by Nasir Alsharif, Khaldoon Tabaza, and Adey Salamin, iMENA operates digital platforms in online classifieds, automotive commerce, and mobility services, including OpenSooq, SellAnyCar, and Jeeny. Its businesses serve well over 100 million users across over 20 countries in the region.
- iMENA's investor base includes Sanabil Investments and several Saudi institutional investors. The announcement did not disclose the individual contributions to the capital increase or identify which investors participated in each tranche.
- The proceeds will support the group's investments in Saudi Arabia, expansion of its digital platforms and greater integration of technology, data and operational capabilities across its portfolio. The transaction was announced at the Digital Entrepreneurship Council, held under the patronage of Saudi ministers Abdullah Alswaha and Fahad Al-Saif.
- In April 2025, iMENA closed a $135 million pre-IPO investment from Sanabil Investments, along with other investors.
Press release:
Saudi Arabia-headquartered technology group iMENA has completed a SAR 802 million ($214 million) capital increase to support its expansion in the kingdom and across the Middle East and North Africa.
The capital increase was completed in two tranches and will strengthen the group's financial position as it expands its investments and digital platform businesses.
iMENA operates a portfolio of technology companies spanning online classifieds, automotive commerce and mobility services, including OpenSooq, SellAnyCar and Jeeny. Collectively, its platforms serve more than 100 million users across over 20 countries in the region.
The group's investor base includes Sanabil Investments and several Saudi institutional investors. However, iMENA did not disclose the investors participating in the latest capital increase, their individual commitments or the group's valuation.
The announcement was made during the Digital Entrepreneurship Council, held under the patronage of Saudi Minister of Communications and Information Technology Abdullah Alswaha and Minister of Investment Fahad bin Abduljalil Al-Saif.
Nasser Al-Sharif, chairman of iMENA, said the capital increase marks a step in the group's efforts to build technology businesses serving regional markets, highlighting opportunities for expansion under Saudi Vision 2030.
Chief executive Sara Al-Sheikh said the group's next phase would focus on closer integration between its portfolio companies, allowing them to draw on shared technology, data and operational expertise to accelerate growth.
Saudi Arabia will remain central to iMENA's strategy as it expands its presence and investments in the kingdom.
The transaction comes as the group seeks to increase the scale of its digital businesses and pursue further growth across regional markets.

articles.title: Cuándo se puede cargar el teléfono con el cargador de una notebook y qué precauciones tomar
articles.text:
Cargar el celular es seguro con el transformador de una computadora portátil siempre que ambos aparatos compartan la ficha USB-C y cuenten con el protocolo de entrega de energía, una tecnología inteligente que dosifica la electricidad para proteger la batería. Gracias a esta compatibilidad, cualquier persona puede llevar un solo enchufe en la mochila y utilizarlo tanto para trabajar como para revivir el teléfono sin correr riesgos de cortocircuitos o averías.
La unificación de estos conectores se aceleró a partir de las regulaciones que sancionó la Unión Europea, cuyo propósito fue terminar con la proliferación de cables incompatibles. Sobre esta tendencia de consumo, el diario estadounidense The Washington Post constató que los cargadores de laptops y tabletas resultan alternativas muy confiables para dar energía a los teléfonos móviles, dejando atrás aquellos viejos enchufes de cinco vatios que demoraban horas enteras en completar el proceso.
Las condiciones técnicas para conectar el teléfono a la fuente de la computadora
La tranquilidad detrás de esta conexión descansa en USB Power Delivery, un mecanismo de comunicación digital que dialoga entre la fuente y el receptor antes de transferir electricidad. De acuerdo con las especificaciones técnicas del fabricante HP, el transformador no empuja toda su fuerza a ciegas: el teléfono solicita el voltaje exacto que puede tolerar y el cargador restringe su entrega a ese límite concertado.
Por este motivo, enchufar un teléfono moderno a una fuente potente de 65 vatios no arruina los componentes. El circuito regulador del propio teléfono actúa como un filtro que toma la energía necesaria y descarta cualquier excedente.
En este mismo sentido, la compañía Apple aclara en sus guías oficiales que los iPhone y las tabletas iPad pueden conectarse sin problemas a los adaptadores USB-C de las computadoras MacBook, siempre que se utilicen cables en buen estado y homologados bajo normas de seguridad eléctrica.
La potencia de la notebook no acelera la recarga más allá del límite del celular
Tener a mano un enchufe de gran capacidad no significa que el teléfono vaya a llenarse en un abrir y cerrar de ojos. La velocidad depende del fabricante del teléfono, sumado a la resistencia que ofrezca el cable. Si un modelo se diseñó para absorber hasta 25 vatios, ese será su techo inamovible, aunque la fuente conectada a la pared pueda entregar 100 vatios o 140 vatios.
Cuando alguno de los accesorios conectados carece de soporte para transferencias veloces, el sistema recurre automáticamente a una marcha lenta de resguardo. Esta protección previene subidas bruscas de temperatura y prolonga los años de funcionamiento útiles del teléfono, destacan desde The Washington Post.
Qué precauciones tomar con los cables, el calor y las certificaciones
Los peligros reales al momento de recargar no radican en la potencia del transformador, sino en el deterioro físico de los accesorios y el ambiente circundante. La tecnológica Google advierte en las guías oficiales de seguridad de sus adaptadores de 30 vatios sobre el riesgo crítico de emplear cables dañados o pelados.
Al mismo tiempo, la empresa exige asegurar una ventilación adecuada tanto para el cargador como para el dispositivo y evitar fuentes de calor, una pauta que en la práctica desaconseja apoyar los equipos sobre superficies blandas que atrapen temperatura mientras reciben energía.
La pauta preventiva indispensable consiste en utilizar accesorios que exhiban sellos de certificación oficiales, como las normas de seguridad eléctrica y el aval de la asociación USB Implementers Forum, aseguran expertos consultados por The Washington Post.
La aparición de calor excesivo al tacto, zumbidos extraños, olor a plástico quemado o mensajes en la pantalla que alerten sobre accesorios incompatibles representan avisos inmediatos para desenchufar el equipo de la pared y verificar su estado antes de volver a conectarlo.

articles.title: Google a découvert des agents IA pirates à l'assaut de plusieurs sites français
articles.text:
Google tire la sonnette d’alarme au sujet des cyberattaques animées par l’IA. Dans son nouveau rapport AI Threat Tracker, le Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), la division de veille du géant américain, révèle avoir franchi un cap inquiétant dans ses découvertes.
« Au cours du dernier trimestre, le GTIG a identifié pour la première fois des acteurs malveillants utilisant des outils reposant sur des LLM (NDLR : large language model) pour automatiser entièrement la découverte et l’exploitation de vulnérabilités, sans humain dans la boucle », écrivent les chercheurs de Google.
 Hackers are now using LLMs to continuously scan software updates, spot newly fixed bugs, and build attacks before teams can apply the fix — all without human involvement. That’s according to the latest report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group.
We're helping defenders…
— News from Google (@NewsFromGoogle) November 16, 2026
Des sites français dans le viseur
La France est en première ligne, indique Google. D’après les données récupérées par les chercheurs, les pirates s’en prennent en priorité à des sites basés en France. L’enquête a commencé par une erreur des pirates. Les chercheurs de Google ont alors découvert un serveur malveillant, laissé accessible en ligne par les truands. À l’intérieur, ils ont trouvé un outil de piratage. En s’appuyant sur différents grands modèles de langage, celui-ci fait travailler plusieurs agents IA ensemble dans le but de commettre des cyberattaques.
Les pirates s’intéressent « particulièrement aux sites web français liés aux secteurs des médias et du divertissement, ainsi qu’au secteur de l’éducation », détaille le rapport. Sur le serveur, Google a aussi trouvé des données dérobées aux victimes. Il est possible que les cybercriminels à l’origine de l’opération proviennent de Russie. En effet, l’outil de piratage basé sur l’IA était configuré en russe. Néanmoins, Google n’attribue l’opération à aucun groupe criminel ni à aucun État.
À lire aussi : Google corrige d’urgence une 8e faille Chrome exploitée par des pirates, installez vite la mise à jour
Des correctifs de sécurité transformés en armes
L’outil est redoutablement simple. L’outil « compare le code avant et après l’annonce des correctifs, analyse les résultats pour identifier des vulnérabilités potentielles, rédige des exploits et les exécute automatiquement sans intervention humaine », explique Google. En clair, les pirates n’ont même plus besoin de dénicher eux-mêmes des failles inédites. Il leur suffit d’attendre qu’un éditeur publie une mise à jour de sécurité, pour en déduire la vulnérabilité qui a été colmatée. Les pirates s’en servent alors pour attaquer les sites qui n’ont pas encore installé la mise à jour.
Les pirates « utilisent ces technologies pour mener leurs opérations à grande vitesse et à grande échelle, sans avoir besoin de vulnérabilités zero-day pour y parvenir », explique John Hultquist, analyste en chef du GTIG. Les hackers n’ont plus besoin de s’embêter à dénicher des failles inconnues. Ils se servent simplement du travail effectué par les chercheurs et les éditeurs pour arriver à leurs fins. Pour John Hultquist, « il est bien plus facile de procéder à la rétro-ingénierie d’un correctif que de rechercher une vulnérabilité zero-day ».
À lire aussi : « Ils se sont fait passer pour des membres de l’équipe » – plusieurs IA Gemini ont lancé une cyberattaque
Une course contre la montre
L’outil déniché par Google n’est pas un cas isolé. Les chercheurs ont aussi découvert que des cybercriminels et des espions ont exploité des outils de piratage dopés à l’IA, comme CAIRN, PentAGI ou CyberStrikeAI, pour faciliter les intrusions. Selon les chercheurs de CrowdStrike, quatre autres gangs ont déjà confié leurs cyberattaques à l’IA au cours des derniers mois. Google a cependant une bonne nouvelle. Selon l’entreprise, les IA exploitées par des hackers ne sont pas infaillibles. Certains des programmes d’attaque générés par l’IA n’ont tout simplement pas fonctionné comme prévu.
Selon Google, l’IA réduit considérablement le délai dont disposent les entreprises pour installer leurs mises à jour avant d’être attaquées. C’est désormais la période entre le correctif d’une faille, et son installation, qui est la plus exploitée par les cybercriminels. Google cite l’exemple de PaperCut, un logiciel de gestion d’imprimantes. Quatre jours seulement après la divulgation de deux failles, la société GreyNoise a repéré une campagne menée avec l’aide de l’IA contre des centaines d’organisations.
« Dans un avenir proche, les entreprises vont subir une pression considérable pour accélérer leurs cycles de déploiement des correctifs de sécurité et pourraient même devoir faire des choix difficiles pour suivre le rythme », prévient John Hultquist.

Source : Google Threat Intelligence Group

Cómo se han escogido los ganadores de los Premios Xataka
Para elegir a los ganadores de los Premios Xataka Verisure 2026 seguimos la mecánica de ediciones anteriores, que está dividida en tres fases:

articles.title: Some of the world's largest brands hit following Optimizely flaw — Salesforce, CNN, Fox News, BBC sites hit with malware
articles.text:
Some of the world's largest brands hit following Optimizely flaw — Salesforce, CNN, Fox News, BBC sites hit with malware
A bug in Optimizely allowed an attacker to deploy malicious JavaScript across the web
- Attackers compromised Optimizely and injected malicious JavaScript into more than 100 popular websites through a trusted content delivery path
- The payload stole cryptocurrency, harvested payment-card data, captured user information, and targeted iPhone visitors with exploit kits
- Optimizely removed the malicious code, revoked access, and patched the signup-flow vulnerability used in the attack
Threat actors broke into Optimizely and used it to deploy malicious code to more than 100 popular websites across the internet, with the code replacing people’s cryptocurrency wallet addresses, stealing credit card information, and even allowing attackers to take over iPhones, experts have said.
Optimizely is a digital experience platform that businesses use to manage their websites, create and optimize digital content, run A/B tests, and personalize customer experiences. It is used primarily by marketing and product teams to experiment with different features of the website, improving engagement, conversions, and ultimately - sales.
It is a hugely popular tool, one that’s used by hundreds of organizations in all sorts of industries. The attacker deployed 188 snippets onto 178 organizations. Most of them were in banking & finance (32), technology & SaaS (23), and retail & fashion (20), with some major names on the list: HSBC US, Equifax, Zoom, Salesforce, IKEA, ASOS, Peacock, CNN, BBC, Fox News, Alaska Airlines / Hawaiian Airlines, Virgin Media, Virgin Media O2, Vodafone Australia, O2, Ledger, and many others.
Exploiting a flaw
In a blog post, security researcher Scott Helme, who discovered the attack, explains what happened - each customer loads a JavaScript snippet from Optimizely’s Content Delivery Network (CDN), containing the company’s code, the customer’s experiments, and an optional field called Project JavaScript. This is custom code the customer writes in their own Optimizely dashboard which runs on every page.
According to Helme, the attacker wrote their own code into the Project JavaScript of customer projects and the file was served to multiple victims. It still went out from cdn.optimizely.com, with Optimizely’s certificate, from a known and trusted host.
In a statement, Optimizely said the attacker exploited a flaw in its Experimentation account signup flow to inject the malicious JavaScript code.
"Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in the Experimentation account signup flow," Optimizely said.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"They used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects. We have blocked access to the vulnerable path and deployed a fix. We have removed the injected code from affected projects. We have also ended active sessions, revoked tokens, and reset access for affected user accounts. Finally, we have blocked any code from being delivered in Cloudflare.
Helme says the threat actors rebuilt the payload 26 times in one day, adding features and cryptocurrency wallets. The payload did four key things: stole people’s crypto, skimmed compromised websites for customer credit cards, stole cookies and took screenshots, and deployed iOS hacking toolkits.
Fighting back
Crypto theft worked through clipboard jacking: the code would monitor the clipboard for copied wallets and replace them with attacker-owned ones when pasting.
That way, victims would copy one address and unknowingly paste an entirely different one, sending money to the attackers. The skimmer would monitor the sites for card numbers, expiry dates, and CVV secrets, and when it finds all three, it would send them to an attacker-owned server. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes (Stripe, Adyen and similar) were out of its reach, it was said.
Victims opening the websites on iPhones and iPads were served Coruna and DarkSword, exploit kits designed to abuse unpatched iOS vulnerabilities and steal sensitive information, including cryptocurrency wallet credentials and recovery phrases.
Helme says the threat actors stole just over $7,000 in this campaign. Most of it was in bitcoin (around $5,300), with the rest split between litecoin, USDT, and ether.
Most of the malicious code has now been removed, Helme stressed. Less than 24 hours after the first attack was spotted, the number of infected snippets was down to just one - TalkTalk.

articles.title: Air France, CNN, Zoom... 178 organisations touchées par une cyberattaque
articles.text:
C'est une cyberattaque d'ampleur qui a eu lieu en début de semaine. Car elle a touché de très nombreux grands noms, comme Air France ou CNN.
On n'arrête plus la scansion des cyberattaques, comme encore on l'apprend aujourd'hui avec une offensive qui a touché le géant des sondages Ispsos. Et ce début de semaine, il y a même eu une opération d'ampleur internationale par ses répercussions, qui ont touché des grands noms dans des secteurs aussi divers que la banque et la finance, la tech ou bien le commerce.
Un prestataire attaqué, 178 organisations majeures victimes
Vous ne connaissiez jusqu'à a aujourd'hui sûrement pas ce nom : Optimizely. C'est celui d'une société américaine éditrice d'outils de test de page web, et qui est le prestataire de nombreuses grandes entreprises internationales.
Elle a été la cible d'un malware, qui a exploité une faille dans le processus d'inscription d'Optimizely, diffusé ensuite chez ses clients. Et selon les premières analyses de Report URI, 188 fichiers contenant du code malveillant ont été à ce jour repérés, dans 178 organisations différentes.
Peu de résultats pour les attaquants
Leurs noms devraient vous dire quelque chose, puisque parmi ceux-ci, on compte par exemple CNN, Air France, IKEA, HSBC, la BBC ou bien Zoom. Le Javascript malveillant diffusé par les pirates pouvait détourner des transactions en cryptomonnaies, dérober des données bancaires, ou bien même permettre de cibler des iPhone dont l'iOS ne serait pas à jour.
Il faut noter que les 178 organismes victimes listées ne constituent pas une liste définitive, et que d'autres découvertes ne sont pas à exclure. Mais si celle-ci est impressionnante, le butin pour le moment recensé est à l'inverse assez faible. Report URI a pu, le 16 novembre, à 20h25, compter au total 7 040 dollars de fonds en cryptomonnaies transférés sur plusieurs adresses liées à la cyberattaque. L'attaque a au total duré 16 heures, avant qu'Optimizely ne bloque la faille.
Source : Cyberattaque.org

articles.title: Intel Prepares "Razor Lake" in Three Flavors: S, U, and L
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Intel Prepares "Razor Lake" in Three Flavors: S, U, and L
Intel appears to have prepared three versions of its next-generation "Razor Lake" platform, designated as S, U, and L, which provides a clearer picture of the company's future lineup, according to the latest set of Linux kernel patches. Additionally, there is a separate "Razor Lake" entry without a suffix, bringing the total to four processor identifiers. Intel engineer Tony Luck submitted the patch on November 13, following the publication of model numbers in Intel's updated instruction set reference. All four client entries belong to CPU Family 18. The desktop models use identifiers 0x06 and 0x0A for "Razor Lake" and "Razor Lake-S," respectively, while the mobile entries assign 0x07 to "Razor Lake-L" and 0x09 to "Razor Lake-U." There is no "Razor Lake-H" definition in this submission. However, these internal labels do not determine the final product range, and Intel has yet to explain what differentiates the underlying configurations.
Compiler work published on the same day provides another detail: GCC initially treats "Razor Lake" as an alias of "Nova Lake." Both targets share the instruction capabilities listed in the patch, including AVX10.2 and APX. This informs developers about which instructions the compiler can generate but reveals little about potential changes to core designs, cache capacity, or performance. A shared compiler profile alone cannot establish how closely the finished processors will resemble one another.For "Razor Lake," the kernel change is only a preparatory step. It provides identifiers that subsequent code can reference when handling particular processors. Core counts, clock speeds, power limits, and launch dates remain outside the scope of these submissions. More detailed patches will be needed before the software work offers a fuller view of how Intel intends to distinguish these variants. We hope to see more "Razor Lake" details next year, as the launch date is currently rumored to be 2028.
