articles.title: Cade deve abrir processo contra Apple por restrições ao NFC do iPhone • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Cade deve abrir processo contra Apple por restrições ao NFC do iPhone
Negociação entre as partes não avançou. Órgão deve investigar se as restrições da Apple dificultam a oferta de Pix por aproximação no iOS.
O Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) deve abrir um processo administrativo contra a Apple para investigar se as condições impostas pela empresa para acessar o NFC do iPhone prejudicam a concorrência no mercado brasileiro de pagamentos.
A discussão também afeta a falta de oferta do Pix por aproximação no iOS por bancos e fintechs. Segundo a Folha de São Paulo, a Superintendência-Geral do órgão deve avançar com o caso após não chegar a um entendimento com a empresa.
Instituições já se manifestaram sobre as limitações. Segundo o Banco Central, a integração no iPhone oferece condições que dificultam a criação de alternativas ao Apple Pay, inclusive para o Pix por aproximação. Há cerca de um ano, o PicPay também atribuiu à Apple a ausência do recurso no iPhone.
A Febraban argumenta que o sistema da Apple limita as opções oferecidas aos consumidores, enquanto a Zetta diz que as “APIs necessárias para processar o Pix na tecnologia NFC” são bloqueadas pela Apple, que “exige a utilização da sua própria plataforma paga”.
Segundo a Folha, a autarquia discutiu com a Apple uma saída para ampliar o acesso ao NFC, mas as conversas não avançaram. A empresa estaria resistindo a adotar no Brasil condições semelhantes às oferecidas na União Europeia, onde a Apple concordou (após uma multa de cerca de R$ 230 bilhões) em liberar o acesso ao NFC para desenvolvedores.
A Apple contesta a interpretação do órgão de que mantém o NFC fechado a concorrentes. Nos autos, a companhia afirma que desenvolvedores já dispõem de duas formas para oferecer pagamentos por aproximação: integrar cartões ao Apple Pay ou usar a plataforma NFC & SE, aberta a aplicativos externos desde outubro de 2024.
A empresa defende, também, o uso do Secure Element, componente físico dedicado a proteger informações usadas nas transações. Segundo a Apple, a arquitetura oferece mais segurança contra fraudes e malwares do que soluções baseadas em software, como o HCE. Segundo a Apple, as tarifas que cobra ajudam a financiar a manutenção desse sistema.
Na avaliação da companhia, o NFC não é indispensável para competir no mercado brasileiro. Dados do Banco Central, apresentados pela empresa, mostram que houve registro de cerca de 2,09 milhões de transações com Pix por aproximação em setembro deste ano, contra 3,14 bilhões feitos por QR Codes dinâmicos.
Para as entidades que questionam as práticas da Apple, porém, o QR Code não elimina o problema concorrencial envolvendo o acesso a tecnologia dos aparelhos.
A conversão do inquérito em processo administrativo leva o caso a uma etapa formal de investigação, na qual a empresa poderá apresentar sua defesa e a Superintendência-Geral aprofundará a análise sobre as condições impostas ao acesso ao NFC.
Se entender que houve abuso de poder econômico ou outra infração prevista na Lei 12.529/2011, o caso seguirá para julgamento pelo tribunal do Cade.
Após uma outra investigação, concluída no ano passado, a Apple passou a permitir outros meios de pagamento no iOS, após decisões parecidas nos Estados Unidos e na Europa. Em um acordo posterior com o Cade, a companhia também passou a permitir a instalação de lojas de aplicativos alternativas no sistema.

articles.title: Brazilian businessman arrested for attempted murder after planting explosive-filled game console that detonated in electronics store — perp tried to kill business rival, device delivered by unsuspecting motorcyclist working for a delivery service
articles.text:
Brazilian businessman arrested for attempted murder after planting explosive-filled game console that detonated in electronics store — perp tried to kill business rival, device delivered by unsuspecting motorcyclist working for a delivery service
The target suffered minor injuries
A São Paulo businessman has been arrested by police on suspicion of sending a game console stuffed with explosives to the electronics store of a rival in an attempt to kill him. The device then exploded. On Monday, Military Police executed a warrant against Everton Yoshizumi Lima, who is suspected of perpetrating the outrageous attack, G1 reports.
On October 23, 2026, at around 5:30 pm, a delivery person dropped off a video game console at an electronics repair shop, with the cover that it was being left for modifications requested by the customer. Police say the device had an explosive planted inside that was programmed to detonate upon receipt. "Unaware of its contents, the store owner put the video game console in a drawer and continued working," the report states. The device ignited and exploded, causing severe damage and injuring two people: the owner of the store and a friend who was at the scene. The whole thing was captured on video, which you can see by expanding the tweet below:
The device was found to have two explosive charges of the same magnitude inside, but only one of the devices went off, possibly limiting the capacity for damage and injury. The report notes that investigators believe the intent of the device was to kill the victim, given the amount of explosives. The console was delivered to the store by an unsuspecting motorcyclist who was working for a delivery app company and had no idea they were carrying a bomb.
The request appears to have been traced back to Lima, who is the main suspect in the attack. Lima purportedly owns other electronics stores in the area, including two on the same street where this store was recently opened, labeling the motive as "business competition." "The new store had been advertised through a social media campaign and the distribution of flyers," the report states. "Annoyed by the competition, the suspect allegedly decided to eliminate the competitor, according to the line of investigation."
According to the report, Lima was arrested during the course of an investigation into a possible motorcycle theft. It appears that Lima was the owner of the target vehicle, and that police visited in advance, suspecting someone might try to steal it. While checking his data, it was found that Lima had an outstanding arrest warrant for his suspected involvement in the attack.

articles.title: Meta warns it may pull encrypted services from Canada over controversial bill C-22
articles.text:
Meta warns it may pull encrypted services from Canada over controversial bill C-22
Speaking before a Senate committee, Meta executives warned that complying with Ottawa's surveillance bill while keeping services like WhatsApp secure is technically impossible.
- Meta warned Canadian senators that Bill C-22 would make secure end-to-end encryption technically impossible
- Executives testified before the Senate national security committee alongside Signal and Tailscale
- Meta refused to rule out pulling services like WhatsApp from Canada rather than compromise user security
Meta has joined the escalating industry revolt against Canada's proposed lawful access legislation, warning lawmakers that it may have to consider pulling encrypted communications tools from the country.
The tech giant behind Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp cautioned that the draft law would undermine user security by demanding data access capabilities that cannot coexist with mathematical privacy.
Whether you are using a secure chat app or setting up the best VPN to shield your web traffic, these apps rely entirely on strict end-to-end encryption. Under Bill C-22, known as the Lawful Access Act, Canadian authorities could compel electronic service providers to modify their systems to help police and intelligence agencies intercept communications.
Appearing on Monday evening before the Standing Senate Committee on National Security, Defence and Veterans Affairs, Meta delivered a blunt challenge to the proposal.
The hearing took place as Prime Minister Mark Carney's government faces growing pressure from digital rights groups and tech firms, with representatives from Signal and Tailscale also appearing before the committee to lodge objections, according to Bloomberg.
'Technically impossible' to comply
During Monday's committee hearing, Meta told lawmakers that Ottawa's demands ignore software realities.
"Ultimately, the Canadian government would be enforcing and imposing a law that it is not technically feasible to comply with and still offer secure, end-to-end encrypted services to Canadians," Robyn Greene, Meta's director of privacy and public policy, told senators, as reported by CBC.
When asked if the legislation would prompt Meta to withdraw services from Canada, Rachel Curran, Meta's head of public policy for Canada, said the company would have to "review all of our options". However, Curran confirmed that leaving is something the company would have to "consider".
Curran previously told Bloomberg that weakening system security is a "red line" for the company, warning that the bill would turn private platforms into "an arm of the government's surveillance apparatus".

Why tech platforms and VPNs oppose Bill C-22
Opposition to the draft law has mounted steadily since Canada's Bill C-22 passed the House of Commons in June.
The primary friction point lies in Part 2 of the bill, which authorizes confidential ministerial orders requiring electronic service providers to build ways to give access to law enforcement upon request. It also allows regulations compelling providers to store sensitive customer metadata, such as connection records and IP addresses, for up to six months.
Can police really access private chats without breaking security for everyone? Cryptographers and privacy advocates insist they cannot. If software engineers build an interception mechanism for domestic authorities, cybercriminals and foreign spies will inevitably find and exploit that same mechanism.
Ottawa introduced amendments barring orders that mandate a "systemic vulnerability," but industry leaders argue that definition is vague and leaves essential protections open to interpretation.
The coalition resisting the bill extends well beyond social media.
Google warned Bill C-22 could break end-to-end encryption, while Apple warned the powers risk customer security. Messaging provider Signal announced it would rather leave Canada than weaken its protocol. Canadian provider Windscribe pledged no changes to its no-logs policy, while advocacy groups have urged the government to fix the bill and pushed for European authorities to intervene.
With the Senate committee representing the bill's final legislative hurdle before potential passage, platforms are betting that the threat of service withdrawals will push Canadian lawmakers to amend the text.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return to Nvidia, in first statement since resignation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return to Nvidia, in first statement since resignation
Former Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang today said he’s open to returning to his old post.
Huang expressed his willingness to be reinstated in a post on X. It marks his first public statement since his ouster from Nvidia last week. He resigned following revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former cloud executive suspected to be a Chinese spy.
Huang apologized for his conduct in today’s X post. He went on to cite recent calls for him to return as a factor behind his willingness to resume his work at Nvidia.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
Huang’s statement isn’t a complete surprise. On Sunday, the Financial Times reported that he had discussed a comeback with confidants. The paper said that a member of Huang’s circle was working to assemble a group of tech executives to support the effort.
Last Thursday, an anonymous user launched an online petition to reinstate Huang. It drew the support of several prominent tech executives including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games Inc. CEO Tim Sweeney. The petition also garnered 180,000 other signatures, although it appears that not all of them are genuine. One entry spotted by Business Insider read “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor.”
It’s unclear whether the efforts to reinstate Huang are realistic. On Monday, CNBC reported that Nvidia’s board is not considering bringing him back. And today, on Nvidia’s earnings call, Chair Harvey Jones repeated that the board doesn’t intend to reinstate him. Earlier, sources had told Reuters that he had misled the chipmaker’s general counsel and chief marketing officer about his relationship with Alice Huang.
While some U.S. officials believe Alice Huang was part of an espionage operation, others see the evidence as inconclusive. On Thursday, sources told CNN that the intelligence collected on her doesn’t prove she’s a spy. The same day, the Justice Department stated it had not yet concluded Alice Huang is a Chinese asset.
Huang is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider that has ordered billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips. The Justice Department is investigating the company over alleged export control violations. As early as 2024, officials identified “suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion.”
The Wall Street Journal today reported that Nvidia has hired a prominent executive search firm to find a new CEO. According to the paper, it plans to evaluate both internal and external candidates. Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress currently leads the company as interim CEO.
Kress also supervises a new national security and export control oversight committee that Nvidia formed today. It will be responsible for the company’s national security policies, adherence to export control rules and global trade risk management.
The committee comprises three Nvidia directors on launch. It will carry out its work in collaboration with the chipmaker’s executives and external experts in fields such as law, national security and global trade compliance. Nvidia says that the committee will meet at least once per quarter.

articles.title: Everspin Looks to Broaden MRAM Adoption with LPDDR Standard - EE Times
articles.text:
Giving magnetoresistive RAM (MRAM) access to the low power DDR (LPDDR) ecosystem requires more than adapting a memory interface; it needs controller developers to have confidence there is enough customer demand to put support into silicon.
Everspin Technologies sees the development of a standard as the pathway forward. That is why Steffen Hellmold, the company’s VP of corporate strategy, is chairing a new JEDEC task group under JEDEC’s JC-42.6 Low Power Memories Subcommittee to explore an LPDDR persistent memory (PMEM) standard, he told EE Times in an interview. “If you want to have something to happen, then you need to be willing to contribute.”
Everspin’s motivation is practical because its experience adapting DDR controllers for MRAM does not translate readily to the newer LPDDR implementations it wants to target, Hellmold said.
The company’s DDR4 MRAM has been implemented in systems such as IBM’s FlashCore Module by tweaking DRAM host controllers to handle smaller page sizes and slightly different timings. Hellmold said that was workable because the controllers were soft IP. In AMD Xilinx FPGAs, for example, the memory interface generator could adapt DDR4 soft IP for MRAM.
Looking toward LPDDR5 and LPDDR6, Hellmold said the available controller implementations instead rely on hard IP, shifting those changes upstream to controller suppliers. “Hard IP means that you need to convince a host controller manufacturer to modify their host controller to also support MRAM,” he said.
IP vendors will only make that investment if there is a standard and enough customer demand, Hellmold said, but the payoff is the size of the LPDDR controller ecosystem. “If we can leverage that and slightly adapt those host controller IP blocks to work with MRAM, then we have a ubiquitous on-ramp for MRAM to easily dovetail into a much larger number of systems and applications.”
Details of the JEDEC work are confidential, Hellmold said, but he outlined three types of changes that will need to be made to achieve a standard. The proposed work involves additions, substitutions, and reductions rather than reproducing every capability of an LPDDR DRAM interface. He said MRAM does not require refresh or support for DRAM’s highest speed bins, but it does need accommodation for page sizes measured in tens or hundreds of bytes rather than kilobytes, along with somewhat longer timings.
Hellmold said these accommodations must be configurable, and that the flexibility previously available through soft IP needs to become part of what controller implementations expose to software.
For now, the JEDEC task group is an exploratory initiative, not an approved specification, aimed at leveraging existing LPDDR infrastructure while limiting changes to DRAM standards and host controllers.
Hellmold said participants in the group span edge AI, IoT, industrial, automotive, enterprise storage, and hyperscale data centers, including prospective users as well as suppliers. Even with a standard, controller IP vendors must still adopt it and get it into silicon, so he’d like to see as many potential users as possible come forward with their requirements.
There are several applications that could benefit should a standard come to fruition, Hellmold said. Everspin customers are asking for gigabyte-scale solutions, and higher-density MRAM coupled with an LPDDR persistent-memory interface would address that requirement.
Hellmold said MRAM’s trajectory puts a more cost-effective alternative to battery-backed DRAM within reach, while using MRAM as a persistent write cache ahead of NAND for checkpointing could reduce the time processors wait while preserving state. “There are tangible opportunities within line of sight,” he said.
This JEDEC initiative aligns with other efforts to broaden MRAM’s reach. Everspin recently demonstrated a 4-GB pool of CXL-attached DDR4 MRAM at the SNIA Developer Conference, which Hellmold presented as a persistent cache tier between DRAM and NAND rather than a replacement for NAND.
MRAM in the data center isn’t new either, but NOR flash shortages and AI workloads are helping to broaden its use in servers, data centers, and satellites.

articles.title: Recherches secrètes : Google ajoute un mode « temporaire » à son Mode IA, voici comment l'activer
articles.text:
Une idée de cadeau à garder secrète, une question médicale gênante ou encore une recherche ponctuelle qui n’a rien à faire dans vos recommandations ? Pour ce genre de requête, Google a décidé de lancer les discussions temporaires dans le Mode IA, la version conversationnelle de son moteur de recherche. La fonction est en cours de déploiement dans le monde entier, sur ordinateur comme sur smartphone, et dans toutes les langues où le Mode IA est disponible, dont le français.
Pour l’utiliser, il suffit de cliquer sur l’icône des discussions temporaires, en haut à droite de l’interface du Mode IA, puis de poser ses questions comme d’habitude. La session est alors « déconnectée de votre compte », explique Google : les réponses ne tiennent pas compte de vos préférences passées, les échanges n’influencent pas votre personnalisation future et ils ne sont pas sauvegardés dans votre historique. La discussion disparaît dès que l’onglet est fermé, et l’on retrouve ensuite son Mode IA habituel, sans avoir à modifier le moindre paramètre.
Temporaire ne veut pas dire totalement privé
Google ne précise pas, en revanche, si ces échanges sont conservés pendant un certain temps sur ses serveurs. La nuance a son importance. Dans l’application Gemini, qui propose une fonction similaire depuis l’an dernier, les discussions temporaires sont gardées « jusqu’à 72 heures » pour formuler les réponses et traiter d’éventuels retours, selon Google, même si elles ne servent ni à personnaliser l’assistant ni à entraîner ses modèles. Chez OpenAI, les discussions temporaires de ChatGPT peuvent être conservées jusqu’à 30 jours pour des raisons de sécurité. Une discussion temporaire n’est donc pas une discussion totalement privée : elle évite surtout que vos recherches ressurgissent plus tard dans votre compte.
À lire aussi : Google dévoile Gemini 4 Carbon, l’IA qui veut repousser les limites de l’IA
Cette nouveauté arrive alors que Google pousse de plus en plus son Mode IA, qui capte désormais une part croissante des recherches, au point de bousculer le modèle publicitaire du moteur aux États-Unis.

articles.title: Intel Publishes Benchmarks for D270 "Crescent Island" GPU, Claims Wins Over RTX PRO 6000
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Intel Publishes Benchmarks for D270 "Crescent Island" GPU, Claims Wins Over RTX PRO 6000
Intel's GPU D270 AI accelerator card, previously known as "Crescent Island," just got some first-party benchmarks. According to Intel, the GPU is up to 5.9 times faster than NVIDIA's RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition in FP64 financial workloads. Going through the individual test results, the D270 system posted a 5.6x lead in European Black-Scholes, 4.6x in Binomial, and 1.92x in American Black-Scholes. Intel also points out the fact that the D270 runs at 350 W, while the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 has a 600 W power limit. Most of the lead seems to come from the D270's 32 Xe3P cores, each handling 64 FP64 FMA operations at native full rate. These benchmarks were published at SC26 in Chicago.
As for the AI figures, they are a lot more modest. Intel claims up to 29% lower latency on the Drex decision model and 1.12x the output token throughput on Qwen3-30B-A3B in FP8. These tests were both run against a single RTX PRO 6000. In the financial tests previously mentioned, the NVIDIA system had eight RTX PRO 6000 cards running against a single D270, though Intel doesn't mention how many were used per run. Intel also showed FP32 seismic modeling with Veridien, although performance figures were left out for this one. All results come from pre-production silicon, and it is important to note that these are first-party results that are intended to showcase the best-case scenarios for the D270. As a reminder, the D270 "Crescent Island" GPU can pack up to 480 GB of memory, while Intel-branded cards come with 160 GB of LPDDR5X as standard. There's still no official word on pricing or launch date.

articles.title: Amazon Prime se partage désormais à deux en France, et sans payer un euro de plus
articles.text:
Amazon lance le service Amazon Family en France. Gratuit, il permet aux membres Prime de partager les avantages de leur abonnement avec un autre adulte du foyer, qui profite de la livraison gratuite et de Prime Video sans payer.
Depuis ce mardi 17 novembre officiellement, Amazon Family est disponible pour les membres Prime en France, qui peuvent partager une partie des avantages de leur abonnement avec un autre adulte de leur foyer. Le service, sans frais supplémentaires, couvre notamment la livraison Prime, Amazon Music et Prime Video. Chacun garde son compte, son historique et ses recommandations. Dans la foulée du lancement d'« Alexa pour vos Achats », Amazon encadre aussi l'utilisation d'un moyen de paiement partagé, pas obligatoire pour autant. On observe que la France rejoint un club fermé de cinq pays où la formule existait déjà.
Amazon Family débarque en France, voici ce que votre abonnement Prime permet de partager
Le premier avantage du lot Amazon Family, et non des moindres, c'est la livraison Prime gratuite et illimitée sur les articles éligibles. En France métropolitaine (hors Corse), Prime promet en effet une livraison en un jour ouvré sur des millions d'articles éligibles. À Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Lille et dans huit autres villes, la livraison peut même arriver le soir même pour les commandes éligibles de 35 euros ou plus. L'invité a aussi accès aux plus de 100 millions de titres d'Amazon Music en France métropolitaine, aux jeux vidéo gratuits d'Amazon Luna et aux remises réservées aux abonnés, Prime Day et Jours Flash Prime compris.
Pour les séries et les films, attention, il faut lire les petites lignes. Prime Video fait bien partie du lot, mais Amazon précise « avec publicités et SVOD uniquement ». L'invité a donc droit au catalogue inclus dans l'abonnement, version avec pub. Amazon ne dit pas si l'option sans publicité est partagée. D'autres avantages de Prime manquent aussi dans la liste, comme la sélection d'ebooks et de livres audio ou le stockage illimité d'Amazon Photos.
Concernant le prix, on vous le disait et c'est une bonne nouvelle : il reste la même. Oui, Amazon Family est inclus sans surcoût, à condition toutefois que l'un des deux adultes ait un abonnement Prime actif, à 6,99 euros par mois ou 69,90 euros par an. L'invité n'a strictement rien à payer. En revanche, on ne peut inviter qu'un seul adulte du foyer. Il faut savoir être raisonnable, nous fait comprendre le géant américain, il s'agit ici d'une formule pour deux, pas pour toute la tribu.
Chacun son compte, c'est possible, même avec Amazon Family
N'ayez crainte, vivre ensemble ne veut pas dire tout mettre en commun. Chaque membre du service garde son propre compte Amazon, avec son historique de commandes et ses recommandations. Les achats de l'un ne viennent donc pas parasiter les suggestions de l'autre, et aucun mot de passe ni code à usage unique ne circule entre eux.
Il y a aussi la question ô combien importante du paiement. De facto, celui qui envoie l'invitation devient « Administrateur Amazon Family » et choisit un moyen de paiement commun. L'autre peut l'utiliser, il n'en voit que les quatre derniers chiffres, le nom du titulaire, la date d'expiration et l'adresse de facturation. Chaque achat payé avec cette carte envoie à l'Administrateur une notification avec le montant total. Mais cette carte reste facultative. Chacun des membres peut aussi payer avec son propre moyen de paiement, c'est à noter.
Pour activer Amazon Family, il faut aller dans « Votre compte », puis dans la rubrique « Votre Amazon Family ». On y invite alors l'adulte de son choix, qui accepte et a tout de suite accès aux avantages. Trois étapes seulement, et aucun abonnement en plus. Pour Amazon, c'est aussi une façon d'installer un peu plus dans les foyers un abonnement qui revendique désormais plus de 200 millions de membres dans le monde.

articles.title: Los 30 FPS de 'GTA VI' en todas las consolas es un fastidio. También el compromiso para que se vea como se ve
articles.text:
'GTA VI' está al caer y, superada la polémica por la ausencia de un formato físico de verdad y por lo que puede ocupar en consolas con un almacenamiento tan comprometido como Xbox Series S, la pregunta es por qué el juego más caro y ambicioso de la historia sólo va a 30 frames por segundo en todas las consolas, incluida PS5 Pro.
Y la respuesta es que no tiene nada que ver con el presupuesto, sino con una mezcla entre la ambición desmedida de este juego y la limitación de las consolas: el procesador.
Los 30 FPS. Hace unos días, cuando Rockstar confirmó que la predescarga del juego ya estaba disponible, también dio algunos detalles sobre el apartado visual. Hasta ahora, todo lo que hemos visto (incluidos los 30 minutos de Netflix) se ha visto corriendo en una PS5 base y se especulaba con que PS5 Pro podría tener algunas mejoras visuales y de rendimiento.
Lo primero sí parece asegurado, ya que la compañía detalló que "la experiencia visual en PS5 Pro presentará una mayor claridad de imagen gracias al PSSR y sombras con trazados de rayos". Sin embargo, también señalaron que el juego irá a 30 frames por segundo en todas las plataformas, lo que hizo que se levantara alguna queja porque cómo era posible que un juego con este presupuesto fuera sólo a 30 FPS.
El precio del fotograma. La respuesta es que no tiene nada que ver con lo que haya costado el juego, sino con los compromisos. Cuando el medio especializado Digital Foundry puso sus analíticos ojos sobre el vídeo de Netflix, comentaron que era "el ejemplo de renderización en tiempo real más impresionante que han visto", estimando una resolución 1.440p nativa. También calcularon los 30 frames por segundo cuya confirmación llegó a posteriori, y la explicación es que el cuello de botella está en la CPU.
A 30 frames por segundo, la consola tiene unos 33 milisegundos para calcular y dibujar cada imagen. Eso permite que el mundo tenga el detalle que tiene y, sobre todo, que haya tal cantidad de NPC con sus rutinas únicas. en conjunto, es una simulación extremadamente viva que es posible gracias a que Rockstar ha optimizado todo alrededor de esos 30 frames por segundo.
Si se hubiera optado por ir a una tasa de 60 FPS, la consola tendría la mitad de tiempo para calcular cada imagen, unos 16,7 milisegundos. Habría que recortar todo lo que depende de la CPU como peatones, tráfico, físicas, objetos e IA. Y ahí está el compromiso: Rockstar quiere un mundo vivo que una consola actual, simplemente, no puede simular debido a ese cuello de botella de la CPU.
PS5 Pro no cambia la ecuación. Xbox Series X es algo más potente que PS5 en cuanto a su GPU, pero no en su CPU y, por eso, las dos van a 30 FPS, pero había quien tenía la esperanza de que una PS5 Pro más potente que la máquina de Microsoft pudiera 'tirar' al doble de fotogramas. La situación es exactamente la misma.
Aunque la GPU sí es claramente más potente que la de PS5 base, y por eso puede mostrar en el mismo mundo un trazado de rayos en tiempo real para sombras, la mejora en la CPU respecto al modelo base es de apenas un 7%, insuficiente para aumentar la tasa de fotogramas manteniendo la simulación del mundo, pero aprovechando la GPU para mejorar la calidad de imagen.
Está por ver que añadan en algún momento un modo a 40 FPS o con el frame-rate desbloqueado gracias a VRR, aunque no está confirmado.
¿Esperanza? Esta generación hemos tenido ejemplos de títulos que llegaban y, al tiempo, añadían modos de más rendimiento o incluso pantalla partida (algo que consume una burrada de recursos y que se acaba de anunciar para 'Star Wars Galactic Racer', por ejemplo). Sin embargo, en el caso de 'GTA VI', parece que no depende de la optimización porque habría que hacer brujería para que, de pronto, se pudiera configurar un modo "Rendimiento" que se sacara otros 30 frames por segundo de la manga manteniendo la simulación del mundo.
Sería algo digno de ver, pero aquí la esperanza queda en esa futura versión de PC en la que el juego no esté costreñido por el procesador de unas consolas que no dejan de tener seis años a sus espaldas. Y, claro, esa esperanza también está en una versión más optimizada para Xbox Helix y PS6, ya que si 'GTA V' salió en tres generaciones distintas, añadiendo mejoras visuales en cada una de las reediciones en consolas y PC, nada impide que Rockstar repita jugada con 'GTA VI'.
Hay que amortizar los más de 1.000 millones que se estima habría costado el desarrollo.

How did a Philips spinoff that began with a machine nobody wanted become Europe’s most valuable tech company and the sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography tools? In this video interview, EE Times talks with Marc Hijink, a technology reporter at Dutch daily NRC and author of “Focus: The ASML Way.” Hijink covered ASML for years, then got rare, independent access to the company’s sites, suppliers, and customers around the world.
Hijink explains how ASML’s early reliance on outside partners such as Zeiss made it a “lightweight boxer.” The company could spread the pain of industry downturns across its supply chain and keep spending on research while competitors cut back. He also discusses the confrontational engineering culture that former CTO Martin van den Brink built on purpose. And he describes the surprising chaos that remains at a company that builds $400 million machines. The alignment among customers, suppliers, and research partners that makes each new generation of lithography possible depends on globalization, Hijink said, and geopolitics is now pulling that apart.
The conversation also covers ASML’s partnership with imec, which dates back to the late 1980s. Hijink describes how a temporary High-NA EUV lab on ASML’s Veldhoven campus saved the industry about a year. He also previews his next project: Nexperia, the Chinese-owned Dutch maker of legacy chips at the center of a diplomatic clash between the Netherlands and China.
Nitin Dahad is executive editor of EE Times. An electronic engineering graduate from City University, he’s been an engineer, journalist and entrepreneur. He was part of ARC International’s startup team and took it public, and he co-founded a publication called The Chilli in the early 2000s. Nitin has also worked with National Semiconductor, GEC Plessey Semiconductors, Dialog Semiconductor, Marconi Instruments, Coresonic, Center for Integrated Photonics, IDENT Technology and Jennic. Nitin also held a role with government promoting U.K. technology globally in the U.S., Brazil, Middle East and Africa, and India.

articles.title: GTA 6 cambia el clima de Leonida: las tormentas y la niebla afectarán la forma de conducir y explorar
articles.text:
GTA 6 tendrá un sistema climático localizado y dinámico en Leonida, con tormentas tropicales, lluvias torrenciales y niebla que afectarán la conducción, la navegación y la exploración. Rockstar Games presentó estos detalles antes del lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto VI en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
La novedad importa porque el clima dejará de ser un cambio visual de fondo. La baja visibilidad en carretera, el oleaje en las zonas costeras y las aguas turbias en los pantanos modificarán situaciones habituales dentro del mundo abierto. La compañía desarrolló el sistema junto con The Weather Channel, que difundió pronósticos ficticios de distintas áreas de Leonida.
Rockstar Games recrea la inestabilidad meteorológica de Florida
El estado ficticio de Leonida se inspira en Florida, una región de Estados Unidos caracterizada por cambios meteorológicos frecuentes. Por esa razón, Rockstar Games renovó la tecnología encargada de simular el tiempo en GTA 6, con condiciones que variarán entre zonas y se mantendrán durante periodos determinados.
Owen Shepherd, vicepresidente de Arte, Iluminación y Renderizado de Rockstar Games, explicó que el equipo buscó un sistema más persistente, localizado y dinámico que el de entregas anteriores. Los jugadores pasarán de cielos despejados a grandes nubes cumulonimbos, propias de tormentas intensas.
La colaboración con The Weather Channel funcionó como una presentación de las condiciones que podrán aparecer durante la partida. Los reportes describen cómo el clima puede alterar la visibilidad, los desplazamientos y la percepción de los peligros que rodean a cada zona.
Las lluvias dificultarán los trayectos por carretera
En los Cayos de Leonida, las previsiones incluyen lluvias intensas que reducirán de forma considerable la visibilidad al conducir. La recomendación ficticia de revisar los faros apunta a que los vehículos deberán adaptarse a trayectos con menor campo de visión.
En Key Lento, las precipitaciones y las rachas de viento también complicarán la circulación. Las tormentas no solo cambiarán la imagen de la carretera, sino que podrán modificar las condiciones de conducción durante los desplazamientos entre ciudades y zonas rurales.
El diseño del clima plantea una diferencia frente a sistemas que alternan entre sol y lluvia sin mayores efectos. En GTA 6, un cambio meteorológico puede condicionar la elección de una ruta, la velocidad de un vehículo o la planificación de un viaje por zonas expuestas.
Rockstar Games todavía no detalló todos los efectos jugables. Sin embargo, los partes difundidos sugieren que la meteorología tendrá consecuencias directas en actividades que hasta ahora podían realizarse sin prestar atención al entorno.
La niebla y el oleaje cambiarán la exploración costera
Las zonas costeras de Leonida tendrán condiciones propias. En South Ocean Beach, una niebla marina densa podrá ocultar la vista del océano desde los hoteles. En Gambit Bay, la humedad podrá dejar una capa espesa sobre el agua al comienzo del día.
Cerca del Rusty Anchor, una tormenta tropical provocará fuerte oleaje y dificultará la navegación. La exploración por mar dependerá de las condiciones del agua y de la visibilidad, dos elementos que pueden variar según el lugar y el momento de la partida.
Los pantanos de Pelican Valley presentarán otro tipo de riesgo. Las tormentas enturbiarán aún más el agua, con lo que resultará más difícil detectar a los caimanes que habitan el área. El fenómeno conecta el clima con la exploración de la fauna y con los peligros de cada ecosistema.
Ese enfoque refuerza la idea de un mapa con condiciones propias para cada región. Los fenómenos costeros no tendrán el mismo efecto en los pantanos, las carreteras interiores o las áreas urbanas cercanas a Vice City.
GTA 6 llega el 19 de noviembre a PS5 y Xbox Series X|S
Grand Theft Auto VI se estrenará el jueves 19 de noviembre de 2026 en PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X y Xbox Series S. Rockstar Games eligió un desbloqueo regional: el juego estará disponible a las 00:00 de la hora local de cada tienda digital.
La predescarga está habilitada desde el 10 de noviembre para quienes reservaron la edición digital. El título requerirá hasta 212 GB de espacio libre en la unidad SSD. Las copias físicas incluirán un código de descarga y no un disco, por lo que también exigirán conexión a internet.
No habrá versión para PC en el lanzamiento. Rockstar tampoco comunicó una fecha para computadoras. Los usuarios de Xbox One no tendrán una edición nativa, aunque podrán acceder mediante Xbox Cloud Gaming con la configuración de Xbox Series S.
La campaña principal podría durar cerca de 50 horas, según información no confirmada por Rockstar. Completar el 100% del juego podría requerir hasta 200 horas, con actividades de exploración, misiones secundarias, fotografía de fauna y objetivos con elementos aleatorios.

articles.title: Senha mais usada do mundo em 2026 é velha conhecida • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Senha mais usada do mundo em 2026 é velha conhecida
Sequência numérica lidera ranking pela sétima vez em oito anos. Lista também inclui referências a jogos, memes e celebridades.
“123456” é novamente a senha mais comum do mundo, segundo levantamento da NordPass.
Estudo analisou credenciais expostas em vazamentos de dados de 44 países.
Referências a jogos, filmes, artistas e memes também aparecem entre as combinações identificadas.
A senha mais usada do mundo em 2026 continua sendo a conhecida sequência “123456”. Segundo levantamento da NordPass, a combinação liderou sete das oito edições anuais do ranking, mostrando que muitos usuários ainda recorrem a senhas fáceis de descobrir para proteger suas contas.
O relatório divulgado pela empresa na segunda-feira (16/11) analisou credenciais expostas em vazamentos de dados e repositórios da dark web entre setembro de 2025 e setembro de 2026. O estudo reuniu informações de 44 países.
Mesmo após anos de alertas sobre segurança digital, combinações previsíveis continuam entre as mais utilizadas. As senhas “admin” e “12345678” aparecem na segunda e terceira posições, respectivamente. Segundo a NordPass, essas três combinações mantêm as primeiras colocações do ranking há oito anos.
Outra sequência simples, “1234”, entrou no grupo das cinco mais frequentes. Já a palavra “password”, que significa senha em inglês, caiu da sexta para a sétima posição em relação ao levantamento anterior. O resultado reforça uma tendência observada em pesquisas anteriores.
No Brasil, o cenário também é marcado por escolhas previsíveis. Um levantamento anterior da NordPass identificou referências a Flamengo, Palmeiras, Santos e outros clubes entre as senhas utilizadas por brasileiros.
Como o levantamento considera apenas credenciais encontradas em vazamentos, os resultados não representam necessariamente todas as senhas utilizadas na internet.
A edição de 2026 também analisou a influência da cultura pop sobre as senhas. Entre as combinações identificadas estão referências a jogos como Minecraft e Roblox, o meme “skibiditoilet” e o jogador de basquete LeBron James, citado na senha “Lebron0319”.
Segundo a NordPass, essas escolhas apresentam riscos porque costumam seguir tendências conhecidas. Isso facilita a inclusão de nomes populares em listas utilizadas por ferramentas de tentativa automatizada de senhas.
Para reduzir o risco de invasões, a recomendação é utilizar combinações longas e exclusivas para cada serviço, além de recorrer a gerenciadores de senhas. Reutilizar uma mesma credencial em diferentes contas aumenta as possibilidades de comprometimento quando ocorre um vazamento.
Outra alternativa é ativar a autenticação de dois fatores, que exige uma verificação adicional durante o acesso. O uso de chaves de acesso, ou passkeys, também é recomendado. A tecnologia permite entrar em contas com recursos como biometria ou PIN do dispositivo, reduzindo a dependência das senhas tradicionais.

Points faibles
- Pas de prise de risque.

Le Pixel 11 Pro ne bouleversera pas le marché et décevra les fans hardcore, mais Google a bel et bien amélioré sa copie. Son écran très lumineux, ses performances solides, son excellent suivi logiciel et sa polyvalence photo en font un smartphone premium fiable et performant. La puce Tensor G6 assure une meilleure endurance, même si Google reste en retrait face aux premiers de la classe, tandis que la charge filaire à 30 W paraît désormais datée. Sans révolutionner la gamme, ce cru 2026 affine donc une prestation déjà convaincante, mais devra compter sur l’expérience utilisateur et ses fonctions d’IA pour justifier une facture en hausse.

articles.title: How we test enterprise SSDs — our new test suite pushes enterprise and data center SSDs to their limits
articles.text:
How we test enterprise SSDs — our new test suite pushes enterprise and data center SSDs to their limits
Our enterprise and data center SSD reviews show how a drive performs in real-world service, not just on its best day.
After a hiatus of several years, Tom's Hardware is expanding its in-depth testing and analysis to enterprise and data center SSDs. Consumer SSDs and conventional hard drives lack the performance and endurance for extensive AI workloads. This has increased demand for enterprise SSDs. Form factors like U.2, U.3, E3.S, and E1.S, once rare, are now common in high-end workstations and home labs. These enterprise storage solutions provide higher capacities, better performance, and greater reliability than consumer drives.
Comprehensive reviews of enterprise and data center SSDs are therefore more important than ever. Buying a drive of this caliber is a major decision and a significant investment for organizations of all sizes. With this latest venture, Tom's Hardware will continue to help buyers make informed decisions with comprehensive reviews and performance analyses.
Inside The Tom's Hardware Enterprise SSD Test System
Reviewing enterprise and data center SSDs required us to build a workstation that could truly challenge these drives. This project would not have been possible without the support of several component makers, including Asus, Corsair, G.Skill, Icy Dock, and Noctua, who made the workstation a reality, a challenging prospect in the current market.
The Xeon 658X, a 24-core, 48-thread chip from the Granite Rapids family with a 4.9 GHz boost clock speed, powers the testing workstation. Single-core performance and total core count matter just as much when reviewing storage. Clock speed determines how many IOPS one core can push and how fast it answers a single request, while 24 cores let us spread a drive's load across eight fio jobs and later test several drives at once. The Xeon 658X ticks all those boxes.
We've entrusted the Xeon 658X's cooling to Noctua's NH-U14S DX-4677 air cooler, which supports both LGA4677 and LGA4710 sockets. The single-tower CPU air cooler delivers high-performance cooling at very low noise levels thanks to its dual NF-A15 140mm cooling fans.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
With its server-grade components and robust enterprise features, the Asus Pro WS W890E-Sage SE is the ideal motherboard to pair with the Xeon 658X. Its extensive feature set includes an onboard MCIO x8 connection, split into x4/x4, that allows for evaluating two U.2 or U.3 drives. The board also provides seven PCIe 5.0 expansion slots (six at x16 and one at x8) to fully leverage the Xeon 658X’s 128 PCIe 5.0 lanes, so the SSDs and graphics cards never hit bandwidth limits.
We're still in need of support for an RTX Pro graphics card, which would be an invaluable asset for enterprise SSD reviews for real-world AI workloads, but our current test platform allows us to test the most important aspects of performance.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Despite the memory and storage shortage, G.Skill and Corsair have stepped up to provide crucial components for our enterprise SSD test bench. G.Skill sent a G5 DDR5-6400 C32 64GB (4x16GB) R-DIMM memory kit, which runs at the stock DDR5-5600 speed. The decision to keep it at the JEDEC baseline has nothing to do with the memory kit: Memory frequency does not affect performance in enterprise SSD tests.
Meanwhile, Corsair provided the speedy MP700 Pro XT 2TB, one of the best SSDs, as the test bench's primary storage. The PCIe 5.0 drive delivers sequential read and write speeds up to 14,900 MB/s and 14,500 MB/s, respectively, and keeps the workstation snappy, especially when it hammers enterprise drives all day long.
No power supply is better suited to the job than the Corsair HX1500i. It offers a massive 1,500W capacity with plenty of headroom for future upgrades, and it runs quietly and stably, two qualities that matter when you keep the test system running for countless hours. It is an 80 Plus Platinum power supply with at least 89% efficiency at full load.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Testing enterprise drives in a standard PCIe expansion slot is more convenient. For that purpose, Icy Dock has provided us with the ExpressSlot Elite MB221E5P-B and MB303E5P-B to accept one and two E1.S SSDs. Unlike other generic designs on the market, these adapters feature tool-less installation mechanisms that don't require removing them from the PCIe expansion slot, and they include 50mm fans for active cooling.
The list also included the ToughArmor MB218E5P-B, a 5.25-inch drive bay that supports up to eight E1.S SSDs for future projects exploring RAID arrays. To test E3.S drives, we use a JMT ADT-R27C adapter strapped to a Noctua NF-F12 industrialPPC-24V-3000 IP67 PWM cooling fan, which can run at 12V and still provide substantial airflow to actively cool the SSDs under evaluation.
A TGDGamer E-ATX test bench houses the hardware for the enterprise SSD system. It may not look flashy, but it does the job, and that is what matters. As an open-air test bench, it is easy to install and remove hardware, and it eliminates variables when it comes to heat generation and buildup. The test bench also supports motherboard form factors up to SSI-EEB, so the Asus Pro WS W890E-Sage SE feels right at home.
Inside the Torture Chamber: Assembling an Enterprise-Grade Benchmark Suite
A spec sheet only tells you what a drive can do on its best day. The real world is not as pretty. The drive is mostly full, garbage collection is constantly at work, and multiple workloads are hitting it simultaneously. Our enterprise benchmark suite is built to measure the drive in service: at steady state, under load, through write bursts, and with other jobs running. Every drive gets the same automated run on the same test bench. Every result is stored with the exact parameters that produced it, so we can trace how we got there.
This can take some time. A full run takes most of a day on a 7.68TB PCIe 5.0 drive, and it writes the drive end-to-end many times over. To make life a bit easier on us, the benchmark can be run unattended, and it’s crash-resumable from the last stage. A shorter express mode handles bench checks and quick triage. When a result looks odd, express runs and variant runs, which repeat just the tests in question or change one setting, help us find the cause before we take it to the vendor.
One OS, One Engine
One OS, One Engine
We run the bench on a custom Debian 13 image that we build and maintain ourselves, with the suite copied in at build time. This image gets installed on the bench’s OS drive, and the kernel is pinned so every drive has the same software stack. Right now that’s Linux 7.2.6 from Debian backports, because Debian 13’s stock 6.12 kernel predates support for the Asus Pro WS W890E-Sage SE’s Intel E610 10GbE controller. The suite is also designed to be run remotely if needed, but we need a tester at the bench to switch the drives, of course.
Debian is our pick over Ubuntu for a few reasons: it has fewer background services, no Snap, and no unattended upgrades by default. We hold the kernel so nothing changes between runs. We remove AppArmor and turn off scheduled jobs that could fire mid-run, like the weekly TRIM timer and the drive-health service that polls every drive, and the suite records any that are still running. The suite also turns off NVMe autonomous power-state transitions (APST) at the start of every run and checks that the drive reports it off, so no drive drops into a low-power state during an idle gap and adds wake-up latency to the next I/O.
Every test runs in fio 3.42, using io_uring and direct I/O against the raw block device. This means no filesystem and no page cache sitting between fio and the drive; the bench’s 64GB of RAM never caches a byte of test data. We compile fio from source because Debian’s packaged version lacks SPRandom, which we’ll get to in short order.
Some enterprise storage reviews run application profiles in Oracle’s Vdbench, but we decided to go full fio. This makes for a more consistent suite with one set of latency accounting across every chart. And fio is open source and actively maintained, while Vdbench hasn’t had a new release since 2018. Vdbench profiles are built from the same parts fio uses, such as read/write ratio, block-size mix, and random or sequential access, and our mixed-workload sweeps cover the common read/write ratios at 4K and 8K, though not mixed-block-size profiles. Running Vdbench ourselves wouldn’t make our results comparable to other outlets’ anyway, since they use different hardware, preconditioning, and profile definitions.
Steady State or Nothing
Steady State or Nothing
A key element of benchmarking SSDs is making sure the test drive is at steady state, with the performance it can sustain rather than the peak you can see after a fresh erase. Our first stage is a secure erase using nvme format. If a drive refuses, the suite falls back to a plain format, then a full-drive discard, and records which one it used.
Next comes preconditioning. SPRandom, SanDisk’s open-source contribution to fio, is a faster alternative to filling the drive over and over for hours. It takes user capacity and over-provisioning (OP) as inputs, which SanDisk says lets it reach a steady-state layout in just one pass. Overprovisioning (OP) is inferred from the capacity point or given by the tester. NVMe drives don’t report their raw flash, so a 7.68TB drive like our first one, assumed to sit on 8TiB of actual NAND, works out to having about 14.5% OP.
We don’t take SPRandom’s result on faith. A steady-state gate follows, running 4K random writes at queue depth 256 (QD256) until the drive’s write speed stops moving. It uses the two tests from the Storage Networking Industry Association’s (SNIA) steady-state rule, with limits ten times tighter, applied to the last 30 minutes: split into five six-minute rounds, the round averages must sit within 2% of one another, and the trend line across the window can’t move more than 1%.
That takes a while, but that’s the point: an earlier, looser version of the gate passed our first drive while its write speed was still climbing. The whole settling curve is saved with every run, and a drive that doesn’t settle within three hours is marked as not reaching steady state, though the run continues. As a backstop, the suite repeats the four-corner 4K write after the random sweep, hours later, and flags the run if the two results differ by more than 3%.
The suite also checks its own results as it goes. If a test’s slowest moment falls below 70% of its average, that test is run again on the spot. If a point in the random sweep lands more than 10% off the curve set by its neighbors, it’s measured again before the drive is erased for the sequential tests. Both results are kept, and any re-test is noted in the review.
Following the random tests, the tool erases the drive again and writes it end to end once, with 128K sequential writes at QD64. We run it before the sequential and AI tests, so the drive is conditioned with the kind of I/O we’re about to measure. It matters because sequential writes can swing wildly on a randomly written drive: on our first test drive, the fastest result was more than three times the slowest. After a sequential fill, they held flat from QD2 through QD1024, at both 128K and 1MB.
Drives are formatted to 512-byte logical blocks when they support it, so our block size sweep can go down to 512-byte transfers, which a 4K-native namespace can’t issue. SNIA’s enterprise IOPS test uses 512-byte transfers too, and Kioxia pitches 512-byte access for its GP Series, which is aimed at GPU-initiated storage. Drives without a 512-byte format are tested as shipped, and their sub-4K results are marked unsupported. The switch happens in the same format command as the secure erase, so it adds no time.
Measuring The Drive, Not The Bench
Measuring The Drive, Not The Bench
A fast enough SSD will happily benchmark your host, or your tools, instead, and our early runs turned up three ways that could happen. The first is CPU idle states, or C-states: waking our Xeon 658X cores from their deepest idle state can take up to 170 microseconds, and at QD1 that directly impacts the results. Holding the cores awake for the whole run cut the first drive’s average 4K QD1 read latency by about a sixth.
The second is the CPU itself: a single fio job can saturate its core well short of what a PCIe 5.0 drive can manage. Split across eight jobs, the same test runs several times faster, so random tests now spread their queue depth across up to eight fio jobs. That’s also why fast cores, and enough of them, matter for this test bench.
The third is fio itself. By default, fio seeds its random generator the same way every run, so it replays the same sequence of random offsets, and each random write test rewrites the previous test’s blocks in the same order. On our first drive, that was the main reason 4K random writes came in at more than twice the sustained figure. Every random test now runs with a fresh random seed.
What we don’t change matters, too. Completions arrive by interrupt rather than polling, and the IOMMU stays in its default mode, because that’s how most applications use a drive. On our first drive, polling and IOMMU passthrough would each have shaved some latency off 4K QD1 writes.
Interrupts also set a ceiling at the other end of the scale: this bench tops out near 2.8 million 4K random read IOPS, and adding fio jobs doesn’t lift it, though polling does. So on the fastest drives, our 4K random read result can sit below the spec sheet’s, and that’s our bench’s limit, not the drive’s. Our low queue depth latencies, writes especially, run higher than a tuned host would show, but they’re closer to what you’d actually see. To show the drive’s limit at both ends, the suite repeats three tests with polled I/O at the end of the random stage: the 4K random read peak, plus 4K random reads and writes at QD1. Those results get their own charts and never mix into the main ones.
What We Test, How, and Why
What We Test, How, and Why
| Test | What it runs | Why it’s there | 
|---|---|---|
| Four corners | 4K random read and write at QD256; 128K and 1MB sequential read and write at QD64 | The headline numbers, measured on a preconditioned drive instead of fresh out of the box | 
| Random and mixed sweeps | 4K and 8K, QD1 to QD4096, eight read/write mixes from 100% read to 100% write | Servers rarely run flat out; QD1 is what latency-bound software feels, and 8K is a common database page size | 
| Drive limit (polled) | 4K random read at QD1024 across eight jobs, plus 4K random read and write at QD1, all with polled I/O | What the drive can do with the host’s interrupt overhead out of the way; the results to set against a spec sheet | 
| Sequential sweep | 128K and 1MB sequential reads and writes, QD1 to QD1024 | How much parallelism a drive needs to reach full speed; low queue depths are what a single restore or scan gets | 
| Block size sweep | Random reads and writes from 512 bytes to 1MB at QD32 | Writes smaller than a drive’s mapping unit can pay a read-modify-write penalty; large blocks show its bandwidth cap | 
| Tail latency | 4K and 8K reads and writes at QD1, QD4, and QD16, from the median (P50) to the 99.999th percentile (P99.999) | Averages hide the stalls applications notice; at a million IOPS, the slowest 0.001% is still ten requests a second | 
| Saturation curve | 4K 70/30 at 13 queue depths from QD1 to QD4096, plotted as a share of the drive’s own peak | Finds the load where latency starts to climb | 
| Sustained write | One hour of 4K random writes at QD256 | Whether sustained writes hold a flat line or sawtooth as garbage collection struggles | 
| Write-to-read recovery | 4K QD1 reads for four minutes right after a heavy write burst | How far reads drop after heavy writes, and how fast they recover | 
| Idle recovery | Write bursts after idle gaps of 0 to 300 seconds | How much write speed a quiet spell buys back | 
| Database I/O patterns (simulated) | 4K QD1 log writes with a sync after each, a random 8K 70/30 mix at QD16, and a 256K sequential read scan | Log-write latency, page I/O, and analytics scans, without benchmarking a database’s RAM cache | 
| AI checkpoints | Checkpoint-sized saves and restores modeled on 8B- and 70B-class models (105GiB over eight writers, 912GiB over 64) | Time until the slowest writer finishes, which is when a real checkpoint would be done | 
| Checkpoint interference | A fixed 4K read load, alone and during a checkpoint save | What a checkpoint does to serving traffic on the same drive | 
| Thermals | Drive temperature through the hour-long sustained write test | Measured against the drive’s own warning and critical thresholds | 
Some things are out of scope by design. We review drives; we don’t certify them. That rules out dual-port failover, power-loss validation, and single-root I/O virtualization (SR-IOV), which belong in a qualification lab. We’ll add tests when they prove themselves on the bench. Many of the tests in the table are old standbys and still earn their place. Others are newer and require further explanation.
For one, we chart latency against load: the 70/30 4K mix from the random sweep, at 13 queue depths from QD1 to QD4096, with throughput shown as a share of the drive’s own peak. Tail latency climbs as the load grows, and the point where it turns sharply upward (on our first drive, that was write latency) represents the practical operating ceiling, or the load you can plan a server around without giving up low latency.
We also test write-to-read recovery, which measures how a drive’s reads hold up after a heavy write burst. A few minutes of 4K random writes at QD256 leave the drive with cleanup to do, and QD1 reads are then timed over the next four minutes. If a drive is still busy collecting garbage, it will read slower before climbing back; the extent and duration of the drop are the result.
Idle recovery measures what downtime buys back. After a minute of sustained writes, the drive sits idle for anywhere from zero to five minutes, then a 10-second write burst, logged second by second, shows whether background cleanup freed enough blocks to run faster.
Checkpoint interference shows what an AI checkpoint does to anything else sharing the drive. A light 4K read load, which stands in for inference or database queries, runs alone, and then again during a checkpoint save. Each read is timed from when it was due, not when it was sent, so reads stuck waiting behind a stalled one count too.
Lastly, we test thermals. Drive temperature is tracked through the hour-long sustained write test and charted against the drive's own warning and critical thresholds.
The full process means every drive is treated the same and compared fairly, with a method built to give the same results run after run. This allows us to provide a level playing field built on accurate and repeatable performance characterization.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Cet aspirateur robot Roborock noté 4,5/5 perd 166,75 € pendant le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – L'aspirateur robot Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro à 549,00 € (-23%)
L'aspirateur robot Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro passe sous les 550 € chez Amazon Marketplace soit une baisse d'environ 23% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro arrive sur le marché avec la promesse d'un nettoyage plus puissant et une station encore plus automatisée. Davantage compact, doté d'un lavage à l'eau chaude et un système d'aspiration renforcé, il entend succéder au Curv première génération, tout en se rapprochant des modèles haut de gamme de la marque.

Points forts
- Très bonnes performances d'aspiration sur sols durs et moquettes.
- Lavage efficace sur l'huile et les taches liquides.
- Station très complète.
- Robot plus fin.
- Vidange automatique efficace.
- Niveau sonore contenu.
Points faibles
- Obstacles évités trop largement.
- Franchissement de seuils parfois défaillant.
- Brossette latérale qui repousse certains déchets.
- Nettoyage des coins et bords perfectible.
Le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro renforce clairement les atouts de la gamme Qrevo en proposant un robot plus compact, plus puissant et doté d'un système de lavage plus ambitieux grâce à l'eau chaude à 100 °C. Ses performances d'aspiration figurent parmi les meilleures que nous ayons mesurées, tout comme son efficacité sur les taches grasses et liquides. La station, toujours très complète, assure un entretien quasi intégralement automatisé et se montre irréprochable sur la vidange. Cette montée en gamme ne gomme pas tous les défauts hérités de son prédécesseur. La navigation manque encore de précision : franchissement de seuils hésitant, gestion approximative de certains obstacles et trajectoires qui s'écartent parfois des zones définies. La brossette latérale, trop énergique, nuit ponctuellement à l'efficacité sur les petits déchets. Le Qrevo Curv 2 Pro demeure néanmoins un excellent robot pour celles et ceux qui privilégient la puissance d'aspiration et l'automatisation complète du lavage.

articles.title: GTA 6 is here: everything Indian players need to know
articles.text:
GTA 6 is here: Everything Indian players need to know
The biggest game launch in years arrives on 19 November. Here is what it costs in India, what you need to play it, and what is still unclear.
Grand Theft Auto VI goes live on Thursday, 19 November 2026, more than 13 years after GTA V. Store listings in India show a 12:00 am IST start. The game arrives on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X and S only. There is no PC version, and none for the PS4 or Xbox One.
The price in rupees
PlayStation India lists the Standard Edition at Rs 5,999 and the Ultimate Edition at Rs 7,499. Both come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription service. The Ultimate Edition adds an upgrade pack, and buyers of the Standard Edition can reportedly move up later for Rs 1,500, so there is no need to decide in a hurry.
For anyone who already owns a console, that is the whole bill. For everyone else, the game is the small part of the cost. Amazon India listed the PS5 Slim Digital at Rs 64,990 and the Disc model at Rs 69,985 on 28 October. Add the Standard Edition and a new buyer pays about Rs 70,989 on the digital console. Prices move, so check the final checkout figure before buying.
Do not pay extra for the disc drive
There is one trap for new buyers. The boxed version of GTA 6 reportedly contains only a download code, not a game disc. So the Rs 4,995 extra for the disc-drive PS5 buys you nothing for this game at launch. It may still make sense for other games or for resale, but if GTA 6 is the reason you are buying, the digital console is the cheaper route.
Blinkit will deliver it in minutes
Indian players do not have to wait for a courier. Quick-commerce platform Blinkit announced on its official account that GTA 6 is now available on its app, with delivery in minutes. It is live in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad, and Blinkit says more cities will follow over the next day.
What arrives is a physical box with a download code inside, which matches the disc-free boxes described above. Blinkit pitched the box as a collectible for the shelf. Buyers can redeem the code and start downloading at once, so the game is ready to play when it unlocks on 19 November. Blinkit's post ended with a joke that it expects a suspicious number of sick leaves in the next few days.
Get the download done early
Pre-loading opened on 12 November. On the PS5, the game needs at least 212 GB of free space, according to PlayStation's store page. That is a long download on a slow connection and a big bite out of a standard broadband data cap, so it is worth checking both. Players on the Xbox Series S, which has less storage, should clear space first.
The free month that costs money later
Pre-orders include one free month of GTA+. PlayStation India says the offer needs a digital pre-order before 20 November and must be claimed by 31 March 2027. After that month, GTA+ becomes a paid plan that renews automatically unless you cancel. Set a reminder if you do not want to keep paying.
What the game is about
The story follows two lead characters, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Rockstar Games describes a criminal conspiracy that spreads across the state of Leonida after a bank job goes wrong. Leonida is a fictional take on Florida, and it includes a modern Vice City, a place longtime fans will know from the series' past. It is the first numbered GTA with a female lead, and the two characters can work together or split up. Reports suggest the map is roughly twice the size of GTA V's, though Rockstar has not given an official figure.
The game is single-player at launch. In the US it carries a Mature 17+ rating from the ESRB, so this is not a game for children, and Indian parents buying it as a gift should keep that in mind.
What is still missing
Rockstar has not announced a PC version. That matters in India, where many serious gamers play on PCs and gaming laptops because consoles are expensive. A gaming laptop will not help on launch day. Rockstar has also not confirmed a date for GTA Online, the multiplayer side of the series.
Reports point to a PC release in the first quarter of 2027, but that is a rumour and Rockstar has not confirmed it. For Indian players with a capable gaming PC, the choice is between playing now on a console and waiting a few months. For those who do not own a console, waiting could save close to Rs 65,000.
Consoles are selling out
Demand for consoles has jumped since Rockstar's extended gameplay look appeared on Netflix. Reports from other countries say resellers have bought up stock and are charging nearly double the usual price for the PS5 Pro and the Xbox Series S, with many listings sold out.
It is not yet clear how far this has reached India, and the figures quoted for Indian listings are not reliable. Still, a buyer who needs a console for launch day should expect tight stock. Buy from authorised sellers, compare the final checkout price, and treat any listing far above the price Sony or Microsoft lists with suspicion.
Why India is watching
The console barrier is the story here. At about Rs 65,000 for the cheapest PS5, the machine costs ten times as much as the game. GTA 6 may push a number of Indian buyers into their first console, but it also shows how far the console market still has to travel in a country where most people play on phones. Whether this launch widens that market, or simply sells to those who already own a console, is the question to watch in the weeks ahead.
Prices and times are as listed by PlayStation India and retailers in early November. "

articles.title: SFR lance la Box 10 : le Wi-Fi 7 n’est plus réservé à son offre haut de gamme
articles.text:
Nous en avions découvert l’existence début octobre grâce à des pages d’assistance, elle est désormais officielle. SFR a annoncé ce mardi le lancement de la Box 10, disponible dès aujourd’hui avec l’offre SFR Fibre Power, facturée 36,99 euros par mois. Elle y remplace la Box 8, une box Wi-Fi 6 sortie il y a plusieurs années, et se positionne sous la Box 10+, le modèle haut de gamme lancé en septembre 2025 avec l’offre Fibre Premium. L’opérateur entend ainsi « démocratiser l’accès aux technologies les plus avancées du marché », selon Pierre Clément, directeur exécutif Grand Public et Entreprises de SFR.
Du W-Fi 7, mais en version allégée
La principale nouveauté de cette Box 10 est l’arrivée du Wi-Fi 7, mais seulement bi-bande. Il exploite les fréquences 2,4 et 5 GHz, là ou la Box 10+ plus premium ajoute la bande des 6 GHz. Cela reste toutefois une amélioration bienvenue et SFR annonce un débit théorique cumulé de 6,8 Gbit/s, soit 25 % de mieux qu’avec la Box 8 précédemment fournie avec cette offre. Un répéteur Wi-Fi 7 est également inclus pour étendre la couverture dans le logement.
Côté fibre, les concessions sont plus nettes et la Box 10 reste compatible uniquement avec la technologie GPON. Elle offre des débits jusqu’à 2 Gbit/s en téléchargement et 1 Gbit/s en envoi, loin des 8 Gbit/s symétriques de la Box 10+, qui profite du XGS-PON. La nouvelle box de l’opérateur au carré rouge dispose de quatre ports Ethernet, deux à 1 Gbit/s et deux à 2,5 Gbit/s. Contrairement à sa grande sœur, elle fait l’impasse sur le port 10 Gbit/s.
Pour les amateurs de domotique, on note l’intégration d’un module Thread pour piloter des objets connectés basse consommation comme des capteurs de mouvement, des prises ou des interrupteurs.
Un écran e-ink, du braille et un mode éco
La Box 10 reprend le design de la Box 10+, dans un format un peu plus compact. On retrouve un petit écran tactile à encre électronique, comme sur une liseuse, qui donne accès aux principales fonctions. Développée avec l’association HandiCaPZéro, elle porte aussi un marquage en braille, et sa connectique a été disposée pour être plus facile à repérer.
La coque est fabriquée en plastique 100 % recyclé, et les pièces métalliques contiennent 46 % de matières recyclées. Le mode éco programmable, activable depuis l’écran ou l’application SFR & Moi, permet de réduire la consommation électrique de la box de près de 40 %, selon SFR, qui annonce 5,9 watts en mode éco contre 9,4 watts en mode standard.
L’offre SFR Fibre Power comprend, en plus de la box et du répéteur, le décodeur SFR Box 8 TV et les appels illimités vers les fixes et mobiles en France. Une remise de 3 euros par mois s’applique sur une option TV ou streaming au choix, parmi Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max ou Ciné+ OCS. À noter que l’offre est assortie d’un engagement de 12 mois, et qu’il faut ajouter 49 euros de frais d’ouverture de service.
Ce lancement intervient dans un contexte particulier pour SFR, qui doit être racheté et découpé entre Bouygues Telecom, Free et Orange. L’opération est toujours entre les mains de l’Autorité de la concurrence, et aucune décision n’est attendue avant plusieurs mois. En attendant, l’opérateur continue donc de renouveler ses équipements.

articles.title: Test Acer Googlebook 14 : Google veut concurrencer Windows avec Android, mais le compte n'y est pas
articles.text:
Acer compte parmi les cinq premiers constructeurs à s’aventurer sur le terrain des Googlebook, les nouveaux ordinateurs portables premium à la sauce Android. Un pari risqué compte tenu des limites propres à la nouvelle plateforme voulue par Google… Et de l’actuelle flambée des prix de la RAM.
Vous connaissiez les Chromebooks et leur environnement ChromeOS ? Vous avez alors sûrement appris à connaître au moins un peu les nouveaux Googlebook et leur environnement basé sur le système d’exploitation mobile le plus répandu à la surface du globe : Android.
- Belle qualité de construction, appareil élégant
- Le seul Googlebook 2-en-1 (pour l’instant)
- L’écran OLED, son contraste, ses couleurs
- Chauffe peu, reste silencieux
- Autonomie solide (entre 12 et 15 heures)
- Centre du clavier trop mou, pavé tactile non haptique
- Performances suffisantes, mais modestes
- L’expérience de bureau Googlebook OS frustrante
- Aussi cher qu’un MacBook Air M5… mais infiniment moins polyvalent
Annoncée par Google au printemps et lancée en bonne et due forme début octobre, la plateforme Googlebook doit permettre au géant californien d’offrir une troisième voie entre Windows et macOS sur le terrain des ordinateurs portables haut de gamme. Un objectif dont on serait presque tenté de parler au passé, tant les ambitions de Google semblent élevées au regard des capacités réelles de son nouveau système d’exploitation Googlebook OS en l’état, comme nous l’expliquions dans un long article dédié à la question.
C’est dans ce contexte qu’arrive l’Acer Googlebook 14, premier modèle Googlebook du constructeur taïwanais, et seul modèle convertible de cette nouvelle gamme d’appareils conçus en collaboration étroite avec Google. Un ordinateur portable à écran OLED réversible élégant et bien construit, mais cher et limité, comme nous allons le voir.
Avant d’aller plus loin, voici la fiche technique précise du modèle qu’Acer France nous a fait parvenir en prêt :
