articles.title: UGREEN ya calienta motores para el Black Friday: descuentos de hasta el 40% en baterías, cargadores, NAS, cables y mucho más
articles.text:
Estamos en el mes del Black Friday, la cita comercial que esperan millones de personas en todo el mundo y que se celebra el 27 de noviembre. Sin embargo, cada vez más marcas adelantan sus ofertas para dar la oportunidad al consumidor de ahorrarse un dinero importante durante más tiempo. En el caso de UGREEN, hay dos periodos, el de calentamiento que transcurre hasta el 18 de noviembre, donde ya hay importantes descuentos, y luego las ofertas del Black Friday que es donde podremos ver descuentos de hasta el 40%.
Lo mejor es que estas ofertas afectan a todos sus productos por lo que seguro que encuentras ese dispositivo que te ayuda en el día a día. Aunque UGREEN empezó a ser mundialmente conocido por su cables de carga, desde hace años su portfolio ha crecido muchísimo y ahora tiene equipos de muy alta calidad, como cargadores, bases de carga inalámbricas, PowerBanks de todos los tamaños y capacidades e incluso otros más profesionales como NAS, donde almacenar toda nuestra información de manera local y segura. Y por si todo eso fuera poco, ahora también tiene auriculares que sólo costarán durante los próximos días, quince euros.
Para que sea más sencillo, hemos organizado las mejores ofertas de UGREEN para este Black Friday que hemos encontrado por categoría de producto.
Cargadores con el 33% de descuento
Ahora que prácticamente todos los teléfonos vienen sin cargador, UGREEN ha encontrado el nicho perfecto para crecer. Basta con dejarse caer por su web para ver la inmensa cantidad de cargadores que tiene. Aquí hemos seleccionado dos. Por un lado, el UGREEN Nexode 65W, pequeño, compacto pero suficientemente potente como para cargar portátiles, tablets y cualquier otro dispositivo. Tiene dos salidas USB C y una USB A para cargar hasta tres dispositivos a la vez. Con los descuentos del Black Friday se queda en tan sólo 18,79 euros.
El segundo es un cargador más Pro, para todas aquellas personas que necesitan más. Es el UGREEN Nexode Pro de 100W. Tiene una pantalla de lo más práctica, donde ver todo lo relacionado con la velocidad y la potencia de carga. También tiene cuatro puertos (3 USB C y uno USB A). Una bestia que con los descuentos del Black Friday se queda en menos de 40 euros.
Y si lo que buscas es un cargador inalámbrico, hace poco probamos el UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 25W Cargador Inalámbrico 2 en 1 para poder cargar de manera simultánea, y sin necesidad de cables, el teléfono y los auriculares. Es una base de carga flexible, que se puede colocar en varias posiciones y plegar para que no ocupe nada de espacio en la mochila o en el bolsillo. La bajada de precio es espectacular, durante estos días sólo cuesta 34 euros.
Powerbanks
Es posiblemente la mejor compañera para todos los que tenemos que vernos muchas horas fuera de casa, ya sea de viaje o en largas jornadas usando el teléfono. Las PowerBanks han evolucionado mucho en los últimos años: ahora son más potentes, más rápidas y más ligeras y compactas. UGREEN tiene dos que son top, por un lado la UGREEN Nexode 45W Power Bank 20000mAh Cable USB con cable Integrado, una verdadera bestia capaz de recargar la batería de hasta cuatro teléfonos con una sóla carga. En estos días llegará a su precio histórico más bajo, de sólo 25,6 euros.
También tienes un modelo de 10.000 mAh con un innovador sistema de enfriado y que puedes ver a través de su pantalla. 25W de potencia de carga y puedes cargar todo tu ecosistema Apple al mismo tiempo: el teléfono usando la carga inalámbrica y reloj y AirPods usando el cable. Sólo cuesta 89,9 euros.
Y si quieres algo mucho más ligero, tienes UGREEN MagFlow Air Qi2 25W de 10.000 mAh de capacidad y que es de las baterías externas más delgadas que he visto nunca. Puedes cargar tu teléfono con el cable o de manera inalámbrica. Ahora su precio es de tan sólo 66 euros.
NAS: da el salto al almacenamiento local
Es una opción que cada vez se ve más, no sólo en oficinas, sino también en casas particulares, por ejemplo para montarse un servidor donde meter toda la información y domótica. Los NAS de UGREEN han sido una gran sorpresa para nosotros que, tras probar un par de modelos, nos hemos vuelto usuarios. En concreto, ahora mismo estamos probando la serie UGREEN NASync DXP. Está disponible en una configuración desde dos bahías hasta ocho. Pues bien la de dos bahías, el modelo UGREEN NASync DXP2800 GT ahora tiene un descuento del 21% y se queda en menos de 400 euros. Es la típica inversión que rentabilizas desde el primer día. La mejor puerta de entrada al almacenamiento local de lo más preciado que tenemos: la información.
Auriculares, Docking Station y un cable trenzado
En esta sección hemos metido varios productos que nos han sorprendido mucho. Por un lado, unos auriculares Open Ear (de los que están de moda ahora), con más de 30 horas de autonomía y que sólo cuestan 15 euros.
El segundo es un Docking Station, perfecto si eres creador de contenido o necesitas conectar varios puertos al mismo tiempo. Muchos PCs, para abaratar costes, han reducido el número de puertos así que un Docking de este tipo es súper útil. Este es un adaptador siete en uno y cuesta menos de 20 euros. Es el gadget perfecto.
El tercero es el más sencillo, pero útil en todas las casas. Un cable con dos puertos USB-C. Por fuera, es un elegante cable trenzado de nylon y, por dentro, ofrece una potencia de carga de hasta 100W. Lo tienes disponible desde medio metro hasta los 3 metros y cuesta a partir de los 7 euros.
Estos han sido sólo algunos de los productos recomendados, pero hay muchos más. Seguro que si echas un vistazo a la web de UGREEN o de Amazon en este Black Friday y donde se agrupan todos los productos, encontrarás ese complemento que se volverá indispensable en tu día a día.

articles.title: Kaufen statt gründen: Warum Startups jetzt den deutschen Mittelstand aufrollen
articles.text:
Roll-ups: Warum Startups jetzt lieber kaufen, statt zu gründen
Tausende Mittelständler:innen suchen Nachfolger:innen. Immer mehr Startups nutzen diese Gelegenheit, übernehmen etablierte Unternehmen und wollen sie mithilfe von KI effizienter machen. Auch Venture-Capital-Investor:innen entdecken das Geschäftsmodell. Erste millionenschwere Exits zeigen, welches Potenzial in diesem Markt steckt.
Warum mühsam ein Startup aufbauen, wenn man ein funktionierendes Unternehmen einfach kaufen kann? Genau darauf setzen immer mehr Gründer. Und die Auswahl ist riesig: Laut Institut für Mittelstandsforschung (IfM) stehen zwischen 2026 und 2030 rund 186.000 Unternehmen in Deutschland zur Übergabe an. Für Gründer:innen, die lieber bestehende Geschäfte übernehmen, statt neue Produkte zu entwickeln, sind das interessante Aussichten. Zumal inzwischen auch Venture-Capital-Investor:innen bereitstehen, um solche Übernahmen zu finanzieren.
Kaufen, bündeln, digitalisieren: So funktionieren Roll-ups
Die Idee ist nicht neu. Finanzinvestor:innen kaufen seit Jahrzehnten Unternehmen einer Branche, führen sie zusammen und versuchen, durch ihre Größe Kosten zu senken und Gewinne zu steigern. In der Finanzwelt heißt das Buy-and-Build, in der Startup-Szene meist Roll-up. Das Prinzip: Ein Gründerteam übernimmt einen etablierten Betrieb und kauft weitere Unternehmen derselben Branche hinzu. Verwaltung, Einkauf, Personalwesen und IT lassen sich gemeinsam organisieren. Die Betriebe können ihre Namen, Standorte und Kundenbeziehungen behalten.
Besonders interessant sind Märkte mit vielen kleinen Anbietern, etwa Handwerk, Ingenieurbüros, IT-Dienstleister, Versicherungsmakler und Steuerkanzleien. Viele Betriebe sind profitabel und haben langjährige Kunden. Häufig fehlen ihnen jedoch Nachfolger, moderne IT-Systeme oder Kapital für größere Investitionen. Genau solche Betriebe kaufen Roll-up-Startups. Anders als klassische Finanzinvestoren wollen die Gründerteams nicht nur Unternehmen bündeln, sondern deren Prozesse mit gemeinsamer Software, Automatisierung und KI grundlegend verändern.
Das unterscheidet sie auch von früheren Amazon-Aggregatoren wie Razor Group und SellerX, die zahlreiche Onlinehändler und deren Marken kauften. Die neue Roll-up-Welle konzentriert sich dagegen auf traditionelle Unternehmen – vom Ingenieurbüro bis zum Dachdeckerbetrieb.
Arsipa und Entro: Millionenexits mit Mittelständlern
Wie schnell solche Unternehmensgruppen wachsen können, zeigen zwei deutsche Beispiele. Die 2020 von Felix Jander, Stefan Schmidt und Alexander Keil gegründete Berliner Arsipa Gruppe übernimmt Dienstleister für Arbeitsmedizin und Arbeitssicherheit. Durch zahlreiche Zukäufe entstand eine Gruppe mit rund 1.100 Mitarbeitenden an mehr als 70 Standorten in Deutschland und Österreich. 2025 übernahm der US-Finanzinvestor Warburg Pincus Arsipa. Der Kaufpreis blieb geheim, in der Branche war jedoch von einer niedrigen dreistelligen Millionensumme die Rede. Zu den frühen Investoren gehörte Tengelmann Ventures.
Auch das Hamburger Startup Entro schaffte einen millionenschweren Exit. Die 2022 von Claudio Tubach und Philipp Westphal gegründete Gruppe bündelt Betriebe für Zutrittssysteme, Brandschutz und Sicherheitstechnik. Im September 2025 übernahm die US-Beteiligungsgesellschaft Levine Leichtman Capital Partners die Mehrheit. Die Bewertung soll bei rund 100 Millionen Euro gelegen haben.
Solche Exits machen Roll-ups auch für Venture-Capital-Investoren interessant. Statt auf den Durchbruch eines neuen Produkts zu warten, finanzieren sie Gründerteams, die Unternehmen mit bestehenden Kunden, Umsätzen und Geschäftsmodellen übernehmen. Das Wachstum entsteht vor allem durch weitere Zukäufe. Das benötigt allerdings viel Kapital. Anders als bei klassischen Software-Startups fließt ein erheblicher Teil direkt in Übernahmen. Mit jedem Zukauf wächst zudem die Herausforderung, unterschiedliche Betriebe zu einer funktionierenden Gruppe zusammenzuführen.
Wie KI das Roll-up-Modell verändern soll
Beim Zusammenlegen von Betrieben soll es nicht bleiben. KI soll Verwaltungsaufgaben automatisieren, Prozesse beschleunigen und Mitarbeiter:innen entlasten – besonders in Branchen mit viel manueller Arbeit.
Ein Beispiel ist die Kölner MoIn Group. Das von Moritz Delbrück, Philipp Kanschik und André Hoendgen gegründete Startup übernimmt etablierte Versicherungsmakler, will deren Verwaltungsaufwand mit KI reduzieren und gleichzeitig ihre Eigenständigkeit erhalten. „Mit der MoIn Group kaufen wir Maklerhäuser und helfen ihnen mit Künstlicher Intelligenz. So wird der Papierkram schneller erledigt und sie haben wieder mehr Zeit für die Beratung ihrer Kunden“, sagt Gründer Moritz Delbrück. Mit Compari aus Mellrichstadt und der Sünderwald-Gruppe aus Chemnitz gehören bereits zwei Maklerunternehmen zur Gruppe. KI-Agenten sollen zunehmend administrative Aufgaben übernehmen. Ob die versprochenen Effizienzgewinne eintreten, muss sich noch zeigen.
Auch Steuerkanzleien geraten ins Visier der Roll-up-Startups. Laut einer Auswertung des Investors Resat Ozutok (TechCredit Partners) gibt es europaweit bereits 72 Roll-up-Plattformen in 16 Ländern. In Deutschland verbinden unter anderem Integral, Limetax, Skalar und Taxforce Steuerberatung, Software und Unternehmensübernahmen. Während einige Anbieter zunächst Kanzleien kaufen und anschließend digitalisieren, gehen andere den umgekehrten Weg: Sie entwickeln zuerst die Software und suchen dann passende Übernahmekandidaten. KI soll insbesondere die Verarbeitung von Belegen und Dokumenten vereinfachen.
Allerdings lässt sich nicht jede Tätigkeit automatisieren. Fachliche Verantwortung, Datenschutz und berufsrechtliche Vorgaben bleiben entscheidend. Ob die Gruppen dauerhaft effizienter arbeiten als unabhängige Kanzleien, ist offen.
Warum Investoren auf Roll-ups setzen
Trotz solcher Herausforderungen entdecken immer mehr Investoren das Roll-up-Modell für sich. Zu den Vorreitern im boomenden Segment gehört der Geldgeber Tengelmann Ventures, der bereits Arsipa finanzierte und inzwischen mehrere Roll-up-Startups unterstützt. Mit Aven Capital Partners gibt es zudem schon einen spezialisierten Investor, der 50 Millionen Euro für solche Geschäftsmodelle bereitstellt. Hinter dem Fonds stecken unter anderem Arsipa-Gründer Felix Jander und der frühere Arsipa-Investor Frederik Brandis. Und auch bekannte VCs wie Cherry Ventures und Vorwerk Ventures sind inzwischen im aufstrebenden Segment aktiv. Das Kalkül der Investoren: Viele kleine, profitable Unternehmen könnten zusammen deutlich mehr wert sein als einzeln – erst recht, wenn Software und KI ihre Kosten senken.
Wo die Risiken liegen
Doch der Erfolg ist keineswegs garantiert. Unterschiedliche Unternehmenskulturen, IT-Systeme und Arbeitsabläufe zusammenzuführen, ist aufwendig. Hinzu kommen hohe Übernahmekosten und die Gefahr, wichtige Mitarbeiter:innen nach einem Eigentümerwechsel zu verlieren. Auch die versprochenen KI-Effizienzgewinne müssen sich erst beweisen.
Zudem eignet sich nicht jeder Mittelständler für eine Übernahme. Investoren suchen vor allem profitable Betriebe, die sich in größere Gruppen integrieren lassen. Unternehmen zu kaufen, ist schließlich nur der erste Schritt. Die eigentliche Herausforderung beginnt danach: Aus vielen eigenständigen Betrieben muss eine funktionierende Gruppe werden. Und ob KI dabei tatsächlich den erhofften Unterschied macht, ist noch längst nicht bewiesen.
In Kooperation mit deutsche-startups.de & STARTUPLAND: Das Magazin deutsche-startups.de berichtet täglich über die Gründerszene und veranstaltet am 10. März 2027 die STARTUPLAND Conference in Köln. Exklusiv für t3n-Leser:innen: 35 Prozent Rabatt auf Tickets mit dem Code STARTUPLANDt3n.

articles.title: Xiaomi renouvelle ses montres et écouteurs, avec une nouveauté bienvenue pour payer au poignet
articles.text:
Xiaomi annonce la Watch S5 41 mm, le Smart Band 11 et ses premiers écouteurs ouverts à clip. La montre accueille Google Wallet dès son lancement, tandis que le bracelet devra patienter pour profiter du même service.
Après la Watch S5 de 46 mm présentée au printemps, Xiaomi s’adresse aux poignets plus fins avec une nouvelle déclinaison de sa montre. Mais la marque ne se contente pas de revoir les dimensions : elle ajoute Google Wallet à sa série Watch S. À ses côtés, le Smart Band 11 poursuit sa route sur le terrain des bracelets accessibles et les Xiaomi Clip inaugurent un format d’écouteurs qui laisse les oreilles dégagées.
Une petite Watch S5 qui veut espacer les recharges
La Xiaomi Watch S5 41 mm associe un boîtier en acier inoxydable de 9,9 mm d’épaisseur, hors parties saillantes, à un écran AMOLED de 1,32 pouce. Xiaomi annonce une luminosité maximale de 3 000 nits et une batterie de 590 mAh, pour jusqu’à 14 jours d’autonomie. Ce dernier chiffre correspond toutefois à un usage allégé, avec plusieurs suivis continus désactivés.
L’arrivée de Google Wallet permet d’enregistrer des cartes bancaires compatibles pour payer sans contact. La disponibilité dépendra des banques et des régions, mais le service est annoncé dès le lancement de la montre. HyperOS 4 apporte également une interface remaniée, tandis que le Wi-Fi doit accélérer les mises à jour et les téléchargements de musique ou de cartes hors ligne.
Le suivi sportif compte plus de 150 modes. Xiaomi ajoute notamment la mesure de la variabilité de la fréquence cardiaque pendant la nuit et des suggestions d’entraînement. Les progrès revendiqués dans le suivi du sommeil restent, à ce stade, des résultats de laboratoire du constructeur.
La montre coûte 229,99 € en noir ou bleu clair, avec une offre de lancement à 194,99 € jusqu’au 30 novembre. La version blanc céramique passe de 249,99 à 229,99 € sur la même période.
Smart Band 11 et Xiaomi Clip : deux façons de voyager léger
Le Smart Band 11 conserve une approche plus économique, à partir de 59,99 €, ou 54,99 € au lancement. Son écran AMOLED de 1,72 pouce atteint un pic annoncé de 2 000 nits. L’autonomie maximale s’établit à 21 jours pour la version standard et 18 jours pour les modèles NFC, là encore avec plusieurs mesures continues désactivées.
Le bracelet suit notamment le sommeil, la fréquence cardiaque et la VFC nocturne. Il peut aussi recevoir les notifications d’un smartphone Xiaomi et d’un iPhone simultanément, sous réserve d’utiliser les appareils, applications et comptes compatibles. Attention au paiement : Google Wallet sur le Smart Band 11 est prévu par une mise à jour en février, selon les notes du communiqué. Les versions NFC commencent à 79,99 €, ou 67,99 € jusqu’au 30 novembre.
Enfin, les Xiaomi Clip se fixent autour de l’oreille sans entrer dans le conduit auditif. Leur conception ouverte permet de rester attentif à son environnement, mais n’offre pas l’isolation d’écouteurs intra-auriculaires.
Chaque écouteur pèse 5,5 g. Xiaomi annonce jusqu’à neuf heures d’écoute, ou 38 heures avec le boîtier, dans ses conditions de test. La compatibilité avec le réseau Localiser d’Apple concerne uniquement le boîtier, pas chaque écouteur séparément. Les Clip sont proposés à 149,99 €, ramenés à 126,99 € jusqu’au 30 novembre.

articles.title: “Cuando salió GTA V tenía su edad y recuerdo las ganas de llegar a casa a jugar”: profesor aplaza examen por GTA 6
articles.text:
Una historia está en tendencia en redes sociales. Un profesor aplazó el examen de su asignatura previsto para el 23 de noviembre de 2026, tras el lanzamiento de GTA 6, para que sus alumnos tengan una semana sin tareas, trabajos ni entregas y puedan dedicar tiempo al nuevo juego de Rockstar Games.
La decisión coincide con una expectativa que ya se tradujo en más de 11 millones de reservas antes del estreno. Algunos aficionados incluso contemplan pedir días libres en sus trabajos para jugar desde el primer momento.
El docente explicó en un correo electrónico enviado a sus estudiantes que comprendía la importancia del lanzamiento porque vivió una situación similar con la entrega anterior.
La anterior entrega de la saga se publicó en 2013, cuando él tenía una edad parecida a la de sus alumnos. “Recuerdo perfectamente las ganas que tenía de llegar a casa para jugar y cómo solo hablábamos de eso entre mis amigos. Por eso, puedo imaginarme perfectamente lo que supone para muchos de ustedes”, dijo.
El profesor resolvió eliminar temporalmente las obligaciones de su materia durante la semana del estreno. “He querido que durante la semana del lanzamiento de GTA 6 no tengan tareas, trabajos ni entregas de mi asignatura”.
A su vez, la medida modificó el calendario de evaluación: el examen programado para el 23 de noviembre se realizará el día 30. El profesor anticipó que el alivio académico será momentáneo: “La semana siguiente tendremos que volver a apretar”.
Cuándo sale GTA 6 para todo el publico gamer
Rockstar Games lanzará Grand Theft Auto VI el jueves 19 de noviembre de 2026 para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, trece años después de Grand Theft Auto V. El acceso se habilitará a las 00:00 de la hora local de cada país o región configurada en la tienda digital de la consola.
El sistema implica que no habrá una activación simultánea en todo el mundo. Nueva Zelanda y Australia podrán entrar antes que Europa y América por sus husos horarios, mientras que Argentina, Colombia, Chile, México y Perú tendrán acceso a medianoche según su horario local; el mismo criterio regirá en España, el resto de Europa, Asia y Oceanía.
El lanzamiento nativo estará limitado a PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X y Xbox Series S. No habrá versión para computadoras el día del estreno y Rockstar Games no comunicó una fecha para esa opción.
Cómo descargar GTA 6 en diferentes consolas de videojuegos
La predescarga está disponible desde el 10 de noviembre para quienes reservaron la edición digital. El juego requerirá hasta 212 GB de espacio libre en la unidad SSD, una capacidad que puede demorar el inicio si la instalación se realiza cuando se active el lanzamiento.
En PlayStation 5, la descarga se inicia desde la biblioteca de juegos o la PlayStation Store. En Xbox Series X|S, queda habilitada desde la Xbox Store después de completar la reserva.
Las copias físicas tampoco incluirán un disco: la caja contendrá un código de descarga. Por ese motivo, los compradores necesitarán conexión a internet y espacio suficiente en la consola incluso si eligen esa edición.
Cuánto tiempo tomaría pasar GTA 6
La campaña principal podría durar cerca de 50 horas, de acuerdo con una filtración difundida por el periodista Tom Henderson. Esa versión calcula unas 100 misiones distribuidas en cinco capítulos centrados en Jason y Lucia.
La extensión situaría a GTA 6 por encima de las cerca de 32 horas de historia de GTA V y en un rango similar al de Red Dead Redemption 2. El tiempo aumentaría al combinar la trama principal con la exploración y las actividades del mundo abierto.
Rob Nelson, responsable de desarrollo y codirector de Rockstar North, contó que una de sus partidas se prolongó durante 80 horas. Su recorrido incluyó objetivos opcionales, interacciones con otros personajes y desplazamientos por el mapa.
Asimismo, completar el 100% del título podría demandar hasta 200 horas. Entre los retos figurarían identificar y fotografiar más de 170 especies animales en Leonida, además de cumplir logros vinculados con elementos aleatorios que impedirían seguir una ruta fija; Rockstar Games no confirmó oficialmente esos datos.

articles.title: Xiaomi dévoile la Watch S5 et la Smart Band 11 : prix, autonomie, nouveautés… tout ce qu’il faut savoir
articles.text:
Xiaomi vient de dévoiler une nouvelle montre connectée : la Xiaomi Watch S5 – 41mm. Celle-ci a tout d’une montre connectée, mais ressemble davantage à une montre classique. Le constructeur chinois a également dévoilé le Xiaomi Smart Band 11, un bracelet connecté à l’écran ovale. Ces deux produits sont dès à présent disponibles sur les canaux officiels de Xiaomi et auprès des revendeurs agréés. Spécificités et prix : voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir.
La Xiaomi Watch S5 – 41mm
Avec la Watch S5 – 41mm, Xiaomi propose une montre connectée qui ressemble à une montre traditionnelle. On retrouve un écran Amoled de 1,32 pouce placé sur un boîtier en acier inoxydable de 9,9 mm d’épaisseur. La luminosité de l’écran peut quant à elle atteindre 3 000 nits. La montre propose par ailleurs quatre cadrans animés qui mettent en scène des animaux qui réagissent au toucher, à la progression de l’activité physique, à l’heure et à la météo. L’atteinte d’objectifs sportifs permet de débloquer de nouvelles postures pour ces animaux.
En parlant de sport, cette montre connectée propose 150 modes sportifs, ainsi que des indicateurs de suivi. La fonction « Sélection d’entraînements », par exemple, propose des types et des durées d’exercices en fonction de la météo, de la condition physique, des habitudes sportives et du niveau de forme. La fonction « Aperçu de la santé » analyse quant à elle plus de 50 indicateurs de forme, de sommeil et de santé afin de mettre en évidence les évolutions notables. Les bilans sont consultables aussi bien sur la montre que sur un smartphone connecté.
Côté suivi du sommeil, l’algorithme de nouvelle génération promet d’améliorer de 11 % la précision de détection de l’endormissement et du réveil, et de 14 % celle des phases de sommeil, par rapport à celui de la génération précédente. À noter également que la montre propose un suivi de la variabilité de la fréquence cardiaque (VFC) pour apporter davantage d’informations sur la récupération. Côté connectivité et applications, la montre offre une connexion Wi-Fi (pour télécharger plus rapidement les mises à jour, des musiques, des cartes hors ligne, etc.), et intègre Google Wallet, Google Pay et les paiements NFC.
La Xiaomi Watch S5 41 mm promet par ailleurs un suivi précis du cycle menstruel grâce à un capteur de température amélioré, capable de prédire les règles et l’ovulation. Attention toutefois, l’accès à certaines analyses approfondies requiert un abonnement à Clue Plus (trois mois gratuits sont offerts à l’achat de la montre). Enfin, précisons que Xiaomi annonce jusqu’à 14 jours d’autonomie grâce à une batterie de 590 mAh.
La Xiaomi Watch S5 41mm est déclinée en Noir et Bleu Clair. Ces deux modèles sont équipés d’un bracelet en sport souple et sont vendus au prix de 229,99 €. Un troisième modèle, Blanc Céramique, bénéficie quant à lui d’un bracelet en cuir et est vendu au prix de 249,99 €. Du 17 au 30 novembre 2026, dans le cadre d’une offre de lancement, les modèles Noir et Bleu Clair sont vendus au prix de 194,99 € (soit 35 € de remise), tandis que le modèle Blanc Céramique est proposé au prix de 229,99 € (soit 20 € de remise).
Le Xiaomi Smart Band 11
Ce bracelet connecté présente un écran Amoled ovale de 1,72 pouce, dont la luminosité maximale peut atteindre 2 000 nits. Il intègre par ailleurs 150 modes sportifs et la reconnaissance automatique de six activités. Notons également la présence d’un capteur PPG à double LED et double photodiode, fonctionnant simultanément avec l’algorithme propriétaire de Xiaomi, qui permettrait d’atteindre une précision globale de la fréquence cardiaque allant jusqu’à 98,2 %.
Il est possible de nager avec ce bracelet connecté puisqu’il est étanche jusqu’à 5 ATM, tandis que le suivi de la fréquence cardiaque continue de fonctionner sous l’eau. Bien entendu, on retrouve un suivi du sommeil avec une détection de l’endormissement et des cycles de sommeil. À noter que ce bracelet peut être connecté aussi bien à un smartphone Xiaomi qu’à un iPhone, afin de recevoir des alertes d’appel, des messages ou encore des rappels. Enfin, notons que Xiaomi annonce jusqu’à 21 jours d’autonomie pour la version standard et 18 jours pour les modèles NFC.
Le Xiaomi Smart Band 11 se décline en plusieurs versions. Le modèle standard, dont le cadre en aluminium est proposé en noir, argent ou rose, est vendu au prix de 59,99 € (ou 54,99 € du 17 au 30 novembre 2026, soit une remise de 5 €). Les modèles NFC (paiement sans contact) se déclinent également en deux éditions spéciales : une version Céramique blanche et une version Unibody entièrement métallique, proposée dans un coloris lavande. Côté tarifs, la version NFC classique est affichée à 79,99 €, mais bénéficie d’une offre de lancement à 67,99 € du 17 au 30 novembre 2026. Les éditions Céramique et Unibody sont quant à elles proposées à 89,99 €, avec des prix de lancement respectifs de 75,99 € et 79,99 €, soit 14 € et 10 € de réduction.

articles.title: Surprise! Windows 11 26H2 makes multitasking on 8GB PCs remarkably smooth
articles.text:
The takeaway: With DRAM prices continuing to hit record highs, consumer electronics manufacturers are working on software optimizations to ensure decent performance, even on modest hardware. Microsoft recently claimed that the latest Windows 11 update makes the operating system faster and more responsive on devices with just 8GB of RAM. New reports suggest there may be some truth to that claim.
Earlier this month, Microsoft released Windows 11 26H2 with a series of optimizations that it claimed will improve performance on PCs with just 8GB of memory. According to Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft's EVP of Windows and Devices, the improvements will make Windows up to 20% more responsive and boost multitasking performance by up to 40% on devices with 8GB of RAM.
Early reviews suggest Davuluri's claims may not be just a PR exercise after all. The Verge tested the same 13-inch Surface Laptop with 8GB of RAM before and after installing version 26H2, Build 26300.9974, and found that multitasking performance improved noticeably following the update, with no apparent drawbacks.
According to the report, before the update, running 20 Chrome tabs while streaming a 4K YouTube video and using Slack and Signal simultaneously made the device extremely sluggish. Browser tabs and apps also had to reload whenever the reviewer switched between them. The fan ran at full speed, while Resource Monitor reported between 700 and 29,000 hard faults per second, resulting in a severely degraded experience.
After the update, Windows still slowed down somewhat when performing the same tasks, but the device remained usable. "I could feel things like Task View get a little less responsive, but it was the way you'd expect when taxing a system. Chrome tabs required less frequent refreshes (and) the fan took longer to kick in and ran quieter," the reviewer noted.
Explaining how Microsoft managed to reduce lag on Windows 11 devices with 8GB of memory, Davuluri said the improvements came from better memory compression and more efficient management of which apps remain in memory and which are offloaded to storage. He added that the biggest change involves how the operating system accesses data that has been paged out from RAM to an SSD.
Traditionally, when there isn't enough memory to handle all active data, some of it is moved to the SSD. Since storage drives are considerably slower than RAM, retrieving this data takes much longer than accessing information stored in memory, resulting in slowdowns that can disrupt users' workflows.
According to Davuluri, Microsoft addressed this issue in the latest update by allowing Windows to keep up to an additional 2GB of active data in memory rather than moving it to slower storage. "So an app or tab you left open is less likely to reload when you return," he explained, helping prevent interruptions and slowdowns even on devices with just 8GB of RAM.

articles.title: “Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia
articles.text:
On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.
“Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Big Tech.”
Currently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board said reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.
Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.
If Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN said. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.
Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.
“Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”
Trump officials accused of “corruption”
What Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who plan to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”
“I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon said. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”
Yoon noted that evidencesuggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon said. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.
The White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.
Other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.
“It is not just an intelligence issue; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal said. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”
Trump officials profit off Nvidia policies
Trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.
Other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP said. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”
“The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth said. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.
“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth said.
If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth said.
Nvidia “lucky” to have Sacks
Detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited New York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang quickly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.
Also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.
Huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that showed Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.
TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report said. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.
Lutnick “benefited greatly”
Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.
Lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP said. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.
“In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the company he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”
After Lutnick was required to hand that company over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.
Those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP said.
However, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the company helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.
Among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.
“Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon said.
Probes may delay Huang’s return
Haworth said the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.
“I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth said.
But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”
It seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon said. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal showed that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.
If US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.
Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon said could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.
“I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon said. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Receita Federal publica códigos no GitHub pela primeira vez • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Receita Federal publica códigos no GitHub pela primeira vez
Três projetos de software incluem calculadoras de CBS e IBS e poderão ser usados, modificados e distribuídos por desenvolvedores.
A Receita Federal publicou pela primeira vez projetos de software em repositórios públicos no GitHub. A iniciativa envolve a Calculadora de Tributos, ferramenta que aplica as regras da reforma tributária sobre o consumo e pode ser incorporada aos sistemas utilizados por empresas.
Segundo comunicado divulgado pelo órgão nessa segunda-feira (16/11), os projetos adotam a licença MIT, que permite utilizar, modificar e distribuir o código, inclusive em aplicações comerciais. A medida foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União.
A Calculadora de Tributos integra as regras de cálculo da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e de outros tributos previstos na reforma. O objetivo é permitir que desenvolvedores utilizem a mesma lógica da Receita em programas de faturamento, gestão e emissão de documentos fiscais.
O órgão disponibilizou três projetos no GitHub:
A expectativa da Receita é reduzir diferenças de cálculo, custos de desenvolvimento e dificuldades na adaptação às novas regras.
Com a publicação no GitHub, desenvolvedores poderão consultar as versões dos projetos, acompanhar alterações e analisar como os tributos são calculados. A licença MIT também permite adaptar os códigos para diferentes aplicações.
A Receita afirma que a iniciativa pretende aumentar a transparência e a segurança jurídica na implementação da reforma tributária. Vale destacar que o uso de softwares de código aberto não significa ausência de regras. Mesmo licenças permissivas, como a MIT, estabelecem condições para a redistribuição e reutilização dos projetos.
A calculadora já estava disponível para download na Plataforma CBS desde 2025. A novidade é sua publicação no GitHub, ambiente que facilita o acompanhamento de versões e a análise do código pela comunidade de desenvolvedores.
Desenvolvidos em parceria com o Serpro, os projetos não substituem os programas utilizados pelas empresas. A proposta é oferecer componentes oficiais que possam ser incorporados às soluções existentes durante a transição para o novo sistema tributário.

articles.title: Q.ANT Unveils NPU Gen 2+: Photonic Fourier Transforms Power Large Language Model
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
Q.ANT Unveils NPU Gen 2+: Photonic Fourier Transforms Power Large Language Model
Q.ANT, the pioneer in commercial photonic computing, today unveiled the NPU Gen 2+, the latest generation of its Native Processing Unit (NPU) technology, at SC26 in Chicago. The NPU Gen 2+ adds optical Discrete Fourier Transforms (DFTs), which expands the set of mathematical functions developers can run directly in light with photonic computing. With it, developers can build faster, leaner AI models and high-performance computing (HPC) applications.
Advanced functions like the DFT let AI models work with fewer parameters and less data. On digital hardware, however, computing the transform itself with high data volumes costs time and energy. Because the NPU Gen 2+ delivers DFTs natively in light, Q.ANT demonstrates the potential algorithmic and performance advantages of photonic computing already now.Developers can now approach computationally intensive functions in new ways using the DFT capabilities of the NPU Gen 2+: Light carries out complex computations in a single pass, extending the set of available instructions beyond add and multiply functions of classical computing and making AI models more expressive and more powerful. For data center operators, integrating photonic hardware into their environments opens new capabilities for users while potentially lowering energy consumption and operating costs significantly.
Today's language models rely on attention mechanisms that require massive compute to model relationships between tokens, but Q.ANT's NPU Gen 2+ gives developers a new way to explore these mechanisms leveraging photonic computing as an expansion to classical computation.
At SC26, Q.ANT demonstrates this potential in a hybrid computing system coupling the NPU Gen 2+ with an AMD GPU to run a large language model (LLM) for the first time with optics. The demonstration shows how these mathematical functions performed in light can replace a computationally intensive attention layer and address a major computational bottleneck in generative AI.
Rethinking AI Algorithms for a New Computing Architecture
The NPU Gen 2+ performs these DFTs in a single operation using the physical properties of light, instead of the sequence of energy-intensive electronic calculations that classical computing demands. These advances help establish photonic processors as a complementary computing architecture, with the NPU as a co-processor alongside CPUs and GPUs, so developers can distribute the specific workloads that are most computationally intensive, to where they can be processed the most efficiently.
At the heart of the NPU Gen 2+ is an optical component on the photonic chip that allows the processor to directly perform DFTs, a fundamental mathematical operation used in signal and image processing, simulations, and data analysis. The NPU Gen 2+ extends photonic computing to workloads that are typically expensive for electronic processors. It builds on the processor generation NPU Gen 2, launched in 2025, and its focus on matrix multiplication and non-linear operations.
Michael Förtsch, CEO of Q.ANT"With Gen 2+, we're opening the door to software that uses what light does naturally. That allows leaner AI models with fewer parameters and less data, and that is what will make the next wave of AI affordable," "With the DFT performed natively, developers now have a new tool to reshape the mathematics of AI models. This is an important step on our roadmap to combine more optical components on our chips for even more sophisticated functions, driving new algorithms and applications. By running a large language model in a hybrid system with an AMD GPU, we have shown that our processors work as co-processors with GPUs. We're building a community with pioneering developers on the journey to a new era of computing."
Giving Developers New Tools to Compute with Light
The introduction of the NPU Gen 2+ also expands the potential of Q.ANT's software development ecosystem.
In September 2026, Q.ANT launched its open-source software development kit (SDK), providing developers with APIs for C and Python, example applications, documentation, and a CPU-based simulation environment. The toolkit allows programmers to begin designing and testing applications for photonic computing without requiring direct access to optical hardware, while the company's recent launch of its photonic pilot with IONOS allows access to real hardware.
Q.ANT is now extending its SDK to support NPU Gen 2+ capabilities, enabling developers to experiment with Fourier-based algorithms and investigate how these operations can be incorporated into AI and HPC software.
Utz Bacher, VP of Software at Q.ANT"Photonic computing gives software developers a chance to rethink the mathematics behind their applications," "When a complex mathematical operation can be performed directly through the physics of light, it changes the questions developers can ask. Instead of simply optimizing existing code, we can explore different algorithms that use these native operations to solve problems in new ways. Our work with Fourier-based attention layers in language models is an early example of that opportunity."
Building the Foundation for Hybrid Photonic Computing
The NPU Gen 2+ represents another step in Q.ANT's roadmap toward more advanced photonic computing architectures.
The new processor retains the integration through PCIe into standard rack-mountable server systems for ease of integration, as the future of computing will depend on the evolution of hybrid systems. Optical processors like Q.ANT's NPU Gen 2 and Gen 2+ complement the capabilities of CPUs and GPUs with their ability to perform select mathematical functions. Q.ANT plans to offer commercial systems combining Gen 2 and Gen 2+ processors in the second half of 2027.
Going forward, Q.ANT is exploring how multiple optical functions can be combined on its chips to support increasingly complex computational workflows. By expanding the mathematical functions available to developers, it aims to create the foundation for algorithms and applications that optimize data processing across AI and HPC with native photonic computation.
