articles.title: Philips Hue Liane 360° Rope Light review: a sculptural, all-angle glow that turns any room into a design magazine spread — for a luxury price
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light is the latest product to use Philips' very impressive OmniGlow technology, which delivers seamless gradients and shades without the visible LEDs of lesser lightstrips. As a piece of technology it's flawless: it's beautiful, incredibly flexible and easy to control and automate. But it's also three times the price of an OmniGlow strip.
Reasons to buy
- + The most beautiful Hue ever
- + Super-smooth gradients and solid colors
- + Illumination in every direction
Reasons to avoid
- - The most expensive Hue light ever
- - Cuttable but not expandable
- - Don't forget to dust it
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light: two minute review
The Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light is the most stunning Hue light to date, taking Philips' impressive, seamless OmniGlow technology and turning it into a very bright rope light that emits white and colored light in all directions. It's architectural lighting rather than functional or task lighting: this is a light made to be looked at, whether that's in a huge contemporary kitchen or on the wall of a hip and cosy café.
The Liane Rope Light delivers everything that's great about Hue's OmniGlow Lightstrip, which uses miniLEDs to deliver a completely seamless light without visible LEDs spoiling the illusion, and it extends that light in all directions so it can be located anywhere. One Liane Rope Light is striking; multiple ones in different colors are stunning.
Once connected to a Hue hub you can use the Hue app to create light recipes and automation either for the Liane on its own or as part of a wider Hue setup. Hue's technology is well established and its app is highly polished, so setting up your Liane and getting it just-so is very straightforward.
The Liane Rope Light is the most beautiful Hue light yet. But the Hue OmniGlow is likely to be a better buy for most due to its much lower price.
Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light: price and release date
- 3m/10ft: $399.99 / £379.99 (about AU$740)
- 5m/16ft: $529.99 / £469.99 (about AU$920)
- Launched September 2026
The Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light was unveiled in September 2026 and is available in two lengths, 3m (10ft) and 5m (16ft). The 3m has an list price of $399.99 / £379.99 (about AU$740), and the 5m is $529.99 / £469.99 (about AU$920).
That's roughly three times the price of the equivalent OmniGlow lightstrip, but the OmniGlow lightstrip is single-sided. The Liane 360º emits light in all directions at once: it's effectively two OmniGlow lightstrips back to back, which is why it costs so much.
Although the Liane Rope Light is expensive for a consumer lighting product I suspect it'll find a home in commercial premises such as shops, bars, hotels, cafés and so on thanks to its neon-esque brightness, its controllability and its flexibility: being able to do colors and gradients is a big plus compared to other rope lighting. Commercial lighting is much less price-sensitive than lights for your living room.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Value score: 4/5
Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light review: design
- Featureless white silicone
- Seamless colors and smooth gradients
- Complete with mounting accessories
If you've ever seen one of those 'painting with light'photographs, the Liane Rope Light looks like that: it resembles a really thick halogen filament or a neon light floating in space. Using this as a traditional lightstrip feels like a waste of its potential: I'd say it's best thought of as architectural lighting, a talking point rather than task or ambient lighting.
The Liane is designed to be seen, and to look good both on and off. Switched off it's a completely featureless, flexible white silicone tube with a diameter of 22mm and a cable to the power supply on one end. Philips also includes discreet transparent mounts so you can hang the Liane from the ceiling or mount it across a wall without the mounts spoiling the Liane's looks. The only downside to the white silicone is that it's a material that attracts dust, dirt and dog hair very easily, and that dust is quite visible when it's powered off or brightly lit.
This is an OmniGlow light, and that means unlike cheaper lightstrips there aren't any visible, distinct LEDs: it uses microLEDs to deliver unbroken illumination. Installation is simple, and the Hue app also tells you how to put the parts of your light together and how to hang it from the ceiling. The Liane we tested came with a ceiling hook for easy installation, a weight for the other end, and a bag of transparent clips for hanging it from walls and other surfaces.
Like other OmniGlow lightstrips, the Liane can be cut to reduce its size but it can't be extended. It's rated IP20, which means it's designed for dry indoor environments only.
Design score: 5/5
Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light: performance
- Stunning colors and gradients
- Up to 3,750 lumens (5m)
- Wide range of colors and temperatures
Length: 3m or 5m
Mounting options: Ceiling, wall
Bulb type: Dimmable gradient coloured and white light (RGB1CW)
Colour temperature: 1,000-20,000K
Output (4000K): 2,250 lumens (3m) / 3,750 lumens (5m)
Output (2700K): 1,950 lumens (3m) / 3,250 lumens (5m)
Wattage: 60W
Zigbee repeater: Yes
The Hue Liane 360º Rope Light is capable of very high brightness: the 5m version can put out up to 3,750 lumens of brightness at a color temperature of 4,000K, which is the sweet spot between warm white and cool white if you like a halogen-style warmth. It can deliver color temperatures between 1,000K and 20,000K, and it's capable of subtle effects such as emulating a flickering campfire or a running a subtle color-changing loop.
When I first tried the Liane Rope Light there were some issues with the motion effects and color transitions, with visible banding rather than the smooth movement I've already enjoyed in the OmniGlow lightstrip. The culprit appears to have been a software or firmware bug, as updating the Liane's software made the banding go away. Once updated the lighting was completely seamless, with colors blending happily and motion effects coming and going smoothly.
The Liane Rope Light responds quickly to commands from the app, and you can group it with other Hue lights and bulbs for multi-light scenes and for controlling via your voice assistant; I used Apple's Siri but Hue also works with Alexa, Google Assistant and Sonos Voice Control.
Performance score: 5/5
Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light: should you buy it?
| Design | 5/5 | Genuinely gorgeous, with thoughtful design and mounting options | 
| Performance | 5/5 | Exceptionally bright for a smart light with wide color range and extensive customization. | 
| Value | 4/5 | Good tech costs money, we know, but you can get an OmniGlow for a third of the price if you don't need 360-degree illumination. | 
Buy it if...
You've got great style
The Liane Rope Light is more of a statement than a smart light: it's made to be seen, and to attract attention.
You're so modern
Smart rope lighting is always going to be a bit Blade Runner, and that might be incongruous if installed in a non-contemporary space.
You've got cash to splash
There's no getting away from it: this is really expensive compared to an ordinary smart lightstrip.
Don't buy it if...
You're on a budget
Normal OmniGlow lightstrips are a third of the price, and basic Hue lightstrips are even cheaper.
You've got a small space
3m of rope lighting might not sound big, but it's taller than most ceilings.
You're a hermit
The Liane Rope Light is a feature, a talking point rather than an ordinary light. Using it for ordinary illumination that others won't see is a waste of its talents.
Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light: also consider
When we reviewed the OmniGlow lightstrip we said that it was "the best Hue lightstrip yet", and it still is: if you don't need the 360-degree illumination of the Liane the OmniGlow delivers the same seamless colors and smooth gradients for considerably less money.
If you're not already on board the Hue train, Govee's OmniGlow rival isn't quite as bright as Hue's lightstrips but it's a lot cheaper at under $90/£90 for 2m. Its more rounded shape means it's more curvy-looking than the OmniGlow and like the Hue lightstrip it's extendable.
Philips Hue Liane 360º Rope Light: how we tested
I used the Hue Liane 360º Rope Light in my already Hue-happy home, draping it over curtains and bookcases, wrapping it around guitars and grouping it with other Hue products in scenes and automations. My Hue hub is the standard, non-pro model and I have a mix of Hue lightstrips and color & ambience bulbs around my living room and kitchen/dining area.
First reviewed November 2026
Contributor
Writer, broadcaster, musician and kitchen gadget obsessive Carrie Marshall has been writing about tech since 1998, contributing sage advice and odd opinions to all kinds of magazines and websites as well as writing more than twenty books. Her latest, a love letter to music titled Small Town Joy, is on sale now. She is the singer in spectacularly obscure Glaswegian rock band Unquiet Mind.

articles.title: Après un flop en Europe, la marque officielle du Parti chinois brade son prestige avec un SUV à 35 000 €
articles.text:
Hongqi est la marque de prestige du groupe public chinois FAW. Elle a été créée à la fin des années 1950 pour fabriquer les voitures des dirigeants du Parti communiste, et elle avait fait son entrée au Mondial de Paris 2024. Sur son stand, ses grandes électriques EH7 et EHS7 étaient affichées autour de 50 000 €. Deux ans plus tard, Hongqi revoit sa copie et redescend en gamme.
La marque a donc présenté à Venise ce lundi 16 novembre 2026 l’EHS4, un SUV électrique compact que son communiqué décrit comme son premier modèle conçu pour le marché européen. Pour tenter de se relancer, Hongqi a ainsi pris la base d’un modèle déjà « éprouvé » en Europe : le Leapmotor B10.
Un Leapmotor B10 rhabillé, en plus cher
Côté fiche technique, l’EHS4 reçoit un moteur à l’arrière de 218 ch, alimenté par une batterie LFP de 68,7 kWh. Hongqi promet jusqu’à 470 km d’autonomie en cycle WLTP, soit 20 km de plus que le B10 (450 km), et une recharge de 30 à 80 % en 18 minutes, avec une puissance maximale de 168 kW.
Dans sa présentation, Hongqi ne cite pas Leapmotor et préfère parler de son centre de design de Munich. Pourtant, l’EHS4 a la même plateforme, le même moteur et la même suspension que le B10. Il s’en distingue par une face avant redessinée, une nouvelle planche de bord, un autre volant et 25 mm de longueur en plus.
Ce partage s’explique par les maisons mères : FAW a signé un accord de coopération avec Leapmotor en mars 2025 et détient environ 5 % de son capital. Stellantis figure lui aussi parmi les principaux actionnaires de Leapmotor, dont il vend les modèles en Europe.
Côté prix, Julien Gautherot, directeur de Hongqi France, indiquait à nos confrères du Journal de l’Automobile une fourchette comprise entre 35 000 € et 40 000 € pour la France. En Italie, l’EHS4 démarre à 35 900 €, ou 32 900 € avec l’offre de lancement.
Sauf que le B10 démarre à 29 400 € en France. Depuis fin octobre, il descend même à 25 750 € avec la prime CEE de 3 650 €. Hongqi demande donc au moins 5 600 € de plus pour une technique identique.
Hongqi pourrait aussi s’appuyer sur Stellantis pour produire. Au printemps, la marque était en discussion avec Stellantis pour fabriquer ses voitures à Saragosse, en Espagne, dans l’usine où est justement assemblé le Leapmotor B10. De quoi éviter la surtaxe douanière et se rendre éligible aux primes en France.
Un réseau à monter en 18 mois
Hongqi n’est pas venu au Mondial de l’Auto 2026, mais vise toujours un lancement en France ce mois de novembre. La marque passe par l’importateur Car East France, ancien distributeur de MG et importateur de Maxus. Celui-ci prévoit d’ouvrir d’abord dans les 12 plus grandes métropoles, puis d’arriver à une cinquantaine de points de vente d’ici 18 mois. Il financera lui-même le stock de voitures, sans passer par les concessionnaires.

articles.title: Sony accélère le déploiement de son QSSR (au goût de PS5 Pro) sur PS5 classique
articles.text:
Sony poursuit le déploiement de son QSSR sur les PS5 classiques. Après Marvel's Wolverine et Ghost of Yotei, c'est au tour de Marvel's Spider-Man 2 d'en profiter. Et plusieurs autres jeux sont déjà annoncés, dont Control Resonant.
La PS5 classique n'a pas dit son dernier mot sur le terrain des améliorations graphiques. Annoncé en octobre dernier, le QSSR (pour Quick Spectral Super Resolution) continue de faire son chemin dans la ludothèque de Sony. Cette technologie d'upscaling assistée par l'IA s'inspire directement du PSSR de la PS5 Pro, mais dans une version « allégée », adaptée aux capacités de la console standard.
L'objectif reste néanmoins le même, à savoir reconstruire une image plus détaillée à partir d'une résolution inférieure, tout en améliorant sa stabilité et sa netteté. Le QSSR ne pousse donc pas le traitement aussi loin que son grand frère sur PS5 Pro, mais il permet d'obtenir un rendu plus propre, sans avoir pour cela à changer de machine.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Spider-Man 2 rejoint Wolverine et Ghost of Yotei
Après une première apparition dans Marvel's Wolverine et Ghost of Yotei, le QSSR débarque désormais dans Marvel's Spider-Man 2. La technologie est prise en charge dans les deux modes graphiques du jeu, Fidélité et Performance.
Un ajout intéressant pour le titre d'Insomniac Games, dont les environnements particulièrement détaillés et les déplacements rapides de l'homme-araignée mettent rudement à l'épreuve la stabilité de l'image. Le QSSR doit notamment contribuer à mieux restituer les détails fins et à limiter certains défauts visuels.
Cinq autres jeux vont bientôt profiter du QSSR sur PS5
Sony ne compte visiblement pas s'arrêter en si bon chemin, puisque plusieurs studios ont déjà confirmé leur intention d'intégrer cette technologie QSSR à leurs productions.
C'est notamment le cas de Remedy, qui prévoit de proposer le QSSR dans le récent Control Resonant dès le mois de décembre. Selon les développeurs, cette intégration doit permettre d'obtenir une image visiblement plus stable et détaillée. La vidéo ci-dessus permet de visualiser une partie des bienfaits du QSSR.
D'autres jeux sont également concernés :
- ARC Raiders (Embark Studios)
- The Finals (Embark Studios)
- No Man's Sky (Hello Games)
- Hell Let Loose (Expression Games)
Ces différentes intégrations doivent arriver au cours des prochaines semaines, au gré des mises à jour proposées par les studios.
Alors non, le QSSR ne va pas transformer votre PS5 classique en PS5 Pro, et tous les jeux ne pourront pas nécessairement en profiter. Mais cette déclinaison du PSSR a le mérite d'offrir une forme de « seconde jeunesse » visuelle à certains titres, sans imposer aux joueurs de passer à la caisse pour changer de console.
Concernant la PS5 Pro, depuis plusieurs semaines, la console est en rupture de stock chez de nombreux revendeurs (y compris chez PlayStation), et certains vendeurs n'hésitent pas à faire flamber les prix… jusqu'à 1 500 euros sur Amazon ! Et il y a fort à parier qu'un certain GTA VI, dont la disponibilité est fixée à ce jeudi 19 novembre, n'y est pas totalement étranger.
- Améliorations graphiques significatives
- Technologie PSSR efficace quand bien implémentée
- Efficacité énergétique

articles.title: GTA 6 Speicher-Check: So machst du deine PS5 & Xbox fit für den 200-GB-Giganten
articles.text:
GTA 6 braucht 200 GB: So rüstest du deine Konsole jetzt auf
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Am 19. November 2026 erscheint GTA 6. Fans der Reihe mussten sich lange gedulden, denn die Veröffentlichung des Vorgängers liegt mehr als 13 Jahre zurück. Während die Vorfreude steigt, machen neue Details allerdings klar, dass das Spiel die bisherige Hardware an ihre Grenzen bringen könnte – auch beim Speicherplatz. Wir erklären dir, wie groß der Download des langersehnten Spiels ausfallen könnte und mit welchen externen Festplatten du deine Konsole aufrüstest.
Speicherlösungen für PS5 und Xbox bei GTA 6
Mehrere Medien, darunter Yahoo Tech, berichten, dass der Download von GTA 6 über 200 Gigabyte groß sein soll. Grund dafür könnten das aufwendige Design und das immersive Spielerlebnis sein. Rockstar Games hat den Umfang bisher zwar nicht offiziell bestätigt, aber auch frühere Titel brauchten viel Platz. So kam beispielsweise Red Dead Redemption 2 auf rund 125 Gigabyte. Der interne Speicher von Playstation- und Xbox-Konsolen ist allerdings begrenzt. Oft startet er bei einem Terabyte, die kompaktere Xbox Series S gibt es sogar mit nur 512 Gigabyte. Der tatsächlich freie Speicher fällt noch geringer aus, weil die Konsole einen Teil für das Betriebssystem und weitere Systemfunktionen reserviert. Wenn du ein Spiel wie GTA 6 installieren willst, wird es also schnell eng.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Die gute Nachricht ist, dass du deine Konsole um eine externe Festplatte oder SSD erweitern kannst. Dabei gibt es aber einiges zu beachten. Anders als bei älteren Konsolen kannst du Spiele für die Playstation 5 nämlich nicht direkt auf einem externen USB-Speicher zocken. Der Grund: Diese bieten nicht die nötige Geschwindigkeit. Zum Spielen müssen die Games also zuerst auf den internen Speicher der Konsole kopiert werden. Eine externe Festplatte oder SSD dient bei der Playstation 5 daher eher als Archiv für Spiele, die du länger nicht gezockt hast, und schafft Platz auf der internen Festplatte.
Xbox Series X und S mit Speichererweiterungskarten aufrüsten
Auch bei der Xbox hängt die Nutzung eines externen Speichers von der Konsolengeneration ab. Bei älteren Modellen kannst du direkt von einer externen Festplatte oder SSD spielen. Bei der Xbox Series X und Series S geht das nicht. Eine Ausnahme bildet die externe Speichererweiterungskarte: Sie wurde in Zusammenarbeit mit Xbox entwickelt und bietet ein nahtloses Spielerlebnis, weil du hier Games direkt von der Karte starten und spielen kannst. Sie ist so konzipiert, dass sie die gleiche Speicherleistung wie die interne SSD bietet. Laut Herstellerangaben sorgt eine Übertragungsrate von 3.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde für schnelle Ladezeiten und geringe Latenzen. Du steckst die Karte auf der Rückseite der Xbox direkt in den dafür vorgesehenen Steckplatz. Das Modell von Seagate ist mit einem oder zwei Terabyte erhältlich. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 282,99 Euro.
Seagate Game Drive als externe Festplatte für PS5 und Xbox
Sony bietet selbst einige externe Speicheroptionen an, die auf die Playstation 5 optimiert sind. Eine davon ist der Game Drive von Seagate. Der Durchmesser des Geräts beträgt 2,5 Zoll. Das Design ist der Konsole angepasst – inklusive Logo. Die externe Festplatte ist mit zwei oder fünf Terabyte erhältlich und bietet somit ausreichend Platz, um ältere Spiele zu archivieren oder überall hin mitzunehmen. Du schließt sie per USB-3.0-Schnittstelle direkt an die Konsole an. Ein erneutes Herunterladen entfällt somit. Bei Amazon kostet die kleinere Variante aktuell 150,99 Euro. Das gleiche Modell gibt es auch für die Xbox mit der klassischen schwarzen Optik der Microsoft-Konsole. Es ist mit zwei, acht und 20 Terabyte verfügbar, der Preis startet bei 128,99 Euro.
- Seagate Game Drive für Playstation 5 bei Amazon*
- Seagate Game Drive für Xbox Series X und Series S bei Amazon*
Sandisk Extreme Portable SSD für die Playstation 5
Auch Sandisk bietet externen Speicher, der offiziell für die Playstation 5 lizenziert ist. Die SSD misst ebenfalls 2,5 Zoll und orientiert sich mit ihrer weißen Farbe am Design der Sony-Konsole. Laut Hersteller bietet sie eine hohe Geschwindigkeit von bis zu 1.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde, um Spiele schnell vom externen SSD-Archiv auf den internen Speicher der Playstation 5 zu übertragen. Zudem ist sie besonders robust: Sie bietet IP65-Schutz und ist fallsicher aus bis zu drei Metern Höhe. Wie die Seagate-Festplatte schließt du die SSD per USB an die Konsole an. Das Modell gibt es mit einem oder zwei Terabyte Speicherplatz. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 200,99 Euro. Laut etablierten Preisvergleichsportalen ist das aktuell das günstigste Angebot. Trotzdem kann es sich lohnen, mit dem Kauf noch etwas zu warten, denn bis vor Kurzem war die SSD schon ab 179 Euro erhältlich.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 02.11.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Netflix estrenó una pestaña con IA en la TV que recomienda qué ver según el ánimo del usuario
articles.text:
Netflix comenzó a probar el 3 de noviembre una pestaña llamada AI Discover en su aplicación para televisores. La función usa inteligencia artificial para sugerir series y películas según el estado de ánimo, el tiempo disponible y el historial de cada persona. Por ahora la tiene un grupo reducido de suscriptores.
Según el anuncio de la empresa, el despliegue empezó en Estados Unidos, para quienes usan Netflix en inglés en televisores compatibles. Netflix indicó que ampliará el acceso a más personas “en las próximas semanas”. No precisó si la función llegará a otros países ni cuándo.
Quien la tenga verá en el menú superior de la pantalla una opción llamada Discover, con un ícono de gema roja y una etiqueta de “Nuevo”. Los elegidos también reciben un correo electrónico. Los perfiles infantiles quedan fuera.
Cómo funciona la pestaña
La primera versión se basa en temas. El usuario elige uno, cada uno ilustrado con un fragmento de una serie o película, y la aplicación muestra recomendaciones relacionadas. Hay temas por ánimo, como “Algo ligero” o “Asústame”, por compañía, como “Noche de cine en familia”, o por tiempo, como “Vistazos rápidos”.
Después aparecen temas más específicos para afinar la búsqueda. Quien no quede conforme puede elegir “Algo diferente” y recibir un grupo nuevo de títulos. Según la revista Variety, las sugerencias se generan en tiempo real a partir del historial, las preferencias y lo que está de moda en la plataforma.
Cada título trae un botón para ajustar las recomendaciones, junto a “Reproducir” y “Mi lista”. Sirve para conservar una sugerencia o pedir que no se vuelva a mostrar. Según el Centro de ayuda de Netflix, ese rechazo solo vale dentro de AI Discover y no cambia lo que se recomienda en el resto del servicio.
Variety precisó que no se trata de un chatbot: el usuario no escribe preguntas, sino que navega por temas. Netflix dijo que la herramienta funciona con una “capa de inteligencia” nueva que responde en tiempo real a lo que dicen los usuarios y sigue aprendiendo.
Una prueba, no un reemplazo
Netflix describió la pestaña como su “cocina de pruebas”, donde ensaya fórmulas nuevas de descubrimiento según el uso y los comentarios de los suscriptores. Algunas podrían pasar luego a la experiencia principal. La empresa aclaró que probar la función es opcional y que el servicio habitual no cambia.
El Centro de ayuda advierte además que la herramienta sigue en una etapa temprana y que, como cualquier función con inteligencia artificial, puede cometer errores. Para opinar, los suscriptores pueden escribir a Netflix y mencionar “AI Discover”.
Según Variety, es la primera función de cara al público que Netflix presenta con la marca de inteligencia artificial, aunque la compañía usa aprendizaje automático para personalizar recomendaciones desde hace años. El 7 de mayo de 2025, TechCrunch informó que Netflix había lanzado una búsqueda conversacional basada en ChatGPT, como prueba opcional en iPhone.
Los límites que señalan los críticos
La revista Inc cuestionó el alcance de la novedad. Su columnista Amy Zwagerman sostuvo que el problema de fondo del streaming está fuera de Netflix, porque la herramienta filtra solo dentro del catálogo de la plataforma y no indica si un título está en otro servicio.
Esa limitación es inherente al diseño: la pestaña recomienda únicamente contenido de Netflix. La empresa no publicó cifras sobre cuántos suscriptores tienen acceso ni resultados de la prueba.
El único plazo que dio Netflix es el de la ampliación gradual del acceso en las semanas posteriores al 3 de noviembre, sin fecha concreta ni lista de países.

articles.title: British Scattered Spider hacker sentenced to 6 years in prison
articles.text:
A leader of the Scattered Spider cybercrime collective has been sentenced to six years in prison in the United States for stealing millions in cryptocurrency and conspiring to hack a dozen companies.
US prosecutors charged 24-year-old British man Tyler Robert Buchanan and four other suspects in November with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft in relation to a series of phishing attacks between September 2021 and April 2023.
According to court documents, their victims include companies across a wide range of industries, such as telecommunications, technology, business process outsourcing (BPO), entertainment, and information technology (IT) suppliers, as well as virtual currency providers, cloud communications providers, and individuals.
Buchanan and his accomplices sent hundreds of SMS phishing messages to victim companies' employees' phones (while impersonating the companies or a contracted IT or BPO supplier) to trick them into entering sensitive information (including credentials and personally identifiable information) into phishing pages that looked like their employers' legitimate websites.
The stolen information was used to steal over $11.6 million of virtual currency after compromising victims' cryptocurrency accounts and wallets via Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) swaps (also known as SIM swapping attacks).
"Those thefts had severe, life-altering consequences for many victims and underscore both the seriousness and far-reaching impact of this conspiracy," the prosecutors argued in a sentencing memorandum.
"In April 2023, on a digital device found at Buchanan's Scotland residence, he possessed the names and addresses of numerous individual victims, including a text file that contained cryptocurrency seed phrases and login information for one victim's account," the US Justice Department added.
Buchanan was arrested in Palma de Mallorca, Spain, in June 2024, has been in US federal custody since April 2025, and pleaded guilty to crypto theft charges in April.
Three of his accomplices (Evans Onyeaka Osiebo, Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy, and Joel Martin Evans) were also charged in November 2024 with wire fraud, wire fraud conspiracy, and aggravated identity theft and are now serving multi-year prison sentences after pleading guilty.
Noah Michael Urban (also known online as Sosa and Elijah), a fourth conspirator and another Scattered Spider key member, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to wire fraud and conspiracy charges in April 2025.
Scattered Spider hacking collective
The Scattered Spider gang (also tracked as 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Octo Tempest, Starfraud, UNC3944, and Muddled Libra) is a loose-knit group of young, English-speaking threat actors that orchestrates attacks through Telegram channels, Discord servers, and hacker forums.
Scattered Spider has also partnered with several Russian ransomware operations since early 2023, including BlackCat/AlphV, Qilin, and RansomHub.
This cybercrime group was previously linked to breaches at multiple high-profile companies and organizations, including Caesars, Riot Games, MailChimp, Twilio, DoorDash, and Reddit.
According to the FBI, they're using a wide range of tactics to breach corporate victims' networks, including social engineering, multi-factor authentication (MFA) bombing (targeted MFA fatigue), phishing, and SIM swapping.
Some Scattered Spider members have also previously been linked to "The Com," another hacking collective behind violent incidents and cyberattacks.

articles.title: Para Pattinson, "el honor de una vida". Para Hollywood, no salir de los cinco nombres de siempre: Zendaya, Holland, Hathaway...
articles.text:
Las dos películas más taquilleras del año comparten tres actores, las dos más esperadas de diciembre comparten una actriz y el nuevo James Bond ha coincidido con Zendaya en tres estrenos en 2026. La impresión que dan estos nuevos repartos de jóvenes estrellas es que Hollywood tiene actualmente un reparto fijo y con muy pocas variables.
Pattinson 007. Amazon MGM Studios acaba de anunciar que Robert Pattinson será el nuevo James Bond en la próxima película de la franquicia, que dirigirá Denis Villeneuve, un papel que el actor describe como "el honor de una vida". El propio comunicado repasa un año especialmente fértil para el intérprete: 'El drama', 'La Odisea', 'Primetime' y 'Dune: Parte Tres', que llega en diciembre. Todo ello compaginado con el rodaje de 'The Batman Part II'.
Cambio de planes. En septiembre de 2025, el equipo de Villeneuve buscaba a un británico poco conocido de entre veintitantos y treinta y pocos años. Por contra, Pattinson tiene 40 y lleva la capa de Batman desde 2022, y ya se habla de él como el actor más asentado que ha recibido nunca el papel. El fichaje interesa sobre todo por lo que retrata: en una saga donde el personaje siempre ha ido por delante del actor, el papel ha acabado recalando dentro del grupo reducido de intérpretes que copa los grandes estrenos del año.
Zendaya es el núcleo. Este año, Zendaya ha sido Emma en 'El drama', Atenea en 'La Odisea' y MJ en 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', y cerrará 2026 como Chani en 'Dune: Parte Tres'. Coincide con Pattinson en tres de esos cuatro títulos. ¿Más casos? Tom Holland es su compañero de reparto en dos: Telémaco en 'La Odisea' y Peter Parker en la de Spider-Man. Ojo a Jon Bernthal también: Menelao en ‘La Odisea’ y Punisher en ‘Brand New Day’. Visto de otro modo: dos de las películas más taquilleras del año comparten tres actores.
Y muchos más nombres propios: Anne Hathaway suma cinco estrenos, entre ellos ‘El diablo viste de Prada 2’ y la película de Nolan. Florence Pugh hizo un cameo en ‘Spider-Man’ y el 18 de diciembre estrena el mismo día ‘Dune: Parte Tres’ y ‘Vengadores: Doomsday’. En esta última coincide con Pedro Pascal, que en mayo protagonizó ‘The Mandalorian and Grogu’. Timothée Chalamet entró en 2026 con ‘Marty Supreme’, la película más taquillera de la historia de A24, y lo cierra con ‘Dune: Parte Tres’.
¿Por qué existe esta concentración de actores? Fácil: la taquilla. 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' (2.521 millones de dólares), ‘La Odisea’ (1.805 millones) y ‘El diablo viste de Prada 2’ (693 millones) suman 5.020 millones este año: el 47% de lo que recaudan las diez películas más taquilleras del año, y el 64% si solo se cuentan las siete de imagen real. Universal comunicó en septiembre que ‘La Odisea’ ya era la película más taquillera de su historia, y el primer fin de semana en que coincidió con ‘Spider-Man’ ambas se repartieron el 94,6% de la recaudación.
Concentración de poder. Un estudio de la Universidad de California contó 128 estrenos de los grandes estudios en 2006 y 66 en 2025, y sus autoras lo atribuyen a una estrategia deliberada de concentrar el dinero y las pantallas en cada título. En taquilla se nota: en 2019 hubo 20 películas que superaron los diez millones de entradas, y en 2025 fueron 12. Una lectura posible es que, con la mitad de estrenos que hace veinte años, cada película pesa el doble en las cuentas del estudio.
Y detrás de la cámara, igual. El circuito también es reducido al otro lado de la cámara. Nolan, que ya funciona como una franquicia en sí mismo, y Villeneuve se reparten a Pattinson y a Zendaya, y Bond ha ido a parar al actor con el que Villeneuve acababa de rodar 'Dune'. Todo eso impacta en los calendarios: ha habido retrasos en rodajes y estrenos porque Hathaway ha tenido que promocionar cinco películas en seis meses.
Una cuestión de público. Todos estos intérpretes apelan a públicos distintos. La generación Z es la que más entradas compra y adora a Zendaya y a Holland, los millennials veneran a Hathaway y a Pascal, y Pattinson conecta con los dos públicos. Sin embargo, no siempre funciona: Pascal no evitó que ‘The Mandalorian and Grogu’ firmara el peor estreno de Star Wars en la era Disney. Y Pattinson no salvó ‘Mickey 17’, mientras que el casi siempre infalible Tom Cruise encaja con ‘Digger’ una pérdida que se estima en unos 250 millones.
Excepciones que confirman la regla. 'Obsession', la película de terror del youtuber Curry Barker, se rodó en 20 días con 750.000 dólares con un reparto mayoritariamente desconocido. Es la décima película más taquillera del año, con 521 millones recaudados. Este año, los directores formados en YouTube están ganando a Disney en taquilla. El círculo de elegidos, en cualquier caso, busca rápido nuevos miembros: al parecer su protagonista, Inde Navarrette, ya prepara su debut en Marvel.

articles.title: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.
While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).
Even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the company. When Amazon invested billions in Anthropic in 2023 and 2024 (long before Claude Code took the enterprise world by storm, back in the days when Anthropic looked like it would forever be a speck in OpenAI’s shadow), the cloud giant obtained promissory notes that could convert into equity.
These notes carry conversion prices of about $2.09 or $5.05 per share, depending on the year of investment. Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership. (The shares can receive dividends and convert to standard voting Class A shares when sold, the filing says.)
But it has also opted to hold on to billions of dollars’ worth of the notes for now. If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise).
Google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO. A group of major tech companies (AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners) have agreed to buy $26 billion worth of this non-voting stock. Google and Nvidia each agreed to buy $10 billion worth.
So while a lot of investors stand to make billions of dollars in Anthropic’s IPO, Amazon is one of the biggest winners, and that doesn’t even count what AWS stands to earn from Anthropic’s commitment to spend more than $100 billion on its cloud services over the next decade.

articles.title: Le hacker de GTA 6 plaide coupable : il a bien piraté Rockstar Games en 2022
articles.text:
Le 18 septembre 2022, Rockstar Games était victime de l’une des fuites les plus importantes de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Arion Kurtaj, alors âgé de 17 ans, a récupéré 90 séquences de gameplay. Arrêté et condamné depuis, il est repassé devant la justice pénale et pour la première fois, il a reconnu les faits.
Arion Kurtaj reconnaît enfin le piratage de Rockstar Games
Fin 2022, Arion Kurtaj, alors âgé de 17 ans, est impliqué dans les intrusions du groupe Lapsus$ contre Nvidia, BT/EE, Revolut. Il est arrêté et placé en détention provisoire, puis libéré sous caution dans l’attente de son procès. Une période durant laquelle il est hébergé dans un hôtel sous protection policière, puisque menacé par d’autres pirates à propos de bitcoins volés.
Privé d’ordinateur, Arion Kurtaj a utilisé un Amazon Fire Stick à l’arrière de la télévision de sa chambre, un clavier et une souris et a piraté Rockstar Games. Avec ce hack, il a récupéré 90 séquences de gameplay de GTA VI, accède au canal de communication interne de l’entreprise et menace de publier le code s’il n’est pas contacté. Faute de réponse, le jeune homme a diffusé toutes les vidéos et le code source sur un forum.
Sauf qu’il est repéré et devra rendre des comptes. En 2023 lors de son procès, les médecins ont estimé que la gravité de son autisme rendait Arion Kurtaj inapte à être jugé dans un procès pénal ordinaire. En décembre de la même année, le jury a conclu qu’Arion Kurtaj a bien commis ces actes et a prononcé une ordonnance d’hospitalisation sécurisée à durée indéterminée. Pour lui, le jeune hacker représentait toujours un danger ; il pourrait retomber dans le cybercrime.
Mais voilà, fin 2025, une évaluation médicale de routine l’a déclaré apte à être jugé. Une décision qui a entraîné son transfert d’un hôpital sécurisé vers une prison classique en janvier dernier. Ce changement de statut médical a permis l’ouverture d’une procédure pénale classique devant la Woolwich Crown Court. Le 16 novembre, Arion Kurtaj a enfin plaidé coupable pour l’ensemble des chefs d’accusation, dont le piratage de Rockstar Games, en plus des attaques contre Uber, BT/EE et Revolut.
Désormais âgé de 21 ans, le hacker recevra sa sentence le 23 novembre prochain selon plusieurs médias. Le tribunal devra déterminer la peine appropriée ; les préjudices causés s’élèveraient à 10 millions de livres sterling. À noter qu’Arion Kurtaj a commis des violences physiques en détention et avait réussi à s’y procurer un téléphone portable, ce qui est interdit.
Un traumatisme pour les développeurs de GTA VI (et pour les fans)
Ce nouveau procès s’est ouvert en marge de la sortie de GTA VI, le jeu vidéo le plus attendu de tous les temps qu’Arion Kurtaj avait fait fuiter en 2022. Face à l’ampleur de ce piratage et des séquences du jeu, Rockstar Games avait dû confirmer l’authenticité de ces extraits, tout en précisant que le jeu était encore en développement. L’éditeur ne prévoyait pas du tout de parler de GTA VI aussi tôt : la première bande-annonce n’est arrivée que le 5 décembre 2023, plus d’un an après la fuite.
L’entreprise a estimé le coût de cette attaque à environ 5 millions de dollars, ce qui comprend notamment des milliers d’heures de travail pour ses équipes. En effet, il a fallu analyser l’ampleur de la compromission, sécuriser les systèmes et surtout gérer les conséquences de la publication de ces extraits du jeu. Un traumatisme pour les développeurs du jeu, mais aussi pour les fans : beaucoup auraient préféré que ce soit le studio qui montre en premier le jeu, pour respecter son travail. Une blessure qui va s’atténuer avec l’excitation de la sortie du jeu ce jeudi 19 novembre, 13 ans après l’arrivée d’un certain GTA V.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo can now unlock with your face, no Face ID required
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Most iPhone owners haven't touched a fingerprint reader in years, so when the iPhone Duo arrived with Touch ID in its side button instead of Face ID, the change quickly became one of the foldable's most common complaints. Apple's fix doesn't involve any new hardware, though. The second developer beta of iOS 27.3, released Monday, lets the Duo recognize your face using the ordinary front camera on its outer screen.
The new option shows up as Unlock with Front Camera under Touch ID & Passcode in Settings. It only works while the phone is folded shut, though. Opening the Duo still means reaching for the fingerprint reader it launched with, or typing in a passcode.
Apple's own setup screen is surprisingly blunt about the trade-off, warning that the feature "isn't as secure as Touch ID or Face ID." That's likely because an ordinary selfie camera only sees a flat picture of you. Face ID, on the other hand, maps your face in 3D using more than 30,000 infrared dots.
As a result, the feature only gets you past the lock screen. Apple Pay, saved passwords and app sign-ins all still need a fingerprint. Even then, it won't kick in unless you've recently unlocked with Touch ID or a passcode. Leave the phone untouched for roughly 45 minutes, and it's back to the side button.
From what we saw in MacRumors' hands-on, setup feels closer to a quick head-turning drill than Face ID's slow circular roll. The phone simply asks you to turn your head left, right, up and down. Notably, Apple steers clear of the Face ID name entirely – the setup screens call it "Face Recognition" instead.
Once face recognition was set up, the closed Duo went from its lock screen to the home screen in roughly a second and a half, without a single button press.
The same beta also fixes a smaller annoyance. Until now, closing the Duo handed whatever app you were using over to the outer screen. A new Close to Lock setting under Display & Brightness simply locks the phone instead. Both features should reach everyone when iOS 27.3 rolls out in December.
As for proper Face ID, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has reported that iPhone Duo 2 prototypes already hide the sensor under the outer display. Until then, the Duo sits closer to Samsung's foldables. Their camera-based face unlock can't approve payments either. Google's Pixel foldables remain the exception, with face unlock that's trusted for payments and banking apps.

articles.title: Announcing AI data preparation capabilities in Amazon SageMaker: Build high-quality datasets for model development workflows | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Announcing AI data preparation capabilities in Amazon SageMaker: Build high-quality datasets for model development workflows
Teams that ship generative AI to production know that a model is only as good as its data. That is why preparing high-quality training and evaluation data comes first. Fine-tuning an open-weight model, running reinforcement learning, or building an evaluation suite all depend on data that is accurate, well-labeled, and representative of your task. For narrow, well-defined tasks, a smaller model customized on clean, task-specific data can often match or exceed the accuracy of a larger general-purpose model prompted into shape, at a lower cost per inference.
In practice, though, preparing that data is often the slowest part of the project. Labeled examples are scarce or expensive, and privacy rules limit what you can use. Quality problems such as duplicates, label noise, and answer leakage go unnoticed until a training run disappoints, and every training technique expects data in its own format. As a result, data scientists spend weeks wrangling data instead of building models.
Today, we’re expanding Amazon SageMaker AI with new AI data preparation capabilities for model development workflows. You can generate synthetic examples, assess and improve existing datasets, and bring expert feedback into the process through Python SDK APIs and the AWS AI-ML agent skill. You work in your notebook or IDE, with specifications and code that you can inspect and change.
Prepare data without hand-building pipelines
With AI Data Preparation capabilities, you don’t need to stitch together labeling tools, generation scripts, and validation jobs. Each capability is a standalone building block. You can use one of them on its own or chain them together according to the workflow you want.
- Auto-labeling: Label data at scale from an unlabeled dataset, a small labeled seed set, or no labels at all. Built-in task types include classification, named entity recognition, extractive question answering, ordinal rating, and summarization, and you can define custom tasks. You describe the task in a short labeling spec, which is validated against your own examples before the full dataset is labeled. For tasks with a fixed set of possible answers, such as classification, named entity recognition, and extractive question answering, a jury of several models labels each row, and their level of agreement becomes that row’s confidence score.
- Human review: Rows below your confidence threshold go to a review queue in Amazon SageMaker Studio, which uses the open-source Label Studio Community Edition. Outside subject matter experts can access the review app through the link in the partner app box in SageMaker Studio. Reviewer corrections feed back into auto-labeling, and you can generate consensus metrics and labeling reports.
- Synthetic data generation: Generate training, evaluation, and test data from a specification. You can ground the output in your own seed data and documents, and the service generates a code-based data generation pipeline that you can review, modify, reuse, and scale.
- Data quality evaluation: Check datasets against your own business rules, built-in metrics, and LLM-as-a-judge metrics. Find duplicates and near-duplicates, and surface issues you didn’t think to check for, such as label noise or answer leakage.
- Data transformation: Clean and reshape data for your target training technique. Describe the change in plain language and have the code generated for you, use built-in operations such as dedupe, merge, split, and filter, or run your own Python at scale.
You work wherever you already work. Use the SageMaker Python SDK directly or provide your coding agent the AI-ML skill in the agent toolkit and let your agent invoke the APIs according to established data science best practices. Describe what you need, and the agent selects and runs the right capability in SageMaker Studio JupyterLab, Kiro, or your local IDE with your coding assistant of choice.
For teams building specialized models, the hardest part is often finding enough task-specific data. Splunk, a Cisco company, faced exactly this when building evaluation models for its Agent Observability product.
        “For Splunk Agent Observability, our ability to train robust GenAI Eval models relies on access to high-quality, diverse datasets which are hard to curate for very specific tasks. Amazon SageMaker AI data preparation capabilities for synthetic data generation is meaningfully helping us scale these capabilities. We’ve been able to generate statistically representative synthetic datasets reliably and fast, while preserving the underlying patterns our models depend on. The seamless integration with the rest of our SageMaker workflow means our data scientists and customers spend less time wrangling data and more time building models that drive real enterprise value through Splunk.”
— Yash Sheth, Director of Engineering, Splunk Agent Observability
Chain capabilities from raw data to training
The value grows when you combine the capabilities. Some common patterns:
Build a golden evaluation dataset: Auto-label your raw data from a small seed set. High-confidence rows are accepted automatically, and low-confidence rows go to human reviewers. Their corrections improve the next labeling pass, resulting in a trusted, human-validated dataset to benchmark your models against.
Go from raw documents to a trained model in one workflow:
- Generate data: Synthetic data generation creates task-specific examples grounded in your documents and seed data.
- Transform it: Data transformation reshapes the data into the format your training technique expects, such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), or reinforcement learning (RL).
- Validate it: Data quality evaluation checks the dataset for duplicates, leakage, and rule violations before you spend compute on training.
- Train: Train with SageMaker AI model customization.
How it works
Consider a team preparing data to evaluate agentic customer support assistants. Its product guide says that a factory reset erases saved settings. The team wants to test whether the assistant preserves that warning when answering reset questions.
One pass through the preparation workflow looks like this:
- Define the requirements: Supply the product guide as context and describe the questions and reference answers you need. Include the requirement that answers about a factory reset preserve the warning about saved settings. Review the specification produced with your coding agent.
- Generate and inspect a sample: Generate a small batch and check the records against the guide. Review the generation and check the code. Confirm that the examples cover the intended questions and that the reference answers follow the source material.
- Assess and review: Run a data quality assessment and inspect the record-level findings. Ask a subject matter expert to review ambiguous answers or disputed assessments. Use the results and annotations to request improvement recommendations.
- Apply changes and repeat: Revise the specification if the requirements need clarification or transform the dataset to address issues such as duplicates. Generate additional examples where needed, then reassess the revised dataset before using it to evaluate the assistant.
This example workflow illustrates how the capabilities fit together.
Keep control of your preparation workflow and data
With the AI-ML skill, you describe the task in natural language while your coding agent helps build specifications, prepare code, and coordinate the data preparation steps. You can open those artifacts to see how the workflow is configured and make changes directly.
If you prefer to invoke the APIs yourself, use the Python SDK APIs to call individual capabilities from your own code. The SDK APIs take a specification as input, so we recommend creating it with the help of an agent. You can add quality assessment to an existing process, generate data for a new task, or combine several operations. You choose the preparation steps your project needs and how they fit into your model customization and evaluation processes.
AI Data Preparation runs with an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) execution role that you control. Your source data, generated datasets, and labels stay in your own Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) buckets, in the AWS Region you choose.
Get started today
The AI data preparation capabilities are generally available in the US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) Regions.
There are two ways to get started:
- With your coding agent – Set up the data preparation skills in your supported notebook or IDE. Describe one training or evaluation task and review the resulting specification before generating a sample.
- With Python – Use the SageMaker Python SDK directly to run individual data preparation capabilities from your own code. The SDK takes a specification as input, so we recommend creating your specifications with the AI-ML skill first, then using the SDK to run them in your workflow.
For more information, see the Amazon SageMaker AI documentation.

articles.title: Red Hat and Microsoft bring OpenShift virtual machines to Azure - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Red Hat and Microsoft bring OpenShift virtual machines to Azure
IBM Corp. subsidiary Red Hat and Microsoft Corp. are expanding their longtime engineering partnership to enable enterprises to run virtual machines on Microsoft Azure using Red Hat’s OpenShift Virtualization platform, providing an alternative to traditional hypervisors and what Red Hat called a path to modernizing legacy applications.
The collaboration, announced today, involves changes to Azure’s underlying computing architecture to connect it natively with Linux through Microsoft direct virtualization. That’s an Azure feature that gives performance-sensitive workloads near-bare-metal access to underlying hardware components.
Red Hat said this provides a direct pipeline between key hardware such as graphics processing units and isolated workloads. The companies are also working to give Linux-based workloads more direct access to Azure’s hardware resources, including graphics processing units.
Separately, Red Hat said it’s making its Lightwell Network vulnerability remediation service available through Microsoft’s Azure Marketplace.
The virtualization initiative addresses growing enterprise concerns about hypervisor licensing costs, hardware availability and the complexity of managing virtual machines alongside newer containerized applications. Red Hat said those pressures have intensified as organizations seek to accommodate AI workloads without abandoning existing applications.
Virtualization market leader Broadcom Inc. recently took aim at the same issue by open-sourcing its software for provisioning and managing virtual machines using the same protocols that the Kubernetes container orchestrator uses. At the center of the effort is Microsoft’s direct virtualization, which lets Linux-based and cloud-native platforms running on Azure virtual machines access the same virtualization and hardware capabilities available to Azure-native services.
Red Hat said it will be the first commercial Microsoft partner to support the technology through OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift, the jointly engineered and managed Kubernetes service offered by the two companies.
The agreement includes collaboration on several upstream open-source projects, including KubeVirt, LibVirt, QEMU and the Linux kernel. KubeVirt enables organizations to manage virtual machines and containers using Kubernetes tools.
Microsoft has extended KubeVirt beyond the Linux Kernel-based Virtual Machine hypervisor by adding support for its own hypervisor. That allows OpenShift Virtualization to run on Azure virtual machines using Microsoft’s direct virtualization technology.
Simpler migration
The approach is designed to let organizations consolidate traditional virtual machines, containerized applications and AI workloads on a common platform. Red Hat said its migration toolkit for virtualization will help customers move workloads from existing hypervisors.
The companies said the architecture will also improve resource utilization by supporting CPU and memory overcommitment, enabling more workloads to share available infrastructure. Kernel-level isolation is intended to protect sensitive workloads without compromising performance.
“Enterprises shouldn’t have to choose between managing rising hypervisor costs and accelerating their IT roadmaps,” Chris Wright, Red Hat’s chief technology officer, said in a statement. He said the collaboration would provide a common foundation for modernizing existing virtual machines and running AI workloads.
The companies did not announce a general availability date for the new virtualization capabilities.
Red Hat also said Lightwell Network is immediately available through private offers on Azure Marketplace, allowing customers to obtain remediated versions of vulnerable open-source software dependencies.
Lightwell addresses a persistent application security problem: correcting vulnerabilities in third-party software without forcing upgrades that could disrupt production applications.
The service provides version-specific fixes through secured repositories, accompanied by signed software artifacts and supporting provenance, software bills of materials and vulnerability information where applicable.
Customers can incorporate those fixes into existing development and deployment pipelines without replacing their vulnerability scanners, artifact repositories or build systems. Findings can surface in Microsoft Defender for Cloud, while Azure Policy provides governance controls.
Customers can purchase Lightwell subscriptions through Azure Marketplace and apply eligible spending toward their Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitments.

articles.title: Ticketmaster, NHL lobby Alberta over ticket reselling bill
articles.text:
The provincial government of Alberta is considering new measures to address high ticket resale prices, as new regulations are being debated in the provincial legislature. However, the National Hockey League (NHL) and its ticket partner, Ticketmaster, are lobbying officials to ensure the proposed consumer protection laws don’t conflict with business interests.
Dave Nally, the minister of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, introduced a new piece of legislation, Bill 34, on Oct. 28 that would require all ticket resellers to disclose all associated prices and fees.
This new bill doesn’t include a price cap on resale tickets, but one could come into effect later. The government added that the legislation opens the door to additional protections, which will be determined through future consultations. Alongside this, members of the official opposition criticized the legislation’s lack of concrete price caps during a Nov. 3 debate in the legislature.
According to Alberta’s lobbyist registry, the NHL registered to lobby the provincial government on Nov. 2. on consumer protection and resale tickets to “ensure the interests of the NHL (e.g., World Cup of Hockey 2028, Calgary Flames, Edmonton Oilers) are not negatively impacted.”
Ticketmaster, unsurprisingly, registered to lobby the Alberta government back in August and sought to meet with officials to “discuss the government’s ongoing consideration of measures to protect consumers in live event ticketing.”
The NHL and Ticketmaster work together to manage an official ticket resale platform, the NHL Ticket Exchange. However, the exchange has no cap on ticket resale, and both organizations profit off resale according to the Investigative Journalism Foundation (IJF).
Interestingly, the IJF also noted that a private members’ bill voted down by the UCP caucus would’ve banned secondary ticket platforms from charging a fee to transfer a ticket.
Now, as pointed out by the IJF, ice-level tickets for the Calgary Flames’ final home game of the season, and the last game at the Scotiabank Saddledome, are anywhere between $1,200 and $11,800 for verified resale. Alongside this, there is a pair of tickets in section 119 priced at a whopping $23,600, with $20,000 as the face value and $3,600 as the service fee. For comparison, this used 2020 Toyota Corolla on Clutch is going for $390 more than these tickets.
However, this is a special-occasion game, as it is the last game at the iconic stadium, originally built for the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics. In other words, it’s not entirely reflective of a typical ticket resale.
Looking at other regular-season games, like this Thursday’s home match against the Minnesota Wild, shows that verified resale tickets like Section 119, Row 5, Seats 9-10 are going for $290 apiece.
For context, Ontario already capped the price of resale tickets in April, when Bill 97 was enacted.
Source: Investigative Journalism Foundation
Image Credit: Ticketmaster

articles.title: Alfonso, funcionario de la Seguridad Social: “Quien retrase un año su jubilación podrá recibir un pago de 8.500 euros”
articles.text:
Explica Alfonso Muñoz Cuenca que uno de los incentivos que tienen los trabajadores que deciden continuar trabajando tras alcanzar su edad ordinaria de retiro es el de poder acceder a un pago único de 8.000 o 8.500 euros. Es decir, se trata de un incentivo que puede pagarse si se retrasa un año la jubilación. Depende de la situación de cada trabajador.
Con la jubilación demorada, el trabajador puede optar por retrasar de manera voluntaria su acceso a la pensión a cambio de un complemento económico. Este complemento puede ser en forma de incremento de la pensión mensual o bien a tanto alzado. También puede haber una mezcla de ambos. En este caso sí que hace falta que se haya retrasado un mínimo de dos años completos. Es decir, que si solo se retrasa un año, no se puede pedir la opción de pago mixto.
Este pago se calcula de manera individual. Depende de la cantidad de la pensión y de los años cotizados que tenga el trabajador en el momento de alcanzar la edad ordinaria de jubilación. Por ello, en algunos casos, los 8.500 euros de los que habla Muñoz pueden ser superiores. De hecho, en algunos casos pueden llegar a ser superiores a los 10.000 euros por año de demora. En los ejemplos que pone el organismo ya se contempla esta posibilidad. Es el caso de las personas que tienen una carrera de cotización más larga y una pensión más alta.
Qué hay que decidir al solicitar la pensión
Esta elección solo hay que hacerla una vez. Es decir, en el momento de solicitar la pensión (cuando se adquiere el derecho al complemento). Una vez elegida la opción, no se puede cambiar (artículo 210.2 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social). Como insiste Muñoz, el trabajador tiene estas opciones:
Es importante pensar si queremos recibir el dinero en un solo pago (al jubilarnos) o si preferimos que nos aumenten nuestra pensión mensual. Hay que saber que podemos trabajar y cobrar pensión si cumplimos los requisitos de compatibilidad y que tenemos estos incentivos por retrasar nuestro retiro.
También es relevante pensar en cómo afectará a nuestros impuestos. Este pago único se considera rendimiento del trabajo (por ello tributa en el impuesto sobre la renta de las personas físicas (IRPF)). La Agencia Tributaria contempla una reducción del 30 % en el caso de que se cumplan los requisitos. Hay que saber que el importe bruto del complemento no es necesariamente equivalente al importe neto.
Muñoz también apunta a que hay que pensar en otros aspectos. Por ejemplo, en nuestra salud. O en las características de nuestro puesto de trabajo. También es importante pensar en la calidad de vida.
Además, debemos tener en cuenta nuestros proyectos personales. Saber que existe este incentivo económico nos va a permitir tenerlo en cuenta en nuestra planificación de la jubilación. También hay que tener en cuenta aquellas circunstancias que hacen más o menos viable continuar trabajando.

articles.title: India has 300,000 startups; farmers open to using technologies, says Union minister Jayant Chaudhary
articles.text:
India has 300,000 startups; farmers open to using technologies, says Union minister Jayant Chaudhary
The conference was held alongside the Singapore-India Hackathon at the Singapore Management University (SMU) here.
India has around 300,000 registered startups, many of which are led by women, Union minister Jayant Chaudhary told global tech leaders on Tuesday, and underlined that farmers across the country are also enthusiastic about using technology.
"Farmers are not going to be developers of any tech solutions for the future, but they are users (and) they are very open to using technologies," he told over 300 delegates at the TIECON 2026 conference organised by The Indus Entrepreneurs (TiEcon) in Singapore.
"With the farmers, there is great enthusiasm," the minister of state for skill development and entrepreneurship said.
The conference was held alongside the Singapore-India Hackathon at the Singapore Management University (SMU) here.
Highlighting the success of startups in India, the minister said that the country has nearly 300,000 registered startups today, which are from Tier-II and Tier-III cities. A lot of these startups are led by women.
"Our seeds are sown throughout the country," he said, adding that it is not just Bengaluru, Mumbai or Hyderabad -- the traditional power centres where the startups have grown and established a global footprint.
"So, that is the great potential," Chaudhury said as he described the Indian startup ecosystem. "India's startup story today is very, very robust."
"A great depth is in the fact that our academia is also contributing today to the research. Our universities are no longer closed. They are contributing to research innovation. Our professors are part of some of these boards (of the startups)," said the minister.
He further shared that the Indian Institutes of Technologies are now launching deep tech funds. "They (the IITs) are working with some of the fund management companies, and trying to get even small ticket investors to come (to India) and work for the future."
"So, that gives me great confidence that the Indian story is (scaling) with such a young population," he underlined.
TiE Singapore President Prantik Mazumdar welcomed Minister Chaudhary's update on the startup ecosystem in India.
"We are grateful to Shri Jayant Chaudhary for his presence and support of our ambitions, and share his belief in the importance of investing in human capital.
"With TiEcon SG 2026, we want to explore how we can harness the complementary strengths of Singapore and India to build the next generation of global technology giants from Asia. By deepening our collaboration with institutions such as Singapore Management University, we hope to nurture entrepreneurial talent and facilitate greater talent mobility between the two countries," said Mazumdar.
Themed 'Frontier Tech Reshaping The Coming Decade', the one-day conference brought together a distinguished community of founders, investors, policymakers, business leaders, and technology and innovation leaders to explore trends, technologies, and opportunities shaping the next decade of venture building.
The TIECON SG 2026 conference celebrated 25 years of TiE in Singapore.

articles.title: Mercedes-Benz lanzará en 2027 un asistente de conducción aprobado por las Naciones Unidas: exige usar las manos
articles.text:
Mercedes-Benz anunció que ofrecerá en Alemania y Estados Unidos un asistente de conducción que guía el auto desde el punto de partida hasta el destino, incluso en el tránsito denso de la ciudad. El sistema, llamado MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO, llegará en 2027 y exige que el conductor mantenga la atención y las manos en el volante.
La empresa lo presentó el 16 de noviembre junto con otra función: el asistente de autopista que permite soltar el volante. Ambos son sistemas de nivel 2, según la escala de la industria. Eso significa que el conductor sigue siendo el responsable de la conducción y debe estar listo para tomar el control en cualquier momento.
Una vez que se carga un destino en el navegador, el sistema se activa con un botón del volante. Según la compañía, puede salir de la autopista, cambiar de carril, incorporarse al carril correcto, doblar en las intersecciones y frenar o arrancar en los semáforos.
Para eso usa 27 componentes de detección: 10 cámaras, cinco radares y 12 sensores de ultrasonido. Una computadora procesa los datos con una capacidad de hasta 254 TOPS, una medida de operaciones por segundo. El sistema combina el software de la marca con tecnología de Nvidia, según informó la empresa en octubre.
Fechas: diciembre para pocos, 2027 para el resto
El acceso anticipado empezará en diciembre. En Estados Unidos, algunos clientes elegidos de California podrán probar ambas funciones. En Alemania, el programa llegará a Stuttgart y Múnich, y allí incluirá el asistente de punto a punto.
La venta general será después. El asistente urbano estará disponible en Alemania y Estados Unidos en el primer semestre de 2027, para todo tipo de motorización. En Estados Unidos, la conducción sin manos en autopistas se sumará en la primavera de 2027, y en Alemania ya a fines de 2026.
La empresa dijo que será el primer fabricante en ofrecer un sistema así en Estados Unidos, Alemania y China. En China, según la empresa, está disponible desde la introducción del nuevo CLA.
En Estados Unidos, el hardware necesario ya viene instalado en algunos modelos 2027, entre ellos el CLA eléctrico, el GLE, el GLS y el Clase S. Desde el año modelo 2028, más autos de la marca estarán equipados. Los dueños de autos compatibles podrán sumar las funciones con una actualización remota.
Manos en el volante, a diferencia de Tesla
The Verge comparó el sistema con el Full Self-Driving de Tesla y destacó una diferencia: el de Mercedes-Benz exige las manos en el volante mientras recorre la ciudad. El conductor puede corregir la dirección en cualquier momento. En autopista, en cambio, el asistente de Mercedes permite soltar el volante.
En esas vías, el sistema funciona sin manos hasta 130 kilómetros por hora en Alemania. En Estados Unidos, el límite es de 85 millas por hora (unos 137 kilómetros por hora), solo en autopistas de acceso controlado y bajo ciertas condiciones. También puede iniciar los cambios de carril sin que el conductor los confirme.
El precio no está definido. La compañía informó que anunciará los detalles de modelos y precios antes del lanzamiento en cada mercado, y que habrá un mes de prueba gratuito para quienes tengan el equipamiento necesario. The Verge informó que las funciones se desbloquearán con suscripciones de un mes, un año o tres años.
El sistema se desarrolló bajo la normativa de las Naciones Unidas para asistentes de conducción, según el comunicado de octubre. La empresa señaló que esa base regulatoria permitiría llevarlo a otros mercados, sin precisar cuáles.
El primer hito está fijado para diciembre de 2026, cuando empiecen las pruebas con clientes seleccionados en California, Stuttgart y Múnich.

articles.title: U.S. Cracks Down on China Renting AI GPUs Through Overseas Data Centers
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 17th 2026
U.S. Cracks Down on China Renting AI GPUs Through Overseas Data Centers
Yesterday, the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released an interim final rule to address remote access to advanced AI chips and servers. This rule significantly addresses a long-standing gap in U.S. export controls, where Chinese companies that are barred from accessing NVIDIA's latest GPUs have been renting overseas computing power instead of purchasing the chips outright. Notably, BIS states that the rule was written by and at the direction of the Department of the Treasury and the National Security Council.
Under the new rule, a license is required to ship any advanced accelerators to any data center worldwide that provides more than 12 million "aggregate TPP" of computing power to companies headquartered in Macau or Country Group D:5, which includes China. TPP, or Total Processing Performance, is BIS's metric for chip computing power, calculated as a chip's peak dense throughput multiplied by the bit length of the operation. For example, an H100 rates about 15,800 TPP. "Aggregate TPP" sums up every accelerator in the facility, so the cap equates to roughly 750 H100s or around 330 B200s. The limit also applies to "linked data centers" and indirect access, such as a cloud reseller training models for a Chinese firm. Data centers already serving such customers have 90 days to obtain a license. Only "commercial recommender systems" are exempt, and anything that generates text, images, video, or code does not qualify.The rule also requires a license for advanced AI chips shipped to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, which the Commerce Department says carry a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. Shipments to U.S.-headquartered companies are exempt if they meet new reporting requirements. Foundries and packaging houses also lose some of the methods to clear advanced-node chips for designers in restricted countries. Finally, the rule formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule, eliminating its country tiers, the Data Center VEU program, and model-weight controls. Reflecting the current trends and the times under the U.S. administration led by Donald Trump, the document uses "Super Intelligence" instead of "AI," citing Executive Order 14434.
Source:

articles.title: The data is very preliminary, but Vulcan failure may not be due to BE-4 engines
articles.text:
United Launch Alliance (ULA) confirmed Tuesday morning that its return-to-flight launch of the Vulcan rocket began failing during the initial stages of the mission.
“While we appear to have lost telemetry and the mission at approximately 10 minutes into flight, early indications are that just after liftoff, the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance, resulting in stage separation occurring when the vehicle was low in altitude and below minimal velocity to reach orbit,” the company said.
The launch company also confirmed reporting by Ars that the Centaur V upper stage and the solid rocket boosters performed nominally during the flight.
Critically, ULA did not provide any specific information about the “low booster performance.” This matters greatly because the core stage of the Vulcan rocket is powered by two BE-4 engines, which are provided by Blue Origin. That company’s own New Glenn rocket uses a similar but slightly more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. And New Glenn experienced its own catastrophic failure in May during a ground test, a failure that later was attributed to a main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines.
Preliminary data review
Information about the Vulcan failure is being closely held by ULA and Blue Origin, who have only acknowledged that they’re working together to investigate the cause. According to two sources, the investigation is “incredibly complicated” and remains in the early stages.
However, according to preliminary data, two independent sources indicated to Ars that the problem is currently believed to have originated on the launch vehicle side rather than in the engines themselves. The issue may be related to systems that feed methane and liquid oxygen propellant to the engines.
ULA engineers are looking at the possibility that one of the two BE-4 engines started producing lower thrust shortly after liftoff and never ramped back up to full throttle for the remainder of the burn. Video observations from high-zoom tracking cameras appeared to show one engine slightly dimmer than the other after Vulcan jettisoned its solid rocket boosters nearly two minutes into flight. An asymmetric shutdown of the BE-4 engines could also have contributed to the sudden attitude motion indicated by ULA’s telemetry-driven real-time animation near stage separation.

articles.title: La pantalla del Galaxy S27 podría cambiar para siempre el diseño de los Galaxy
articles.text:
Samsung no ha cambiado mucho el diseño de los Galaxy en los últimos tres años. Fuera de algunos ajustes en el módulo de la cámara y esquinas más redondeadas, la serie Galaxy S mantiene el mismo lenguaje visual desde 2023. Esto podría acabar con el Galaxy S27, ya que Samsung prepara uno de los cambios estéticos más ambiciosos al desarrollar un móvil con pantalla sin bordes.
De acuerdo con SamMobile, Samsung desarrolla una nueva tecnología de pantalla capaz de reducir al mínimo los marcos del dispositivo. Una filtración en Naver Blog afirma que la división móvil de la compañía explora posibles diseños para un Galaxy sin bordes. Aunque todavía no hay detalles sobre la tecnología, Samsung podría volver a un concepto similar al que vimos hace una década con el Galaxy Edge.
Si hacemos memoria, el Galaxy S6 Edge debutó en 2015 con una pantalla curva en ambos lados. Aunque el diseño era interesante, este formato tomó más fuerza un año más tarde con el Galaxy S7 Edge, que se convirtió en uno de los móviles más exitosos de la época. Su pantalla se extendía hacia los laterales, eliminando los marcos y aprovechando todo el espacio.
Es probable que Samsung explore nuevamente este concepto, aunque ahora con una pantalla curvada en los cuatro lados. La compañía quiere ser la primera en estrenar esta innovación, por lo que ha posado el acelerador para lanzarla antes que el iPhone. Según la fuente, Apple también está pensando en aplicar una dirección similar para sus próximos móviles, aunque Samsung tendría ventaja en este terreno gracias a su posición como uno de los mayores fabricantes de pantallas del mundo.
Samsung podría volver a las pantallas sin bordes con el Galaxy S27
Un detalle que no se menciona es que el diseño de las pantallas curvas que se popularizó con el Galaxy S7 Edge también acarreaba algunos problemas. Eliminar los marcos laterales implicaba que el usuario tocaría siempre alguna parte de la pantalla para sujetar el móvil. Las críticas por los toques accidentales con la palma de la mano no se hicieron esperar y Samsung se vio obligada a mejorar su algoritmo para resolverlo.
Otro problema de estos bordes curvos es que los usuarios no podían sujetar el terminal con seguridad, sobre todo en los modelos con pantalla más grande. A esto se suman detalles como que los elementos cercanos a los bordes se deformaban por la curvatura o que los reflejos eran más notorios al ver fotos o vídeos bajo la luz intensa.
Además de Samsung, otras compañías probaron conceptos similares para eliminar los bordes. El Huawei Mate 20 Pro se copió la pantalla OLED curvada de Samsung, mientras que el Vivo NEX 3 llevó la idea más lejos con una pantalla tipo cascada que se extendía sobre los laterales. Motorola y OnePlus también exploraron alternativas, pero todo se acabó cuando Samsung decidió abandonar este tipo de pantalla con el Galaxy S20.
Por el momento no existe más información sobre la nueva pantalla sin marcos o cuándo podríamos verla implementada en los Galaxy S. Lo único que menciona es que la tecnología se aplicará a los móviles que no forman parte de la categoría de plegables.

articles.title: Manitoba pledges to ban AI images in real estate | BetaKit
articles.text:
Manitoba says it is planning to ban the use of AI images in real estate within the province.
The news: The province’s Lieutenant Governor, Anita Neville, laid out the plan on behalf of the government on Tuesday during the provincial throne speech. Limited to a single line pledging to “put a stop” to the use of AI images in real estate, the idea was delivered during a portion of the throne speech dealing with consumer protections and cost-of-living policy.
From the source: “We are leading the way in Canada when it comes to growing the economy in the right way while protecting our environment and our way of life,” a portion of the throne speech reads. “We listened to the community and stopped an AI data centre from being built in Île-des-Chênes.”
The context: The provincial government’s outline of any potential ban was sparse, with no detail given as to how or when such a prohibition might come into effect, what it might look like, and how it could be enforced. BetaKit reached out to the Manitoba government to ask those questions but has not yet received a response.
Manitoba has taken a decidedly cautious approach to AI regulation. In addition to proposing a ban on real estate imagery, the Province was also the first Canadian jurisdiction to propose a ban on AI chatbot use for youth younger than 16. It also enacted some of the most restrictive regulations around AI data centre development in the country.
Final thought: AI is increasingly being used to virtually stage homes in online real estate listings. Some argue that such staging is misleading to buyers, while others argue it allows buyers to visualize what a space might look like. Manitoba currently governs marketing in real estate through the Real Estate Services Act (RESA), which includes provisions around false or deceptive information and furnishings. It does not specifically mention virtual staging or include rules around AI use.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.
