articles.title: Un ferretero, sobre el frío en casa: "Recomiendo abrir el cajón de la persiana y pegar una tira de aislamiento térmico"
articles.text:
No importa si tienes buenas ventanas en casa si el frío hace de las suyas, y lo curioso es que el problema no está en los cristales. Aunque no lo sepas, el cajón donde se enrolla la persiana es un espacio que puede dejar pasar aire del exterior si no está bien aislado, así que Toño Escrig (ferretero y divulgador de consejos de bricolaje) ha explicado cómo solucionar este problema sin necesidad de cambiar las ventanas ni meterse en reformas.
Como recoge El Español en su información sobre este truco para aislar las persianas, Escrig señala que no importa lo buena que sea tu ventana, ya que el fresco seguirá entrando por el cajón de la persiana. Así, recomienda abrir el compartimento y colocar una lámina de aislamiento término en su interior, algo que puedes hacer en pocos con unas tijeras y ningún conocimiento técnico.
Cómo colocar el aislamiento térmico en el cajón de la persiana
El primer paso consiste en quitar la tapa que protege el mecanismo, aunque la forma de hacerlo depende del modelo que tengas en casa. “La mía es con clecs, se quita haciendo presión, hay otras que van con tornillos”, explica el ferretero. Una vez abierto el cajón, recomienda limpiar bien la superficie antes de pegar el aislante, ya que el polvo acumulado puede impedir que el adhesivo se fije correctamente.
A partir de ahí, el procedimiento es sencillo: hay que medir el espacio disponible, cortar el material aislante a medida y retirar la protección del adhesivo para colocarlo dentro del cajón. Se trata de láminas flexibles, elaboradas con materiales como el polietileno o las espumas técnicas, que ayudan a reducir las pérdidas de calor. Eso sí, antes de terminar hay que comprobar que la persiana puede subir y bajar sin problemas (el aislamiento no debe interferir con el mecanismo).
Por último, solo queda volver a colocar la tapa. Con esta pequeña intervención se puede mejorar el aislamiento de una zona que muchas veces pasa desapercibida cuando intentamos mantener la casa caliente. De hecho, el Instituto para la Diversificación y Ahorro de la Energía (IDAE) también recomienda que los cajones de las persianas estén bien aislados y no tengan rendijas, ya que pueden convertirse en un punto de entrada de aire exterior.

Le voilà donc dans notre labo, ce Narwal Flow sorti il y a quelques mois et qu'on trouve aujourd'hui pour 899 €. Armé d'une puissance d'aspiration de 22 000 Pa, ce robot nettoyeur de sol compte aussi sur sa serpillière atypique pour effacer les traces les plus retorses.

articles.title: Fausses pubs sur Facebook et Instagram : la Française des jeux attaque Meta en justice
articles.text:
Face à la multiplication des publicités frauduleuses sur les réseaux sociaux, le groupe FDJ United a porté plainte contre Meta. Au cœur de cette bataille judiciaire, on retrouve la diffusion sur Facebook et Instagram de campagnes publicitaires trompeuses qui vantent des offres illégales tout en s’appropriant l’image de l’entreprise. Ce n’est pas la première fois que Meta est accusée de la sorte.
Une usurpation à grande échelle sur Facebook et Instagram
La FDJ indique avoir recensé « 226 nouveaux contenus illicites » en seulement quatre jours, du 18 au 21 mai dernier. Pour l’entreprise, c’est l’occasion de mettre en lumière un procédé particulièrement bien ficelé que vous avez peut-être déjà croisé sur les réseaux : des contenus sponsorisés conçus pour « reprendre à l’identique » une marque ou un média bien connu, ici la FDJ, qui renvoient vers un faux site interne pour mieux vous soutirer de l’argent ou voler vos données personnelles.
Selon FDJ United, ces publicités trompeuses assurent la promotion de jeux d’argent totalement illégaux, comme le casino en ligne par exemple. En créant une confusion délibérée avec les activités régulées de l’entreprise, ces campagnes publicitaires exposent directement les utilisateurs de Facebook et d’Instagram à d’importants risques d’escroquerie en ligne et de vol de données personnelles.
Meta va devoir serrer la vis autour de la validation de ses pubs
En engageant cette action en justice, FDJ United pointe du doigt la responsabilité de Meta dans la modération de ses espaces publicitaires. L’entreprise conteste le fait que de telles publicités trompeuses puissent circuler librement sur ces plateformes. Pour l’opérateur, il devient urgent d’obliger les géants de la Tech à contrôler de manière plus rigoureuse les annonces qui exploitent illégalement des marques déposées.
FDJ United espère ainsi pousser les réseaux sociaux à renforcer leurs mécanismes de filtrage automatique et de vérification des annonceurs. Ces arnaques sponsorisées sont malheureusement monnaie courante et l’IA offre malheureusement aux arnaqueurs professionnels une force de frappe inédite. Si vous avez déjà été victime d’une arnaque en cliquant sur une publicité Facebook ou Instagram, n’hésitez pas à partager votre expérience dans les commentaires.

articles.title: Jensen Huang rompe su silencio tras dejar NVIDIA: "Sería un honor regresar como CEO"
articles.text:
Cada día que pasa se escribe un nuevo capítulo del culebrón por la salida de Jensen Huang como presidente y CEO de NVIDIA. El ejecutivo aprovechó hoy su perfil en X (Twitter) para pronunciarse en público por primera vez desde su renuncia a la conducción de la empresa. En su comunicado no solo reconoció sus errores, sino que también mostró su interés por volver a liderar la compañía que cofundó en 1993.
El mensaje de Jensen Huang marca todos los casilleros de lo que se podría esperar de un discurso de arrepentimiento. El exCEO de NVIDIA agradeció las muestras de cariño de quienes se comunicaron con él en los últimos días, como también de quienes pidieron por su regreso al gigante verde. Asimismo, celebró su historia como inmigrante y las posibilidades que le abrió Estados Unidos desde su llegada, hizo un mea culpa de su comportamiento, se comprometió a colaborar con la investigación sobre su accionar, le pidió disculpas a su familia y sentó las bases para un potencial vuelta al rol principal de la empresa.
Las repercusiones del primer mensaje público de Jensen Huang tras renunciar a NVIDIA no se hicieron esperar. Al momento de redacción de este artículo, el posteo acumula más de 39.000 republicaciones y 238.000 likes. No quedan dudas de que sus palabras eran las más codiciadas, especialmente tras un anuncio de salida de la compañía que no incluyó ningún comentario de su parte.
A continuación, el mensaje completo que publicó Jensen Huang en X (Twitter), traducido al español:
Durante la última semana, me he sentido profundamente conmovido por el cariño y el apoyo de amigos, colegas del sector y personas a las que ni siquiera conozco. Gracias a todos los que han mostrado tanta amabilidad hacia mí y mi familia. Significa muchísimo para mí.
Llegué a Estados Unidos hace 53 años, y convertirme en ciudadano estadounidense fue uno de los mayores regalos y uno de los momentos de mayor orgullo de mi vida. NVIDIA fue el proyecto de mi vida. Haber contribuido, junto a mis colegas, a convertirla en la empresa que es hoy ha sido un privilegio y un honor. Solo en Estados Unidos podría haber surgido una compañía como NVIDIA. Amo a nuestro país y amo a NVIDIA.
No estuve a la altura de los estándares que se esperan de todos en NVIDIA, y he cometido errores graves en mi vida personal. He causado problemas a la Junta Directiva, algo de lo que me arrepiento profundamente. Asumo la total responsabilidad por mis errores y me comprometo a colaborar con la investigación independiente que está llevando a cabo la Junta.
Desde mi salida, he recibido numerosas peticiones por parte de empleados, inversores, socios comerciales y clientes de NVIDIA para que regrese como CEO. Muchos siguen contactándome directamente mientras la empresa navega por complejas dinámicas tecnológicas, de mercado, competitivas y geopolíticas. NVIDIA es una empresa excepcional, de esas que solo aparecen una vez por generación. Si la Junta Directiva considera que mi regreso favorece los intereses de nuestros accionistas, empleados, la propia compañía y Estados Unidos, sería un honor atender estas peticiones y volver a ocupar el cargo de CEO.
Gracias, de nuevo, a todos los que me han hecho llegar sus buenos deseos. Me siento profundamente conmovido por su apoyo. A mi familia: los amo, y dedicaré el resto de mi vida a ser digno de su cariño.
Jensen
Jensen Huang, en X (Twitter).
Jensen Huang está dispuesto a regresar a NVIDIA, pero es más difícil de lo que parece
Queda claro que Jensen Huang no ha tirado la toalla de forma definitiva con NVIDIA. Tras el escándalo por sus aventuras con la supuesta espía china Alice Huang y con la ejecutiva Kimberly Powell, la renuncia del empresario parecía ser el abrupto final de una historia hasta aquí plagada de éxitos. Pero unos pocos días le han bastado para tratar de recuperar el trono perdido.
Un reciente reporte de Financial Times indicaba que Huang supuestamente había manifestado su deseo de regresar a NVIDIA a personas de confianza. La compañía ya ha puesta en marcha la búsqueda de un sucesor y todo apunta a que el Consejo de Administración prefiere dar vuelta la página antes que darle una segunda oportunidad al exCEO.
Con el mensaje de hoy, Jensen Huang pone su destino en manos de la Junta Directiva. Y si bien a primera vista puede parecer un gesto de nobleza y colaboración, también impone una gran presión sobre los integrantes de la mesa. Después de todo, si eligen a otro CEO y no se logran los resultados esperados, la culpa será de ellos.
El timing del mensaje de Jensen Huang tampoco es casual. La publicación se da justo el mismo día en que NVIDIA presentará los resultados financieros del último trimestre. Wall Street proyecta cifras de ventas que dupliquen las del trimestre previo, aunque la verdadera atención estará en lo que responda Colette Kress, la CEO interina, a las consultas de los inversores y accionistas. Con el comunicado de Huang en boca de todos, es lógico pensar en un bombardeo de preguntas sobre si la empresa analiza o no traerlo de regreso. Pase lo que pase, se esperan reacciones drásticas (para bien o para mal) en el valor de la acción del gigante verde.

articles.title: Kurz vor Anthropic-IPO: OpenAI bringt GPT-6.2 Astra und Sol
articles.text:
Kurz vor Anthropic-IPO: OpenAI bringt GPT-6.2 Astra und Sol
Nur zwei Tage vor dem geplanten Börsengang des Rivalen Anthropic hat OpenAI mit GPT-6.2 Astra und Sol zwei neue KI-Modelle an den Start gebracht. Nach der Ankündigung des aktuellen Top-Modells Anfang September 2026 hatte ein wahrer Run auf Astra eingesetzt und dafür gesorgt, dass OpenAI den Zugang zu seinen Pro-Tarifen einschränken musste.
Neue OpenAI-KI: Mehr Leistung, weniger Kosten
Eine ähnlich hohe Nachfrage ist für die beiden Update-Modelle zwar nicht zu erwarten. OpenAI hat aber trotz Fortschritten bei der Leistung die Kosten noch einmal deutlich gesenkt. So sollen die Preise für Input- und Output-Token von GPT-6.2 Astra im Vergleich zu GPT-6 Astra um 20 Prozent geschrumpft sein. GPT-6.2 Sol bleibt auf dem Preisniveau des Vorgängers GPT-6.1, wie OpenAI mitteilt.
Das neue GPT-6.2 Astra soll sich vor allem für die Erledigung von komplexen beruflichen Aufgaben eignen. Bei der Erstellung von Präsentationen, Tabellen und Dokumenten hält sich die KI laut OpenAI strenger an die Vorlagen und branchenspezifische Standards. Die Ergebnisse sollen zudem weniger nach KI aussehen.
Außerdem soll GPT-6.2 Astra saubereren Code schreiben und optisch ansprechendere Frontends erstellen, die besser funktionieren sollen. Das gilt OpenAI zufolge vor allem in den Bereichen Webentwicklung, Gaming und 3D-Design.
GPT-6.2 Astra punktet bei komplexen Aufgaben
Im Test „Agent‘s Last Exam“, bei dem mehrstufige berufliche Aufgaben abgeprüft werden, soll GPT-6.2 Astra einen neuen Bestwert erreicht haben. So soll das neue Modell hier 5,2 Punkte mehr als GPT-6 Astra erreicht haben – und das zu weniger als einem Drittel der Kosten. Im Vergleich zur kürzlich veröffentlichten Anthropic-KI Claude Fable 5.2 gibt OpenAI hier eine Verbesserung um 5,5 Punkte an. Die Kosten sollen aber nur fünf Prozent derer des Konkurrenzmodells betragen.
Ähnliches soll für die Tests „Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1“ und „Vals Science Index“ gelten. OpenAI sieht GPT-6.2 Astra daher als „bestes KI-Modell“ für Forscher:innen an. Beim sogenannten „Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index“ bleibt GPT-6.2 Astra mit 62,1 Punkten zwar knapp hinter Claude Fable 5.2 zurück (64,6 Punkte), arbeitet aber zu einem Bruchteil der Kosten.
GPT‑6.2 Sol ist im Vergleich zu OpenAIs Frontier-Modell als günstigere Alltagsvariante positioniert. OpenAI zufolge soll die KI smarter und effizienter sein als der direkte Vorgänger GPT‑6.1 Sol. Mit dem neuen Modell sollen sich mehrstufige, agentenbasierte Arbeitsabläufe bewältigen lassen. OpenAI setzt GPT‑6.2 Sol eigenen Angaben zufolge intern als Standardmodell sowohl für technische als auch nicht-technische Aufgaben ein.

articles.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
articles.text:
It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design. The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app.
The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road.
As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You’ll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It’s under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity.
Importantly, this only applies to future interactions with Gemini. If you have previously fed any data into Google’s AI, that’s already part of the training data. That can include your inputs, Gemini’s responses, uploaded files, tool calls, your location, and data from connected apps. Google says it may retain this data for up to three years to improve its models. The company has previously noted it attempts to filter personal information out of the Gemini activity history, but that isn’t a guarantee.

articles.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it's not having one | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages? The company took to X on Tuesday to announce that its Gmail service is actually running just fine. In a post, the company said it was not currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded users they could always check Gmail’s real-time status on its online dashboard.
As it turns out, the company was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own. While some posts on the social network suggested Gmail was experiencing a disruption, others said they were not having any problems.
The concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where users can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems. Downdetector is not an official source for verifying or understanding the true scope of internet outages, and as people become more concerned about possible cyberattacks, the site’s data may become less valuable over time if every minor glitch and hiccup is reported as an “outage” by non-technical users.
The fact that Google had to announce it was not having an outage speaks to the growing anxiety around the reliability of major tech services. Over the past week, Apple and Microsoft experienced outages, an FAA network failure led to a nationwide ground stop, and some banks and airlines also reported disruptions.
However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Fox Business Network’s “The Claman Countdown” on Tuesday that the U.S. is not currently facing coordinated cyberattacks. He told the outlet, “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here.”
Instead, Clayton attributed the rise in issues to businesses patching their systems. The patching may be a downstream effect of AI, as newer models have become increasingly adept at uncovering previously unknown vulnerabilities. “They’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place,” he said, adding that this is happening at “a much larger scale” than before.
As a result, some of the systems are “not coming back as expected in all cases,” he added.

articles.title: Accessibility isn’t “a niche problem,” says organizer of inaugural assistive tech conference | BetaKit
articles.text:
Toronto-based disability-focused accelerator Access to Success wants to raise the profile of assistive technology with the first-ever Canadian Disability Tech Summit in Toronto on Wednesday.
The event will gather hundreds of founders, investors, healthcare leaders, researchers, corporations, policymakers, and other members of the disabled community in the Automotive Building at Exhibition Place for a full day of mainstage programming and an exhibit floor featuring more than 50 innovations.
“Disability is not a monolith … so getting the word out across that entire diversity of this population … was one of the bigger challenges.”
The summit will facilitate discussions on the “entire spectrum of disability” and the pipeline of innovation, Access to Success executive director Varun Chandak told BetaKit in an interview. That’s unique in Canada, Chandak explained, because usually events are disability-specific, with respective events for vision loss or autism, but no opportunities for the disabled community to get together in one place.
“There’s no reason why somebody working in pediatric brain health is going to talk to somebody working in mobility devices,” Chandak said. “Disability is not a monolith … so getting the word out across that entire diversity of this population, around this community, [about] all of the work that’s happening was one of the bigger challenges.”
The summit has already met the challenge, with more than 800 people registered to attend in-person and online, double what the organizers expected, Chandak said. Attendees will take part in conversations about disability and tech, commercializing disability innovations, and see startup pitches. While most pitch competitions are typically in front of investors, these startups will instead pitch potential industry partners who may be interested in buying their products.
”Everyone needs more money, but what [these assistive technology startups] tell us they need, based on the forms that they fill out with us, is that they need partners and they need procurement,” Chandak said.
RELATED: Enabled Talent’s new program aims to help disabled Canadians become entrepreneurs
The summit will also feature sessions on disability tech at scale, an investor panel, and a conversation on co-designing innovations with input from people living with disabilities. Speakers slated to appear include Maverix Private Equity founder John Ruffolo and Enable Ventures founder Gina Kline.
Chandak said everyone in the assistive tech industry has the same experience of travelling to attend trade shows and conferences outside of Canada, and that he’s excited to bring a Canadian option to the table himself.
“When they hear that something like this is happening in Canada, the response was pretty much universally along the lines of, and I’m paraphrasing here, … ‘hell yeah,’” Chandak said.
The plan is to turn the Canadian Disability Tech Summit into an annual affair, and given it sold out in its inaugural year, Chandak thinks the demand is there. He hopes attendees leave Wednesday’s event realizing how more accessible design choices just result in better design, period.
“I need the tech sector to start realizing that [accessibility] is not a niche problem anymore,” Chandak said. “The things that we are working on [have] already gone on to change millions and millions and millions of lives, if not billions. It’s an untapped opportunity waiting to be invested in.”
UPDATE (11/17/2026): This article has been updated to note that Ontario’s accessibility minister is no longer attending the event.
Feature image courtesy Access to Success.

articles.title: Exclusive: Envoy targets defense contractors and semiconductor fabs with Visitors Critical - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Envoy targets defense contractors and semiconductor fabs with Visitors Critical
Workplace management platform company Envoy Inc. today launched Visitors Critical, a new tier of its visitor management service for defense contractors, semiconductor fabs and other high-security sites.
The new tier is aimed at a problem Envoy says is common at those sites, where visitor security is still run across email, spreadsheets and separate systems and letting the wrong person in can be costly. Penalties, debarment or a lost facility clearance are all possible after a wrong entry at a compliance-driven site. The person who signed the authorization can also be held liable, according to the company, which noted that settlements under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations have reached $51 million.
“We’ve spent the last 13 years building Envoy to deliver the highest levels of security, safety and compliance in a way that feels natural to the people using it,” said founder and Chief Executive Larry Gadea, who worked as an engineer at Google LLC and Twitter Inc. before starting the company in 2013.
Visitors Critical scans a visitor’s government-issued ID and matches their face to the photo on it. Names are also screened against denied-party and export-control lists through Visual Compliance and Descartes MK, both from The Descartes Systems Group Inc. Contractor qualifications are checked through ISN Software Corp. From there, visits are sent for approval based on the organization’s own written policies. The approver’s reasoning is then kept on record in case of an audit.
Among Envoy’s existing customers is Attalon Inc., the former aerospace and defense business of Coherent Corp. Every visitor to all 12 of Attalon’s sites has their ID scanned by Envoy before being screened against denied-party lists. Tim Carr, Attalon’s director of security and environment, health and safety, said that an auditor who inspects one site “has effectively inspected them all.”
The launch comes as new Envoy research of 1,000 security leaders found that 62% of enterprise leaders are very confident they would pass a physical security audit without preparation. Some 63% of that group had a security incident in the past year. At sensitive workplaces, 44% of leaders could not say with confidence who was in their building the previous day.
Visitors Critical is available now. Hardware-based ID verification, which uses supported readers to authenticate the document itself and catch forged IDs, is being offered through an early access program.
Envoy claims more than 16,000 workplaces in 170 countries as customers, including 92 of the Fortune 500. The company launched Response, a threat intelligence and incident management product, in August. It raised $111 million in a Series C round in January 2022 at a $1.4 billion valuation.

articles.title: Dans cet immeuble défraîchi, 20 salariés assemblaient des batteries : le début fou de BYD — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le 18 novembre 1994, Wang Chuanfu, un chimiste de 28 ans passé par un institut de recherche public sur les métaux, lance BYD avec une vingtaine de personnes à Buji, dans la banlieue de Shenzhen. La société est enregistrée en février 1995 avec 2,5 millions de yuans de capital (environ 300 000 euros au cours actuel). Le groupe raconte cette histoire dans un long texte publié ce mercredi sur WeChat, illustré de photos d’archives.
BYD commence par des piles rechargeables au nickel-cadmium, une technologie que les fabricants japonais délaissent, puis passe au lithium-ion en 1996. L’entreprise n’invente rien (Sony commercialise la batterie lithium-ion depuis 1991), mais elle apprend à la fabriquer pour moins cher.
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500 passe à 1 399 € au lieu de 1 899 €, support de lavage offert ! Sans fil, navigation LiDAR 360°, évitement précis des obstacles, tonte des bordures… La tonte sans effort, même pour les jardins les plus complexes.
Faute d’argent pour acheter des machines, elle remplace les robots par des ouvriers et des gabarits conçus en interne : « homme + gabarit = robot », résume BYD. Sanyo devient client dès 1996, puis Motorola, Philips et Panasonic ainsi que Nokia. En 2002, BYD assure 65 % de la production mondiale de batteries nickel-cadmium.
En 2003, BYD est déjà le deuxième fabricant mondial de batteries de téléphone, et il est coté à la Bourse de Hong Kong depuis juillet 2002. En janvier 2003, il rachète 77 % de Xi’an Qinchuan Automobile pour environ 270 millions de yuans (environ 33 millions d’euros au cours actuel), un petit constructeur alors détenu par le groupe d’armement public Norinco. Les actionnaires apprécient peu ce projet, qui ne figurait pas dans le prospectus d’introduction en Bourse. Wang Chuanfu tient bon : « Je consacrerai la seconde moitié de ma vie à l’automobile. »
La première voiture conçue par BYD est une berline thermique, la F3, produite à partir d’avril 2005. Trois ans plus tard, le 15 décembre 2008, BYD lance la F3DM, présentée comme la première hybride rechargeable produite en série au monde. Elle coûte 149 800 yuans (environ 18 000 euros au cours actuel), et seules les administrations et les entreprises peuvent l’acheter au départ. Les particuliers devront attendre 2010.
Trente-deux ans après les débuts à Buji, BYD a produit plus de 19 millions de véhicules électriques et hybrides rechargeables, contre 10 millions le jour de ses 30 ans, le 18 novembre 2024. Le 19 millionième, un SUV hybride rechargeable Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9, est sorti le 9 novembre de l’usine de Xi’an, la ville de Qinchuan. Le groupe assemble aussi des voitures en Thaïlande, dans une usine de 150 000 voitures par an, et au Brésil depuis 2025, exploite huit navires rouliers, et le 1er novembre, sa supercar Yangwang U9 Xtreme a atteint 503,17 km/h sur une autoroute fermée d’Abu Dhabi, un record homologué par la FIA et le Guinness pour un passage dans un seul sens.
Le mois d’octobre montre tout de même un début de redressement : avec 490 168 véhicules vendus, BYD signe son meilleur mois de l’année et sa sixième hausse mensuelle d’affilée sur un an, portée par l’export (170 194 unités, deux fois plus qu’en octobre 2025). En Chine, les ventes reculent encore de 10,6 % sur le mois. L’objectif de 5 à 5,5 millions de ventes en 2026 paraît en revanche hors d’atteinte : pour atteindre le bas de cette fourchette, il faudrait écouler près de 700 000 véhicules par mois en novembre et en décembre.
Le texte d’anniversaire passe en revanche sous silence un chiffre moins flatteur. Sur les dix premiers mois de 2026, les ventes de BYD en Chine ont reculé de 27,8 %, à 2,1 millions de véhicules. Les exportations, elles, ont presque doublé (+93,8 %, à 1,5 million). Au total, les ventes mondiales baissent de 2,2 %, à 3,62 millions de véhicules. À 32 ans, BYD compte sur l’étranger pour compenser le recul de ses ventes en Chine, sans y parvenir tout à fait pour l’instant.

articles.title: Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026
Guia reúne telas IPS de 120 Hz a 300 Hz com baixo tempo de resposta e fidelidade de cor para jogos competitivos, campanhas imersivas e uso diário em 2026
Escolher um monitor gamer IPS em 2026 exige equilibrar taxa de atualização, tempo de resposta e precisão cromática de acordo com o perfil de jogo.
Os painéis IPS (In-Plane Switching) consolidaram-se como o padrão preferido para setups versáteis porque oferecem amplos ângulos de visão de 178° e cobertura de cores superior aos painéis TN e VA tradicionais, sem sacrificar a agilidade exigida em títulos competitivos.
Nesta lista, selecionamos 8 modelos disponíveis no mercado brasileiro que cobrem diferentes faixas de desempenho e orçamento, partindo de opções de entrada de 120 Hz até telas avançadas de 300 Hz com retroiluminação MiniLED e resolução Quad HD.
O TCL 25G64 eleva o patamar dos monitores competitivos ao combinar um painel IPS Full HD (1920 x 1080) de 25 polegadas com retroiluminação QD-MiniLED, taxa de atualização de 300 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
Essa combinação elimina rastros em movimentos bruscos de câmera em jogos de tiro em primeira pessoa (FPS), enquanto o controle local de iluminação proporciona pretos mais profundos e brilho máximo de 600 nits com certificação HDR600.
Para quem busca fidelidade visual além da velocidade, o modelo entrega profundidade de cor de 10 bits, cobertura de 96% do espectro DCI-P3 e calibração de fábrica com precisão Delta E menor que 2.
A conectividade inclui duas portas HDMI 2.1 e uma DisplayPort, acompanhadas de base ergonômica com ajuste de altura e compatibilidade com AMD FreeSync Premium.
Voltado para jogadores que priorizam definição de imagem sem abrir mão da fluidez, o AOC Agon Q27G4F traz tela Fast IPS de 27 polegadas com resolução Quad HD (2560 x 1440 pixels), taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,5 ms MPRT).
A maior densidade de pixels garante nitidez superior para identificar alvos a longa distância e amplia a área útil de trabalho no dia a dia. O painel cobre 120% do espaço de cores sRGB, conta com brilho típico de 300 cd/m² e suporte a HDR10, entregando tonalidades vibrantes em jogos de mundo aberto.
Compatível com NVIDIA G-SYNC e Adaptive Sync para evitar cortes na imagem (screen tearing), o modelo ainda se destaca pela base completa com ajustes de altura, inclinação, giro e rotação (pivô), além de entradas DisplayPort 1.4 e HDMI 2.0.
O Samsung Odyssey G40 de 25 polegadas é projetado especificamente para o cenário de eSports, operando com painel IPS Full HD, taxa de atualização nativa de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
O formato compacto de 25 polegadas mantém toda a ação dentro do campo de visão periférico do jogador, permitindo reações imediatas em partidas ranqueadas de alto nível.
Com brilho típico de 400 cd/m² e suporte a FreeSync Premium e G-SYNC Compatible, o monitor mantém boa visibilidade mesmo em ambientes bastante iluminados e sincroniza os quadros da GPU sem engasgos.
O conjunto oferece duas entradas HDMI, uma DisplayPort e suporte ergonomicamente ajustável em altura, inclinação e modo retrato.
O Dell SE2426HG entrega especificações de nível competitivo em um chassi sóbrio de 24 polegadas, equipado com painel IPS Full HD de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 0,5 ms. Essa configuração garante transições de pixels limpas e baixa latência de entrada, atendendo jogadores de títulos competitivos que buscam alto desempenho com investimento controlado.
O modelo integra suporte a AMD FreeSync, compatibilidade com HDR10 e tecnologias de conforto visual, como tela antirreflexo, redução de luz azul e operação livre de cintilação (Flicker-Free). Conta ainda com conectividade DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI e furação padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm para instalação em braços articulados.
Posicionando-se acima do padrão tradicional de 144 Hz e 180 Hz, o AOC Agon 24G42HE apresenta tela IPS de 23,8 polegadas com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 200 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,3 ms MPRT). O ganho extra de frequência proporciona rastreamento de alvos mais suave e resposta rápida aos comandos do mouse.
Com brilho de 300 cd/m², contraste estático de 1000:1 e cobertura de 116% do padrão sRGB, o painel reproduz cores vivas em jogos e conteúdos multimídia.
O monitor possui certificação NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible, design sem bordas em três lados, entradas HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4, além de ajuste de inclinação e suporte VESA.
O LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B equilibra velocidade e precisão cromática em um painel IPS de 24 polegadas (23,8 polegadas visíveis) com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta real de 1 ms (GtG). A combinação reduz o efeito fantasma (ghosting) em cenas rápidas sem comprometer a estabilidade das cores.
O display cobre 99% da gama sRGB, suporta HDR10 e oferece ampla compatibilidade com NVIDIA G-SYNC e AMD FreeSync. Entre os recursos voltados para jogos estão o Dynamic Action Sync (redução de atraso de entrada), o Black Stabilizer (clareamento de áreas escuras) e mira integrada na tela, conectados via HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4.
Para quem prefere uma área de visualização maior mantendo a resolução Full HD, o LG UltraGear 27G411B traz tela IPS de 27 polegadas com taxa de atualização nativa de 144 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms com Motion Blur Reduction (5 ms GtG nativo).
O tamanho ampliado favorece a imersão em jogos de corrida, RPGs e consumo de vídeos, sem exigir uma placa de vídeo topo de linha para empurrar os quadros.
O painel apresenta contraste estático de 1500:1 — superior à média da categoria IPS —, cobertura de 99% sRGB, suporte a HDR10 e sincronização adaptativa via NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible e AMD FreeSync.
A construção inclui bordas finas em três lados, entradas HDMI e DisplayPort, saída para fones de ouvido e padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm.
O Samsung Essential S3 LS24F320GALMZD é o modelo mais básico da lista, mas ainda usa painel IPS e resolução Full HD, se saindo melhor para jogos casuais, trabalho remoto e uso multimídia.
A taxa de atualização menor que a de modelos gamer avançados limita o apelo competitivo. Mesmo assim, recursos como FreeSync, baixo input lag e boa reprodução de cores ajudam em consoles, notebooks e PCs simples.
A indicação é para quem quer gastar pouco e evitar painéis de qualidade inferior. O Essential S3 funciona como monitor IPS de entrada para jogar ocasionalmente, estudar e montar um setup econômico em 2026.
A escolha do monitor gamer IPS ideal depende da potência da sua placa de vídeo (GPU), dos gêneros de jogos praticados e do espaço disponível na mesa. Antes de fechar a compra, avalie quatro critérios técnicos fundamentais:
Na faixa de entrada intermediária, modelos de 24 polegadas Full HD entre 180 Hz e 200 Hz, como o LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B e o AOC Agon 24G42HE, oferecem o equilíbrio mais eficiente entre preço e desempenho.
Ambos entregam painéis IPS rápidos de 1 ms GtG, boa cobertura de cores sRGB e sincronização adaptativa sem exigir placas de vídeo avançadas.
Para quem busca salto de resolução e ergonomia completa pagando menos que em modelos OLED, o AOC Agon Q27G4F (27″ QHD 180 Hz) destaca-se como a opção mais equilibrada da categoria intermediária.
A taxa de atualização ideal começa em 144 Hz para jogos competitivos. Esse patamar já oferece movimentos mais suaves que 60 Hz ou 75 Hz e melhora a resposta visual em partidas rápidas.
Monitores de 180 Hz são o ponto de equilíbrio em 2026, pois entregam fluidez alta sem exigir tanto quanto 240 Hz. Eles combinam bem com placas de vídeo intermediárias em Full HD.
Modelos de 240 Hz, como o Samsung Odyssey G40, fazem mais sentido para jogadores de e-sports. Para aproveitar a tela, o PC precisa manter taxas próximas em jogos como CS2, Valorant e Overwatch 2.
Os painéis IPS dominam o mercado de monitores gamer por equilibrarem velocidade e qualidade de imagem, mas apresentam limitações físicas inerentes à tecnologia LCD:
O monitor OLED entrega contraste praticamente infinito, pretos reais e tempo de resposta extremamente rápido. Em jogos HDR, terror e single-player cinematográfico, a imagem costuma ser superior à de um IPS tradicional.
O monitor IPS vence em preço, disponibilidade e menor risco de burn-in. Para uso prolongado com HUD fixo, planilhas, navegador e barra de tarefas, ele tende a ser uma escolha mais tranquila.
Em 2026, OLED é a opção premium para quem busca qualidade máxima. IPS continua sendo a melhor compra racional para a maioria, especialmente em monitores Full HD e QHD com 144 Hz a 240 Hz.
O monitor IPS é melhor para quem prioriza cores, ângulo de visão e resposta mais previsível em jogos rápidos. Nossa equipe prefere IPS para FPS competitivo, uso misto e setups com duas telas.
Já o monitor VA oferece contraste maior, com pretos mais profundos e imagem forte em filmes ou jogos escuros. Porém, alguns modelos podem apresentar ghosting em transições rápidas, especialmente em cenas com tons escuros.
A escolha depende do perfil do jogador. Para e-sports e versatilidade, IPS é mais seguro; para imersão, contraste e consumo de mídia, VA pode agradar mais se o modelo tiver boa resposta.

articles.title: Sobrecalentamiento, carga lenta, daños en la batería y más riesgos de cargar el celular con el cargador del PC
articles.text:
La falta de un adaptador a mano lleva a muchos usuarios a preguntarse si pueden conectar el teléfono al cargador de una computadora portátil. La respuesta depende del tipo de puerto, del cable y, sobre todo, de la capacidad del cargador para regular la energía que entrega al teléfono.
Cargar un celular con un cargador de PC puede ser seguro si ambos dispositivos son compatibles, pero una conexión inadecuada puede derivar en calentamiento, una recarga lenta o advertencias de incompatibilidad. La marca Blackview sugiere revisar las especificaciones técnicas antes de reemplazar el cargador habitual del celular.
¿Se puede usar el cargador del PC para cargar un celular?
Sí, siempre que el cargador disponga de un puerto estándar, como USB-A o USB-C. Muchos modelos portátiles actuales incorporan puertos USB-C compatibles con distintos dispositivos, incluidos teléfonos, tablets y auriculares inalámbricos.
Si el adaptador ofrece una salida de 5 voltios, el celular puede cargarse de forma habitual. En los modelos compatibles con USB Power Delivery, conocido como USB-C PD, el cargador y el teléfono intercambian información para definir la potencia adecuada durante el proceso de carga.
Qué pasa si el cargador entrega más voltaje del necesario
Los cargadores de computadoras portátiles suelen trabajar con valores superiores a los de un teléfono. Mientras un smartphone suele requerir 5 voltios y entre 1 y 3 amperios, un adaptador para PC puede ofrecer entre 15 y 20 voltios, con una intensidad de 3 a 5 amperios.
La diferencia no implica por sí sola un daño. Los cargadores USB-C PD compatibles negocian la potencia antes de iniciar la carga. El riesgo aparece si se utiliza un accesorio defectuoso, un adaptador inadecuado o un sistema que no regula correctamente el voltaje.
Cómo el cargador del PC puede provocar el sobrecalentamiento del celular
El calor es uno de los elementos que conviene vigilar durante la carga. Si el teléfono, el cable o el adaptador se calientan más de lo normal, es clave desconectar el dispositivo y comprobar el estado de los accesorios. La temperatura elevada puede afectar el rendimiento de la batería con el paso del tiempo.
Según Blackview, un cargador muy potente o incompatible puede generar un aumento de temperatura que reduzca la vida útil de la batería. Los teléfonos modernos cuentan con circuitos de protección, pero esas medidas no sustituyen el uso de accesorios en buen estado y con especificaciones compatibles.
Además, conviene evitar recargar el teléfono sobre superficies que retienen el calor, como una cama, un sillón o debajo de ropa y mantas. La ventilación del cargador y del dispositivo ayuda a mantener condiciones de funcionamiento más estables.
Por qué el celular puede cargar lento al usar el cargador del PC
Un cargador de PC no siempre activa la carga rápida del teléfono. Para que esa función opere, el cargador, el cable y el celular deben admitir el mismo protocolo de energía. De lo contrario, el dispositivo puede limitar la potencia y completar la recarga a una velocidad inferior a la esperada.
La compatibilidad entre el teléfono y el protocolo de carga es más importante que la potencia máxima indicada en el adaptador. Un cargador capaz de entregar mucha energía no acelera necesariamente el proceso si el celular no reconoce el estándar utilizado.
En algunos casos, sobre todo con iPhone y otros dispositivos que exigen certificaciones específicas, puede aparecer una advertencia sobre un accesorio no compatible. Ese mensaje puede estar relacionado con el cable, el adaptador o la falta de certificación del producto.
Cuál es la forma correcta de cargar un teléfono con el cargador de un PC
Antes de conectar el teléfono, es necesario revisar la etiqueta del cargador. Allí figura el voltaje de salida, el amperaje y, en algunos casos, la compatibilidad con USB Power Delivery. Si el adaptador ofrece 5V/3A o incluye USB-C PD, puede ser una alternativa adecuada para muchos smartphones.
Asimismo, el cargador original del celular sigue siendo la opción sugerida porque fue diseñado para sus necesidades de energía. Si no está disponible, un cargador de portátil con puerto USB estándar, cable de calidad y compatibilidad con el teléfono puede utilizarse de forma puntual.

articles.title: Razer DeathAdder V3 Pro
articles.text:
The Razer DeathAdder V3 Pro is a solid mouse built upon an already great foundation. While I will miss the dedicated DPI buttons on the top of the mouse, it’s a great evolution for the DeathAdder line-up. As a fan of the V2 Pro, it’s nearly everything I wanted it to be. The construction is solid, and the upgraded sensors and switches improve performance, and the battery life is tremendous.
Our editors hand-pick related products using a variety of criteria: direct competitors targeting the same market segment, or devices that are similar in size, performance, or feature sets.
The Razer DeathAdder V3 is lightweight, quick, and extremely powerful, and its sensor includes bonus technologies that make it perfect for high performance in competitive games and esports matches.
This is about as good as it gets for fast, wireless, lightweight gaming mice. The DeathAdder V3 Pro is an outstanding mouse. It's comfortable, consistent, has great battery life and feels very nice to use. The side buttons could have been slightly better quality but overall this mouse lives up to its price tag.
The Razer DeathAdder V3 Pro is another interesting effort from Razer that follows on from the logic of the Razer Viper V2 Pro by shedding weight but improving the specs and design in a number of ways.
The Razer Basilisk V3 Pro is a super kitted-out mouse that’s actually a lot of fun to use. While the weight will deter certain hardcore FPS players, it never bothered me. In fact, the sensitivity clutch actually helped me play games better. While Razer’s Synapse software is starting to show its age when it comes to color customization on the Basilisk’s many flashy lights, just about everything else here feels world-class.
A featherweight high-performance esports mouse crossed with the iconic DeathAdder shape and feel. Throw in an impressive sensor and the Razer DeathAdder V3 Pro more than lives up to its Pro naming.
The Razer DeathAdder V3 Pro is one of the most responsive and fun gaming mice I’ve ever used, and also remains one of the most comfortable thanks to minor changes to the mouse’s signature shape. It’s just a shame that for all the above, Razer has upped the price significantly and sacrificed both Bluetooth connectivity and RGB lighting.
The Razer DeathAdder V3 Pro delivers a bevy of improvements to Razer's long running gaming-mouse line that, while not essential, help solidify its spot at the top of the food chain.
The mouse that rules all other gaming mice, the Razer Deathadder V3 Pro is impressive in so many aspects, we’re hard-pressed to find fault in it. It’s expensive, yes, but it’s worth breaking the piggy bank for.

articles.title: 'Horses are already down the road, I better shut the gate': Nvidia forms national security and export committee, as online commenters wonder why this wasn't already a thing
articles.text:
Nvidia goes into full damage-limitation mode, announcing new 'national security' committee — as Jensen Huang throws in fresh grenade by saying he'd be 'honored' to return as CEO
Where was this when Nvidia's booming profits kicked off during the rise of generative AI?
- Nvidia has announced a new national security and export committee
- This will oversee Nvidia's existing national security and global trade teams
- Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, observed that "advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security"
Update, November 17: Since this story was published, former Nvidia boss Jensen Huang released his first statement on X since resigning from the company. He says that "if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." You can read the full statement below.
Original story follows...
Nvidia has formed a new 'National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee' in the wake of the resignation of Jensen Huang.
A press release from the board explains that the committee will be "responsible for board-level oversight of the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management."
Nvidia already has a National Security Team and a Global Trade Compliance Team, both of which will now report to this committee (as well as reporting to interim CEO Colette Kress), keeping them up to speed on day-to-day operations, we're told.
The committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, will meet at least every quarter, and it'll be advised by "independent third-party experts" in law, national security, and trade compliance.
Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, said: "Nvidia recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security."
He added that: "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation."
Analysis: horse, stable door, and so forth
Did someone say damage control? Clearly, Nvidia is a firm that's reeling from the exit of its CEO, and as you've doubtless seen, this has been a controversial matter for a number of reasons.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While Huang has admitted to having an affair, the allegations around it being with a Chinese spy remain just that – allegations – and there's been no proof of this. So, while this new committee isn't a reaction to this side of the controversy – not as such, as it remains unproven – it is obviously enough a move to shore up any doubt there might be as to Nvidia's stance on national security and global trade therein.
Some of the reaction on Reddit has been predictable, and indeed there's a level of incredulity that Nvidia didn't already have this in place. However, it's worth noting the details here – as the press release states, Nvidia does indeed have teams dedicated to national security and global trade compliance.
Of course, every big tech company has considerable assets in place to guard their intellectual property, and we've also seen Nvidia's export controls in action with the RTX 5090 and China as the most high-profile example (and indeed more broadly in the data center sphere).
What's new with the committee here is that it has oversight across those existing entities, theoretically tightening everything up and bringing in independent experts. Although of course, you could further argue that this should have been in place already on top of the compliance teams. And there are certainly more than a few comments along the same lines as this Redditor's observation: "Horses are already down the road, I better shut the gate..."
Meanwhile, support for the return of Jensen Huang continues to grow, but Nvidia's board is reportedly unmoved – he won't be coming back as CEO, we're told.

articles.title: Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Across Latin America, India, and Southeast Asia, WhatsApp is one of the most widely used messaging applications. That makes it an obvious place to build an AI agent. For many end users, it is how they expect to interact with businesses. However, it is also a genuinely difficult surface to build for, even when your agent already runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
The agent is rarely the hard part. The integration is. Inbound messages arrive as deeply nested, type-dependent payloads that must be authenticated and normalized before your agent can read them. Media such as voice notes, images, and documents each require their own processing pipeline. Beyond message handling, you need conversation memory that survives sessions, durable schedules for reminders, and an authenticated path for external systems to trigger outbound messages. And anything you send more than 24 hours after the end user’s last message must use a pre-approved Meta message template.
Wiring that up means configuring more than 10 AWS services and learning a set of WhatsApp system behaviors that most teams discover only by hitting them. None of it is visible to a customer, but all of it has to work. Most teams either build it from scratch or hand the integration to a third-party service.
SMART (Social Messaging Agent Runtime Toolkit) is a third option: an open source Python SDK and Terraform stack that gives you the full channel layer. You provide an agent that runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, and SMART handles the rest. One command deploys the entire infrastructure to your AWS account.
Teams are already running on SMART with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Webmotors, originally scoped as a two-month engagement, compressed delivery to six weeks and moved their internal team into controlled production ahead of a full launch.
Whether you are starting from scratch or migrating an existing agent, you own the agent’s logic. You let SMART handle the channel.
The channel layer you don’t need to build
The following table compares what each concern costs to build yourself against what SMART provides.
| Concern | Building it yourself | With SMART | 
| Webhook ingestion | Signature verification, nested payloads, a dozen message types | Handled, so you receive a clean prompt | 
| Media | Download, transcribe, store, clean up, and upload outbound files before sending | Full lifecycle, both directions | 
| Message templates and the 24-hour window | Meta approval flow, category rules, tracking which window each conversation is in | Declared in YAML, synced by CLI | 
| Conversation memory | Multi-tier memory, session-break handling | Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, one function call | 
| Scheduling and triggers | Amazon EventBridge Scheduler wiring, authenticated ingress, routing | Built in | 
| Infrastructure | More than 10 AWS services stitched together | One terraform apply | 
| Local development | Redeploy and tunnel on every change | Test locally with the CLI without redeploying | 
The agentic layer
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. SMART builds on two of its main capabilities:
- AgentCore runtime hosts and scales your agent without you managing infrastructure.
- AgentCore memory persists conversation history across sessions and deployments, scoped to each phone number automatically.
Because AgentCore is framework-agnostic, so is SMART. Strands Agents gets memory wired automatically. LangGraph, Pydantic-AI, or another framework that gives you control over the conversation loop can integrate too. The SDK exposes the same memory and session hooks regardless of framework. You keep full control over the elements that differentiate your product: framework, model, prompt, and business logic.
The contract between SMART and your agent is deliberately small. Your agent receives the inbound message and returns text, optionally with rich message attachments. Everything else, session wiring, memory binding, delivery scheduling, is handled for you.
The following example is a complete agent.py for a SMART project. The scaffolding command (socialagent init) creates the project structure and configuration around it. This file is where your agent logic lives.
The create_session_manager() function binds the agent to AgentCore memory scoped to that phone number, so history survives across sessions and deployments for the memory retention period (7 days by default).
The socialagent_notify_context() wrapper is the other pattern worth keeping. Tools sometimes need to send something while the agent is still working, such as a button list or a progress update. Sending it immediately corrupts the conversation history, and the user’s next message fails. The wrapper collects those messages instead, and they go out in order once the turn finishes. Your tools send messages normally and do not deal with the timing.
Architecture
The following diagram shows how an inbound message travels from WhatsApp to your agent and back, and where the shared infrastructure sits.
The SMART core stack is organized into distinct layers: message processing, an agent layer, and a service layer. AWS End User Messaging Social receives inbound WhatsApp messages and routes them to the processing layer. An AWS Lambda function handles the channel logic, while Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides the runtime, memory, and observability for the agent itself. Supporting services such as Amazon DynamoDB (optional, for per-user state), AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) supply state management, credentials, monitoring, and storage across the stack.
Inbound events arrive through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). On each event, the webhook Lambda function verifies the SNS message signature, normalizes the payload, and rate-limits each user (20 messages per minute by default, with the DynamoDB state table enabled). It then fires a read receipt and typing indicator, so the conversation feels alive before the model finishes. Voice notes go through Amazon Transcribe. Other media becomes a descriptor or goes to a hook you register if you want custom handling. When the agent throttles or fails, the user receives a readable message that you can customize, rather than silence.
Agents built on SMART interact directly with end users, so production deployments should include appropriate safeguards. The Terraform stack creates and configures an Amazon Bedrock Guardrails resource by default. With a single guardrail variable in your environment configuration, you can use the stack’s default guardrail, bring your own, or opt out entirely. The controls that you apply are up to you. SMART makes sure the wiring is already in place.
After the message is ready, the webhook function passes it to AgentCore runtime. AgentCore memory maintains conversation context across sessions, and AgentCore Observability, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, traces every step for debugging and audit.
The webhook function sends the reply and messages your tools queued during the turn. A notification function handles sends outside a turn, such as proactive or scheduled messages. External systems trigger your event handlers by posting to an Amazon API Gateway endpoint protected by an API key and a Lambda authorizer. The event is published to Amazon SNS and the event Lambda runs your handler. Amazon EventBridge Scheduler handles time-based outreach, such as reminders and recurring check-ins. With message templates managed through AWS End User Messaging, you can send structured notifications outside the 24-hour WhatsApp session window.
A single socialagent deploy provisions the following resources (it runs terraform apply under the hood).
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime and AgentCore memory.
- The webhook, notification, event, and scheduler Lambda functions, on Python 3.12, each with AWS X-Ray tracing and a dead-letter queue.
- The Amazon SNS ingestion topic and the event API.
- Amazon EventBridge Scheduler.
- Amazon S3 buckets for media and audit trails.
- Amazon CloudWatch dashboards and alarms.
The agent container image and the Lambda layer build in AWS CodeBuild during the apply. Docker isn’t required locally.
What you need
Before you deploy, confirm that you have the following.
- AWS End User Messaging Social, with a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) linked and a phone number registered. That account is the identity Meta issues to a business. For a step-by-step guide, see Getting started with AWS End User Messaging Social, which walks you through linking your WABA and registering a phone number.
- An AWS account with AgentCore runtime and AgentCore memory available in your AWS Region, and model access enabled. This walkthrough uses Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock by default. You can access many more foundation models (FMs) through Bedrock. See model support by Region.
- Python 3.11 or later locally.
- Terraform 1.7 or later, uv, and the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI). The repository ships a starting-point AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy for the deployer role. See the infrastructure README for the full list of actions.
Note: This is sample code, for non-production usage. You should work with your security and legal teams to meet your organizational security, regulatory and compliance requirements before deployment.
Ship it
Start by cloning the repository and scaffolding a project.
The --blueprint flag selects a project blueprint. Three blueprints ship, and minimal is the default if you don’t pass an argument:
- minimal: a bare-bones echo agent with no tools, skills, or message templates. Start here to build from scratch.
- personal-assistant: a general-purpose assistant with conversation memory, per-user state, scheduling, skills, and rich/voice/image media tools, built on Strands. Start here for conversational, do-it-all agents.
- appointment-scheduler: a booking agent that walks the user through a catalog of items and time slots, confirms the appointment, stores it as per-user state, and sends reminders. Start here for scheduling and booking flows.
You get a project with your agent.py, socialagent.dev.yaml (the project’s deployment configuration), handler stubs for the webhook, notification, event, and scheduler paths, and a vendored copy of socialagent_runtime/. The personal assistant and appointment-scheduler blueprints also bring tools, skills, and a templates.yaml for your message templates. minimal ships none of those, so you add them as required.
Next, iterate locally, with no infrastructure at all.
The socialagent dev command runs your real agent loop and real tools in a terminal read-eval-print loop (REPL), with AWS channel I/O stubbed. Memory becomes a local file-backed session, and state becomes a local JSON file shared across your dev sessions. Notifications print to the terminal, including buttons and list rows. One-shot schedules run immediately. Recurring ones are registered but do not fire. Tool calls appear inline. The reply arrives as one message, as on WhatsApp. The /event and /schedule commands exercise the handler paths. No deployment is involved, so you can test a change as soon as you save it.
Two caveats apply. The model call is real, so a blueprint other than minimal needs AWS credentials and Amazon Bedrock access. The REPL also doesn’t simulate IAM or Meta’s template review. Testing through a deployed stack is highly recommended before you consider something done.
You can add capabilities as recipes. Each recipe is a plain Python function plus a markdown skill that teaches the agent when to use it.
Wiring the recipe to the agentic layer is the developer responsibility, which is what keeps recipes portable if you change agent frameworks.
When the behavior is right locally, deploy the stack.
One step Terraform cannot do for you. AWS End User Messaging Social needs to know where to deliver inbound messages. Point your WhatsApp Business Account at the Amazon SNS topic the stack created. That setting lives on the business account, not in the stack. Point the WABA’s event destination at the stack’s SNS topic using the admin console’s Bind action, or with aws socialmessaging put-whatsapp-business-account-event-destinations from the CLI. Until it is linked, inbound messages go nowhere, and nothing errors.
When the project includes a templates.yaml, the deploy step also syncs your message templates with Meta. If you need to sync templates independently, run uv run socialagent templates sync, which reads the phone number ID and prefix from socialagent.dev.yaml and the template definitions from templates.yaml. A rejected template will fail the deploy, so fix the wording before retrying.
Meta sorts templates by purpose, and a transactional one has more permissive sending rules than a promotional one. Keep the wording plain. Emojis and marketing language are the usual reason a template gets reclassified as promotional. Running templates sync --force re-registers every template, sending approved ones back through Meta review. A plain sync skips them. Leave approved templates alone unless you need to change their content.
Now you’re ready to message your WhatsApp number.
Operate it
Shipping one bot is a project. Operating a fleet of them is the part nobody budgets for, so you also get an optional administration console with its own Terraform root. Deploy it once. Each SMART stack that sets admin_registry_bucket registers itself to a shared Amazon S3 registry on deploy, and the administration console discovers those stacks from there.
The console gives you fleet health at a glance, then per-bot depth. From a single stack view, you can do the following.
- Read real conversations and reply by hand.
- Inspect and cancel Amazon EventBridge schedules, and browse per-user state.
- Restart an individual Lambda function or the runtime.
- Review deployment history, recent errors, and Amazon CloudWatch logs.
- Trigger test events.
- Manage message templates with a WhatsApp-style rendering, and see a warning when Meta has reclassified one.
The console also owns the phone-number binding described earlier, so rebinding a number to a different stack is a UI action.
Sign-in runs through Amazon Cognito, with multi-factor authentication (MFA) required. Role-based permissions are then enforced on every API route. The console itself is served from Amazon CloudFront over a private Amazon S3 bucket.
The console runs on AWS services end to end. Every conversation stays within two providers: Meta and AWS. Model calls may be processed in other AWS Regions through Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference. See docs/data-flows.md in the repository for details on inference routing, media processing, and service opt-out options.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, tear down the stacks in the following order.
Terraform will not remove three things. The media and audit S3 buckets block destroy while they hold objects, unless enable_force_destroy is set. Templates registered with Meta persist. Your phone number registration is account-level and stays in place.
Get started
When building a WhatsApp AI product, the agent is where your differentiation lives. The channel integration is what eats your roadmap. SMART moves that boundary for you. Write a prompt, a few tools, and your business logic. In return you get webhook ingestion, media handling, conversation memory, scheduling, and template management. All backed by one-command infrastructure, a local development loop, and an administration console running in your own AWS account.
To go further, take the following next steps.
- Get the code from the SMART repository on GitHub.
- Set up your WhatsApp Business Account with AWS End User Messaging Social.
- Start with socialagent init and socialagent dev, which need no AWS infrastructure.
- Read the documentation in the repository for the areas this post summarized, including notifications, media handling, events and scheduling, per-user state, and message templates.
- For further research, see the AgentCore documentation.
We would love to see what you build with it.

articles.title: XPRIZE launches $6m competition to tackle foundational learning crisis in Africa, India - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Global non-profit XPRIZE has launched XPRIZE Accelerate Learning, a two-year, US$6 million competition seeking tech-driven solutions that help first graders in Sub-Saharan Africa and India master foundational reading and maths.
XPRIZE is an established global leader in designing, launching, and executing large-scale competitions to solve humanity’s greatest challenges.
The competition, which takes place in Rwanda, aims to cut the time it takes children to learn reading and maths skills from four years to one, at a cost as low as US$10 per child, and to reach nearly one million students in target communities. In Sub-Saharan Africa, nine in 10 children cannot read and understand a simple sentence by age 10.
Startups, non-profits, universities, corporates, government agencies and individuals can enter one or both of two tracks. The Core Track, worth US$5 million, seeks end-to-end solutions that improve mastery by at least 25 percentage points at under US$10 per child per year. Up to eight finalists will deploy at school district scale, with the winner taking home US$2.5 million.
The Last Mile Moonshot track, with separate US$400,000 purses for Sub-Saharan Africa and India targets a 50 percentage point improvement at under US$40 per child. Finalists will test their solutions in a six-month randomised controlled trial.
Teams will be paired with local schools or districts to co-design and test their solutions, so that governments can adopt them long term.
“Rwanda’s Vision 2050 depends on a skilled and productive workforce, and that journey begins with children who can read, understand and apply what they learn,” said Joseph Nsengimana, Rwanda’s Minister of Education. “We welcome XPRIZE as a partner in accelerating solutions and invite Rwanda’s innovators, educators and researchers to help transform learning outcomes for every child.”
Partners include the Republic of Rwanda, the African Union Development Agency-NEPAD, Equity Group Foundation, ShikshaNext and IDinsight. Qualified teams will be announced in 2027, and winners in 2029.

articles.title: Panne Microsoft 365 : un bug interne vieux de plusieurs mois à l'origine du chaos
articles.text:
Microsoft vient de révéler les causes de la panne mondiale qui a paralysé Microsoft 365 pendant près de 24 heures. À l'origine du désastre, un bug passé inaperçu pendant plus de trois mois, et des systèmes de secours qui ont aggravé la situation au lieu de la contenir.
Depuis le temps qu'on reproche à Microsoft de laisser traîner des bugs partout, il fallait bien qu'un jour ils finissent par lui exploser à la figure. C'est exactement ce qui s'est passé les 12 et 13 novembre derniers, deux journées noires pour Microsoft 365, resté en carafe pendant près de 24 heures. L'entreprise vient en effet de livrer les premières conclusions de son enquête dans un rapport préliminaire, également commenté sur X par Charles Lamanna, vice-président exécutif chez Microsoft, révélant qu'un défaut logiciel introduit dès juillet dans sa propre infrastructure est à l'origine de la panne. Un bug passé inaperçu pendant plus de trois mois, responsable d’une réaction en chaîne que les systèmes de secours ont eux-mêmes contribué à amplifier.
Microsoft avait tout testé, sauf les bonnes conditions…
Juillet 2026. Redmond l'ignore encore, mais les ennuis commencent. L'entreprise déploie un correctif spécialement conçu pour les serveurs Windows de ses passerelles réseau Microsoft 365, chargées de traiter les demandes de connexion à ses services. La modification est progressivement distribuée à l'ensemble de l'infrastructure concernée, sans provoquer d’incident notable. Pourtant, son code embarque déjà le bug qui mettra ses serveurs à genoux d’ici quelques mois.
En cause, un problème de contention de verrous (lock contention) au sein d'un processus interne de Windows. En temps normal, ces verrous permettent de coordonner l'accès aux ressources partagées : lorsqu'une opération utilise une ressource, les autres doivent attendre qu'elle ait terminé pour y accéder à leur tour. Mais une anomalie présente dans ce processus a enrayé cette coordination lorsque les serveurs ont été fortement sollicités. Les opérations ont alors passé trop de temps à se disputer les mêmes accès, les requêtes se sont accumulées et le processeur comme la mémoire ont fini par saturer, si bien que les serveurs ont cessé de répondre aux demandes de connexion.
Mais comment diable une telle bombe à retardement a-t-elle pu échapper aux batteries de tests menées par Microsoft en amont du déploiement du patch ? Eh bien, parce que les essais en laboratoire n'ont jamais reproduit les conditions dans lesquelles elle risquait d'exploser. L'entreprise a en effet privilégié des machines moins puissantes que ses serveurs de production et simulé un trafic insuffisamment représentatif de celui qu'ils allaient réellement devoir traiter.
… et tout ce qui pouvait mal tourner a mal tourné
Plus de trois mois passent sans que rien ne vienne troubler le fonctionnement des services. Puis arrive le 12 novembre. Vers 2 heures du matin, Microsoft Teams bascule automatiquement vers une passerelle réseau également utilisée par Exchange Online. Rien d'anormal jusque-là, cette opération faisant partie des procédures prévues par Microsoft pour assurer la continuité de ses services. Toujours est-il qu’elle augmente le trafic sur une infrastructure déjà privée de près de 14 % de ses capacités, à la suite d'un incident indépendant survenu la veille.
Au fil des heures, la charge s’intensifie et finit par réunir les fameuses conditions nécessaires au déclenchement du bug de juillet. En pleine période de forte activité aux États-Unis, les premiers serveurs saturent puis cessent de répondre, et la situation dégénère. Les systèmes automatiques de Microsoft redirigent alors les connexions vers d'autres machines encore opérationnelles, comme ils sont censés le faire pour éviter toute interruption de service.
Manque de chance pour Microsoft, les serveurs de repli présentent exactement le même défaut logiciel. À mesure que le trafic est redistribué, ils saturent à leur tour, provoquant une réaction en chaîne. Pour couronner le tout, les dispositifs censés empêcher la panne de se propager d'une région à l'autre ne remplissent pas non plus leur rôle, mis en échec par une défaillance supplémentaire. En moins de deux heures, plus de 80 % des serveurs de la passerelle réseau commune à Teams et Exchange Online tombent.
Un bourbier dont Microsoft a eu bien du mal à sortir
Teams, OneDrive et SharePoint parviennent à limiter les dégâts en basculant vers une autre infrastructure réseau, ce qui leur permet de rétablir une partie de leurs fonctionnalités. Mais Exchange Online ne peut pas en faire autant à cette échelle, si bien que la plupart des utilisateurs et utilisatrices n’ont plus accès à leur messagerie, tandis que les mails en attente de livraison s'accumulent.
Pendant ce temps, les équipes de Microsoft tentent de remettre les serveurs en service, sans grand succès. À peine redémarrées, les machines sont submergées par les requêtes en attente et cessent de nouveau de répondre. Les procédures automatiques de récupération n'ont pas été conçues pour gérer une panne d'une telle ampleur, et l'ancienneté du code défectueux empêche d'annuler rapidement la modification par les moyens habituels.
Les ingénieurs doivent finalement développer une mise à jour rétablissant l'ancien fonctionnement du système, puis l'appliquer progressivement aux machines touchées. Le 13 novembre, à 17 h 10, heure française, Microsoft confirme la fin des perturbations, après presque 24 heures de panne. Depuis, l'entreprise a renforcé ses capacités réseau, sa surveillance et ses dispositifs de répartition du trafic. Un rapport définitif, attendu le 20 novembre, doit encore détailler les mesures supplémentaires prévues pour éviter qu'un tel scénario catastrophe ne se reproduise.
Microsoft 365 offre une solution complète et intégrée pour la productivité, la collaboration, la sécurité et la gestion, ce qui en fait un choix populaire pour les entreprises, les organisations et les particuliers qui ont besoin d'être productifs et sécurisés dans le monde numérique d'aujourd'hui. À télécharger sur Windows et Mac.
- Applications web gratuites pour les besoins simples
- Applications de bureau particulièrement complètes
- Intégration avec OneDrive et les services Microsoft
- Applications de bureau complètes principalement accessibles sur abonnement
- Aucune version desktop officielle sous Linux
- Gamme d’offres difficile à comprendre

articles.title: GTA 6 : comment suivre le match de NBA entre le Miami Heat et les Milwaukee Bucks ?
articles.text:
Le Miami Heat et la NBA se sont associés à Rockstar Games pour promouvoir GTA 6 directement sur les parquets. Le temps d’un match, le Miami Heat devient le Vice City Heat, soit l’équipe fictive du jeu vidéo attendu ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X.
Le Heat et Rockstar Games ont prévu des maillots spéciaux (une édition Cactus Jack, la marque du rappeur Travis Scott) et un parquet redessiné aux couleurs de Vice City. Les joueurs ont même reçu une PS5 Pro collector, arborant une finition aux couleurs de GTA 6 (avec deux manettes et le jeu). Des produits dérivés sont en vente en ligne et dans les boutiques du club. La réplique du maillot, elle, n’est vendue que sur place, en quantité limitée et à raison d’un exemplaire par spectateur.
Où suivre le match entre le Vice City Heat et les Milwaukee Bucks ?
Quand a lieu le match entre Vice City Heat et les Milwaukees Bucks ?
Le match entre le Vice City Heat et les Milwaukee Bucks a lieu ce mercredi 18 novembre, à 19 h, heure locale, soit dans la nuit du 18 au 19 novembre, à 1 h du matin. Oui, GTA 6 sera déjà disponible depuis une heure en France, puisque Rockstar débloque le jeu à minuit, heure locale. Sur la côte Est des États-Unis, il faudra attendre 6 h du matin, heure de Paris.
La rencontre a lieu au Kaseya Center de Miami, salle du Heat, qui affiche désormais « Welcome to Vice City » sur son toit.
Rendez-vous sur beIN Sports pour regarder la NBA
En France, la NBA est partagée entre Prime Video, beIN Sports et le League Pass, la plateforme de la ligue. Pour ce match entre le Vice City Heat et les Milwaukee Bucks, rendez-vous sur beIN Sports, dont l’abonnement démarre à 15 € par mois.
Autre option : le NBA League Pass
La NBA dispose par ailleurs de sa propre plateforme, le League Pass, également accessible en France via Prime Video. Elle donne accès à tous les matchs en direct et permet même d’en regarder jusqu’à quatre en même temps, selon la formule. Deux options sont proposées : League Pass Premium à 199,99 € pour la saison (ou 28,99 € par mois) ou League Pass à 146,99 € (ou 21,99 € par mois).
Qui est le favori entre le Vice City Heat et les Milwaukees Bucks ?
Outre le caractère événementiel lié à GTA 6, ce match de NBA signera les retrouvailles entre Giannis Antetokounmpo et Milwaukee, la franchise avec laquelle il a été champion NBA en 2021 et qui l’a transféré à Miami cet été. Sur le papier, il n’y a pas photo. Le Heat a mal démarré sa saison (quatre défaites de suite), mais reste sur cinq victoires. La franchise floridienne est cinquième de la conférence Est, avec un bilan de 8-6. Les Milwaukee Bucks, eux, sont derniers de la conférence Est, avec un piètre bilan de 1-13, et une série de dix revers de rang.
