articles.title: Your complete guide to AWS Quick at AWS re:Invent 2026 | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Your complete guide to AWS Quick at AWS re:Invent 2026
AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work, where the dashboards, agents, and automations one person creates are available to everyone on the team. Built on AWS with enterprise security and governance from the start, Quick connects to the data and applications you use every day. At AWS re:Invent 2026 (November 30 to December 4), customers including Allianz, Cox Automotive, Mondelez, DXC, and Southwest Airlines, join AWS leaders on stage to share how they govern, extend and scale Quick across their teams. Whether you’re a business or technology leader, a builder, or part of an IT, security, data, or analytics team, use this guide to find the sessions that fit your goals.
Explore the session catalog and learn more.
Keynote
Join AWS CEO Matt Garman for the re:Invent 2026 CEO Keynote on Tuesday from 8:30 AM – 10:30 AM PT as he shares the latest innovations powering the agentic era. From AI infrastructure and inference to data, agent platforms, and the software agents AWS is building, see how AWS gives you the depth, breadth, and integration to build what’s next with new announcements and stories from customers already doing it.
Can’t make it to Las Vegas? Watch 50+ sessions live on the AWS re:Invent livestream, including keynotes, talks, and labs.
Breakout sessions
Hear directly from customers about how they deployed AWS Quick, from first rollout to enterprise scale, and what they learned along the way.
BIZ216: AI assistant for public sector: Governance without compromise with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:00 AM PST
Speakers: Rima Olinger, Sonali Sahu, Mike Shore-Nye
Public sector organizations serve diverse populations with strict boundaries: students and administrators, citizens and case workers, patients and providers. They need AI that works across these groups without compromising data isolation, compliance, or governance. Multi-tenant environments demand security frameworks most AI assistants were not built to meet. Hear from a higher education customer who faced these constraints and displaced their incumbent tool in favor of AWS Quick’s governance-first architecture: tenant-level data isolation, role-based access controls across distinct user populations, and compliance frameworks built for regulated environments. Learn why existing solutions fell short, how Quick’s native governance model met their requirements without custom engineering, and what the transition looked like from decision to deployment.
BIZ219: How a brand turned AI governance into a strategic advantage with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:00 AM PST
Speakers: Steve Vinsik, Mark Huber, Katie Travis
In automotive, data isolation is not optional. You serve thousands of dealer clients who compete with each other, handle consumer financial data under FTC Safeguards rules, and operate across state privacy boundaries. Most AI tools cannot enforce tenant-level separation between competing dealers, restrict access by franchise agreement, or prove compliance across jurisdictions. Hear from a customer who turned that constraint into an advantage: they built a governance model with AWS Quick that enforces fine-grained data permissions across their dealer network, role-based access controls by business function, and audit frameworks that satisfy regulators and competitive separation requirements. Learn how they validated it against compliance requirements, and how governance became the reason they deployed faster than competitors still waiting on security approval.
BIZ112: From zero to 20,000 desktops: Getting started with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Jose Kunnackal John
Your team is drowning in context-switching: toggling between email, documents, data tools, and chat only to complete a single task. Productivity tools promise to help, but most add complexity instead of removing it. In this fireside chat, hear from customers who faced that exact challenge and deployed an AI assistant across 20,000+ users in under 90 days. Learn what convinced their leadership to invest, how they integrated AI into daily workflows without disrupting existing tools, and what the first 90 days of adoption actually looked like. Walk away with a practical roadmap for bringing AWS Quick AI assistant to your workforce at scale.
BIZ214: Empowering 200,000 people without compromising trust: AWS Quick
Tuesday, Dec 1 | 4:30 PM PST
Speakers: Ben Haller, Raji Sivasubramaniam, Axel Schell
Allianz needed to empower 200,000 employees with AI without sacrificing trust. With operations across dozens of regulated markets, the security, privacy, and works council requirements were non-negotiable. Every stakeholder asked the same question: how do you move fast and still earn the trust of those guarding your company’s security? Hear how Allianz partnered with AWS to deploy the capabilities that make AWS Quick enterprise-ready: protection of confidential information, structured approval workflows for agentic actions, custom branding per business unit, and multi-language support. Learn how Allianz navigated the full approval process and moved from “not yet” to “go” in six weeks.
BIZ217: One AI assistant, every data source: Unifying access with AWS Quick
Wednesday, Dec 2 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: David Provan, Jess Wang, Jesse Gebhardt
Your data lives in one platform. Your reports live in another. Your documents live somewhere else. Every time someone needs an answer, they spend time figuring out where to look before they can act. Decisions slow down. Teams duplicate work because they cannot find what already exists. New employees take months to become productive because institutional knowledge is trapped in systems they do not know how to navigate. Hear from a customer who solved this by giving their team a single AI assistant that connects across all their enterprise systems. Instead of training people on where to find information, they ask AWS Quick and get answers grounded in their real business data, regardless of where it lives. Learn how they configured the integration, how their teams adopted it, and what changed about the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.
BIZ113: Getting started with AWS Quick: How a customer went from curious to deployed
Thursday, Dec 3 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Leo Ohannesian, Justin Bundick, Peter Hunn
Your team spends hours on work that should take minutes: summarizing meetings, drafting documents, finding answers buried across systems, pulling data from multiple platforms. You know AI should help, but you need to see it work in a real environment before you commit. In this session, see how a customer put AWS Quick into daily workflows across their organization and watch live as it composes documents, analyzes data, summarizes conversations, and connects to enterprise systems. Hear what problems they were solving, what changed for their teams after deployment, and what surprised them about adoption. Leave with a clear picture of the problems Quick solves and how to evaluate whether it fits your organization.
BIZ213: Accelerating AI adoption and realized value with AWS Quick
Thursday, Dec 3 | 1:30 PM PST
Speakers: Neal Cauley, John Brock, Stefan Schulz
You deployed an AI assistant. Your team tried it for a week and stopped. The tool could not access the systems where real work happens, gave generic answers because it was disconnected from your enterprise context, and security would not approve broader rollout because the governance story was unclear. That is where most AI deployments stall. Hear from a customer who lived that exact cycle: low adoption, frustrated leadership, and a growing sense that the investment was wasted. They evaluated multiple alternatives and made the switch to AWS Quick, an AI assistant with governed access to enterprise data, native connectors to the systems their teams already use, and agentic workflows that span business units. Learn what broke in their first deployment, what they looked for in a replacement, and how governed data access turned single-digit adoption into organization-wide usage.
BIZ215: From pilot to enterprise scale with AWS Quick
Thursday, Dec 3 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: Rekha Seshadrinathan, Gayatri Ohri, Michael Murphy
Your AI pilot proved value with a small team. Now you need to deploy across the organization without a dedicated rollout team and without losing what made it work. Hear from a customer who scaled AWS Quick from an initial deployment to thousands of users across their enterprise. Learn the phased strategy they used to expand Quick’s capabilities: connecting teams to enterprise data, automating repetitive workflows, and rolling out agentic features that kept usage growing after the initial adoption wave. Discover what metrics justified continued investment and the operational model they built so scaling Quick did not create a support burden for IT. Walk away with a repeatable framework for taking AWS Quick from proof-of-concept to production deployment across your organization.
BIZ218: From AI tasks to autonomous multi-agent workflows with AWS Quick
Thursday, Dec 3 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: Ramon Lopez, Mike Hogan
The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team’s time disappears. AWS Quick changes that equation. Instead of one AI assistant doing one task, specialized agents each handle their piece and hand off to the next automatically. The human stays in the loop for judgment calls, not for data gathering and routing. Hear from a customer who moved from standalone AI use cases to compound, multi-agent workflows with AWS Quick. Learn how they identified which workflows to orchestrate first, how they designed agent handoffs that satisfy compliance, and what it means now that the coordination layer runs autonomously.
Chalk talks
Whiteboard architectures and trade-offs with the AWS Quick product and solutions teams. Bring your toughest questions.
BIZ306: Bring your own ontology: Ground AWS Quick in enterprise context
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:00 AM PST
Speakers: Tom Ron, Fatima Khakwani
Enterprise questions rarely have answers in a single document. Your business runs on connections: customers to products, teams to processes, and risks to regulations. But vector search doesn’t see any of that. In this chalk talk, we show how to ground AWS Quick in your enterprise context by integrating it with a knowledge graph built from your domain knowledge. We’ll walk through how we built this pattern using GraphRAG for real customers and the results they achieved. Then we’ll open the whiteboard. Bring your toughest use case and we’ll sketch your ontology live, showing how Quick would traverse it to deliver better answers.
BIZ323: Decision frameworks, evaluation, and cost management with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 10:30 AM PST
Tuesday, Dec 1 | 2:30 PM PST (repeat)
Speakers: Sagar Rao, Sandhya Khanderia
Moving from one agent to enterprise-wide automation means choosing the right path (Flows, Automate, Custom Agents, persistent agents) and the right trigger model. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a decision framework that bakes in evaluation and cost management from the start, not as afterthoughts. We’ll connect orchestration across 25+ connectors, skills, and workstreams to measurable outcomes and dollars. Bring your automation backlog. You’ll leave with a decision matrix, eval harness, and a return on investment (ROI) story.
BIZ307: Architect AI-powered analytics with AWS Quick across your data platforms
Monday, Nov 30 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Vignessh Baskaran, Jackson Dowden
As organizations adopt AI-powered analytics, they need architectures that connect business intelligence (BI) and conversational AI experiences to their existing data platforms. In this session we’ll diagram architectural patterns for connecting AWS Quick to structured data sources and integrating with third-party catalogs and semantic layers. We’ll compare the available connectivity approaches, including data sources and action connectors based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and discuss when to use each. Considerations will span production use cases like BI dashboards, embedded analytics, text-to-SQL Q&A, and agentic workflows. Together we’ll tackle real-world integration challenges including authentication, performance optimization, and governance. This session is ideal for architects and technical leaders looking to build AI-powered analytics across their data platforms.
BIZ404: Teaching Quick to remember and connect with memory and knowledge graphs
Monday, Nov 30 | 1:30 PM PST
Speakers: Thomas Delteil, Adi Kalyanpur
Every conversation with an AI assistant starts from scratch. Your agent doesn’t remember what worked yesterday, can’t tell you who owns a project without searching again, and repeats the same mistakes because failures are never captured. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Quick breaks out of statelessness with two primitives: a continuous-learning memory layer where a background agent extracts reusable knowledge after each session and scores it with a probabilistic confidence model, and a personal knowledge graph that connects people, projects, decisions, and evidence across your tools so the agent has a map of your world before it reads a single document. We’ll whiteboard the architecture and the tradeoffs that shaped it, then open it up. Bring your hardest questions about memory staleness, confidence calibration, graph noise, or making agents that actually get better over time.
BIZ305: Security: Zero-trust identity and data protection in the agentic era
Monday, Nov 30 | 2:30 PM PST
Speakers: Priya Kakarla, Munish Gopal
Security reviews stall AI rollouts more than any capability gap, and agentic AI raises the bar. This chalk talk goes past “is it secure?” to the architecture that gets a CISO to yes. We’ll whiteboard the full identity path: single sign-on (SSO) through providers like Okta and Ping, with end-user identity propagated to the data so authorization is enforced per user, in real time, across 1P AWS and 3P sources. Then we extend that trust to agents: agent identity, deterministic policy checks on every tool call, and data protection: Purview DLP, default guardrails, deny-by-default, and full SIEM auditability.
BIZ310: Secure and scalable multi-tenant deployment patterns for AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 3:00 PM PST
Speakers: Chin Rane, Vineet Kachhawaha
As organizations scale their adoption of AWS Quick across business units, subsidiaries, and partner ecosystems, deploying a secure multi-tenant architecture becomes critical. This chalk talk explores proven deployment patterns that balance tenant isolation, governance, and operational efficiency when rolling out AWS Quick at enterprise scale. We will walk through two primary isolation strategies: multi-account separation using AWS Organizations for environment-level boundaries (dev/staging/prod), and namespace-based logical isolation within a single account for user-cohort segmentation.
BIZ304: Building and governing apps on Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 4:00 PM PST
Speakers: Shane Thompson, Art Chan
Anyone can generate apps from a sentence. The hard part is governing them and getting them in front of the right users. This chalk talk whiteboards the full lifecycle of AWS Quick Apps: building them from natural language with no separate hosting, wiring in data and actions through MCP, and the three sharing paths: private, public URLs, and enterprise sharing gated behind admin approval workflows.
BIZ303: One context layer, every surface: Enterprise knowledge for agents that work anywhere
Thursday, Dec 3 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Suren Raju, Josh DeMuth
Your AI agents are only as smart as the data they can reach. In most enterprises, that data is scattered across dozens of systems, siloed, ungoverned, and invisible to the agents that need it most. In this chalk talk, we architect a context layer from the ground up: connecting enterprise knowledge into a unified index, then enriching that foundation with a knowledge graph that maps organizational relationships, business rules, and domain context, giving agents permission-scoped, relationship-aware intelligence at runtime. Then we take that intelligence to where users work: browser, desktop, mobile, collaboration tools, and productivity suites. Each surface independently governed yet sharing one agent identity, one memory, and one set of guardrails. Bring your architecture. We’ll whiteboard the end-to-end path together.
Workshops
Get hands-on with AWS Quick. Bring your laptop. You’ll leave with something working.
INV001: Ctrl+Alt+Ship: Hands-On with AWS Quick, Kiro, and Amazon Connect Customer
Walk-up, available all week
Speakers: Michelle Koh, Anupa Bhattacharyya, Christopher Lott 
Ctrl+Alt+Ship is a walk-up, self-paced lab area open all week (Nov 30 – Dec 4) in the Venetian Level 2 ballroom. No reservation is needed and workstations are provided. Attendees pick a track (Kiro, Quick or Connect) and a level, 200 or 400. Both Quick labs are business simulations where Quick connects to the company’s business systems through MCP. In the L200 Kōji Fresh lab, attendees lead the response to a product-safety crisis at a fictional Singapore food company. They investigate across email, CRM, social and supply chain, brief the board and supplier, run a recall across three systems from one instruction, and turn five data exports into board-ready charts. In the L400 SkyNova Airlines lab, 14 passengers have fallen ill overnight and an influencer is blaming the airline. Attendees use Quick across six systems to find the pattern and brief the board. They then rebook stranded passengers within a hard budget, build a Flow that runs the recovery for a grounded flight, and ship a Quick App for the airport transfer desk. Facilitators will be on hand to help.
BIZ312: Build AI-powered analytics with conversational BI on AWS Quick
Tuesday, Dec 1 | 3:30 PM PST
Speakers: Neeraj Kumar, Salim Khan
Construct a complete AI-powered analytics pipeline, from data ingestion to conversational consumption. Use AWS Quick’s Data Catalog to discover data, query it live without moving it into SPICE, then enrich and import metadata with semantics inherited to build natural-language Q&A. In this hands-on workshop, you start with seven raw banking tables: no catalog, no definitions. An agent inspects the data and builds the catalog for you. You ask questions in plain English and get answers. An agent generates a dashboard showing which top customers are slipping. Another agent, aware of the bank’s compliance rules, checks every offer before it ships. Then you automate the full response as a Quick Flow and wrap it in a custom app your team can use. You leave with a working banking command center that agents built, and that you can rebuild in your own account using conversational analytics.
BIZ313: Build agentic automations for business processes with AWS Quick Automate
Wednesday, Dec 2 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Reagan Rosario, Zuhayr Raghib
In this session, learn how to build an automation using AWS Quick Automate. Through a financial services example, explore how specialized AI agents work together to handle complex interactions across web pages and business applications. You’ll create a production-ready automation featuring custom agents that use knowledge and tools to transform a merchant onboarding process. Using Quick Automate’s chat-based authoring and visual studio, you’ll configure a workflow with multiple agents, integrate with multiple tools, test and debug the workflow, and then deploy it using robust enterprise controls. Walk away knowing how to develop agentic automations for real-world use cases.
BIZ311: Master agent skills: From desktop builds to production deployment
Wednesday, Dec 2 | 3:00 PM PST
Speakers: Jed Lechner, Leo Mentis Raj Selvaraj
Build, govern, and scale production-ready agent skills across your enterprise on AWS Quick. Author custom skills on Quick, then shift to the admin perspective: register skills in Quick Catalog for org-wide discovery, configure access policies, and schedule autonomous execution at scale. You’ll deploy measurable automation through two business-driven use cases: churn prevention from contact center data, and intelligent claims processing that eliminates manual back-office work. Leave with working skills, a governance framework for hundreds of agents across teams, and a playbook for communicating ROI to leadership.
BIZ314: Build multi-agent workflows with AWS Quick, MCP, and AgentCore
Thursday, Dec 3 | 8:30 AM PST
Speakers: Vishnu Elangovan, Josh Anderson
Design and build a multi-agent system inside AWS Quick where specialized agents collaborate to automate complex business processes. Connect to enterprise systems through MCP servers on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, implement inter-agent communication, configure OAuth 2.0 authentication, and deploy autonomous workflows using Quick Flows. Modeled after production deployments running 12+ coordinated agents across enterprise resource planning (ERP), finance, and procurement, you’ll leave with a working multi-agent solution you can replicate in your own environment.
BIZ402: Configure security and governance controls for AWS Quick
Thursday, Dec 3 | 12:00 PM PST
Speakers: Leo Mentis Raj Selvaraj, Marshall Bunch
Implement comprehensive security and administrative controls for AWS Quick. Practice configuring identity integration, access policies, and data governance frameworks. Learn to establish monitoring, auditing, and compliance controls that meet enterprise requirements. Work through scenarios covering user management, content governance, and security best practices for AWS Quick environments in production.
Builders’ sessions
Build alongside AWS experts in small-group, code-level sessions. Bring your laptop and be ready to build.
BIZ301: Build and ship an AI-powered app with AWS Quick
Monday, Nov 30 | 2:30 PM PST
Speakers: Roy Yung, Oyin Oguntoye, Mei Liu, Vaidy Janardhanam, Douglas Bergquist
In this hands-on builder session, you’ll use AWS Quick to design, iterate on, and publish a fully functional application through natural-language conversation. You’ll connect to a live data source (pre-provisioned through MCP), shape your app interactively with generative AI, persist state across users, and publish something your team or customers can use immediately. Whether you’re accelerating decision-making, automating operational workflows, or putting insights directly in the hands of end users, this session shows how Quick Apps collapses the gap between having an idea and shipping a solution. Bring your laptop and be ready to build.
BIZ302: Embed AWS Quick chat agents in enterprise applications

Speakers: Arun Santhosh, Sujit Singh, Anneline Sibanda, Manasi Karale, Ashok Dasineni
Deploy a fully serverless, production-ready solution that embeds AWS Quick agents and dashboards into your enterprise web applications. Using AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK), configure Amazon Cognito OAuth 2.0 authentication, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon CloudFront, and AWS WAF to create a secure embedding architecture. Implement the Quick Embedding SDK, configure domain security and token validation, and deploy a working chat agent accessible from any enterprise application, turning Quick into the conversational AI layer that meets users where they already work.

articles.title: Semperis updates Lightning identity security platform to defend against AI agent attacks - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Semperis updates Lightning identity security platform to defend against AI agent attacks
Enterprise identity protection and cyber resilience company Semperis Ltd. today released the latest version of its Semperis Lightning identity security platform, which is designed to help organizations defend against identity attacks by artificial intelligence agents and conventional attackers alike.
Delivered through a single console, the new version of Lightning is said to combine exposure management, attack-path analysis and detection-and-response workflows. Along with Microsoft Corp.’s Active Directory and Entra ID, the new release supports Okta Inc.
Semperis says organizations using Lightning can adopt AI tools for productivity while reducing the risk of agents compromising critical resources. According to Chief Executive Mickey Bresman, identity systems have become “the main control plane” in the agentic age.
Though AI agents move at machine speed through the enterprise, Bresman said, they still depend on the identity fabric for access. With Lightning, organizations are said to be able to create, enforce and monitor what he called “agentic execution boundaries.”
Chief Product Officer Alex Weinert, who joined Semperis in April 2025 after serving as vice president of identity security at Microsoft, said security teams “do not need another flat list of identity findings.” Context on what can actually reach the identity control plane is what they need instead, he said. Agentic identities, he added, are opening new routes to privileged systems.
On the exposure side, Lightning, which now comes with a growing catalog of more than 220 security indicators, continuously scans identity infrastructure for exposures in human and nonhuman identities. The results are then scored, according to Semperis, before being triaged in a single workflow.
The platform’s live identity graph, which Semperis describes as a map of relationships and attack paths, covers routes to domain administrators, privileged accounts and other critical assets. According to the company, remediation guidance from the graph is prioritized by risk so that teams can respond faster.
Nonhuman and agentic identities are discovered automatically, Semperis says, and added to a searchable inventory of every identity in an environment. The company claims Lightning can scale to the largest multitenant, multiforest environments.
Built-in rule templates are designed to detect suspicious activity in Active Directory and Entra ID, such as unusual logons over Kerberos and NT LAN Manager. The company is also offering what it calls generative assistance alongside the templates.
Semperis introduced Lightning in April 2024 with Lightning Identity Runtime Protection, a machine learning-powered identity threat detection service. The company extended its resilience offerings to Okta and Ping Identity Corp. environments in February, when it acquired MightyID Inc.
More than 1,200 organizations, including over 25% of the 100 largest U.S. companies, are said to use Semperis. The company last raised $125 million in growth financing from JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Hercules Capital Inc. in June 2024. Earlier investors include Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. LP, Insight Partners, Ten Eleven Ventures and Paladin Capital Group.

articles.title: En 2026, des gens ont encore ce mot de passe hallucinant
articles.text:
Il y a des traditions qui ne meurent jamais. La huitième édition de l’étude annuelle de NordPass, éditeur d’un gestionnaire de mots de passe (et filiale de Nord Security, la maison mère de NordVPN), recense les 200 mots de passe les plus courants dans 44 pays. Elle s’appuie sur des fuites de données publiques et des bases du dark web publiées entre septembre 2025 et septembre 2026. Le podium, lui, n’a pas bougé d’un pouce dans la médiocrité.
Le top 20 français, un musée des horreurs
En France, « 123456 » retrouve la première place, qu’il avait cédée l’an dernier à « admin ». Ce dernier se classe deuxième, devant « password », « 123456789 » et « 12345678 ». La suite du top 10 : « azerty », « 1234 », « Password », « azertyuiop » et « azerty123 ».
Le mot « mot de passe » occupe à lui seul quatre places, en français comme en anglais, avec ou sans majuscule. Les suites de chiffres en prennent sept autres. « Marseille13 » se hisse au 15e rang (le Vieux-Port a des supporters jusque dans les bases de données piratées), et « bebe2012 » au 11e (bébé qui doit avoir aujourd’hui 14 ans et un meilleur mot de passe que ses parents, on l’espère).
Rien de neuf sous le soleil : en 2023 déjà, Numerama jugeait que le top des pires mots de passe en France était un pur désastre. Et l’an dernier, la même étude montrait que les jeunes avaient de pires mots de passe que les boomers.
À l’échelle mondiale, « 123456 » reste numéro un, devant « admin » et « 12345678 ». Les caractères spéciaux progressent (39 mots de passe du top 200 mondial en contiennent, contre 32 l’an dernier), mais sous des formes aussi audacieuses que « Admin@123 » ou « P@ssw0rd ». Le classement compte même des identifiants par défaut de routeurs, comme « ALC#FGU » (116e) ou « adminHW » (118e) : beaucoup de box et d’objets connectés tournent encore avec leur réglage d’usine.
De « metallica » à « skibiditoilet »
Nouveauté de cette édition, NordPass s’est penché sur l’influence de la culture pop et son renouvellement avec le web social. Avant les années 2000, le rock et le cinéma dominent avec « metallica », « Slayer007 », « corleone13 » ou « Rambo017 ». Les années 2000 sont celles des anime et des jeux vidéo (« sasuke », « Bleach15 », « kingdomhearts3 ») et d’« eminem2004 ». Les années 2010 apportent « minecraft », « insta123 » et « neymar10 ». Les années 2020, enfin, ressemblent à un fil TikTok : « skibiditoilet », « squidgamethebest », « roblox.com1 », et la touche sombre de « Covid@19 ».
NordPass reconnaît qu’un « metallica » ne date pas forcément des années 1990 : il peut appartenir à un fan de la première heure comme à un ado converti par le retour du vinyle. Le problème reste le même. Un pirate n’a pas besoin de vous connaître, seulement de deviner ce que vous aimez. Et en bruteforce, même pas besoin de vous : selon l’étude, un nom de groupe accolé à une année de naissance se casse en moins d’une seconde.
« 123456 », une faille bien réelle
Ces classements prêtent à sourire, jusqu’au jour où ils coûtent cher. Mi-octobre, le Danemark a révélé le piratage de son registre central de la population (CPR) : noms, adresses et numéros d’identification d’environ 8,8 millions de personnes ont été aspirés. Selon le pirate, interrogé par le quotidien Politiken, tout est parti du compte d’un ancien employé de Pays ApS, une petite société ayant accès au registre. Au moins trois comptes de l’entreprise, dont un compte administrateur, utilisaient « 123456 ».
Les parades sont connues : une phrase de passe longue plutôt qu’un mot court bardé de symboles, au moins 14 caractères, un mot de passe différent par compte, l’authentification multifacteur partout où c’est possible et un gestionnaire de mots de passe pour s’en souvenir à votre place (oui, c’est justement ce que vend NordPass, voir notre comparateur).
Et si votre mot de passe figure dans cet article, vous savez ce qu’il vous reste à faire avant la fin de votre café.
Les meilleurs Gestionnaires de mots de passe
Proton Pass
- Génère des alias pour cacher son mail
- Même groupe que Proton VPN
1Password
- Le plus connu et l’un des plus vieux
- Interface riche, parfois dense pour les débutants
NordPass
- Appuyé par l’écosystème NordVPN
- Solution de chiffrement atypique

articles.title: La fibre optique cale à 150 km, Thales Alenia Space mise sur l'espace pour l'Internet quantique
articles.text:
Thales Alenia Space et ses partenaires ont lancé une nouvelle phase du projet TeQuantS, mené pour l'Agence spatiale européenne, avec au cœur du dispositif un laboratoire quantique au CNES, qui prépare le satellite QINSAT et l'Internet quantique européen.
Faire voyager de l'information quantique d'un continent à l'autre grâce à un satellite est le pari relevé par Thales Alenia Space avec le projet TeQuantS, qui nous fait avancer d'un cran vers un Internet quantique européen. La coentreprise du Français Thales (67 %) et de l'Italien Leonardo (33 %) a signé deux avenants avec l'Agence spatiale européenne, a-t-on appris le lundi 16 novembre. Elle entame une nouvelle phase de son projet, avec un laboratoire quantique au CNES, le Centre nationale d'études spatiales. Une source de photons « jumeaux », des systèmes de synchronisation entre ciel et sol et des détecteurs de lumière y seront testés en conditions simulées, autant de briques essentielles à la future liaison espace-Terre.
Comment le CNES prépare la liaison quantique entre l’espace et la Terre
Ici, il n'y a pas de fusée ni de compte à rebours pour l'instant. Ce fameux laboratoire doit simuler au sol les conditions réelles d'une liaison quantique entre un satellite et la Terre. Au menu des essais figurent une source de photons intriqués, des systèmes chargés de synchroniser le temps entre l'engin et le sol, ainsi que les outils qui analysent et détectent les photons à leur arrivée.
Des photons intriqués, d'ailleurs ? Ce sont des paires de grains de lumière produites ensemble, qui restent liées comme des jumeaux même une fois séparées. Mesurez l'un, et vous savez aussitôt ce que donnera la mesure de l'autre, qu'il se trouve dans la pièce voisine ou à des centaines de kilomètres. C'est ce lien invisible qu'un réseau quantique doit transporter d'un point à un autre. Avec un atout de taille pour la sécurité, puisque toute tentative d'espionnage perturbe ce lien et laisse des traces repérables, ce qui trahit l'intrus, explique Thales.
Ces essais préparent le terrain pour QINSAT, le satellite qui devra tester la transmission de photons intriqués entre l'espace et la Terre. L'enjeu, à terme, est de relier entre eux des réseaux quantiques terrestres disséminés sur plusieurs continents. Le Dr Kasia Balakier, responsable technique de TeQuantS et des technologies de communication optique et quantique au sein du programme ScyLight de l'ESA, évoque « une occasion unique » pour l'industrie française et européenne. Selon elle, les équipements et le banc d'essai installés au CNES représentent « une étape majeure vers le déploiement d'une connectivité quantique par satellites », autrement dit vers de véritables liaisons quantiques assurées depuis l'espace.
Internet quantique : pourquoi passer par l'espace, et pour qui ?
Alors pourquoi l'espace ? Parce que dans une fibre optique, l'information quantique ne peut être transmise directement que sur 150 kilomètres environ. C'est assez pour relier deux villes proches, mais bien trop peu pour enjamber un océan. D'où l'idée de confier le relais aux satellites. Le projet TeQuantS (pour Technological development for space-based Quantum reSource distribution, rien que ça), lancé en 2023 et soutenu par le CNES, relève du volet Industrial Competitiveness du programme ARTES de l'ESA (Agence spatiale européenne), consacré aux technologies de télécommunications par satellite. Ses premières phases ont déjà livré un prototype de station sol compacte et une première maquette du système.
Qui profitera de ce futur réseau ? Les ordinateurs quantiques, d'abord. Ils devront s'échanger des qubits photoniques, des unités d'information quantique portées par la lumière, pour répartir leurs calculs. Viennent ensuite les capteurs quantiques, qui gagneront en sensibilité en travaillant de concert. Alcino De Sousa, Senior Vice-Président des activités Télécommunications de Thales Alenia Space, évoque un projet qui « adresse à la fois les futurs enjeux de cyber sécurité et de réseau Internet quantique ». Enfin, les opérateurs gouvernementaux peuvent y voir un moyen de garantir des échanges sécurisés de bout en bout, résilients et souverains, c'est-à-dire robustes et maîtrisés par l’'Europe. Y compris face aux attaques des futurs ordinateurs quantiques, qui pourraient un jour venir à bout des chiffrements actuels.
Pour tenir ce cap, Thales Alenia Space, maître d'œuvre du projet, s'appuie sur un consortium aux expertises complémentaires. Airbus Defence and Space apporte les systèmes quantiques, AUREA Technology la source spatiale de photons intriqués et OGS Technologies les stations sol optiques. Bertin Alpao s'occupe de l'optique adaptative, Bertin Technologies de l'optomécanique et Sigmaworks de la synchronisation temporelle. Le LIP6 (Sorbonne Université) et l'INPHYNI (Université Côte d'Azur/CNRS) conseillent sur les protocoles et les systèmes quantiques.
Selon Alcino De Sousa, ces technologies contribueront « à la souveraineté européenne dans ce domaine ». Et ce n'est pas un coup d'essai, puisque l'industriel déroule sa feuille de route quantique depuis 2018, adossée à plus d'un quart de siècle d'expérience du groupe Thales en technologies quantiques. On y trouve QKD-GEO, présenté comme le premier système au monde de distribution quantique de clés depuis l'orbite géostationnaire, et SAGA, qui vise un système orbital européen de clés cryptographiques sécurisées par la physique quantique. S'y ajoute sa participation à EuroQCI, la future infrastructure européenne de communication quantique.

articles.title: Siri AI sur iPhone : on a testé l'assistant d'Apple que l'Europe attend encore (vidéo)
articles.text:
L’attente commence à de venir particulièrement longue pour les utilisateurs d’iPhone en Europe. Depuis le lancement des premières fonctions d’Apple Intelligence, l’accès à l’assistant entièrement revu reste bloqué chez nous en raison des règles du règlement sur les marchés numériques (DMA). Pour contourner cette limitation, l’équipe de Frandroid a configuré un iPhone avec un compte américain afin de mettre à l’épreuve ce Siri nouvelle génération.
Un assistant enfin capable de comprendre votre vie privée
À l’usage, la différence avec la version classique saute aux yeux. Ce Siri version 2026 ne se contente plus d’allumer vos ampoules connectées ou de lancer un minuteur ; il accède à vos messages, vos notes et vos courriels pour en tirer le contexte nécessaire. Lors de nos essais, l’assistant a réussi sans sourciller à retrouver des horaires de vol perdus dans une ancienne conversation ou à localiser une adresse de restaurant griffonnée à la hâte dans l’application Notes.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
L’enchaînement de requêtes complexes s’avère tout aussi convaincant. Demander une recette de cuisine tout en démarrant un minuteur, ou chercher des photos précises pour les envoyer par message s’exécute de manière fluide.
Tout n’est pas parfait pour autant, notamment lorsque l’assistant doit effectuer des recherches d’actualité sur le web, où il se montre parfois moins efficace que Google Gemini.
Pourquoi l’Europe est-elle privée de cette mise à jour ?
Le point de blocage entre Apple et la Commission européenne réside dans ce que la marque à la pomme appelle l’index sémantique. Ce composant stocke et chiffre localement toutes vos données personnelles pour permettre à l’assistant d’y accéder de manière sécurisée. L’Europe exige, au nom de la concurrence, que les intelligences artificielles rivales puissent accéder à ce même index pour proposer les mêmes services. Apple s’y refuse pour des raisons de confidentialité.
En attendant un éventuel accord, le nouveau Siri reste accessible en France sur Mac (non concerné par le DMA), mais nécessite un compte américain sur iPhone. Une manipulation compliquée que nous vous déconseillons de tenter, sous peine de perdre l’accès à vos applications bancaires et à votre catalogue local d’applications. Le potentiel est bien là, mais le feuilleton réglementaire est encore loin d’être terminé.

articles.title: Smart Locks für dein Zuhause: Mit diesen vernetzten Schlössern öffnest du deine Haustür per App
articles.text:
Nie mehr Schlüssel verlieren: Mit diesen Smart Locks öffnest du deine Haustür bequem per App
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Ein Smart Lock ist ein elektronisch gesteuertes Türschloss, das sich ohne klassischen Schlüssel öffnen oder schließen lässt – zum Beispiel per Smartphone, PIN oder Fingerabdruck. Du musst also keinen Schlüssel mehr mitnehmen. Ein Smart Lock ist auch eine praktische Lösung, wenn du Ferienwohnungen vermietest oder regelmäßig Gäste, Lieferant:innen oder Reinigungskräfte ein- und ausgehen lässt. Wir stellen dir drei Modelle aus verschiedenen Preiskategorien vor.
So funktionieren die smarten Türschlösser
Das Grundprinzip ist immer gleich, technische Unterschiede gibt es aber bei der Authentifizierung und bei der Entriegelung. Zunächst müssen Nutzer:innen am Smart Lock ihre Identität nachweisen. Das digitale Türschloss vergleicht daraufhin die übermittelten Zugangsdaten mit den gespeicherten Berechtigungen. Stimmen die Daten überein, gewährt es Zutritt.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Ein Elektromotor im Smart Lock betätigt den Schließmechanismus. Je nach Bauart dreht er entweder den gesteckten Schlüssel oder bewegt den Schließzylinder. Dafür benötigt es keinen Stromanschluss, sondern wird meist mit Batterien oder wiederaufladbaren Akkus im Gehäuse betrieben. Die Wahl des Funkstandards richtet sich nach dem Einsatzzweck, der Entfernung zum Schloss und der Einbindung in ein Smart-Home-System. Oft kombinieren Hersteller mehrere Standards in einem Gerät. Diese kommunizieren meist über Bluetooth, WLAN, NFC, Matter, Thread oder Zigbee.
Das Einsteigermodell: Nuki Smart Lock Go
Nuki gehört zu den führenden Anbietern von smarten Türschlössern. Das Smart Lock Go ist ein günstiges Einsteigermodell und lässt sich laut Hersteller innerhalb weniger Minuten installieren. Standardmäßig öffnet das Schloss lokal per Bluetooth: Es erkennt automatisch, wenn du dich in der Nähe befindest, und entriegelt die Tür. Zusätzlich bietet Nuki einen Remote-Access-Service für einmalig 49 Euro an, der über die App von überall aus Zugriff ermöglicht. Du kannst den digitalen Schlüssel mit anderen teilen und festlegen, wie lange die Freigabe gilt. Über den Smart-Home-Standard Matter lässt sich das Schloss außerdem mit Sprachassistenten wie Amazon Alexa oder Google Home verbinden.
Der integrierte Sensor zeigt den Türstatus als „offen”, „geschlossen” oder „verriegelt” an. Er sendet auch Warnungen – beispielsweise wenn die Tür länger als üblich offen bleibt. Das Schloss wird mit vier AA-Batterien betrieben. Alternativ bietet Nuki ein wiederaufladbares Powerpack gegen Aufpreis an. Käufer:innen schätzen die einfache Installation, kritisieren allerdings teilweise die Haltbarkeit, die Konnektivität und den geräuschintensiven Betrieb. Der reguläre Preis liegt bei Amazon bei 149,99 Euro. Im Rahmen einer Black-Friday-Aktion ist das Modell aktuell um 27 Prozent auf 109 Euro reduziert. Laut etablierten Preisvergleichsportalen war das smarte Schloss bisher nicht günstiger zu haben.
Loxeris One: Smartes Türschloss von Abus
Auch Abus bietet smarte Türschlösser an. Das Modell Loxeris One ermöglicht die komfortable Öffnung und Sperrung per App. Du kannst den Zugriff auf das Smart Lock mit anderen teilen und dauerhafte Berechtigungen zum Beispiel an Familie oder Freund:innen vergeben, während Gäste, Dienstleister:innen oder Handwerker:innen einen zeitlich begrenzten Zugang erhalten. Insgesamt kannst du bis zu 28 Personen registrieren. Per App lässt sich auch nachvollziehen, wer das Schloss wann nutzt. Mit der separat erhältlichen Bridge One steuerst du den Antrieb aus der Ferne und bindest ihn in dein Smarthome ein.
Kund:innen sind mit dem batteriebetriebenen Türschloss zufrieden und loben die gute Qualität, die zuverlässige Funktion und die einfache Installation. Für die Nutzung wird ein Schlüssel gekappt und verbleibt im Zylinder. Dieser verfügt zusätzlich über eine Notfunktion, die das Öffnen und Schließen per Schlüssel auch dann ermöglicht, wenn von innen ein Schlüssel steckt. Der reguläre Preis liegt bei 199,95 Euro. Bei Amazon ist das Modell aktuell um 39 Prozent auf 122,95 Euro reduziert. Zusätzlich erhältlich sind ein Fingerscanner, eine Zahlencodetastatur oder eine Fernbedienung.
Maximale Flexibilität mit der Smart Lock Ultra
Die Smart Lock Ultra von Switchbot bietet diverse Optionen, um das smarte Türschloss zu öffnen. Die Auto-Entsperrfunktion nutzt GPS und Bluetooth, um zu erkennen, ob du dich in der Nähe befindest. Auch die Bedienung per App ist möglich. Dort siehst du außerdem den aktuellen Status der Tür. Zum Lieferumfang gehört ein Touch-Keypad mit Zahlenfeld und Fingerabdrucksensor. Insgesamt sollen bis zu 18 unterschiedliche Entsperrungsoptionen möglich sein. Der Hauptakku hält laut Hersteller bis zu neun Monate. Zusätzlich ist das Modell mit einem Notfallakku ausgestattet. Während der Hauptakku lädt, übernimmt der Notfallakku, sodass sich die Smart Lock Ultra weiterhin normal entriegeln lässt.
Herstellerangaben zufolge arbeitet das Modell mit nur 20 Dezibel, was etwa dem Ticken einer Uhr entspricht. Es stehen drei Entriegelungsmodi zur Verfügung, wobei der schnellste die Tür in nur 1,75 Sekunden öffnen soll. Das Vollmetallgehäuse wird mit drei Blenden in verschiedenen Holzmaserungen geliefert, die zu verschiedenen Wohnstilen passen sollen. Kund:innen loben die schnelle Entsperrung und die unkomplizierte Einrichtung. Bei Amazon gilt das Modell als „Bestseller Nr. 1“ im Segment der Türriegelschlösser. Im Rahmen der aktuellen Black-Friday-Aktion ist die Smart Lock Ultra von Switchbot von 249,99 Euro auf 165,99 Euro reduziert. Die Ersparnis beträgt 34 Prozent.

articles.title: How AI could reshape jobs, investing, and wealth creation in India
articles.text:
How AI could reshape jobs, investing, and wealth creation in India
At TechSparks 2026, Angel One Group CEO Ambarish Kenghe discussed how AI could change the nature of work, make investing more accessible, and create opportunities in healthcare, transportation, fintech and beyond.
AI is changing how people work, how businesses build products, and how investors identify opportunities. As the technology becomes more accessible, the question is how more Indians can participate in the wealth it creates.
At TechSparks 2026, Ambarish Kenghe, Group CEO of Angel One, joined Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, for a fireside chat on investing in India’s AI decade. The conversation covered the future of jobs, AI’s role in making investing more accessible, and the sectors where new opportunities could emerge.
Will AI create more jobs than it replaces?
For Kenghe, the answer lies partly in how technology has changed economies in the past.
He pointed to Jevons paradox, named after British economist William Stanley Jevons, who observed that improvements in steam engine efficiency led to an increase in coal consumption rather than a decline. As engines became more efficient, their use expanded.
Kenghe believes AI could have a similar effect. Citing data from Anthropic, he noted that 57% of the work done with Claude involves augmentation, while 43% involves automation. As AI makes knowledge work more productive, demand for such work could increase in ways that are difficult to predict.
He cited banking as an example. When ATMs and computerized systems began replacing manual transactions at bank counters, it seemed likely that fewer employees would be needed. Instead, banking jobs increased as the industry expanded and new requirements emerged.
Kenghe believes AI could have a similar impact, allowing people to work on problems that have remained unresolved.
However, the transition will require workers to adapt.
“While the demand for knowledge work will go up a lot with AI, each of us will have to transform because it’s not that we will do the same kind of job. We can’t become more efficient tellers. We will have to get to a very different level of operation, and what we do will change. How it will change, only time will tell,” he said.
Making investing more accessible
The conversation then turned to how more Indians could participate in wealth creation.
Kenghe identified three challenges: access, information, and intelligence.
Access to investing has become considerably easier. People can now complete their KYC on their phones and start investing without the physical paperwork and complicated procedures that were once required.
However, access alone does not guarantee participation. Many people know about the stock market but lack the information or confidence to make investment decisions.
“The two other issues which are not fully solved are information and intelligence, and I think AI is solving it in a big way,” Kenghe said.
He cited Angel One’s Ask Angel, an AI-powered tool that allows users to ask questions and receive relevant information. The tool does not provide investment advice because of regulatory restrictions.
Kenghe also believes AI could help reduce some of the advantages institutional investors have over individual investors. Institutions typically have access to more capital, sophisticated technology, and specialized teams. While AI cannot eliminate these differences, it could make information and tools more widely available.
He compared this development to the evolution of computing. The computer used aboard the Apollo mission had far less computing power than modern devices. Today, smartphones offer computing capabilities that far exceed what was available during that mission.
He believes investing could undergo a similar change as AI tools become more accessible.
Citing a SEBI study, Kenghe said 63% of Indian households are aware of the stock market, but only 9.5% invest in it. Better access to information and intelligence could encourage more people to participate.
However, broader participation will not necessarily lead to equal wealth creation. AI could democratize access to investing without socialising wealth. Individual investors would still need to make decisions based on their available capital and appetite for risk.
Building products that solve real problems
Drawing on his experience building Google Pay, Kenghe discussed what it takes to create products that consumers want to use.
For him, the starting point is identifying a genuine problem and solving it well.
A product may be complex behind the scenes, but the experience should be simple for the user. In payments, for example, people want to transfer money quickly and reliably while knowing their transactions are secure.
Adding features serves little purpose if the basic experience does not work.
Kenghe said identifying the right problem is often the harder task. Founders can become distracted by new technologies and trends, but product development should begin with understanding what users need.
Where the next opportunities lie
When Sharma asked about untapped areas for innovation, Kenghe pointed to opportunities beyond building increasingly large AI models.
He cited Jev AI, a model focused on efficiency rather than competing directly on size, as an example of an alternative approach to AI development. He also mentioned Instinct as another example of companies approaching the technology differently.
Healthcare, he believes, offers considerable scope for specialized AI models.
“I don't see anybody coming out with a kick-ass, dedicated healthcare model. You could actually create models that are dedicated to certain diseases, certain areas,” he said.
Rather than approaching healthcare as a single, broad problem, Kenghe suggested developing models focused on specific diseases or areas of care.
He also identified transportation and logistics as sectors with significant opportunities. While self-driving technology is beginning to develop, he believes there is still considerable room for innovation, particularly in India, where traffic and logistics costs remain major challenges.
Other areas he is optimistic about include space exploration, with the long-term possibility of space-based data centres, and fintech.
Balancing ambition with data
For entrepreneurs, identifying an opportunity is only the beginning. They must also make decisions amid uncertainty.
Kenghe believes data should inform these decisions without determining every move.
It can help founders understand market conditions, assess risks, and make more rational choices. But data cannot provide every answer, particularly when entrepreneurs are building something new.
“Entrepreneurs are entrepreneurs because their emotion brings in the passion. Take the emotion out of it, perhaps the passion comes out as well,” he said.
Kenghe believes founders need to balance that passion with evidence. Regularly reviewing data can help them make informed decisions and remain grounded, while recognizing its limitations leaves room for instinct, conviction, and the risks involved in building a business.

articles.title: “Me parece genial que la gente experimente en casa”: Sam Altman defiende la compra de memoria RAM para PC
articles.text:
El CEO de OpenAI, Sam Altman, defendió la compra de memoria RAM para computadoras personales y sostuvo que las personas deberían poder adquirir grandes cantidades para experimentar en sus hogares, pese a que la escasez mundial y el avance de la inteligencia artificial (IA) elevaron los precios de estos componentes.
“Quiero ser claro: quiero que la gente tenga mucha RAM; creo que todos deberían poder comprar mucha RAM para su ordenador”, declaró durante la cumbre Silicon Valley & The World. “Me parece genial que la gente experimente en casa”.
Altman había generado controversia el mes pasado al afirmar, durante el podcast Cheeky Pint, que era “terrible” que todos tuvieran memoria RAM en sus computadoras en vez de concentrarla en centros de datos.
De dónde viene la escasez de memoria RAM a nivel global
Las empresas dedicadas a la inteligencia artificial han concentrado el suministro global de memoria para sus centros de datos, una dinámica que impulsó aumentos de precios en productos como teléfonos y consolas de videojuegos.
OpenAI, según explicó Altman, se ha visto limitada en distintos momentos por la memoria, el ensamblaje de racks, la capacidad de los centros de datos o algún componente imprevisto.
El déficit solo podría corregirse si la industria elevara su producción anual un 12% en 2026 y 2027, según Counterpoint Research. Los planes vigentes, sin embargo, permiten prever una expansión de apenas 7,5%, por debajo del ritmo necesario para equilibrar la oferta y la demanda.
La falta de abastecimiento podría agravarse: los principales fabricantes apenas estarían en condiciones de cubrir el 60% de la demanda global hacia finales de 2027, según estimaciones de Nikkei Asia. La insuficiencia se extendería durante varios años por el auge de la IA y el cambio de prioridades en la producción de chips.
De qué forma están enfocando los recursos los principales fabricantes de memoria
La raíz del problema está en la reorientación de la capacidad industrial. Samsung, SK Hynix y Micron, compañías que concentran cerca del 90% del mercado mundial, priorizan las memorias de alto rendimiento destinadas a centros de datos e inteligencia artificial, mientras la RAM convencional para dispositivos de consumo queda relegada.
Las nuevas plantas de fabricación tampoco podrán responder de inmediato a la escasez, porque tardarán años en alcanzar su funcionamiento pleno. Las inversiones actuales, por lo tanto, no se traducirán en una mejora rápida del suministro disponible para computadoras, teléfonos y consolas.
Ante este contexto, Altman reconoció que los precios de la DRAM, un tipo de memoria dinámica de acceso aleatorio, se dispararon en los últimos meses. “El mundo no se desarrolló tanto, y ahora hemos visto cómo los precios—no sé con exactitud, pero tal vez se multiplicaron por cinco o siete, algo así— se han disparado”, señaló.
El ejecutivo sostuvo que habría sido preferible construir una cadena de suministro de memoria “mucho más extensa”. Agregó que, ante un suministro limitado, compartir la capacidad disponible podría permitir que funcionara por completo en lugar de fallar ocasionalmente en los dispositivos de los usuarios.
A qué dispositivos afecta la crisis global de memoria RAM
La crisis ya impacta sobre los usuarios finales. Microsoft y Sony comunicaron aumentos en productos como las Surface y la PlayStation 5, mientras que Valve advirtió sobre posibles faltantes de la consola portátil Steam Deck en distintas regiones por la carencia de RAM.
Asimismo, el director ejecutivo de Dell, Michael Dell, anticipó que “todavía estamos en las primeras etapas” de la crisis y que no se avizora una pronta solución.
Queda esperar cómo avanza esta crisis a nivel global y si los fabricantes enfocaran sus productos a dispositivos de servicio y no solo a la infraestructura que soporta el avance de la IA.

articles.title: Gonzalo (29 años), instalador de placas solares y empresario: "Una instalación básica de 6 paneles cuesta unos 4.000 €"
articles.text:
Aunque instalar placas solares en tu casa parece una inversión difícil de asumir, sobre todo si nunca has pedido un presupuesto y no sabes cuánto tendrás que gastar, lo cierto es que el precio de una instalación básica es más asequible de lo que imaginas. Gonzalo, instalador de 29 años y socio de Efitar Ingeniería, explica que colocar 6 paneles solares en una vivienda cuesta entre 4.000 y 4.500 euros, y lo mejor es que esa cantidad incluye el inversor, el medidor de energía, los trámites de legalización y las licencias.
Como recoge El Español en su información sobre el coste de las placas solares, Gonzalo habló de estas cifras en una intervención en el podcast Sector Oficios en el que habló de cómo ha cambiado el autoconsumo en España. A su juicio, las viviendas unifamiliares y los chalets son las opciones más interesantes porque la electricidad se consume durante las horas de sol, y también señaló que las bonificaciones municipales del IBI y las deducciones del IRPF pueden ayudar a reducir la inversión siempre que se cumplan los requisitos.
Las placas solares producen más electricidad y las baterías también han cambiado
Gonzalo destaca que el rendimiento de los paneles ha cambiado mucho en los últimos años, ya que antes una placa de unos 2 metros cuadrados producía 200 W y ahora existen modelos que alcanzan 600 W con medidas similares. De esta forma, se pueden aprovechar mejor los tejados y abordar proyectos con más posibilidades, y pone como ejemplo cubiertas industriales con hasta 8.500 paneles y parques solares de 300 MW. Además, también recuerda que el coste alcanzó los 400 euros por MWh durante la crisis energética y esto llevó a algunos clientes a amortizar sus instalaciones con baterías en menos de 2 años (aunque, eso sí, matiza que son casos aislados).
A todo esto debemos sumar el interés por los sistemas de respaldo tras el apagón peninsular de abril de 2025. Gonzalo asegura que los equipos más sencillos parten de 150 euros más la mano de obra, mientras que otros sistemas integrados pueden costar entre 800 y 1.100 euros. También destaca la llegada de dispositivos con IA capaces de analizar los hábitos de consumo y gestionar cuándo comprar o vender electricidad a la red utilizando una batería. Eso no significa que cualquier casa con placas pueda seguir teniendo luz durante un apagón, ya que la instalación necesita estar preparada para funcionar sin suministro exterior.
Por último, el empresario también habló de las condiciones laborales de quienes trabajan instalando estos equipos. Y es que el crecimiento de la energía fotovoltaica no solo se nota en los tejados, también en la necesidad de contar con profesionales cualificados. Según explica Gonzalo, un oficial del sector cobra entre 23.000 y 24.000 euros al año, una referencia salarial que ofrece desde su experiencia en un oficio que exige conocimientos técnicos y trabajar habitualmente en altura.

articles.title: Zipline hires Uber executive to lead African expansion
articles.text:
Zipline has appointed Uber executive Anthony le Roux as its Head of Operations for Africa, effective January 2027, as the autonomous delivery company expands its distribution network through government partnerships across the continent.
le Roux, who has spent 13 years at Uber, will oversee a planned rollout of at least 20 distribution centres, known as “nests,” over two years.
His appointment comes as Zipline embarks on its biggest expansion in Africa. Executing that growth strategy will mean overcoming complex airspace approvals, unreliable off-grid power infrastructure, and sovereign payment risks while scaling its AI-powered medical delivery network across key markets, including Nigeria and Côte d’Ivoire.
le Roux told TechCabal that the company has signed agreements covering 10 centres in Côte d’Ivoire, with additional locations under negotiation. Le Roux declined to identify prospective markets before negotiations were concluded.
“What we’ve formally announced and have been formally agreed upon is 10 new nests as our distribution centres, and that’s in Côte d’Ivoire,” he said in an interview on Friday, November 13.
Zipline describes the nest distribution programme as its largest African buildout yet. The company projects that its expanded services will reach more than 130 million people, serve 20,000 health facilities and delivery sites, and support more than 800 jobs.
From Uber to aircraft
le Roux joined Uber in 2013 as general manager in Cape Town before moving to Warsaw to lead businesses across Eastern Europe. He later became regional general manager for the Middle East and Africa, based in Dubai.
In 2020, he helped build the high-capacity vehicle business that became Uber Group Transportation, an enterprise he led until his departure.
His move to Zipline follows several years working abroad, including five years based in Amsterdam. Earlier in his career, he worked in investment banking and spent a year living in Lagos.
le Roux acknowledged that aviation and fixed logistics infrastructure would present new challenges. However, he argued that building local teams, managing physical operations and navigating regulation were transferable skills.
“There’s an enormous operational component to every Uber business that you’re seeing on the ground,” he said.
Caitlin Burton, CEO of Zipline Africa and Emerging Markets, said le Roux’s operational experience would be important to delivering the expansion.
“He has a proven track record of scaling transformative technologies in Africa and beyond,” Burton said in a statement.
Zipline will prioritise markets combining meaningful population density, gaps in existing logistics infrastructure and supportive government partners, according to le Roux.
The planned network will initially focus on delivering medical supplies, including blood and essential medicines, embedding Zipline’s services within national healthcare systems. The company is already working with the Rwandan and Nigerian governments to integrate its drone delivery infrastructure into public health supply chains, partnerships that provide a foundation for its broader expansion across African markets.
“Without strong government support and backing, that’s just not going to be a feasible product to go and launch,” he said.
le Roux said Zipline could deploy the planned centres within two years, drawing on its existing African operating experience. Whether the total ultimately exceeds 20 will depend on what governments agree to commission.
For Côte d’Ivoire, he said the company already had an agreed rollout schedule. His responsibility would include delivering facilities on time, to specification and within agreed costs.
He did not provide detailed information about aviation approvals or ongoing regulatory discussions.
Healthcare first, diversification next
Medical deliveries will remain the backbone of Zipline’s African expansion, but the company is considering opportunities to carry other products once infrastructure is operational. Its broader offering already includes food, groceries and medicine.
le Roux also pointed to potential expansion in Rwanda using a different delivery system better suited to grocery-style services. However, he did not confirm a commercial rollout or provide a timeline.
Diversification, he said, is central to reducing Zipline’s dependence on government contracts. Making its delivery network integral to national healthcare systems could help sustain demand, while expanding into more countries would spread its market exposure. The company also plans to use its existing infrastructure to serve additional sectors and generate new revenue.
“Once we have the infrastructure to carry out medical and blood deliveries, we’ll obviously look at other opportunities to use that existing infrastructure to diversify revenue streams into other areas,” le Roux said. “That will help make the business model more robust and sustainable.”
But the commercial case remains untested in the details. Le Roux did not disclose delivery costs, revenue targets or the profitability thresholds needed to make the expanded model sustainable.
He added that he was recruiting three senior executives to lead deployment, service delivery and logistics, with a particular focus on talent from Africa or already operating on the continent.
According to him, local teams would handle most daily operations and pointed to Zipline’s engineering presence in Rwanda as evidence of its existing technical footprint.
“I’m looking very specifically for talent from the continent or on the continent because I want people who know how to operate across Africa,” le Roux said. “There’s such phenomenal talent that we’re speaking to as we’re going through this. I’m really excited. We’re going to get absolute world-class African operators to go and help us execute this.”

articles.title: WhatsApp lance son service de stockage sur Android
articles.text:
Vous n’avez officiellement plus besoin de Google Drive pour sauvegarder vos conversations WhatsApp sur Android. L’application de messagerie instantanée est en effet en train de déployer une nouvelle fonction de stockage sur ses propres serveurs pour les utilisateurs sous Android. WhatsApp propose gratuitement 2 Go d’espace pour sauvegarder vos conversations avec la possibilité d’étendre ce stockage moyennant un abonnement payant à Meta One.
WhatsApp veut sauvegarder vos conversations sur son propre Cloud
Cela fait maintenant plusieurs mois que WhatsApp planche sur une solution de stockage indépendante de Google. La messagerie, qui entend se passer de Google Drive sur Android et à terme d’iCloud chez les utilisateurs sous iOS, vient officiellement de commencer à déployer sa fonction de sauvegarde sur son propre cloud dans une récente bêta de son application chez les utilisateurs sous Android.
Les paramètres de sauvegarde de l’application ont ainsi été revus pour vous permettre de choisir entre l’Espace de stockage Google et le Stockage dans le cloud WhatsApp. Pour en profiter, il vous faudra néanmoins configurer une clé d’accès pour sécuriser votre sauvegarde.
Par défaut, WhatsApp propose gratuitement 2 Go d’espace de stockage. Pour aller au-delà, vous devrez donc impérativement passer à la caisse et souscrire à un abonnement WhatsApp Plus. Facturé 2,49 euros par mois, il vous donnera accès à 100 Go de stockage pour sauvegarder vos conversations. Vous profiterez également d’un certain nombre d’autres avantages, comme des stickers exclusifs, la possibilité de changer l’icône de l’application, de modifier le thème de celle-ci, d’obtenir des sonneries exclusives ou encore d’épingler un plus grand nombre de conversations.
Et si toutefois les 100 Go que propose l’offre WhatsApp Plus ne vous suffisent pas, vous pourrez aller au-delà en souscrivant à un abonnement Meta One grâce auquel il est possible d’étendre le stockage jusqu’à 4 To.
Une sauvegarde sécurisée et maintenue après l’abonnement
Quid de la sécurité de la sauvegarde de vos conversations sur le cloud de WhatsApp ? Pour sauvegarder vos conversations sur le cloud de WhatsApp, vous devez impérativement configurer une clé d’accès, la messagerie chiffrant obligatoirement toutes les sauvegardes de conversations, sans possibilité de désactivation de cette sécurité.
Par ailleurs, les conversations stockées chez WhatsApp restent protégées même après la fin de votre abonnement. La messagerie donne en effet un délai de 4 mois, après l’expiration de votre abonnement avant de supprimer votre sauvegarde. Passé ce délai, la sauvegarde des conversations est définitivement supprimée des serveurs de WhatsApp.
Cette nouvelle option de sauvegarde, intégrée à partir de la version 2.26.46.4 de WhatsApp Bêta, est en cours de déploiement et arrivera progressivement chez les bêta-testeurs. Il faudra sans doute patienter encore quelques semaines pour en profiter dans la version stable de l’application, WhatsApp n’ayant pour l’heure donné aucune date de déploiement à grande échelle de cette nouveauté.

articles.title: Ars Live: What do drone strikes on data centers mean for the future? Talk at 1 pm EST today
articles.text:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

articles.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors.
Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022.
Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April.
Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML says it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results.

Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta terça-feira (17/11).
Apagão mundial nesta terça-feira? Entenda a teoria que começou com os Simpsons
Uma teoria viralizada nas redes sociais aponta que a série Os Simpsons teria previsto um apagão mundial para 17 de novembro. A especulação ganhou força após internautas ligarem um episódio exibido em 2023 — no qual Lisa cita um blecaute nessa data em 2060 — a um teste nacional de emergência agendado pelos Estados Unidos para o mesmo dia.
El Niño pode desencadear crise mundial muito além do clima
Pesquisadores alertam que o super El Niño previsto para 2026 e 2027 pode provocar impactos muito além de eventos meteorológicos extremos, ameaçando diretamente a segurança alimentar e a saúde pública global. Diante do risco de crises de abastecimento combinadas a surtos de doenças, cientistas defendem que governos e entidades internacionais adotem respostas coordenadas para conter as consequências humanitárias.
Falta pouco! Espaçonave da NASA chega a um dia-luz de distância da Terra esta semana
Lançada pela NASA em 1977, a sonda Voyager 1 atinge nesta semana um marco inédito na exploração espacial ao alcançar a distância de um dia-luz da Terra. O feito histórico coloca o objeto construído pela humanidade a cerca de 25,9 bilhões de quilômetros de distância, percurso equivalente ao trajeto que a luz faz no vácuo ao longo de 24 horas.
Nvidia cria comitê de segurança nacional após saída do CEO Jensen Huang
A Nvidia anunciou nesta terça-feira (17) a criação de um comitê interno no conselho de administração para fiscalizar políticas de segurança nacional, controles de exportação e riscos comerciais globais.
