articles.title: Can AI Agents Really Shift Chip Design Left?
articles.text:
Agentic AI promises to automate more of the chip flow, but integration with EDA tools and capturing decades of engineering expertise are non-trivial.
Experts at the Table: AI agents are moving into more parts of the chip design flow, but connecting them across different tools and processes remains a challenge. Questions also remain about how to capture decades of engineering expertise, protect proprietary design data, and keep costs manageable. Semiconductor Engineering sat down to discuss these issues with Frank Schirrmeister, executive director of strategy programs and system solutions at Synopsys; Ronen Laviv, vice president of business development and strategic partnerships at Hiveware; Jack Berg, vice president of business development at Silvaco; Ashish Darbari, founder and CEO of Axiomise. What follows are excerpts of that conversation. To view part one of this discussion, click here. Part two is here.
L-R: Silvaco’s Berg; Synopsys’ Schirrmeister; Axiomise’s Darbari; Hiveware’s Laviv.
SE: If AI agents are modifying code, and you keep updating AI models and agents, how much can you really shift left?
Darbari: This is going to be a new methodology direction the industry will be taking, much like UVM, where you combine these different flows together. How do you combine all the agents together? I don’t get a sense that anybody really knows today how this combination is going to work. From what I have seen in different presentations, they’re still looking at how these things unfold. A lot of agentic AI companies lack the field experience of having seen these problems firsthand, so what they’re building is not what the consumer wants. In many cases, the big consumers are building their own stuff because they know what they want. They have the field experience. They have data from many years. So where will the big EDA vendors go to streamline this, and how that will shape the end use? I don’t know.
Laviv: One of the challenges with emulation is that when running in co-simulation mode, the simulation is slowing down. Maybe, instead of having UVM or other languages that slow it down, AI will get its own language and get SystemVerilog RTL synthesizable code that you can put in the machine. Then you’ll need less of the software, and you can run faster in emulation. I’m not sure yet if the methodology would change quickly, but UVM might not stay forever.
Darbari: That’s what Nvidia’s head of GPU said at DVCon U.S., isn’t it? The formal is replacing simulation, or is going to replace simulation. I’m less interested in how each of these individual technologies work with each other, but I’m very interested in whether all of this adoption will lead to a coherent story.
Schirrmeister: You have lifecycle, manufacturing, digital implementation, functional verification, and you have specification engineering. Making sense of it is the light bulb — making sure it works, getting it to layout, getting it into the actual physical silicon and 3D, and then observing it during the lifecycle. Each of these flows has many sub-components. Functional verification to emulation is like one of the five. There is virtual prototyping, formal, simulation, emulation, prototyping. Everybody gets their own agent. So you have an agent doing something localized. Now you start getting an agent that orchestrates these things together as a functional thing, and then you get an agent that connects to the front end. This is an onion of agents, with more and more layers on top. EDA vendors are all saying we have Level 5 stuff, and there’s truth to that within the scope of the operating domain.
Berg: This is very much about hierarchy.
Darbari: But who’s going to pay for all this? Do the small companies have the budget to tokenize their banks and run all of this?
Schirrmeister: Do you mean the guys building the product, or the guys building the tools?
Darbari: The ones running the product. These are the consumers. They would need to pay for the tokens. I have a feeling that only the big companies will be able to afford this. They’ve been running it full-on, saying they haven’t written any code. All of this is agents. But it would get very interesting if the cost of doing all of this could be significantly reduced.
Schirrmeister: What’s exciting about this is that all the smaller designs that used to be difficult because you had to go through all of this will benefit. If you want to be an Nvidia competitor, you still cannot do this out of your garage. That still has to be a big company.
Berg: You’ve got levels of agents at this point, and a Level 5 orchestrating the whole thing. The industry is going to work on building each of these, and then iterating and improving them. That’s the only way in which you’re going to get agents to learn and replace large groups of engineers doing the grunt work that’s necessary here.
SE: But that hierarchy needs to start with whatever shifts left to include to each one of these different blocks, right? You need to at least define, in general, what you’re going to be doing.
Berg: You’re going to have information being fed back to ensure that when they go to specification of functional that there are constraints place here. That way you can improve the probability of manufacturability.
Schirrmeister: Can I have an agent model and predict that path?
Berg: Yes, you can.
Schirrmeister: But you want to check, right? You need to make sure early on what the multi-physics effects of what you’re doing will be.
Berg: Yes, and without that it will be dead on arrival in manufacturing.
Schirrmeister: So now the question becomes, ‘How much can you really abstract?’
Laviv: AI is doing a great job on, say, 80% of the challenges. But then you have experience from individuals who have been in the industry for 30 years with unique skills that AI doesn’t have. We had a discussion where we talked about 250 different skills for power and emulation and format and verification. AI doesn’t have those skills today. The industry needs to figure out how to gather those skills in order to really get to a flow where an agent can talk to an agent and has all decades of experience that is hidden in Apple and Qualcomm and Intel.
Berg: It took 50 years, but in 2024 the Novel Prize in chemistry was given in part to a software called AlphaFold, which predicted with uncanny certainty how proteins fold. Proteins are much more complicated than the crystalline structures that we deal with on a daily basis. But it took 50 years to get there. That said, it’s a proof of concept. Whether or not you believe it can be done in semiconductors, it’s going to happen.
Laviv: The difference is that with proteins, everything is open.
Schirrmeister: Yes. Where does the data come from? Simon Davidmann (currently a professor at the University of Southampton) framed it as, ‘We have the big three. They have the base tools, and they build agent stacks on it. That’s why you have a chip stack, or super stack, or whatever.’ We are doing the same thing at Synopsys, and we’ll see who has the best traditional EDA. People who know AI well found EDA. But they need to learn EDA first, rather than the other way around, and they don’t have access to the data they need. The users have access to the data. Samsung talked about optimizing quality of service for a network-on-chip. They had a fast classic engine, an SoC simulator, an emulator, and they built their own LLM to feed all the data in there. That’s their company data, and it’s not going out to anybody. That’s why they’re doing it themselves. Cognichip said you need LLMs that are trained with real chip designs and people, which is why they hired chip designers and build chips.
SE: They’re also using that intelligence for the LLMs rather than the agents, right?
Schirrmeister: Exactly. And that’s the balance you need.
Leave a Reply

articles.title: Botswanan startup SocialLight brings local depth to Southern African media monitoring - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Botswana-based startup SocialLight is helping organisations keep track of what is being said about them across Southern Africa, with a focus on the print and radio coverage that international monitoring platforms tend to miss.
Founded in 2014 by Tony Mautsu, SocialLight tracks coverage of organisations, their competitors and their industries across print, radio, TV, online news and social media, turning it into alerts, reports and analysis for decision-makers. Its platform monitors more than 1,300 print publications and over 158 broadcast stations across the region, alongside online and social channels.
“Clients choose the keywords that matter to them, such as their brand, executives, competitors or regulatory issues. Every morning they receive alerts and regular reports showing where they were mentioned, what the tone was, and what it means for them,” Mautsu told Disrupt Africa.
“We have integrated AI into the platform so we can process large volumes of coverage quickly. Our in-market analysts then add the local context that software alone misses. The simplest way to put it – you find out first, while it is still a decision and not a crisis.”
The business has unusual origins. In 2012 and 2013, Mautsu volunteered at the Diacore marathon in Gaborone.
“My actual job was managing the toilets and the environment. I saw an opportunity to add more value and prove my worth, so I offered to run the event’s social media,” he said. “That experience became SocialLight, which I registered in 2014.”
The company started out as a social media management agency, and its appetite for bringing new technology into the local market took it into livestreaming and even holograms. The turning point came in 2018, when Mautsu took his first flight to a conference in South Africa.
“Honestly, I was scared of South Africa at the time. At that conference I was introduced to media monitoring. I immediately saw how much it was needed back home, so I built partnerships to bring it into the Botswana market,” he said.
Media monitoring has since become SocialLight’s core business. The startup went through the Botswana Innovation Hub’s First Steps Venture programme, and Mautsu was named on the Forbes 30 Under 30 Africa list in 2020. This year, he was recognised among the Top 10 Men in PR in Botswana. SocialLight saw a gap left by the international providers that dominated the market.
“Most media monitoring providers serving our market were international, and they did not fully understand the landscape. They assumed everyone was online. In Botswana and much of the region that is not true,” Mautsu said. “Power cuts, high data costs and patchy connectivity mean traditional media is still dominant.”
The team tested that belief on the ground, spending time at taxi ranks and other public spots to watch how people consumed news.
“I once took a bus from Gaborone to Lusaka, and for most of that journey people were not on their phones. They were listening to the radio and reading newspapers,” he said. “If you only monitor online and social media in this region, you miss a huge part of the conversation that shapes reputations.”
Mautsu said SocialLight’s edge over international platforms is the depth of its local coverage, especially print and radio, combined with in-market analysts who understand the languages, the politics and the context. “We are globally African and locally unmatched,” he said.
B2B uptake in Botswana has been strong, with SocialLight working with major brands in mining and banking, as well as regulators. It has also served multinational brands monitoring their presence in the region.
“These are sectors where reputation and early warning are critical,” Mautsu said.
The startup is now opening up its platform so organisations can sign up and use it online, with prospective clients able to request a free media assessment and a 14-day trial. It is also building strategic partnerships with PR agencies and other monitoring companies across SADC, some of which use SocialLight’s coverage to strengthen their own offerings.
SocialLight monitors media across most of SADC and currently has clients in Botswana, South Africa and Zambia. It plans to grow in Lesotho, Eswatini, Namibia and Malawi through strategic partners, and to enter Kenya and Nigeria within the next year, also via partnerships.
“Our model is to partner with established local agencies rather than build offices everywhere. They bring the relationships, and we bring the coverage and the technology,” Mautsu said.
The company makes most of its money from subscription retainers for media monitoring, priced mainly on the number of keywords a client tracks and the media types they need, with broadcast monitoring offered as an additional service. It also earns from custom reports and analysis, revenue-share arrangements with partner agencies that resell its platform, and its social media management services. It has been bootstrapped from day one.
“The business has funded its own growth since 2014, through retainer clients in banking, mining and the regulatory space, without outside investment,” Mautsu said. “I believe in starting where you are with what you have, and that is what we did.”
He said the biggest challenge has been finding the right in-country partners.
“They need to share our standards and see media monitoring as a long-term business, not a side offering. Finding that partner in each country takes time, and we have learned to be patient rather than rush into a market with the wrong one,” he said.
The cost of running the platform is another hurdle, with monitoring across multiple countries requiring constant spending on servers, data processing, digitising traditional media and AI tools.
“As a bootstrapped company, we carry all of that ourselves. That forces discipline, and it is why we have built much of our technology in-house rather than relying on expensive third-party tools,” Mautsu said. “Access to capital for SMEs in Botswana is difficult, so every stage of growth has had to pay for itself.”

articles.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
articles.text:
A Lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform allowed researchers to take control of Kokoro, a text-to-speech model used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Amazon Web Services.
An attacker hijacking the account could use it as a distribution channel in supply-chain attacks, potentially leading to data theft or code execution.
However, the researchers demonstrated a stealthier attack: they modified the model's weights so it produced audio that differed from the input text, without changing the underlying application code.
Because only the weights change, there is no malicious code or signature for malware scanners to detect, the researchers say.
"We changed what this model says by fine-tuning its neural weights. Same input text. Same voice file. Same configuration. Same inference code — not a single line touched in the application that runs it," said security researcher Alon Hertz.
Kokoro is an open-weight model that converts text into speech. It supports multiple languages and has more than 50 voice presets.
Although its developer, Hexgrad, has not pushed an update since April 2025, the project continues to be popular, with nearly 13 million monthly downloads on Hugging Face. The GitHub repository and the Python package on PyPI also went silent around the same time.
Kokoro is supported by developer tools from Google, NVIDIA, and Intel, including software for voice agents and on-device speech synthesis. AMD and Amazon Web Services have also published guides demonstrating its use in AI-agent workflows.
Hertz and his team took control of the Kokoro account on Hugging Face by simply registering the domain used by the original owner and resetting the login password.
Over the past weekend, the researchers registered the “hexgrad.com” domain listed on Kokoro’s public DONATE.md file and used it to perform a password reset on the publisher’s account.
They then ran a controlled test in which they modified Kokoro’s model weights in 87 seconds using a gaming GPU, causing the model to produce poisoned output.
Hertz says the team tested the modified Kokoro model locally using its normal inference pipeline, but never uploaded the modified weights to Hugging Face, as that would likely put at risk many production systems depending on the model.
The researcher underlines that an update would still carry all the hallmarks of a legitimate release, as tests from another account showed that Hugging Face would not flag anything as suspicious.
Despite the takeover, the publisher appeared the same, just like the file delivery route, the format, and the architecture. File sizes would be similar, and the release would contain no malware.
A broader trust problem
The researcher notes that the supply-chain risk from compromised publisher accounts distributing altered weights via routine updates to systems that automatically fetch new revisions is significant.
Kokoro was just a high-profile example the team used to highlight the issue.
Hertz says even non-hijacked accounts could pose a risk, as anyone can curate an ostensibly legitimate image for a period of time, then push a malicious update at some point.
“Hugging Face does not vet publishers. It doesn’t verify whether an account is still held by its original, legitimate owner — or by whoever quietly took it over last week. It doesn’t vet the models or datasets those accounts upload,” Hertz says.
“The same unvetted weights and datasets flow through mirrors and converted versions, GitHub releases, package registries, deployment guides, and direct downloads across the entire open-model ecosystem,” added the researcher.
Hertz reported the issue to Hugging Face, hoping for quick action, but received no response.
BleepingComputer has also contacted Hugging Face for comments, but we have not received a response yet.

articles.title: L’immense marche en avant de la Chine : après Mars, elle veut se poser sur Callisto, une lune de Jupiter
articles.text:
Aucun engin spatial ne s’est posé sur l’une des nombreuses lunes de Jupiter. Mais la Chine entend bien devenir la première à réussir cet exploit. Cap sur la mission Tianwen-4.
Depuis 2021, le programme Tianwen contribue à placer la Chine à l’avant-garde de la conquête spatiale. À commencer par Tianwen-1, qui a placé un orbiteur autour de Mars et posé le rover Zhurong sur la planète rouge dès sa première tentative. Lancée en 2025, Tianwen-2 a atteint en juillet dernier l’astéroïde Kamoʻoalewa, d’où elle doit rapporter des échantillons fin 2027.
Pékin prépare déjà la suite avec Tianwen-3, qui doit repartir vers Mars à la fin de 2028. Cette fois, il s’agira de ramener sur Terre au moins 500 grammes de roche pour y débusquer quête de traces de vie passée. Une prouesse qu’elle pourrait accomplir avec les États-Unis. Mais l’Empire du Milieu n’est pas rassasié et vise encore plus loin.
La Chine accélère
Dans les tuyaux depuis 2022, Tianwen-4 entre enfin dans une phase concrète avec un appel à propositions formulé par l’agence spatiale chinoise (CNSA), rapporte Space News. Celui-ci invite des équipes de recherche, chinoises comme étrangères, à proposer des instruments scientifiques qui viendraient compléter les douze dispositifs déjà prévus.
La mission transportera deux vaisseaux. Un orbiteur d’abord, qui survolera plusieurs lunes de Jupiter avant de se placer autour de Callisto, puis un atterrisseur qui viendra se poser à la surface de la lune. Au programme : l’étude de la plus grande planète du Système solaire, notamment de son champ magnétique, des particules qui l’entourent et de ses aurores.
Concernant Callisto, des caméras ainsi qu’un altimètre laser doivent cartographier son relief. De même, des spectromètres se chargeront d’analyser la composition de sa surface. L’atterrisseur, lui, embarquera un instrument doté d’un laser pour identifier les matériaux au sol, en plus d’un magnétomètre. Associé aux mesures de l’orbiteur, ce dernier doit aider à savoir si un océan d’eau salée se cache sous la croûte de glace.
La lune galiléenne la plus éloignée de Jupiter
Le choix de Callisto pour Tianwen-4 n’a évidemment rien d’un hasard. Plus éloignée de Jupiter que les autres lunes galiléennes, Io, Europe ou Ganymède, elle reste en grande partie à l’écart des puissantes ceintures de radiations de la planète qui mettent l’électronique à rude épreuve. C’est, en outre, celle qui exige le moins de carburant pour freiner, se mettre en orbite et se poser. Enfin, sa surface, l’une des plus anciennes et des plus criblées de cratères du Système solaire, conserve une archive intacte de l’histoire géologique de la région.
Si aucune date fixe n’a pour l’instant été fixée, le lancement devrait avoir lieu aux alentours de 2030 à bord d’une fusée Longue Marche 5. La sonde enchaînera ensuite des survols de Vénus et de la Terre pour gagner en vitesse sans épuiser son carburant. Elle devrait atteindre le système jovien en 2035, avant de se placer en orbite autour de Callisto, à environ 300 kilomètres d’altitude, vers 2038.
Pour rappel, la sonde américaine Juno s’y promène depuis 2016. Elle sera rejointe par l’européenne JUICE en 2031, quelque temps après Europa Clipper de la NASA, déjà en route et consacrée à Europe. Mais aucune de ces missions ne prévoit de se poser. Si Tianwen-4 y parvient, la Chine signerait le premier atterrissage de l’histoire sur une lune de Jupiter.
Une mission de retour d’échantillons doit non seulement collecter de la matière sur un corps céleste, mais aussi la conditionner, la faire décoller, puis la ramener sur Terre pour une rentrée atmosphérique contrôlée. Cela implique généralement plusieurs véhicules (atterrisseur, module d’ascension, orbiteur) et des opérations de rendez-vous et d’amarrage automatisés en espace lointain. Les contraintes de masse et d’énergie sont plus strictes, car chaque gramme ramené coûte cher en propulsion. La protection planétaire complique aussi le design : il faut éviter de contaminer l’échantillon et, inversement, limiter tout risque biologique lors du retour. Enfin, la chaîne de responsabilité est longue : chaque étape est un point de défaillance potentiel.
Un appel à propositions sert à sélectionner des instruments capables de répondre à des objectifs scientifiques précis, tout en respectant des contraintes d’ingénierie (masse, consommation électrique, volume, résistance aux radiations). Les équipes candidates doivent détailler les performances attendues (résolution, sensibilité, cadence de mesure), mais aussi les besoins opérationnels (température, pointage, débit de données). Ce processus permet aussi de définir l’architecture de la charge utile : quels capteurs travaillent ensemble et comment leurs données se complètent. Ouvrir l’appel à des équipes étrangères peut accélérer la maturité technologique et diversifier les expertises, mais suppose des règles claires sur l’export, la propriété intellectuelle et le partage des données. À la fin, l’agence spatiale arbitre entre ambition scientifique et faisabilité industrielle.
Le système jovien baigne dans des ceintures de radiations intenses alimentées par le champ magnétique de Jupiter, ce qui peut endommager l’électronique et dégrader les capteurs si la conception n’est pas fortement durcie. La distance à la Terre impose des communications à faible débit relatif et avec un délai de plusieurs dizaines de minutes, ce qui limite le pilotage en temps réel et exige beaucoup d’autonomie à bord. Les conditions locales sont difficiles : températures très basses, faible lumière solaire et, selon la lune visée, surface glacée potentiellement instable pour l’atterrissage. La navigation et l’atterrissage demandent des capteurs précis (altimétrie, imagerie) et des algorithmes capables d’éviter les zones à risque. Enfin, les contraintes énergétiques poussent souvent à utiliser des générateurs nucléaires ou des batteries dimensionnées pour des phases critiques, car les panneaux solaires deviennent moins efficaces aussi loin du Soleil.

articles.title: Sortie de GTA 6 : suivez toutes les infos en direct — Frandroid
articles.text:
GTA 6 sort dans la nuit du 18 au 19 novembre en France. Après des années d’attente, le jeu est déjà un phénomène culturel hors du commun qui attire tous les regards. Suivez donc en direct cet événement avec les dernières informations.
Grand Theft Auto VI sort sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Il sera aussi jouable sur Xbox One dès sa sortie, mais pas sur PS4. Rappel des prix officiels :
- édition standard à 79,99 € ;
- édition Ultimate (exclusivement numérique) à 99,99 €.
    À lire aussi : 
GTA 6 : où le précommander, date de livraison, consoles, version PC, date de sortie – tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Les dernières infos sur GTA 6
Les réglages à faire sur votre PS5 pour préparer GTA 6
Pour bien préparer vos parties de GTA 6, nous avons publié un dossier détaillant quelques astuces pratiques pour le stockage et les réglages vidéo ainsi que les ajustements graphiques de la PS5 Pro.
GTA 6 déjà nommé aux Game Awards
GTA 6 a déjà huit nominations aux Game Awards dont celui de jeu de l’année, sans être encore sorti. Cela s’explique par le fait que, parmi les votants, il y a des professionnels qui ont pu déjà testé GTA 6 sous embargo.
Cependant, on ne sait pas combien de ces jurés ont vraiment pu jouer à GTA 6 cependant. toutefois combien de jurés ont vraiment eu GTA 6 entre les mains. Les premiers tests du jeu de Rockstar sont attendus ce mercredi 18 novembre, mais le studio n’a rien confirmé à ce sujet.
À la sortie de GTA 5, Frandroid était encore FrAndroid
13 ans se sont écoulés entre les sorties de GTA 5 et GTA 6. C’est long, très long. Assez long pour qu’on se rende compte des grosses évolutions qui ont marqué notre site. À l’époque, la ligne édito de FrAndroid était plus restreinte et axée sur l’écosystème Android. Et notre site était très vert.
C’est en 2019 que nous avons officiellement élargi notre couverture à plus de produits et d’univers, même si cette ouverture avait, dans les faits, commencé depuis quelques temps déjà. FrAndroid est alors devenu Frandroid avec le relooking que vous pouvez admirer en consultant désormais notre site.
GTA 6 : un outil pour apprendre à parler anglais
Privé de doublage en français (comme tous les GTA), GTA 6 serait un outil efficace (mais incomplet) pour apprendre à parler anglais si l’on en croit un communiqué publié par Babbel (une application pour apprendre à parler une nouvelle langue).
L’astuce pour jouer à GTA 6 dès mercredi midi (sur Xbox)
Les joueurs Xbox n’auront pas à attendre minuit. Il suffit de régler sa Xbox Series S ou X sur la Nouvelle-Zélande pour lancer GTA 6 dès ce mercredi 18 novembre à midi, avec douze heures d’avance sur la France.
Sur PS5, en revanche, l’astuce ne fonctionne pas : il faudrait un compte PlayStation Network néo-zélandais.
Les dernières captures officielles de GTA 6
Rockstar a encore dévoilé six nouvelles captures officielles de récemment.
Le but étant ici de montrer la météo dynamique de GTA 6 sous forme de bulletins météo à Leonida, l’État fictif inspiré de la Floride.
Rockstar avait déjà publié une flopée de captures officielles avant cela. Début novembre, on avait encore droit à 39 nouvelles images montrant l’atmosphère qui règne dans la ville de Vice City et dans l’État de Leonida.
Licenciements chez Take-Two
À deux jours de la sortie de GTA 6, son éditeur et maison mère de Rockstar Games, Take-Two, taille dans ses effectifs. Ce mardi 17 novembre, le groupe a supprimé une soixantaine de postes chez Firaxis Games, le studio derrière Civilization et XCOM, soit un tiers de ses équipes.
Malgré le phénomène GTA 6, le secteur du jeu vidéo reste en crise.
Ce qu’il faut savoir sur le « gel réseau » d’Orange pour la sortie de GTA 6
Une capture d’écran partagée sur Reddit sous le titre « Panique chez Orange France » évoque un « gel réseau » les 18 et 19 novembre, pile pour la sortie du jeu. Il n’y a pourtant aucune raison de s’inquiéter, au contraire. Dans le jargon des opérateurs, un gel réseau ne veut pas dire que la fibre ou le mobile seront coupés. Il signifie que toutes les interventions techniques non urgentes sont suspendues, et que seules les réparations urgentes sont maintenues. Le but est de réduire le risque de panne nationale au moment où un pic de trafic est attendu, avec des millions de joueurs qui lancent le jeu et ses 212 Go à télécharger.
La mesure n’a rien d’exceptionnel : Orange l’avait déjà appliquée fin septembre pour la visite du pape Léon XIV en France, et les opérateurs y recourent aussi pour les grandes compétitions sportives ou le Black Friday. En revanche, cela ne protège pas d’une panne côté plateformes : si les serveurs de Rockstar, Sony ou Microsoft flanchent, comme ceux de Netflix lors de l’aperçu de GTA 6, l’opérateur n’y pourra rien.
Mise à jour importante à faire sur PS5
Sony vient de déployer en urgence la version 26.07-14.23.00 du logiciel système de la PS5 et de la PS5 Pro, et elle est indispensable pour lancer GTA 6. Le compte X du support PlayStation invite les joueurs à l’installer avant minuit le 19 novembre pour pouvoir jouer dès la sortie. Pour la faire : Paramètres > Système > Logiciel système > Paramètres et mise à jour du logiciel système. Si la console affiche « À jour », il n’y a rien à faire.
Sur le papier, ce correctif se contente de combler quelques failles. Il fait toutefois suite au piratage de la version précédente du micrologiciel, qui aurait pu permettre à des pirates de récupérer les fichiers d’installation de GTA 6. Ces fichiers sont très convoités à l’heure où l’IA permet de décompiler des jeux à toute vitesse.
GTA 6 arrive à grands pas
Préparez-vous, GTA 6 sort cette nuit (entre le 18 et le 19 novembre) en France !
GTA 6 : l’essentiel à retenir
- Sortie : dans la nuit du mercredi 18 au jeudi 19 novembre, à minuit en France. C’est un lancement pays par pays, à minuit heure locale, et la Nouvelle-Zélande ouvre le bal.
- Histoire : Jason Duval et Lucia Caminos, un couple de braqueurs, dans l’État de Leonida et à Vice City, inspirés de la Floride. Lucia est la première héroïne jouable de la série.
- Jouer en avance sur Xbox : en réglant la console sur la Nouvelle-Zélande, on peut jouer dès ce mercredi 18 novembre à midi. Le jeu doit être entièrement préchargé.
- Mise à jour obligatoire sur PS5 : Sony déploie, en urgence, une mise à jour indispensable à installer sur ses PS5 pour pouvoir jouer à GTA 6.
- Consoles : PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Jouable aussi sur Xbox One dès la sortie, mais pas sur PS4. Pas de version Switch 2.
- PC : pas de version au lancement. Rockstar n’a rien annoncé, mais une version PC pourrait arriver début 2027.
- Préchargement : ouvert depuis le 10 novembre. Jusqu’à 212 Go selon la console.
- Performances : 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles, PS5 Pro comprise.
- Édition physique : pas de disque dans la boîte physique, seulement un code de téléchargement. Il faut donc tout télécharger de toute façon.
- Multijoueur : solo uniquement au lancement. La refonte de GTA Online viendra plus tard.
- Ventes : les précommandes « dépassent largement » les prévisions de Take-Two. Sensor Tower estime à près de 8 millions les exemplaires vendus, pour environ 750 millions de dollars avant la sortie.
- GTA 6 en chiffres : plus de 8 ans de développement, plus de 4700 employés, plus d’un milliard de dollars de budget estimé. GTA 6 arrive 13 ans après GTA V, vendu à plus de 230 millions d’exemplaires.
Nos vidéos sur GTA 6
Nous avons sortie trois vidéos concernant GTA 6 sur la chaîne YouTube de Frandroid.
La plus récente fait l’analyse d’une génération de consoles en crise avant l’arrivée de GTA 6.
Pendant l’été, nous avions décortiqué les 27 premières minutes de gameplay de GTA 6 à l’occasion de l’Aperçu étendu sorti sur Netflix (puis sur YouTube).
Enfin, notre première vidéo dédiée à GTA 6 concerne l’attaque frontale de Rockstar Games au marché physique et donc, par ricochet, à celui des jeux d’occasion.

articles.title: Mettez à jour votre PS5 si vous voulez jouer à GTA 6
articles.text:
À la veille du lancement de GTA 6, Sony impose une nouvelle condition pour y jouer sur PS5 : installer la version 26.07-14.23.00 du logiciel système, publiée ce mardi 17 novembre. Sans elle, le jeu de Rockstar Games ne se lancera pas.
« Sony Interactive a publié une mise à jour du logiciel système de la PS5 qui est requise pour pouvoir jouer à Grand Theft Auto VI. Les joueurs doivent télécharger cette mise à jour avant minuit le 19 novembre afin d’être prêts à jouer dès le jour de la sortie, le 19 novembre », fait savoir Sony par le compte PlayStation Support, dans un message publié sur X ce mercredi 18 novembre. Le préchargement de GTA 6 est ouvert depuis le mardi 10 novembre pour les précommandes numériques, et depuis le 12 novembre pour les versions en boîte, qui contiennent un code de téléchargement.
Une mise à jour de sécurité, la quatrième en deux mois
Les notes de version de Sony évoquent seulement « des correctifs de sécurité du logiciel système ». Le constructeur ne dit ni quelles failles il corrige, ni si la mise à jour vise le piratage de la console. Avec l’essor des outils IA, la PS5 est particulièrement visée par le piratage ces dernières semaines et Sony se doit de réagir en colmatant un maximum de brèches. C’est déjà la quatrième mise à jour en moins de deux mois.
Sony invite les joueuses et les joueurs à télécharger la mise à jour dès maintenant, afin d’être prêts pour minuit, heure de lancement de GTA 6 en France, dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi. Les retardataires devront patienter au moment de lancer le jeu, le temps de télécharger puis d’installer les 1,3 Go de la mise à jour (en priant pour que les serveurs tiennent).
Comment mettre à jour sa PS5 ?
Pour mettre à jour sa PS5, il faut aller dans les paramètres, puis sélectionner Système > Logiciel système > Mise à jour et paramètres du logiciel système > Mettre à jour le logiciel système > Mettre à jour via Internet. Une fois le téléchargement effectué, la console redémarre automatiquement pour installer la mise à jour.
À noter qu’il existe une option pour que la PS5 installe d’elle-même une mise à jour quand elle est disponible. Dans le menu Mise à jour et paramètres du logiciel système, il faut cocher les cases Télécharger automatiquement les fichiers de mise à jour et Installer automatiquement les fichiers de mise à jour. Il faut ensuite aller dans Paramètres > Système > Gestion de l’alimentation > Fonctionnalités disponibles en mode repos, activer Rester connecté à Internet, puis laisser la console en mode repos.

articles.title: Cuatro juegos gratis en Steam para PC: terror psicológico, rol online y ciencia ficción
articles.text:
Steam incorporó cuatro juegos gratis para PC que combinan terror psicológico, rol online, acción aérea y ciencia ficción, una selección disponible sin fecha límite que permite ampliar la biblioteca digital sin pagar. Los títulos son Demersus, EmberQuest, Mars Directive y One More Wave.
La novedad importa por la variedad de propuestas y por el formato de distribución: los cuatro juegos llegaron a la tienda en octubre y siguen disponibles de forma gratuita este martes 17 de noviembre. No es necesario reclamarlos de inmediato, aunque añadirlos a la cuenta permite conservarlos en la biblioteca para descargarlos más adelante.
Steam reúne terror psicológico, fantasía y combates espaciales
La lista ofrece estilos muy distintos. Demersus aborda el terror psicológico desde una historia centrada en la adicción al alcohol. EmberQuest propone un mundo persistente de fantasía para jugar con otras personas, mientras que Mars Directive utiliza inteligencia artificial para alterar las conversaciones. One More Wave apuesta por el ritmo arcade y los enfrentamientos aéreos.
La selección llega un día después de otra tanda de cuatro juegos gratuitos en la plataforma. Aunque comparten la condición de acceso sin pago, la propuesta del 17 de noviembre se centra en proyectos con mecánicas y escenarios alejados entre sí.
Demersus convierte los conflictos internos en un escenario de arcilla
Demersus, desarrollado por Darklim Studios, es una aventura de terror psicológico en primera persona. El jugador debe resolver puzles y reconstruir episodios de la vida del protagonista a través de entornos que representan su mente.
Su apartado visual utiliza figuras y decorados de arcilla, un recurso que contrasta con los temas de la historia. El juego fue creado por dos estudiantes universitarios y está dirigido a un público adulto por el tratamiento de la adicción al alcohol.
La propuesta no se apoya en combates ni en una experiencia multijugador. Su avance depende de la exploración de los escenarios, la resolución de acertijos y la interpretación de elementos vinculados con el pasado del personaje.
EmberQuest propone un MMORPG con oficios, gremios y combates PvP
EmberQuest, de Faded Scroll Games, es un videojuego de rol multijugador masivo en línea, conocido como MMORPG. Ofrece cuatro clases de personaje y 10 habilidades que se pueden mejorar durante la partida.
El mundo del juego permite pescar, cocinar, extraer minerales, fabricar equipamiento y comerciar con otros usuarios. También incluye misiones, gremios, jefes de mundo y enfrentamientos entre jugadores, una modalidad identificada como PvP.
Entre sus objetos aparece un anillo mágico que permite transformar al personaje en delfín. Esa posibilidad se suma a un sistema que combina exploración, progreso de habilidades y actividades compartidas dentro de un entorno de fantasía persistente.
Mars Directive usa inteligencia artificial en las conversaciones
La propuesta más particular de la selección es Mars Directive, una aventura de ciencia ficción que comienza cuando una explosión interrumpe el viaje de una nave con destino a Marte.
El jugador observa la situación a través de cámaras de seguridad y se comunica con Patty, una mujer que despierta sin recordar qué ocurrió. A partir de ese momento, el diálogo no depende de respuestas fijas incluidas en un guion.
Los personajes utilizan modelos de lenguaje para interpretar las frases escritas por quien juega, examinar objetos y tomar decisiones. La conversación puede cambiar según las palabras utilizadas por el jugador, lo que modifica la forma de abordar la situación dentro de la nave.
One More Wave apuesta por el cooperativo y las oleadas enemigas
One More Wave es un shooter arcade de desplazamiento lateral. El objetivo es pilotar un avión y sobrevivir a oleadas de aeronaves enemigas, ovnis y jefes de gran tamaño.
El juego admite partidas en solitario, cooperativo local y cooperativo online. Su estructura se centra en resistir ataques sucesivos y superar cada ronda con una combinación de reflejos, movimiento y disparos.
Cómo añadir los cuatro juegos gratis a una cuenta de Steam
El proceso para reclamarlos se realiza desde la aplicación de escritorio o desde la tienda web:
- Iniciar sesión en una cuenta de Steam.
- Buscar Demersus, EmberQuest, Mars Directive y One More Wave.
- Verificar que el precio figure como 0.
- Pulsar “Obtener”, “Añadir a la biblioteca” o “Jugar”.
- Confirmar que cada título aparezca en la biblioteca personal.
Reclamar un juego no obliga a descargarlo en ese momento. La adquisición queda vinculada a la cuenta como una licencia de uso, por lo que los títulos no se pueden revender y el acceso depende de las políticas y los servidores de la plataforma.

articles.title: Fadnavis’ vision for a new Maharashtra: Gen Z, deep tech and $1 trillion
articles.text:
Fadnavis’ vision for a new Maharashtra: Gen Z, deep tech and $1 trillion
At The Governance Challenge 2026, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis judged ideas from 13,000+ B-school students and shared his roadmap for a trillion-dollar, drought-free, deep-tech Maharashtra by 2035.
Few sitting Chief Ministers would spend four to five hours judging student presentations. Devendra Fadnavis did exactly that at the summit of The Governance Challenge (TGC) 2026 in Mumbai, where six finalist teams pitched their answers to one question: what can the Government of Maharashtra do to make the state an innovation hub by 2035?
The challenge drew more than 4,400 three-member teams, over 13,000 students from 30 of India’s leading business and policy schools. After several elimination rounds, six teams presented ideas on healthcare, education, farming and access to credit. The Chief Minister, the 18 finalists and Gaurav Goel, founder & CEO of Samagra, which runs the challenge, then joined Shradha Sharma, Founder & CEO at The Bharat Project, YourStory Media for an open conversation.
A government willing to admit it doesn’t have every answer
Fadnavis opened with an unusually candid view of how governments tend to think.
“Normally, in government, we always feel that we know everything, and that we are the ones who will create solutions for every problem. But in my experience of the last 10 years, I feel you need a very fresh perspective to look at every problem.”
The finalists, he said, brought exactly that. They understood technology and how to deploy it, and despite being outsiders to the system, they had clearly thought hard about the problems. Their ideas may not be complete solutions, he added, but they give the government a strong base to build on with its own experience and data.
Why B-schools need a dose of governance
Goel explained that TGC was created to fill a gap in management education. Business school case studies, campus events, internships and placements all lean heavily towards the corporate and startup world, leaving students with little exposure to governance or social impact. TGC tries to change that through immersion, in the hope that the experience stays with students and later draws them towards nation-building.
After the national round, finalists spent two days meeting officials across departments and visiting model schools and primary health centres, while mentors from government and industry helped refine their pitches. The students said the visits upended their assumptions. One admitted that problems look simple from the outside, and that proposing a fix from an air-conditioned room is very different from delivering it on the ground. He was struck by how much infrastructure already exists, including 3D printers in government schools. Others said the competition felt different from the usual hackathons because it pointed towards execution, not just a certificate, and that some teams worked until 3 am refining their ideas.
An 11-year experiment with young talent
For Fadnavis, young people in government is not a new idea. Since 2015, the Chief Minister’s Fellowship, run with IIT Bombay, has placed bright young graduates inside government for a year through a competitive selection process. Some leave jobs at multinationals to join.
One fellowship team built a platform to run and evaluate the state’s farm-pond-on-demand scheme for drought relief and water conservation. The scheme created around 1.5 lakh farm ponds, and the platform won a Prime Minister’s Award. Senior bureaucrats who were sceptical in the early years now compete for fellows, with district collectors asking for two or three at a time.
In 2019, the state also launched a Village Social Transformation initiative with CSR partners across 1,000 villages, asking young people to live in a village for a full year and use CSR funds to fill gaps that rigid government budgets could not. Of 5,000 applicants, roughly 900 to 950 took up the challenge, and not one dropped out.
Goel said Samagra runs on the same belief. Its team of 90 to 100 people has had an average age of 25 to 30 for over a decade. He looks for energy, an impact orientation and raw smarts, and says young recruits are easier to groom because they arrive without baggage.
Experience plus fresh ideas
Fadnavis called Gen Z the first generation born entirely into technology and constantly connected to global best practices. Properly channelled, he said, that exposure produces bright ideas. But he stressed balance: new ideas need mentoring and oversight, and real innovation comes from pairing fresh thinking with experience.
Maharashtra in 2035
Asked what transformation he wants the state to be known for, Fadnavis began with the government machinery itself. Its people, he said, are its most neglected resource, and good work too often depends on an individual minister or officer rather than the institution. Building the state as an institution, with Samagra’s help, is now a priority.
He then set out the economic goal. Maharashtra is a $660 billion economy that he believes can overtake the UAE and Singapore within two years and become India’s first trillion-dollar state economy by 2030. A true welfare state, he argued, must earn before it spends on social programmes. With the state already about 50% urbanised, he wants that urbanisation to drive jobs and sustainable growth.
His vision for 2035 includes a drought-free Maharashtra with water reaching every area, 65% of power from clean sources, and a state that serves as India’s home for startups, frontier technology and deep tech.
Skills over degrees
His advice to students was to stop chasing degrees for their own sake. Future jobs, he said, will depend on the skills people actually acquire. A skilled workforce attracts investment, and investment creates demand for more skilled people. Getting that cycle right would put Maharashtra in a different league.
Innovation for the village
When a student asked what innovation means for a villager with little exposure to technology, Fadnavis gave the line of the day.
“Innovation is a simple solution for a very complex problem. Unless it is a simple solution, it is not an innovation.”
He pointed to the state’s AI advisory tools for farmers and AI models already lifting farm productivity. The problem is that many depend on costly IoT hardware that a farmer with one acre cannot afford. The next round of innovation, he said, must make these tools cheaper and more sustainable.
Purpose first
In closing, Fadnavis told the students that serving the nation does not require a uniform or public office.
Creating jobs, improving livelihoods, lifting people out of poverty and extending healthcare are all forms of service, in any field. Whether they build a startup or chase a unicorn, he urged them to anchor their work in purpose, because purpose matters more than how much they earn.
Shradha called the day a glimpse of what a Viksit Bharat could look like: a Chief Minister who listens, and young people ready to do the work.

articles.title: À quoi servent ces nouvelles boîtes bleues installées au bord des routes ?
articles.text:
Si vous avez emprunté la RN44 ou la RN4, vous avez peut-être cru apercevoir des radars automatiques de dernière génération au bord de la chaussée. En réalité, ces imposants poteaux métalliques abritent des boîtiers d’écocontribution poids lourds (ECPL). Ce nouveau dispositif a pour but de mettre en place une redevance kilométrique qui cible uniquement les véhicules de plus de 3,5 tonnes transportant des marchandises sur le réseau routier régional.
Des bornes déjà déployées pour taxer dès 2027
Ces nouvelles bornes bleues serviront à appliquer une taxe au kilomètre estimée par la Fédération nationale des transports routiers (FNTR) à environ 15 centimes par kilomètre. La mesure s’étendra sur 525 kilomètres de routes dans le Grand Est, dont 145 kilomètres pour le seul département de la Marne sur la RN4 et la RN44. Thibaut Duchêne, conseiller régional, confirme que ces bornes ne sont pas encore opérationnelles et qu’aucune action préventive ni sanction n’est menée pour l’instant.
Leur déploiement anticipé s’explique par l’attribution d’un marché public qui demande de caler l’installation technique en amont du calendrier. L’objectif des autorités régionales est une mise en service prévue pour le 2 avril 2027. Cette planification évite d’éventuels retards qui repousseraient l’application de l’écocontribution. Le projet suscite la colère des transporteurs qui ont multiplié les mobilisations, comme le 15 octobre devant la Maison de la région à Metz pour exiger la suspension du texte. Des discussions et des négociations restent engagées avec les différents acteurs pour tenter de trouver un accord qui donne satisfaction aux transporteurs.
Un milliard d’euros pour rénover le réseau routier
L’enjeu financier derrière l’installation de ces boîtes bleues n’est pas négligeable dans la mesure où, sur dix ans, l’écocontribution poids lourds doit générer (selon les estimations) un gain d’un milliard d’euros au profit de la Région Grand Est. Une somme importante qui sera intégralement réinvestie dans les travaux de modernisation et de mise à niveau du réseau routier. Elle vient abonder un programme routier régional global d’un montant total de 2,1 milliards d’euros s’étalant jusqu’à l’horizon 2035.
À lire : Deux nouveaux panneaux de signalisation apparaissent sur les routes : voici ce qu’ils signifient
Parmi les chantiers financés, on retrouve en priorité le contournement ouest de Vitry, un projet évalué à 250 millions d’euros. En discussion depuis des années, ce grand projet franchira une nouvelle étape au premier semestre 2027 avec la révision de ses études de faisabilité. Les données récoltées par ces grosses boîtes bleues permettront ainsi de financer les transports régionaux pour les dix ans à venir.

articles.title: Costco prevé abrir una nueva macrotienda de 15.000 m² en Madrid: así es el famoso supermercado de Estados Unidos donde sólo puedes comprar con una tarjeta de socio
articles.text:
Costco, la cadena estadounidense en la que sólo se compra con tarjeta de socio, prepara su tercera tienda en la Comunidad de Madrid, concretamente en Torrejón de Ardoz. Con este movimiento, la cadena parece seguir adelante con su expansión en nuestro país.
Suelo e inversión. Costco Wholesale Corporation ha cerrado, a través de su filial en España, la compra de unos 60.000 metros cuadrados de suelo en Torrejón, con una inversión aproximada de 80 millones de euros, cifra cubre toda la apertura y no sólo el terreno.
Cómo será la tienda. Tendrá unos 15.000 metros cuadrados y gasolinera propia, y abriría en septiembre de 2027. Para comprar dentro habrá que ser socio, porque Costco funciona como un club de precios al que se accede pagando una cuota anual. Vamos, que sin tarjeta no se pasa por caja. Y vende la mayoría de sus productos en formatos extragrandes o packs familiares para mover volumen y ajustar precios.
El mapa en España. Con Torrejón, la cadena tendría tres tiendas en la región, junto a las de Getafe y Las Rozas. Fuera de Madrid suma otras tres, en Sevilla, Sestao (Vizcaya) y Zaragoza, además de un almacén logístico en Torija (Guadalajara), datos que recoge la agencia.
La apertura encaja en la estrategia de crecimiento de la multinacional en España, aunque la fecha no es definitiva. Habrá que ver si la licencia municipal llega a tiempo, porque de ella depende ese plazo.

articles.title: 👨🏿🚀TechCabal Daily – Cassava seeks $1 billion for AI - TechCabal
articles.text:
Happy midweek. ☀️️
Mzansi, we’ve got our eyes on you! 🇿🇦 TechCabal is bringing you TC Mzansi, a brand-new newsletter covering Southern Africa’s tech news: big deals, big moves, and all the industry gist worth knowing, straight to your inbox.
Join the waitlist and be the first to know when we launch.
TC Mzansi, our newsletter covering South African tech is coming on November 23.
AI
Cassava seeks $1 billion to buy Nvidia chips for AI data centres across Africa
Cassava Technologies, the pan-African technology group founded by Zimbabwean billionaire Strive Masiyiwa, is in talks with investors in the Middle East and the United States to raise up to $1 billion to buy NVIDIA-made graphics processing units (GPUs) and upgrade its fibre and data-centre networks to handle demanding AI workloads. The fundraising is still under discussion, and there is no guarantee it will close.
Explain like I’m new here: In 2025, Cassava partnered with the chipmaker to build what it called Africa’s first AI factory, using Nvidia’s computing systems and software.
Cassava became Nvidia’s first Cloud Partner in Africa and began deploying its AI infrastructure in South Africa, with plans to expand into Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, and Morocco. It has also launched its AI Multi-Model Exchange, a platform that gives African developers access to different AI models and tools to build and deploy applications.
Why it matters: Africa accounts for just 0.6% of global data-centre capacity, according to the Africa Data Centres Association’s 2026 report. There is plenty of room to grow, but building these facilities requires enormous investment. Local AI infrastructure could help businesses run applications faster, keep sensitive data within national borders and develop products around African languages and markets.
Cassava is not alone. Amazon Web Services (AWS) says it has invested more than $819 million in its South African cloud infrastructure since 2018, with another $1.5 billion committed by the end of 2029.
Microsoft and UAE-based AI company G42 announced a $1 billion investment in a data centre and cloud region in Kenya in 2024, although the project encountered delays in 2026. These investments are building the cloud infrastructure that AI services depend on.

Internet
Telkom lines up to sell Amazon’s satellite Internet in South Africa
Telkom, South Africa’s third-largest telecoms company by subscribers, has signed up to distribute Amazon Leo, Amazon’s satellite broadband service. Telkom signed the agreement through Openserve, its wholesale network business, covering all three of the group’s businesses.
How it will work: Openserve will sell satellite connectivity to large businesses and eligible public-sector customers. BCX, Telkom’s IT services subsidiary, will bundle it with managed networks, cloud computing and cybersecurity services, while Telkom Business will serve small businesses in rural and remote areas.
Telkom can also use satellite connections as primary or backup links for its mobile towers, connecting sites where conventional network infrastructure is hard to deploy.
Explain like I’m new here: In July, Amazon partnered with Herotel, a local Internet service provider, to launch a residential and small-business service called evry. It marked its commercial entry into the country, with commercial availability expected in 2027.
Why this matters: The partnerships also offer Amazon a way into a market where Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite service, has struggled to secure approval. South Africa requires companies holding certain telecoms licences to include historically disadvantaged groups in ownership. This has been a major obstacle for Starlink. Amazon’s distributor-led approach allows Herotel to handle the necessary local licensing and regulatory requirements.
The deal comes as Telkom becomes more selective about where it spends money on fibre. In the six months to September 2026, its fibre investment fell by more than a third. Extending fibre into remote areas can be expensive, but satellite offers another option. There are no prices or launch dates yet, but Telkom says it will share availability details closer to launch.
Streaming
MTN: Lights, camera, data!
MTN has a new show about staying single. The telecoms giant is looking for a long-term relationship with your screen.
MTN One TV, its streaming platform, has started producing original content, beginning with 100 Ways to Stay Single in Lagos, a Nigerian series featuring Ghanaian, Nigerian, and South African actors.
The show is currently available in South Africa and Zambia, with plans to roll it out to other MTN markets. More original productions are on the way.
Explain like I’m new here: MTN has been down this road before. In 2014, it launched FrontRow, a streaming service that became VU a year later. By May 2017, VU was dead, and MTN had retreated to partnerships with other entertainment providers.
Nine years later, the telco is giving streaming another shot. It launched MTN One TV in June 2026, starting with South Africa and Zambia. The platform is free to watch and supported by advertising, but viewers still need an internet connection.
So far, it has attracted 20,000 registered users in South Africa.
What’s MTN really after? Data consumption. MTN’s digital services chief, Burak Akinci, says video is driving data traffic growth, and the company wants to profit from more than simply providing the connection.
MTN has 317 million customers across 16 markets, including roughly 170 million smartphone users. Getting even a fraction of them hooked on its streaming platform could boost its data business.
The company isn’t building a traditional film studio. Instead, it’s commissioning African productions and plans to introduce free-to-air channels and premium viewing options.
Zoom out: Netflix and other global streamers spend billions competing for viewers. MTN believes its advantage lies elsewhere: an enormous existing customer base and a direct route to their phones.
But having millions of people on your network doesn’t mean they’ll watch your shows. MTN learned that lesson with VU.
This time, I hope100 Ways to Stay Single in Lagos becomes a lasting relationship.
Capital Markets
Juice Global wants to trade Africa’s IOUs
If you’re a business waiting to get paid, you have two options: wait patiently or chase your money. Juice Global wants to introduce a third: sell the “I owe you” (IOU).
The company behind Nigerian cross-border payments platform Juicyway and payout network Nairagram has unveiled Eko Securities Exchange, a new trading platform designed to turn money owed to African businesses into investments that people can buy and sell.
Explain like I’m new here: Juice Global has spent years helping businesses move money across borders. Along the way, it discovered another problem: businesses need money available before they can complete transactions.
Eko Securities is its proposed solution, and the idea is surprisingly simple.
Here’s how it works: Imagine a Nigerian exporter expecting payment in 60 days. Instead of waiting two months, the exporter could package the money owed into an investment that someone else buys today. The investor gets the right to receive the future payment, and takes on the risk that it might not arrive.
Eko wants to make such investments easier to trade by turning them into digital tokens. It plans to start with payment receivables and other short-term debts, before expanding into corporate bonds, private company shares, and other investments.
Why it matters: Africa has roughly 29 stock exchanges and trading venues, each operating under different rules, currencies, and systems. According to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), African companies raised just 1% of the world’s equity capital between 2000 and 2024.
Zoom out: Eko has received approval in principle from Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), but its broader ambitions still require regulatory approval. Expanding into other African markets will also mean getting permission from local regulators.
