articles.title: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.
Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model.
TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).
However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his company is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately.
The action is happening on both ends of the ecosystem: Sqwish, a U.K.-based AI startup behind a decision model called kettei fat, announced a $3 million pre-seed round today. Co-founders Ushnish Sengupta and Federica Freddi, who met as Cambridge grad students, had been developing small LLMs when Jev arrived on the scene, and they realized their architectures could be repurposed as a powerful decision model.
Data appears to be the key to a successful model in this category — TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida told TechCrunch that the hardest part of building Jev was finely calibrating its judgement using statistically-adjusted synthetic data. Sqwish, too, has been working with synthetic data, but its unique offering is built-in post-training tools that use a customer’s own data to improve the model’s judgement.
“What makes us not a commodity, I think, is the fact that we are offering our customers the same power…they can keep uploading their production data, and just the same way that we trained our models, their models can also keep getting better at the tasks that they care about,” CEO Ushnish Sengupta told TechCrunch.
Attempting to rank decision models is difficult; Sqwish’s “kettei fat” model has performed well on some benchmarks, but most builders of the technology say that the real proof is in the pudding: It’s generally simple for developers to sub in one model for another and see how it does in a specific context.
“The benchmark is more of an invitation to try the model out, and then the continual tuning is the reason why they should stick to us,” Sengupta said.
The Microsoft-Decision-1.1 model is also the result of the company carefully balancing across cost, latency, intelligence and calibration. Achint Srivastava, the engineering VP who led the project, agreed that too much focus on benchmarks is a mistake.
“What we see is that ‘benchmaxed’ models fall flat under real enterprise usage very quickly,” Srivastava wrote in an email. “Our testing underscores just how challenging it is to deliver accuracy, reliability, speed and cost efficiency in a single model. Microsoft-Decision-1.1 and Jev are among the few that perform strongly across all four dimensions, even when evaluated on ‘held out’ or unseen benchmarks reflective of real use cases.”
For startups like Sqwish, competition with hyperscalers and frontier labs is an opportunity. Freddi predicts that future systems will see so-called System One intelligence, like decision models, working in concert with System Two intelligence, like frontier LLMs.
“Even in that future, System One is maybe a $10 billion, $50 billion [opportunity], and OpenAI is doing this IPO with you know $1 trillion, $2 trillion market value in mind,” she told TechCrunch. “This is all we care about; whereas for them, this is just a side project.”

articles.title: Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking the new James Bond
articles.text:
Robert Pattinson’s casting as James Bond made enough sense given his recent work with director Denis Villeneuve, who’s making the franchise’s next film over at Amazon. But it turns out that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos played a significant role in making the final decision, too.
Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking the new James Bond
Bezos said that he was immediately drawn to Robert Pattinson’s performance during screen tests.
During Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World conference today, Bezos said that he was “heavily involved” in the process of casting the newest 007:
We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. Then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists, and it was really interesting — full costume, real sets, other actors. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all those screening tests, and reviewing all of that. And all of the actors were extraordinarily talented.
By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances. It was kind of immediately undebated. Denis — the director — we all sort of gravitated to Rob. By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him, just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, ‘maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown.’ But in the screen test, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.
It’s not exactly surprising that a studio leader would want to have a say in casting the new face for one of their most lucrative franchises. But with Bezos being so hands-on, one can only image what this new era of Bond films will look and feel like once Amazon starts releasing them in theaters.

Researchers at Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) published “Clock Distribution Network with Backside Clock Mesh in BSPDN Architecture.”
Abstract Excerpt
“We propose a clock distribution network (CDN) in which the clock mesh is located on backside metal (BM) layers, while the rest of the network remains on the frontside. Since the backside power distribution network (BSPDN) also uses the BM layers, the clock mesh and power network must share them. We identify an important problem of placing mesh receivers while accounting for keep-out zones (KOZs) between clock- and power-nTSVs. articles.title: CoreWeave connects custom training loops to model serving
articles.text:
CoreWeave connects custom training loops to model serving
Production traffic shows failures that benchmarks or pre-deployment evaluations can’t fully reveal. It tells you which edge cases matter and what users need. Turning that signal into the next model version requires an upfront decision: does the model need to change, or is the problem in retrieval, context, prompts, tools, or serving?
Changing weights won’t fix a failure elsewhere in the system. When the model is the right place to intervene, production evidence can improve both quality and economics. A smaller model might reproduce a more expensive model’s behavior; better examples might improve consistency; an outcome-based reward might suit the task. Refining a capable model can also avoid another migration to a new model generation.
Choose a technique from the failure mode
Model distillation fits when a stronger model already produces the desired behavior and you want a smaller, more economical model to reproduce it. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) fits when high-quality examples can teach more consistent behavior. Reinforcement learning (RL) fits when you can reliably evaluate an outcome but cannot readily specify the ideal response in advance.
“Changing weights won’t fix a failure elsewhere in the system. When the model is the right place to intervene, production evidence can improve both quality and economics.”
You may use all three approaches over a model’s lifecycle. Choose from the evidence in your workload, even when that means using a technique that takes more setup.
Production traces have to become training data. Post-training needs compute and orchestration, and the resulting model has to be evaluated and returned to inference. That is the work of closing the loop. In RL, inference generates rollouts during training, and new weights must return to serving throughout the run.
At Fully Connected 2026, we introduced CoreWeave Model Distillation, CoreWeave RL Rollouts on CoreWeave Inference, and a programmable training API. These workflows connect in CoreWeave Forge. The programmable API is in limited preview, with an official launch planned for later in 2026.
Keep the data fresh when the base model stays
CoreWeave Model Distillation provides a managed workflow. CoreWeave Agent Lens captures inference traffic as the application runs. The workflow turns it into training data, relabels weak outputs, tests base models and hyperparameters, deploys candidates to Serverless Inference, and compares them with the production model.
If the model already has the capabilities your task needs, fresh production data can improve its fit without changing the serving profile you know. Compare the new version against the model already running before you move traffic.
Method used this workflow to revisit a model it had already deployed. In 2024, it used OpenPipe to train Llama 3.1 8B to navigate bank interactive voice response (IVR) systems, using GPT-4o outputs. In August 2026, Method brought in fresh production data, relabeled it with GPT-5.6 Sol, and trained another version. The candidate won 57.5% of head-to-head evaluations against the deployed version.
The base model had not changed. Fresh production data and Model Distillation in Forge made another iteration possible sooner. The 57.5% result is the share of head-to-head evaluations the new version won.
Control the training recipe in Python
For teams that want to design their own learning process, the programmable training API for Serverless Training separates training logic from infrastructure operations. You write a Python loop; CoreWeave manages the compute and underlying training infrastructure.
Here’s one way to combine RL updates with periodic supervised updates on verified demonstrations. The example creates a learner and serving adapter, uses an Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-5, and publishes updated weights to the sampler after each step.
Python
learner = await training.create_learner(model=model, lora=lora)
sampler = await serving.create_adapter(name="sampler")
optimizer = AdamConfig(learning_rate=1e-5)
for step in range(num_steps):
    trajectories = await run_agent(sampler, tasks)
    update = learner.batch()
    update.forward_backward(
        build_rl_batch(trajectories), loss="importance_sampling"
    )
    update.optim_step(optimizer=optimizer)
    if (step + 1) % sft_interval == 0:
        update.forward_backward(next_demo_batch(), loss="cross_entropy")
        update.optim_step(optimizer=optimizer)
    update.publish_weights(to=sampler)
    await update.result()
await (await learner.save_state("final")).result()
await learner.close()
The rollout and batch helpers are illustrative. Your agent logic, reward calculations, and data preparation belong in those helpers. The loop uses importance-sampling loss for RL and cross-entropy loss for demonstrations, then waits for the update result. It saves the final learner state and closes the learner.
You choose how often demonstrations enter the loop, how rewards are calculated, and how the recipe evolves. SFT, RL, and distillation share the training primitives, while the platform runs the distributed systems underneath.
Willow began with supervised learning, then added RL scorers to reduce filler words, improve readability, and remove self-corrected phrases. The scorers were combined into a reward function. Lawrence Liu, Willow’s chief technology officer and co-founder, reported better text styling, emoji handling, and responsiveness to commands than in the deployed model.
Remove checkpoint reload delays from RL
RL serving needs enough rollout generation, alignment with the policy being trained, and timely weight updates. The trainer, reward logic, and environment can stay where they are while CoreWeave Inference handles this part of the loop.
CoreWeave RL Rollouts is built on Nvidia Dynamo with vLLM support. When the trainer writes a checkpoint, the service hot-loads it into a live deployment while preserving in-flight requests and endpoint availability. It returns training metadata: token log probabilities (logprobs), token IDs, and expert routing for mixture-of-experts (MoE) models.
“When the trainer writes a checkpoint, the service hot-loads it into a live deployment while preserving in-flight requests and endpoint availability. Serving uses the trainer’s current policy weights, removing staleness and redeployment delays that would otherwise hold up the next batch of rollouts.”
Checkpoints can be full snapshots or incremental deltas, reducing synchronization after the first upload. Serving uses the trainer’s current policy weights, removing staleness and redeployment delays that would otherwise hold up the next batch of rollouts.
Measure quality and infrastructure separately
We validated the workflow with Nvidia and you.com by post-training Nvidia Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for web search. The run combined SFT and RL with you.com’s search tools inside the training loop.
BrowseComp accuracy increased from a 36.97% baseline to 45.45%, a reported 22.94% relative improvement. Average tool calls fell 30.24%. Separately, hot-loading checkpoints into a live deployment was approximately 15 times faster than traditional redeployment cycles.
Better search tooling, post-training refinement, and harness improvements worked together to improve accuracy and reduce tool calls. Hot-loading cut the time spent waiting for checkpoint synchronization. If you’re trying to make a smaller or more efficient model competitive with models an order of magnitude larger, that extra training time matters too.
Keep the model connected to its experiment
CoreWeave Forge connects production inference, training, and serving again. Model Distillation supplies a managed path. The programmable API lets researchers control the training loop without managing its infrastructure. RL Rollouts supports teams keeping their own trainer while using CoreWeave for rollout inference.
Models produced by serverless training return as tagged artifacts that can move into Serverless Inference without a separate registry handoff. Experiments remain logged beside them, keeping the run, model, and eventual deployment connected.
“Choose a failure you can reproduce, use it to guide the training method, and compare the candidate with the model serving users.”
Choose a failure you can reproduce, use it to guide the training method, and compare the candidate with the model serving users. Keep the production examples, evaluation, and resulting artifact together so your team can use them again.
The CoreWeave Forge blog and announcement press release provide context on the capabilities introduced at Fully Connected 2026. CoreWeave also plans further engineering explanations of Model Distillation, the programmable training API, and RL Rollouts.

articles.title: La Chine fait voler un avion électrique à 10 moteurs : l'Europe est définitivement à la traîne
articles.text:
Airbus et Boeing viennent peut-être de se faire ridiculiser par un concurrent chinois baptisé Comac. Ce 14 novembre 2026, le constructeur aéronautique chinois a fait voler pour la première fois le Comac CE-25A, un petit avion uniquement équipé de moteurs électriques.
Un premier vol habité pour le CE-25A, un petit avion électrique chinois
Ce samedi, le CE-25A a décollé de Binzhou, dans la province de Shandong, avec deux pilotes et un ingénieur d’essais à bord. L’avion est resté en l’air 16 minutes et 38 secondes exactement, parcourant 60 kilomètres environ. Comac indique que l’appareil a fonctionné normalement et que ces indicateurs de performance ont répondu à ses attentes.
En vérité, ce n’est pas la première fois que l’avion quitte le sol : en février dernier déjà, l’avion avait volé en total autonomie, sans personne à son bord. Puis ont ensuite été réalisés 19 vols de validation sans pilote avant d’y placer de vrais humains. Ce vol du CE-25A était donc la première démonstration de Comac d’un avion commercial électrique chinois avec un pilote.
Dévoilé pour la première fois à Shanghai en 2023, il aura fallu trois ans seulement à Comac pour développer cet avion. Il est conçu pour transporter 19 passagers sur des liaisons régionales courtes ; son autonomie ne lui permet pas d’aller plus loin. Selon les données communiquées par le constructeur, il affiche une masse maximale au décollage de 10 tonnes, une vitesse de croisière de 300 km/h, une altitude de croisière de 2 400 m et une autonomie annoncée de 400 km. Cet avion dispose de dix ventilateurs électriques carénés installés au-dessus des ailes. Fini les gros moteurs ou les turboréacteurs : Comac fait le pari de multiplier les petits moteurs électriques.
Une prouesse technique dont l’Europe et les États-Unis ne sont pas capable
Faire voler un avion électrique de 10 tonnes avec équipage est une prouesse car à cause de cette masse, il faut des batteries énormes et denses et trouver le bon équilibre entre poids et puissance. Les petits avions électriques existent depuis longtemps, mais concevoir un avion commercial avec plusieurs places à bord est une autre histoire. Pour le moment, le CE-25A n’est pas certifié, mais ça ne saurait tarder. Avec cet avion, la Chine poursuit sa stratégie de décarbonation entamée dans tous les secteurs.
Pour le moment, en Europe ou aux États-Unis, chez Airbus ou Boeing, aucun avion 100% électrique de cette envergure n’a profité d’une démonstration. Il y a bien le français Aura Aero qui développe l’ERA, un avion régional hybride électrique de 19 places dont le premier vol est prévu en 2027. Outre-Atlantique aussi on s’intéresse à l’électrique avec le X1 de Heart Aerospace, mais il est surtout là pour développer des appareils hybrides également. Pour rester dans la course, les constructeurs européens et étatsuniens vont devoir pousser la manette des gaz. D’autant plus que Comac vient concurrencer Airbus aussi sur les avions longs courriers.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse in Australia - a personal AI agent built for everyone - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Muse is now available in Australia. It is the world’s first personal AI agent built for everyone to help users stay on top of tasks and do everything from shopping and monitoring emails to planning workouts and creating designs.
Meta says it built Muse from the ground up and can do more than just answer questions.
It can help keep you get organised, find information, compare products and prices and even explore property listings.
From day one Muse will have connector partnerships with Canva, Domain, Kogan, Mecca, Officeworks, RealEstate.com.au, Sweat, ShopBack and Ticketek.
More connector features will roll out in the coming weeks.
The Canva connector, for example, will allow Muse users to design visuals and content Muse also makes it’s possible to explore property listings on Domain and RealEstate.com.au.
On the shopping front, Muse can also be used to look for value electronics and appliances through Kogan.com, beauty products through Mecca, office supplies, furniture and other devices from Officeworks and tickets through Ticketek.
And with ShopBack, Muse makes it possible to compare prices and earn cash back and rewards for flights, hotels, and shopping.
Muse also works with popular services including Gmail, Google Calendar, OpenTable, and Shopify.
Muse will be available on iOS and Android and at muse.ai and the app can work on your smartphone and on a browser on Mac and Windows computers.
Tech Guide has been using Muse for a few days in an early preview and we gave it access to our email so it could give us an overview of our inboxes so it can highlight and summarise the emails that needed our attention and action.
Users can interact with Muse with their voice in real-time conversations on mobile, web, or Mac so you’re able to talk through an idea or a query and let Muse get to work.
It’s also possible to customise your Muse character and give it a name.
Spaces is another custom experience you can create within Muse simply by describing your idea.
Spaces is home to your ideas, plans, and projects whether it’s planning a wedding or planning a trip.
“With the festive season coming up, the timing couldn’t be better. From finding and buying the perfect gift to planning and booking a holiday, Muse is designed to take work off Australians’ plates,” says Will Easton, Managing Director, Meta Australia and New Zealand.
“As local experiences roll out, familiar services will make Muse even more useful in everyday life.
“And people stay in control, including choosing what Muse can access and approving purchases before they happen.”
Muse is run on MuseSecure VM, which is a dedicated cloud computer that securely stores data and credentials for the services you connect while keeping passwords and payment methods out of the agent’s reach.
Users can decide what Muse can access and will always check with you before any actions including sending an email or making a purchase.
Muse is available now for Australian users on iOS, Android, and Muse.ai and will be coming soon to Meta AI glasses.
Muse is free for most of what people need but subscription plans will be announced soon for those who want to do even more.

articles.title: The Batman 3 menacé ? Robert Pattinson ne serait plus engagé pour la suite
articles.text:
Ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, le média américain The Wrap a rapporté, en citant une source au fait du contrat, que les reports à répétition de The Batman : Part II avaient permis à Robert Pattinson de se libérer de son engagement pour un troisième et dernier film.
6 ans d’attente et une production sous haute tension pour The Batman 2
Il faut dire que la suite de The Batman, qui avait rapporté 772 millions de dollars (environ 665 millions d’euros) dans le monde en 2022, ressemble de plus en plus à un parcours du combattant. D’abord calé pour octobre 2025, The Batman 2 a glissé de report en report jusqu’au 18 février 2028, soit près de six ans après la sortie du premier film en mars 2022. Une éternité à l’échelle d’Hollywood, d’autant que le tournage a été suspendu le 5 octobre, le temps que Matt Reeves règle une affaire familiale. DC Studios a ensuite fait appel à Steven Soderbergh pour l’aider à boucler les dernières semaines de tournage.
Et pour Warner Bros., cette porte de sortie tombe au pire moment. Depuis ce lundi 16 novembre, l’acteur a un nouvel emploi du temps de ministre : Amazon MGM Studios l’a officiellement choisi comme prochain James Bond, dans un film réalisé par Denis Villeneuve. Selon le site américain Puck, le comédien aurait négocié un engagement limité à trois films, un chiffre qu’Amazon MGM n’a pas confirmé. Même à ce rythme, 007 va occuper une bonne partie de ses prochaines années, après une année 2026 déjà très chargée pour lui : The Drama, The Odyssey, Primetime et Dune 3, attendu en salles en décembre.
Le séisme chez DC Studios complique encore l’équation
Comme si le calendrier de sa star ne suffisait pas, l’avenir de la franchise The Batman se heurte aussi aux turbulences qui secouent Warner Bros. Skydance, le groupe de David Ellison déjà propriétaire de Paramount, a bouclé en octobre le rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery. Le 9 novembre, le nouveau propriétaire a annoncé le départ de James Gunn et Peter Safran de la tête de DC Studios. Jeremy Latcham, ancien cadre de Marvel Studios, prendra leur place le 1er décembre.
Jeremy Latcham devra décider quoi faire du « Chapitre 1 » du DCU imaginé par Gunn, et le sort des productions DC en cours reste flou.

articles.title: Le mini vidéoprojecteur laser Anker Nebula Capsule 3 projette en Full HD sur 120 pouces et perd 260 € pour le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
L’Anker Nebula Capsule 3 est un mini vidéoprojecteur qui existe en deux versions : une classique et une laser, qui est celle qui nous intéresse aujourd’hui. Il est vraiment séduisant avec son format canette (en un peu plus gros quand même) qui le rend facile à transporter d’une pièce à l’autre. Avec sa batterie intégrée et sa projection laser, il transforme n’importe quel mur en écran de cinéma. Ses fonctions connectées donnent accès aux principaux services de streaming. Jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026, fin du Black Friday, vous pouvez le commander avec 37 % de réduction.
Les trois points forts du Nebula Capsule 3 Laser
- Une projection laser Full HD 1080p qui peut atteindre 120 pouces
- La batterie intégrée pour 2 h 30 d’autonomie en mode Éco
- La présence d’Android TV 11, avec Chromecast et haut-parleur Dolby Audio de 8 watts
Grâce au Black Friday, vous pouvez économiser 260 euros sur l’Anker Nebula Capsule 3 Laser puisqu’il passe de 699,99 euros à 439,99 euros sur Amazon.
Un vidéoprojecteur laser Full HD qui tient dans une canette
Le Nebula Capsule 3 Laser surprend d’abord par son format : avec ses 17 x 8,4 x 8,4 cm pour environ 900 g, il peut facilement se glisser dans un sac pour vous suivre dans tous vos déplacements. Son châssis métallique lui donne une finition soignée avec une bonne sensation de robustesse. Mais il ne faut pas se fier à son gabarit : cet appareil embarque une technologie de projection laser DLP qui peut afficher une image en Full HD sur une diagonale maximale de 120 pouces. Alors, nous ne vous conseillons pas de pousser jusqu’aux 120 pouces, sinon l’image sera moins nette sur les bords. Avec du 80 ou 100 pouces, vous êtes déjà bien loti.
Sa luminosité est annoncée à 300 lumens ANSI, ce qui impose quelques précautions. Pour garder une image lisible et un bon niveau de contraste, il faut quand même privilégier une pièce sombre, limite totalement obscure. Si vous l’utilisez en pleine journée, vous n’allez pas voir grand-chose. Les couleurs sont plutôt bien restituées pour un appareil de cette taille, et la Full HD offre une image suffisamment précise. Le Nebula Capsule 3 Laser gère aussi tout seul la mise au point et la correction du trapèze. Pour un appareil qu’on trimballe d’une pièce à l’autre, ça simplifie franchement l’installation.
Android TV, batterie intégrée et son Dolby Audio
Le Nebula Capsule 3 Laser se passe aussi de source vidéo externe, puisqu’il embarque Android TV 11 avec un accès aux principales applications de streaming. Petit bémol, Netflix n’est pas disponible nativement sur cette version : Nebula propose une manipulation pour l’installer, mais elle est peu pratique, et le plus simple reste de brancher une clé HDMI. Vous avez aussi Chromecast, pour diffuser une vidéo depuis un smartphone ou une tablette. Le Wi-Fi et le Bluetooth viennent compléter la connectivité, sans oublier le port HDMI pour brancher une console, un ordinateur ou un autre appareil compatible. Il intègre un haut-parleur de 8 watts compatible Dolby Audio, ce qui est juste ce qu’il faut pour ne pas s’encombrer d’une enceinte supplémentaire. Mais pour une installation plus pérenne, il faudra quand même penser à en utiliser une.
Enfin, le vidéoprojecteur intègre une batterie de 15 000 mAh qui lui permet de fonctionner sans prise électrique pendant environ 2 h 30, en mode économie. De quoi regarder un film, à condition de baisser la luminosité : en usage intensif, l’autonomie chute nettement. C’est un vidéoprojecteur qui demande quelques compromis, donc, sur la luminosité et l’endurance notamment, mais si vous cherchez un petit cinéma nomade, cette promotion peut vous faire sauter le pas.

articles.title: Black Friday : l’OLED ultralarge de 45 pouces de LG est à moitié prix chez Amazon, 799,99 € au lieu de 1 599,99 €
articles.text:
À dix jours du Black Friday, qui tombe le 27 novembre, Amazon a déjà fait passer un écran gaming OLED ultralarge sous la barre des 800 €. Le LG UltraGear 45GX90SA-B, un 45 pouces incurvé en 3 440 x 1 440 pixels, est affiché à 799,99 € au lieu de 1 599,99 € de prix conseillé : nous ne l’avons pas testé, mais nous détaillons ce qu’il apporte et ce qu’il impose à votre bureau.
Le LG UltraGear 45GX90SA-B est un écran gaming OLED incurvé de 45 pouces au format 21:9, en 3 440 x 1 440 pixels, rafraîchi à 240 Hz avec un temps de réponse annoncé de 0,03 ms. Amazon l’affiche à 799,99 €, soit 50 % sous son prix conseillé de 1 599,99 €, et présente l’offre comme limitée dans le temps.
La remise vise d’abord les joueurs sur PC qui veulent un écran immersif, à condition d’avoir une carte graphique capable de suivre. Elle intéresse aussi celles et ceux qui travaillent avec plusieurs fenêtres ouvertes en parallèle.
Le LG UltraGear 45GX90SA-B est à 799,99 € chez Amazon, contre 1 599,99 € de prix conseillé.
Pourquoi choisir le LG UltraGear 45GX90SA-B ?
- La dalle OLED : Chaque pixel s’éteint individuellement, ce qui donne des noirs profonds dans une pièce sombre. LG annonce la certification DisplayHDR True Black 400 et une couverture de 98,5 % du DCI-P3.
- Le 240 Hz en 3 440 x 1 440 : Cette définition demande moins à la carte graphique qu’une 4K, ce qui aide à approcher les 240 images par seconde que l’écran peut afficher dans les jeux rapides. G-Sync Compatible et FreeSync Premium sont annoncés.
- Le format 21:9 incurvé : Avec sa courbure de 800R, l’image enveloppe le champ de vision en jeu de course, de simulation ou d’aventure. Au bureau, elle laisse la place à deux fenêtres côte à côte.
Du jeu immersif au bureau : ce que change un écran de 45 pouces
En jeu, la courbure de 800R et le format 21:9 jouent la carte de l’immersion : course, simulation, aventure. Les 240 Hz et les 0,03 ms annoncés par LG profitent surtout aux titres rapides, à condition que votre PC tienne la cadence en 3 440 x 1 440 pixels. L’écran embarque aussi webOS, le système de LG : le constructeur évoque des chaînes gratuites et du cloud gaming, utiles pour lancer un contenu sans allumer le PC. Nous n’avons pas testé ce modèle, ces éléments viennent de la fiche du constructeur.
Au bureau, les 992,7 mm de large annoncés par LG offrent la place de plusieurs fenêtres en parallèle, pour le montage, les tableurs ou la programmation. L’écran mesure environ 66 cm de hauteur et 34 cm de profondeur, selon LG. Il convient moins aux petits bureaux, à celles et ceux qui préfèrent une diagonale de 24 à 27 pouces pour le jeu compétitif, ou qui visent la 4K, car la définition reste celle d’un QHD étiré sur 45 pouces.
Face aux écrans gaming OLED plus compacts
Ce 45 pouces ne répond pas au même besoin que les OLED de 27 pouces ou les ultralarges de 34 pouces, nettement plus compacts. Pour comparer les formats et les tarifs, notre comparatif des meilleurs écrans PC gamer reste le point de départ. En face, le 45GX90SA-B apporte une surface d’affichage et une immersion que ces formats n’offrent pas, mais aussi un encombrement que seul un grand bureau absorbe.
✅ Les points forts
- Dalle OLED incurvée (800R) de 45 pouces en 3 440 x 1 440 pixels
- 240 Hz et 0,03 ms (GtG) annoncés par LG
- Compatible NVIDIA G-Sync et AMD FreeSync Premium
- DisplayHDR True Black 400 et 98,5 % du DCI-P3 annoncés
- webOS intégré, avec chaînes gratuites et cloud gaming selon LG
❌ Les limites
- Remise de 50 % calculée sur le prix conseillé de 1 599,99 € affiché par Amazon
- Près d’un mètre de large : un grand bureau est nécessaire
- Définition QHD étirée sur 45 pouces, moins fine qu’une 4K
- Dalle OLED : mieux vaut éviter les éléments fixes affichés longtemps
Le prix affiché par Amazon au moment de la rédaction est de 799,99 € : vérifiez-le sur la fiche avant de décider.
À 799,99 €, le LG UltraGear 45GX90SA-B coûte la moitié de son prix conseillé et ramène un OLED ultralarge de 45 pouces sous la barre des 800 €. Il s’adresse aux joueurs sur PC dont la carte graphique tient le 3 440 x 1 440 à haute fréquence, et à celles et ceux qui veulent un seul grand écran pour jouer comme pour travailler.
Il convient moins si votre bureau est étroit, si vous cherchez une définition 4K ou si les éléments fixes sur une dalle OLED vous inquiètent. Le Black Friday tombe le 27 novembre et les prix évoluent d’un jour à l’autre, à la hausse comme à la baisse : mieux vaut comparer calmement que décider au dernier moment. Nous n’avons pas testé ce modèle, et la remise se mesure ici par rapport au prix conseillé affiché par Amazon.

articles.title: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
articles.text:
Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them.
Named Remote Lock, this new feature is shipping to devices upgraded to Windows 11 Insider Preview builds in the Beta (Build 26320.10003) and Experimental (Build 26340.10013) channels.
Admins can use Microsoft Intune custom configuration profiles to lock Microsoft Entra-joined, hybrid-joined, or MDM-enrolled devices that run Windows Enterprise, Education, or Pro.
After the IT department remotely locks the device, the system can only be unlocked via Intune, since PINs, passwords, local admins, or web sign-ins will no longer work. Microsoft added that the user's credentials will remain valid and can still be used to sign into other devices that haven't been locked.
"Windows signs out every active session, hides all sign-in options and shows a locked screen," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines. "Nothing is erased: the device stays enrolled and managed, BitLocker stays on and user data stays in place. The lock holds across restarts and while offline, and only an admin can lift it remotely, so the user picks up where they left off."
Admins can lock a device from the Intune admin center using the following procedure:
- Go to Devices > Windows > Configuration > Create > New policy. Choose Windows 10 and later, then Templates > Custom.
- Name the profile (for example, Remote lock - ON) and add the settings below, with LockState = 1.
- Assign the profile to a device group reserved for locked devices. To lock a device, add it to that group; the lock applies at the device's next check-in.
- To unlock, create a second profile with LockState set to 0 and assign it to an unlock group. Move the device from the lock group to the unlock group.
After Remote Lock is enabled, the device is not isolated from the enterprise network or erased. To do that, admins must use the device isolation and wipe controls in Intune.
However, users must keep BitLocker enabled to protect their data if the device is reimaged or the drive is removed because the Windows Recovery Environment, Safe Mode, and booting from USB or other media are not blocked.
With these Windows 11 preview builds, Microsoft has also begun testing new advanced security key management features that let users view and manage passkeys stored on a FIDO2 (Fast Identity Online 2) security key individually.
These new features allow admins to configure enterprise settings such as always-required user verification, minimum PIN length, and enterprise attestation.
In August, Microsoft also announced new privacy controls that let Windows 11 users choose which desktop apps can access their microphone, camera, and precise location.

articles.title: Inside Ivoire Tech Forum: Ten startup pitches, too few women
articles.text:
17 novembre 2026
Hello 👋,
Welcome back to Francophone Weekly by TechCabal, your weekly deep dive into the tech ecosystem across French-speaking Africa. For readers who want to understand Francophone Africa beyond headlines—through markets, startups, and systems. New editions of the newsletter will land directly in your inbox every Tuesday at 12 PM WAT.
By default, this newsletter is in French. If you’re reading this in your email inbox, click the “Read in English” button below to switch to the English version. If you’re reading on our website, you can either click the button below or toggle the language selector at the top right-hand side of the page to view the English edition.
Dix start-up ont présenté leurs projets pour tenter de remporter 35 millions de francs CFA (62 000 dollars) lors de la dernière journée de l’Ivoire Tech Forum, une conférence sur la tech soutenue par le gouvernement à Abidjan, en Côte d’Ivoire. Les équipes les plus convaincantes avaient entraîné leurs modèles sur des données ivoiriennes, chiffres à l’appui. La liste des finalistes montrait aussi à quel point les femmes étaient peu nombreuses à monter sur scène.
La semaine dernière, Francophone Weekly se demandait si les 32 lauréats d’Ivoire Tech Next 15 et d’Ivoire Tech Scale Up trouveraient des financements et des clients. L’Ivoire Tech Forum, tenu du 11 au 13 novembre au Sofitel Hôtel Ivoire, en était le premier test.
Le forum s’est ouvert sur un Business Forum et une Deal Room mettant les lauréats en relation avec plus de 30 organismes de financement.
Le ministre Djibril Ouattara a donné le ton avec un chiffre. La Côte d’Ivoire a capté 1,7 % des montants levés lors des opérations africaines de plus de 500 000 dollars en 2025 et 2026, au huitième rang du continent. « Ce chiffre ne nous décourage pas, a-t-il déclaré. Il mesure la marge de progression qui est devant nous. »
Lors de la dernière journée, j’ai siégé au jury de la finale de la Pitch Competition.
1. Dix pitchs, cinq prix
            Photo de groupe sur scène lors de la finale du concours de pitch de l’Ivoire Tech Forum 2026, à Abidjan. Source de l’image : Lina Kacyem, responsable des investissements chez Launch Africa Ventures.
       
        
    
Chaque finaliste disposait de trois minutes de pitch, suivies d’une question du jury. Florence Fadika, de la Fondation Jeunesse Numérique, présidait le jury, aux côtés de Geth Maiga d’Expertise France, de Steve Tchoumba d’Active Space et de moi-même. Nous avons noté cinq critères : le problème, la solution et sa différenciation, le marché et le modèle économique, la capacité d’exécution de l’équipe, et la clarté du pitch.
L’enveloppe totale s’élevait à 35 millions de FCFA (environ 62 000 dollars) :
- Grand Prix de l’Innovation, 15 millions de FCFA (25 000 dollars) : Connectia. Dirigé par Babel Balsomi, ce laboratoire de données et d’IA entraîne des modèles sur des données africaines. Son produit Neuroverse vise à ramener le diagnostic de l’épilepsie de trois ans à six mois.
- Deuxième prix, 8 millions de FCFA (13 400 dollars) : JPF AerialOps. Drones et capteurs de sol alimentent un agronome numérique, Okani, qui produit un plan d’action et cible la pulvérisation.
- Troisième prix, 5 millions de FCFA (8 400 dollars) : AgriWatch. Surveillance en temps réel de la santé du bétail par l’IA, conçue pour fonctionner sans connexion internet.
- Coup de cœur du jury, 4 millions de FCFA (6 700 dollars) : Terre d’Ivoire. Un jeu multijoueur de simulation de vie situé à Abidjan, conçu par quatre étudiants.
- Prix de l’Impact, 3 millions de FCFA (5 000 dollars) : Baou. Une plateforme d’IA et une valisette éducative connectée pour les enfants ayant des besoins éducatifs particuliers.
Ce qui a départagé les lauréats
Les preuves. Les trois premiers ont tous présenté des résultats de terrain, et tous ont bâti leur IA sur des données locales plutôt que sur des modèles importés.
JPF AerialOps, également lauréat de Next 15, a avancé les chiffres les plus concrets de la journée : des rendements en hausse de 70 % et une consommation d’intrants en baisse de 45 % dans les exploitations qu’elle accompagne depuis fin 2023.
Elle lève 300 millions de FCFA (environ 530 000 dollars) et projette un chiffre d’affaires passant de 101 millions de FCFA (169 400 dollars) la première année à 788 millions de FCFA (1,3 million de dollars) la cinquième.
AgriWatch en est à un stade plus précoce, et l’a dit franchement. Un an de recherche sur fonds propres et un pilote de trois mois dans une ferme de Songon ont fait passer la précision de son modèle de 60 % à 80 %. Elle a besoin de 50 millions de FCFA (84 000 dollars) pour couvrir 2 000 têtes de bétail sur le territoire national.
Connectia s’est distinguée par l’étendue de son offre. Outre Neuroverse, elle développe DataWiz, un outil d’aide à la décision pour les entreprises, et Athéna, un outil vocal multilingue contre le décrochage scolaire.
Éducation : l’usage avant le revenu
Terre d’Ivoire a conquis la salle. Le jeu a attiré 49 000 joueurs en trois semaines, qui y passent en moyenne 40 minutes par jour, et a généré 800 000 FCFA (1 341) sans modèle économique. Le jury a récompensé cet engagement. L’équipe doit maintenant transformer cette attention en revenus au-delà de la publicité. Baou, portée par un couple, a produit et distribué 7 000 kits, fonctionne en neuf langues africaines et a reçu huit distinctions, dont une de l’UNESCO. Son IA réalise un prédiagnostic de la neurodivergence, un besoin que l’école publique couvre rarement.

2. L’économie informelle comme marché
            Djibril Ouattara, ministre de la Transition Numérique et de l’Innovation Technologique, lors de l’annonce des lauréats d’Ivoire Tech Next 15 et Scale Up, le 4 novembre 2026 à Abidjan. Source de l’image : Gouvernement de Côte d’Ivoire.
       
        
    
Trois finalistes ciblent les travailleurs informels, qui occupent environ 90 % des emplois ivoiriens selon Tylimmo. Tylimmo, autre lauréat de Next 15, numérise les quittances de loyer pour construire un score locatif co-développé avec l’agence de notation Bloomfield.
Un bon score ouvre l’accès à la location-vente, avec une garantie contre les loyers impayés pouvant aller jusqu’à 12 mois. L’entreprise revendique 2 500 ménages inscrits et devait lancer un pilote de 120 familles la semaine suivante.
Je Veux Bara, réseau social des travailleurs de l’informel, compte 65 000 utilisateurs après quatre ans et un taux de conversion de 10 % vers ses services payants. Djaya, une plateforme qui met en relation porteurs de projets, investisseurs et experts, est encore en phase de test à Abidjan.
Deux autres pitchs ont montré tout ce qui reste à résoudre à la base de l’économie. Convergence vend des systèmes d’information hospitaliers aux petites cliniques, dont huit sur dix en sont dépourvues selon son fondateur.
AVI Biomasse Hub met en relation coopératives et industriels pour valoriser les cabosses de cacao inutilisées. Son pilote ne demande que 3 millions de FCFA (5 000 dollars), une somme trop faible pour une banque et trop précoce pour la plupart des fonds.
Où sont les femmes ?
La scène du forum ne reflétait pas les entrepreneurs du pays. Seuls deux des 32 lauréats de Next 15 et de Scale Up sont dirigés par des femmes, et tous deux figurent dans la catégorie PME. La cohorte startups n’en compte aucun.
Lors de la finale, trois des dix pitchs étaient portés ou coportés par des femmes. C’est une entreprise dirigée par une femme, Connectia, qui a remporté le Grand Prix. Or près de 30 % des entreprises ivoiriennes sont dirigées par des femmes, selon la presse rendant compte d’une étude nationale sur le financement des femmes entrepreneures lancée en février 2026, et plus de 60 % de ces entreprises évoluent dans l’informel.
En Afrique subsaharienne, environ 26 % des femmes adultes exercent une activité entrepreneuriale, selon BCG. L’entonnoir se resserre fortement à l’approche du capital : les startups dirigées par une femme n’ont reçu que 0,9 % des financements de startups africaines en 2025, alors qu’elles représentaient 9 % des opérations, selon Africa: The Big Deal.
Les Ivoiriennes créent et dirigent des entreprises en grand nombre, mais peu d’entre elles accèdent aux programmes qui orientent l’attention de l’État et l’argent des investisseurs. Le ministère devrait publier la répartition par genre des candidatures à chaque programme, puis recruter la prochaine cohorte via des réseaux qui touchent déjà les fondatrices, comme le Guichet Investir au Féminin du CEPICI, qui prévoit d’accompagner 1 000 femmes entrepreneures dans sa phase pilote.

3. Après les prix
            Des passants dans les rues d’Abidjan, en Côte d’Ivoire. Source de l’image : Eva Blue sur Unsplash.
       
        
    
Un prix de pitch valide une entreprise. Il la finance rarement. Le Grand Prix de 15 millions de FCFA (25 000 dollars) représente 5 % de la levée en cours de JPF AerialOps. Deux des dix finalistes, JPF et Tylimmo, étaient déjà lauréats de Next 15 : les mêmes entreprises concentrent donc une large part du soutien de l’État.
Le ministre a lui-même fixé le critère dès le premier jour. Le succès, a-t-il dit, ne se mesurera pas « au nombre de discours prononcés », mais aux rendez-vous obtenus et aux pilotes lancés. Quatre mesures permettraient de vérifier si le forum a passé ce test :
- Publier les résultats de la Deal Room. Rendre compte, dans les trois mois, des rendez-vous tenus, des lettres d’intention signées et des montants engagés, par financeur.
- Transformer les finalistes en pilotes du secteur public. La surveillance du bétail d’AgriWatch et le logiciel clinique de Convergence répondent à des besoins que l’État finance déjà.
- Suivre le genre à chaque étape. Publier chaque année la part des femmes parmi les candidats, les lauréats, les finalistes et les entreprises financées.
- Financer les petits tickets. Un fonds adossé au ministère pour les tickets de moins de 10 millions de FCFA (16 800 dollars) permettrait à des projets comme celui d’AVI de survivre entre deux compétitions.
Les fondateurs que j’ai écoutés le 13 novembre construisent des solutions à des problèmes ivoiriens avec des données ivoiriennes. Les douze prochains mois diront si les clients et les capitaux suivent, et si la scène de l’an prochain fera plus de place aux fondatrices du pays.

articles.title: Microsoft explica el falló en Outlook, Teams y más: “más del 80 % de los servidores no respondieron”
articles.text:
La explicación llegó de parte de Charles Lamanna, vicepresidente ejecutivo de Copilot en la compañía, a través de una publicación en X con un resumen del análisis de causa raíz.
“El incidente del jueves 12 de noviembre de 2026 fue provocado por tres factores principales que, juntos, causaron una caída global en la pasarela de red que da servicio a muchos servicios de Microsoft 365”, escribió Lamanna.
Un defecto oculto desde julio que nadie detectó
El origen del problema fue un fallo “latente” que llevaba tres meses instalado en los servidores sin generar consecuencias visibles. Según detalló Lamanna, se trató de una contención de bloqueo dentro de un proceso interno que provocaba que la máquina quedara fuera de servicio bajo ciertas condiciones de carga.
Ese defecto surgió como resultado de una corrección preparada específicamente para los servidores de la pasarela de red de Microsoft 365, sin relación con otros despliegues de Windows.
El cambio comenzó a implementarse en julio y se propagó de forma global durante varias semanas sin que se observara ningún inconveniente.
“Nuestras pruebas de carga habituales no detectaron el problema latente debido a la diferente mezcla de tráfico y SKUs utilizada en nuestros laboratorios de prueba”, explicó el directivo. El problema se agravaba en máquinas con más núcleos y hardware más moderno, mientras que los laboratorios de la empresa solían priorizar equipos más débiles y con menos núcleos.
Por qué se afectaron tantos servicios
Microsoft 365 mantiene dos sistemas de pasarela de red independientes, pensados para garantizar aislamiento y alta disponibilidad entre servicios.
Unas 15 horas antes de la caída, Teams se transfirió desde la pasarela alternativa hacia la pasarela principal, la misma que también da soporte a Exchange Online. Ese traspaso, parte de las operaciones normales de resiliencia de la compañía, incrementó la carga y modificó los patrones de tráfico habituales.
Al mismo tiempo, cerca del 14% de la capacidad de servidores de esa pasarela estaba fuera de servicio por un problema no vinculado, registrado el día anterior. Microsoft ya trabajaba en devolver esa capacidad mediante procesos rutinarios de mantenimiento, y aclaró que esa reducción “no tuvo impacto por sí sola”.
La combinación de ambos factores sí resultó determinante. “Tomados en conjunto, el aumento de carga y la capacidad reducida de servidores hicieron que la pasarela de red encontrara el error latente de julio”, señaló Lamanna. Las solicitudes se acumularon hasta que los servidores dejaron de responder, justo durante la ventana de mayor tráfico en Estados Unidos.
Los sistemas de gestión de tráfico redirigieron automáticamente a los usuarios hacia otros puntos sanos, un mecanismo que suele evitar interrupciones ante fallos de hardware, software o red. Pero esa redirección aumentó la probabilidad de que el mismo problema se replicara en los servidores restantes.
Así, en menos de dos horas, el defecto antes desconocido alcanzó a toda la flota de servidores y la dejó inoperativa. En su punto más bajo, más del 80% de los servidores no respondía.
Microsoft precisó además que, por un problema adicional, los compartimentos normales que aíslan las distintas particiones de capacidad no lograron contener la falla en cascada, lo que permitió que el impacto se extendiera a toda la infraestructura global de la pasarela de red.
Cómo Microsoft restableció el servicio
La recuperación demandó más tiempo del habitual porque, cada vez que los servidores volvían a estar activos, la demanda de tráfico acumulado los saturaba de inmediato y los dejaba nuevamente sin responder.
Los procesos automatizados de recuperación de la compañía no estaban diseñados para restablecer el servicio desde un estado de falta de respuesta tan generalizado.
A esto se sumó que, al tratarse de un defecto latente desde hacía meses, los mecanismos habituales de reversión, despliegue controlado y banderas de funciones no pudieron revertir el cambio con rapidez.
Una vez que los ingenieros confirmaron el origen del problema, Microsoft desarrolló una actualización que devolvió el código a su estado anterior conocido como estable. Para aplicar la corrección de forma progresiva, la compañía retiró grupos de servidores del servicio, aplicó el cambio, los reinició y luego los reincorporó de manera gradual, en bloques de gran tamaño que llegaron a superar el 50% de una región a la vez.

articles.title: Mercadona llevó a los tribunales a una clienta por un lápiz de cejas de 3,50 euros: ha sido condenada por un delito leve de hurto
articles.text:
Los hechos ocurrieron en junio de 2025 en un supermercado de Peñarroya-Pueblonuevo (Córdoba). La cliente fue sorprendida por un vigilante de seguridad cuando intentaba salir del establecimiento con el cosmético. Ella admitió sus actos y devolvió el lápiz. Además, este estaba en buen estado y era recuperable.
El Juzgado de Instrucción número dos de Peñarroya le impuso una pena de 25 días de multa (cuota diaria de 6 euros). Así pues, son 150 euros. También tiene que pagar las costas del juicio.
El argumento del precio no ha bastado para anular la condena
Entre otros argumentos, la defensa apuntó que no existían pruebas. También que se vulneraba el principio acusatorio. Asimismo, se invocó el principio de intervención mínima. Se defendía que no debería haber intervención del Derecho penal en casos de tan poca entidad. Más aún en aquellas situaciones en las que había posibilidad de recuperación y reventa.
La Audiencia ha desestimado el recurso. Se ha dicho que, una vez que el legislador ha decidido tipificar como delito una determinada conducta, los jueces tienen que aplicar la ley. Que el precio sea mínimo no puede servir de excusa para no castigar el hecho de sustracción.
En el caso de aplicación del artículo 234 del Código Penal, se contemplaba como regla general que los hurtos de hasta 400 euros serían sancionados con multas de 1 a 3 meses, salvo las excepciones establecidas en el propio artículo. Por tanto, se establecía un límite para diferenciar la respuesta penal. Sin embargo, en el artículo no se establece que haya un límite inferior.
Por qué la multa fue de 25 días
Se ha tenido en cuenta que se trata de un delito en grado de tentativa. Los delitos intentados se castigan con una pena menor (uno o dos grados inferiores) que la del delito consumado. Esto se hace en función del peligro del intento y de la ejecución alcanzada (artículo 62 CP).
En materia de multas es frecuente utilizar el sistema de días-multa. Hay que distinguir la duración de la pena de la cantidad pagada por día. Esta última se determina en función de la situación económica del condenado (artículo 50).
Así pues, en este caso se ha reducido por tentativa a 25 días. Con una cuota de 6 euros diarios, se llega a los 150 euros (más costas).

articles.title: Xiaomi Smart Band 11 ya es oficial: pantalla de 2.000 nits, hasta 21 días de batería y versiones con NFC para pagar desde la muñeca
articles.text:
La familia Smart Band de Xiaomi lleva años siendo la puerta de entrada favorita para quienes quieren monitorizar su actividad física sin gastar lo que cuesta un reloj inteligente completo. Con el lanzamiento de la nueva Xiaomi Smart Band 11, la marca da un paso adelante en materiales, visibilidad en exteriores y conectividad, presentando una gama dividida en cuatro versiones que parten desde los 59,99 euros y que, esta vez sí, vuelve a traer variantes oficiales con NFC para pagar desde la muñeca.
XIAOMI Smart Band 11, pulsera de actividad
Pantalla más brillante, biseles simétricos y salto en materiales
A nivel estético, Xiaomi sigue alejando a su pulsera de la apariencia puramente deportiva para acercarla más a un accesorio de diario. El frontal monta una pantalla AMOLED de 1,72 pulgadas con biseles simétricos muy reducidos y un brillo pico que sube hasta los 2.000 nits, una cifra propia de relojes mucho más caros que asegura una lectura cómoda incluso a pleno sol.
Sensores más precios, seguimiento en piscina e HyperOS 4
En el interior, esta nueva pulsera de actividad de Xiaomi estrena un nuevo sensor PPG de doble LED y doble fotodiodo que, según las pruebas internas de la marca, alcanza una precisión de hasta el 98,2% en la medición de frecuencia cardíaca.
Mantiene la resistencia al agua de 5 ATM, pero añade monitorización del pulso también bajo el agua, algo especialmente útil para quienes nadan de forma habitual. En total, registra más de 150 modos deportivos (con detección automática de seis actividades) e incorpora el indicador Vitality Score para resumir el estado físico reciente.
El análisis del descanso también se actualiza con Sleep Algorithm 2.0, capaz de medir la variabilidad de la frecuencia cardíaca nocturna y generar informes semanales y mensuales con consejos prácticos sobre hábitos que afectan al sueño.
Todo ello queda gobernado por el sistema operativo Xiaomi HyperOS 4, que además de renovar los menús introduce una función muy curiosa: permite vincular la pulsera de forma simultánea a un móvil Xiaomi compatible y a un iPhone para recibir notificaciones de ambos teléfonos en la muñeca.
En autonomía, Xiaomi promete hasta 21 días de uso ligero en la edición estándar y 18 días en las versiones con NFC (que en uso real con notificaciones activas y entrenamientos semanales se traducirán previsiblemente en torno a semana y media o dos semanas reales).
Estas son las diferentes versiones disponibles
Desde ya, puedes comprar en la tienda online de Xiaomi esta nueva pulsera de actividad, la cual llega disponible en un amplio abanico de acabados:
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Standard Edition (59,99 euros): cuenta con marco de aluminio y llega en negro, plateado, rosa, morado y dorado.
XIAOMI Smart Band 11, pulsera de actividad
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 NFC Edition (79,99 euros): añade chip NFC para pagos sin contacto y está disponible en negro, plateado y rosa.
Xiaomi Smart Band 11 NFC
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Unibody Edition (89,99 euros): apuesta por un cuerpo fabricado íntegramente en metal en acabado morado (también con NFC).
Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Unibody
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Ceramic Edition (89,99 euros): la opción más elegante de la familia, con acabado cerámico en color blanco perla y conectividad NFC.

articles.title: AI music company claims copyright over musician's own recording, gets her YouTube video removed
articles.text:
WTF?! There are worse things AI can do to music streaming services than fill them with slop tracks. Take, for example, the recent case of an AI content company founded last year that claimed ownership of a musician's own five-year-old recording.
As reported by 404 Media, writer and musician Samantha Shokin recorded a 50-second version of Bulgarian folk song Bre Petrunko during the pandemic, initially uploading it to SoundCloud before posting it on YouTube. The track didn't attract much attention at first, but it had reached around 125,000 views after four years.
Last summer, after noticing an increase in comments on the video, Shokin discovered that DJs were sampling her voice and using it in dozens of songs.
"The first thing that comes to mind is, 'Oh my god, someone stole my voice and didn't credit me,'" she said.
Shokin later realized that the DJs had purchased a pack of samples from a company called Loopmasters, and her track was part of its "Folk Legends" set.
After she contacted the distributor, it apologized, assured her it was unaware of what had happened, and arranged royalties.
"I didn't love the way that it came about, but whatever, they tried to make right of the situation," she said.
Then, in October, her original YouTube video disappeared following a copyright complaint from a company called Media Nov Records. Shokin filed two counter-notifications, arguing that the video should stay up or not be demonetized, but they failed, and her attempts to contact the company went unanswered.
Media Nov Records is described as a "distribution company" that helps artists get their tracks onto digital platforms, but 404 Media notes that a lot of its website is focused on management and copyright protection.
"Our comprehensive rights management system leverages cutting-edge technology and legal expertise to ensure you receive the royalties you deserve," it reads. There's also mention of automated DMCA takedowns, YouTube content ID management, and AI-powered content recognition.
Media Nov told 404 Media it operates 500 channels. The outlet found AI imagery and repetitive electronic music across those it examined. Corporate records placed the company's founding last year, despite its website claiming roots in 1996.
Media Nov responded after 404 Media contacted it, initially saying it would investigate the claim and correct any error. It then contacted Shokin, requesting original audio files, recording evidence, publication dates, and other documentation proving ownership. The company blamed its failure to answer earlier messages from Shokin and Loopmasters on its spam folder.
It also brought Bulgarian composer Philip Koutev into the dispute. "Regarding 'Bre Petrunko,' we would like to clarify that the musical composition and arrangement rights associated with Philip Koutev's work must be distinguished from the rights in any individual sound recording. Media Nov Records also holds certain rights relating to the relevant musical content," the company told Shokin in an email.
Koutev popularized an arrangement of the traditional folk song in 1963. However, Media Nov did not answer when 404 Media asked which work in its catalog had triggered the complaint against Shokin.
Minutes after requesting proof of ownership, Media Nov emailed both Shokin and the publication to withdraw its removal request. Its bizarre explanation was that the video had "not generated revenue or received views," despite having accumulated around 125,000 views.
The company nevertheless maintained that it was not surrendering any rights, adding: "We intend to initiate appropriate legal proceedings regarding the underlying copyright dispute."
Around 24 hours later, Shokin's video returned. YouTube confirmed it had restored the recording because the claimant withdrew its complaint.
"It's ironic that they're in the copyright business," Shokin said. "It's not the arrangement that's in question. It's the voice and performance [...] they clearly have no clue what they're talking about."
AI music has already brought plenty of problems beyond questionable copyright claims. Platforms are being overwhelmed with fully AI-generated tracks, many of which are fraudulent. Australia is banning them from the charts, and despite Spotify deleting millions of these tracks, it is introducing an AI remixing tool for users next year.

articles.title: Production AI, Architecture Trade-offs & Team Design: InfoQ Opens Registration for 6 January Cohorts
articles.text:
InfoQ has opened registration for six online cohort workshops starting between January 9 and 22, 2027. Covering AI Engineering, Software Architecture, and High-Performing Teams, the five-week programs bring senior engineers, architects, and engineering leaders together to work through technical and organizational decisions with experienced practitioners.
The workshops go beyond studying technical material. Participants apply frameworks from QCon and InfoQ to decisions from their own work, compare approaches with practitioners from other organizations, and return to discuss what they tried and learned. Working across different organizational contexts helps expose trade-offs and assumptions that may not emerge from an internal discussion alone.
Each cohort combines four hours of live facilitated sessions per week, independent application work, and a program-specific capstone.
AI Engineering: Retrieval, Agents, and Evaluation
Production AI involves decisions beyond model selection: how context is retrieved and maintained, how much autonomy agents should have, and how reliability, latency, and inference costs are managed.
The InfoQ AI Engineering Program examines these decisions through RAG architectures, agent design, platforms, and evaluation. Participants work through technical approaches and failure modes, applying them to AI systems or proposals from their own work.
Three January cohorts are planned:
- Hien Luu, AI/ML leader and author of MLOps with Ray, starts January 9, Saturdays at 09:00 PST.
- Adi Polak, Director of Developer Experience Engineering at Confluent, starts January 21, Thursdays at 08:00 PST.
- Lan Chu, principal engineer at Rabobank and author of Post-training LLMs, starts January 22, Fridays at 14:00 CET. Her QCon London 2026 presentation examined a production RAG system built on more than 10,000 documents and used by more than 300 people.
Architecture: Decisions Across Teams and Platforms
Architecture choices are shaped by system requirements, team boundaries, platform ownership, and organizational constraints.
The InfoQ Architect Program covers distributed systems, decentralized decisions, platform engineering, and AI architecture. Participants apply the material to architecture decisions they currently own, compare trade-offs with peers, and practice communicating their reasoning to stakeholders.
The capstone involves co-authoring a technical article examining AI's role in software architecture or platform engineering. Selected articles may be published on InfoQ.
Both cohorts start January 22 and are facilitated by Luca Mezzalira, independent software architect and author of Building Micro-Frontends. Friday sessions are offered at 09:30 GMT and 10:00 EST.
High-Performing Teams: Delivery Flow, Ownership, and AI
Faster coding does not necessarily improve delivery when reviews, approvals, or infrastructure dependencies become the constraint. AI agents also change how responsibilities are divided and which work requires human judgment.
The InfoQ High-Performing Teams Program examines team structure, ownership, delivery flow, AI responsibilities, and engineering metrics as one operating model.
Participants evaluate constraints in their own team environments, compare approaches with peers, and develop a proposed target operating model covering responsibilities, workflow, and measurement.
The January 12 cohort is facilitated by Olimpiu Pop, InfoQ Podcast co-host with experience in solutions architecture, engineering management, and CTO roles. Sessions run on Tuesdays and Thursdays, from 16:00 to 18:00 CET.
Workshop Format and Participation
The live online workshops focus on discussion and application rather than recorded lectures. Participants work with an experienced facilitator and a small cross-company peer group, bringing current engineering decisions into the sessions and testing approaches between meetings.
Sessions are not recorded, allowing participants to discuss organizational constraints more openly. Certification requires attendance, active participation, and successful completion of the program capstone.
Participation costs USD 1,470 per person. Full schedules, syllabi, and registration details are available on the InfoQ Online Certification Programs website.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.text:
Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
- Date:
- November 17, 2026
- Source:
- University of Jyväskylä - Jyväskylän yliopisto
- Summary:
- A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.
- Share:
An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.
The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.
The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.
These questions are especially important because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.
To investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.
More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills
One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.
Cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn new things, and solve problems. These abilities play an important role in school performance and everyday decision-making.
The findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.
"The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.
"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.
Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently
The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.
Among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.
Working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing new information.
Light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.
The differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.
Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity
The study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.
Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.
One possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.
This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.
"Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.
"However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is important to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing."
What the Eight-Year Study Revealed
The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.
The current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.
Researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.
To evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.
Importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.
Nevertheless, the results offer an important perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.
The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.
Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.
The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Jyväskylä - Jyväskylän yliopisto. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Petri Jalanko, Marja H. Leppänen, Bert Bond, Jari A. Laukkanen, Timo A. Lakka, Eero A. Haapala. Associations of Physical Activity and Sedentary Time From Childhood to Adolescence With Cognition in Adolescence: The PANIC Study. Pediatric Exercise Science, 2026; 38 (3): 268 DOI: 10.1123/pes.2025-0083

articles.title: How Canada gets to space on its own terms | BetaKit
articles.text:
Today on The BetaKit Podcast, we’re talking about space.
Why? First and foremost: space is cool as hell. I think most people, at some point in their life, at least consider being an astronaut like our two guests today, the CEOs of Nordspace (Rahul Goel) and Canada Rocket Company (Hugh Kolias).
“It takes us—to launch our small rocket—six months just to get an approval. We can do that in 24 hours in the United States. We can drive our rocket down to the States like a lot of companies have—and they never come back.”
Rahul Goel
There’s another reason: this year’s BetaKit Most Ambitious issue was focused on sovereign technology, nation building, and all the invisible infrastructure Canadians rely on that we don’t currently own or control. It turns out that a lot of that infrastructure lives in space, which we desperately need access to, let alone control of.
SpaceX is scaling back its rocket ride-share program. It could cut off Canada’s access to space. Or, according to our guests, it could be the catalyst for Canada’s sovereign space goals, leading to significant strategic and financial windfalls. In Budget 2026, the federal government earmarked previously committed capital toward sovereign space capacity.
But what does sovereign space capacity look like? And how will it get built?
Our two guests this week, who joined shortly after they were on stage together at tech festival Nrth in September, have significantly different (perhaps competitive) visions of how this will happen. But you’ll find that their debate on how to get to space, while sometimes tense, is always respectful.
Why? Getting to space is hard. Very hard.
And ultimately, they both share the same goal: ad astra Canada.
So prepare for launch, and let’s dig in.

articles.title: Fandango Warns Ticket Buyers of Payment Card Data Exposure
articles.text:
US movie ticketing company Fandango is warning customers that payment card information from some purchases made through its checkout page between October 8 and 11 may have been accessed by an unauthorized party.
Fandango says it launched an investigation, assisted by external cybersecurity experts, after learning of a problem affecting the page.
“Our investigation identified evidence that an unauthorized party could access payment card information associated with certain transactions on our checkout page from October 8-11, 2026,” the company says in its notice to customers.
Fandango recently determined which customers’ data was potentially at risk. It has not disclosed how the incident occurred, but says the problem has been fixed and its security processes have since been strengthened.
Potentially exposed data includes the card number, CVV code, expiration date, and billing ZIP code, as well as the customer’s email address. According to Fandango, customer names, Social Security numbers, government-issued identification details, and other account data were not affected.
“Fandango is not currently aware of any fraudulent use of your information as a result of this incident, but nonetheless is informing customers to take appropriate steps to protect their information,” the notice reads.
Affected individuals can sign up for two years of free IDX services, including credit monitoring, dark web scanning, identity theft insurance, and managed identity restoration.
Fandango has not disclosed the total number of impacted customers. Filings with state regulators list 913 affected residents in Oregon and 18 in Vermont.
A notice was also submitted to the California Attorney General’s office, which requires a copy whenever a breach notification is sent to more than 500 California residents.
Fandango, a Versant Media Group brand, handles online ticket sales for more than 31,000 movie screens in the US and also runs the Rotten Tomatoes review site.
